REVIEW: These are, without question, the best headphones/earbuds I've ever owned. I'll keep this review short, but here are the highlights.Pros:* Affordable: You can buy 10 pairs of these for the price of a single pair of their competitors. After trying out my first pair, I've since bought a pair for my bedroom, home office, and office at work to complement the pair that I bring with me everywhere when out-and-about. Surprisingly high-quality audio: these little earbuds reliably output beautiful, crisp audio with shockingly deep bass that I can feel in my toes. I honestly was shocked to hear so much more in some of my favorite songs with these than my previous, more expensive headphones.* Comfort: This is of course very personal and what works for me may not work for you, but I have had no issue comfortably wearing these through long plane flights, while running on a treadmill/outdoors (connected to my beloved Sansa Clip), gaming, and listening to podcasts/youtube videos at home. I've worn them for 5+ hours before without my ears getting sore.* Noise-cancellation: I forget if they're even billed as doing this, but the earbuds fit snugly enough to REALLY drown out sound. I've been watching a movie on my laptop before when my roommate and several of his friends arrived at home, greeted me, sat down behind me, and scared me half to death after realizing I'd heard none of the above. They're phenomenal for when you need to drown out your surroundings to relax or just get some things done.Cons:None. Seriously these are among my all time most satisfying purchases, and I highly recommend them to anyone looking for earbuds.The only thing that has been a slight inconvenient for me a few times is cord length. These are about 3.6 feet long according to the listing (I was going to guess 3 or 4 feet), which means, for example, they're not going to stretch behind your desk and to the backside of a PC tower sitting on the floor. While there are easy ways to solve these problems (like buying a male-to-female 3.5mm cord (for about �10 or less) and keep the female end on your desk), it is something to keep in mind if you're not intending to use them with a nearby MP3 player or phone.At the same time, the relatively short cord length makes these headphones *ideal* for using while active. I can use these with my Sansa Clip attached to my running shorts when exercising very comfortably. While there is inevitably still some give in the cord (and the cord does sway a bit while I jog), I don't have to worry about it flailing wildly and or having to bundle up the slack cord before I get to exercising. For reference, I'm about 6'2". So if you're in the 7' range you should probably look to use them with an MP3 player/phone on an armband!I'll update this review if and when one of my 4 pairs finally gives out, but at this point you can rest assured that I'll be replacing them with a new pair of these same earbuds!

REVIEW_TITLE: Do these actually exist, because what they do looks a bit like magic, and which one should you choose?
REVIEW:
I've seen these on TV of course, and I'd thought that they were just computer graphics things, so I was surprised to discover they really do exist. I chose this particular one - the Evercross Diablo - based on it having the best specification, and I'm pleased with it. In my video I've shown the first nine rides (and that's rides, not the number of times it's come out of its box to be used) that a 15 year old had on it, really to show just how easy it is to use. The first four were indoors. It had just arrived, and we were all keen to get it out of the box and play with it, but we didn't take it outside until the next day when she'd found her helmet.
The next five rides were outside in a car park. The ground there is reasonably level, though not perfect, so I did worry how the Diablo would cope with the unevenness of the ground, but I needn't have. We started off with the speed and driving force set to minimum, just as we had inside. Each trip down the car park though, she let me gently increase the maximum speed (from 4mph to 12mph) and also increase the maximum driving force (how much push the motors will give to get you out of a dip). You control this using an app on your phone.
Let me tell you a bit about the app, because that's a real game changer for the Diablo. (I only used the android version, but there is an iOS version as well). You load the app on your phone and it gives you complete control over the sensitivity and response of the board. There are some presets - beginner, normal and advanced, but also there is a screen that gives you precise control. You can set maximum speed, driving force and turning response. This gives you a great way into using the board until you get confidence in your control of it. It connects to the board by Bluetooth, and the easy way to get the app is to use the QR code in the instruction book. My only criticism of this board is that there isn't also a sticker on the board with this QR code, so if you're playing with a friend, he or she can easily also get the app. It is findable in the Google Playstore, but a stuck on QR code would be great. Anyway, the app actually works, and works well, so I shouldn't complain too much!
The technical stuff that impressed me includes the hugely powerful motors. These are important not just to accelerate away, but also to get you out of trouble on rough ground. And finally, the braking effect. My girl was really impress with how easily and reliably she could stop the board. Apparently it's got two independent gyroscopes that support this. Whatever! But they do work really well.
The video is worth watching, because it shows how the board performs, and also how quickly children learn. I've briefly shown the board being unpacked, but the maximum length of video review is ten minutes, and I've concentrated on it being used.
So, am I happy? Yes, definitely. And my children? Absolutely delighted!

REVIEW:
There's lots of these drones around for sale now, so it's hard to pick one out. My video shows you the details of this as I unpacked it and flew it for the first couple of times, so let me just tell you the good and bad things about this one. First, the good.
It's easy to charge. For other drones, you've got to actually unplug the battery, sometimes remove it, and fit it to it's own special charger. This means you have a chance to damage the wires into the plugs and sockets, and also (speaking from experience) misplace the charger itself - it's very sad not to be able to fly your drone simply because you've lost the charger. This drone doesn't need any disassembly. It's got a standard usb charger socket on the outside, on the side, so you can charge it from any phone charger, including one in your car.
It's got a big, obvious on/off button. This is opposed to having to connect the wires to start it, or having a silly little slide switch hidden inside.
It has headless mode. Most drones have this now, but don't even think of buying one without. What headless mode is that when it's switched on, when you push the stick away from you, the drone moves away, regardless of which way it's pointing. Normal mode my help your coordination training, but when the bush or the tree is looming you'll be glad of not having to change, in your head, from left is left to left is right if the drone is pointing towards you.
It's pretty light. This means the motors have to work less hard to keep it aloft, and so the battery lasts for longer.
You can use the maker's app to use the camera in real time, so you can see what the camera is seeing, and simultaneously record the video or take photos on both your tablet and a memory card stuffed into the back of the camera.
It's stable, and can be trimmed so that, when there is no wind around, it will hover and stay in one place, making it a lot easier to learn to fly.
It has one touch launch and hover. This starts to drone, and pops it up to about a metre above the ground, and pretty well holds it there. This gives you the chance to concentrate on the steering, letting it maintain its set height.
So, what's wrong with it? Well, two things. First, the legs aren't securely fixed. If (when!) you crash they can fall off, and you need them to let it settle down on. I've dealt with this by using a dab of glue on each one. The second one is that it's a shame that printed onto the drone itself isn't the QR code you need to load the app. Eventually, you'll lose the user guide that has it in, and then you'll be stuck! I suppose if you put the user guide somewhere safe ....
I've included a bit of video taken directly on it's own camera at the end of my video. It's perfectly decent 720p - not 4k, but very acceptable as a record.
If you get this drone, I'm sure that you'll not be sad that you've bought it. I certainly like mine.

REVIEW_TITLE: Works exactly as it's supposed to.
REVIEW:
It's hard to know when to start teaching offspring country crafts, especially those that involve sharp things or fire, but there comes a time when a boy has to be able to set a fire, and I think it's best it's done with adult supervision. So I got this!
It turns out that as part of the residential experience that he's had with school my boy has already seen one of these in action, so he was very keen to give it a go. The easiest way to get a fire going with one of these is with cotton wool and vaseline. You put a tiny amount of vaseline onto and into a cotton wool ball, then what happens is that the cotton wool acts like a wick and the vaseline is like candlewax, and when you get one decent spark onto it it easily catches fire.
This fire stick works great. The striker comes with it. You find the sharp turned over edge of the striker, and rub it over the stick, first of all removing the black protective coating. Then, pointing the stick at the cotton wool, you stroke the stick with slow deliberate movements, and large sparks come off. The first one of these on the cotton wool starts it burning, then you can put twigs and so on onto the the flame and quickly get a fire.

REVIEW:
There are two readers on this product page. I've got the Elite model.
These days, for a hundred quid, you get a surprising amount of technology wrapped up in a very compact package. This device does a full-on reading of your car's engine management system, allowing you to trace faults and clear codes. This is a 'mode 6' device, which is pretty much state of the art. It lets your directly read data from many sensors, including (but not limited to!):
 Exhaust Gas Sensor Monitor
 Catalyst Monitor
 EGR Monitor
 VVT Monitor
 EVAP Monitor
 Exhaust Gas Sensor Heater Monitor
 Heated Catalyst Monitor
 Secondary Air Monitor
 Fuel System Monitor
 Boost Pressure Control Monitor
 NOx Adsorber Monitor
 NOx/SCR Catalyst Monitor
 Misfire Cylinder Data
 PM Filter Monitor
It will also monitor other things as well, though you might have to google to find the meaning of particular manufacturer codes.
Not only can you read error codes, you can also see and record datastreams from a large range of sensors in your car in real time - mine, for instance, has 55 datastreams. There's everything here that you could want to know. I'm well impressed.
What no one tells you though, is that after you've cleared an engine management code, just because the light doesn't come on straight away, it doesn't guarantee that you've cleared the fault. Instead, you'll need to take your car for several miles of driving, which should include idling, accelerating, driving at about 30mph, then at 50-60mph, and doing things like letting the engine do engine braking - slowing the car down without using your brakes. After you've done all of that the computer will have recalibrated itself, and will then show a fault if there are any residual problems. If you google '[your car brand] driving cycle' you can find what an american version of your car has to go through, but I think the cycles for UK cars are not quite so extensive.
This reader is certainly worth having a look at.
PRODUCT: OBDII EOBD Car Diagnostic Automotive Code Reader,Topdon Elite Check Engine Light Scan Tool Auto OBD2 Scanner with Read and Clear ABS/SRS Function,I/M Readiness for 24 Models 2006 and Later Vehicles

REVIEW:
Fifty quid these days buys you an awful lot of technology, and that's what this is. It gives you full access to error codes held in your car's computers, allows you use them for fault tracking, lets you reset them (delete them) and then check to see if the error recurs, or whether you've still got a problem. OBD was originally for checking an engine's emission controls - cars had to start having built in computers to cope with managing fuel and air mixtures, to minimise carbon monoxide and nox gases - but nowadays, to simplify management of cars the computer(s) on board monitor all engine functions, plus air bags and braking systems.
Not only does it do error codes, it can also record moment-by-moment readings of all of the measurements made, for you to examine afterwards.
Something that no one seems to tell you, though, is that when you've reset error codes, that the on-board computer often cannot tell straight away if there is still a fault. Instead, you'll need to take your car for several miles of driving, which should include idling, accelerating, driving at about 30mph, then at 50-60mph, and doing things like letting the engine do engine braking - slowing the car down without using your brakes. After you've done all of that the computer will have recalibrated itself, and will then show a fault if there are any residual problems. If you google '[your car brand] driving cycle' you can find what an american version of your car has to go through, but I think the cycles for UK cars are not quite so extensive.
This is seriously worth considering.
PRODUCT: OBD2 scanner Launch Creader 6001 Auto Car Code Reader Full OBDII/EOBD Diagnostic Functions Scan Tool with O2 Sensor Test and On-board Monitor Test

I also use them for helping to keep spare connecting wires (eg ethernet patch cables and charging cables) wrapped up neatly in my bag.
When I use these I always wrap them so the smoother side of the strip is outwards, and the furry side inwards. This stops one cable wrap sticking to another, and is also good for keeping them clean - the 'hook' side picks up dust and whatever much more than the smooth side. The other thing is that it's good practice to wrap signal wires (hdmi cables, audio cables, ethernet cables) up separately to mains cables, and to keep them apart. This helps prevent mains frequencies interfering with signals, and is safer.
These are fine. I'll end up buying some again when these have run out. There always seem to be more cables in my life!

REVIEW_TITLE: Top of the range phone at about a third of the price.
REVIEW:
I wanted a top-of-the range phone, but over �700 for an iPhone, with a potential lifetime of maybe two or three years at most, I find a bit ridiculous. Even a Samsung android phone of a similar specification to this is well over �500, so choosing this was fairly easy. It's specification is pretty impressive. Certainly, if you pick though it, there are ways that the iPhone and the Samsung beat it. They've got oled screens, and this has LCD - but comparing this to my son-in-laws iPhone plus, the difference is minimal, plus, being oled, his display will deteriorate in time - oled screens aren't perfect yet - and my LCD won't. The basic memory in this phone I find phenomenally huge - I can't see how I'll fill 64GB - but it's twice that of the iPhone - and it can, just like any android, be increased to 256GB with a memory card. But the other trick this phone has is that it accepts two SIM cards.
Two sim cards aren't necessary of course; maybe you have one for personal calls, and one for work. Maybe you do what I do, and save a bit of money by having one permanent card so people can always ring into you, and a second card that I routinely replace with whatever cheap offers are around. And when I go away from home I put a payg data card into that second slot, for cheap internet. Once you've a a dual sim phone you'll possibly not want to go back. And that's another issue with the iPhone and the Samsung. Samsung could easily make dual sim phones, and do for other markets, but telecoms providers don't like you to have that freedom.
Also, not only does this have a very fast, eight core processor, it also has bucketfuls of RAM. I don't play full on games, but this power does mean that the phone is always there - you're never waiting for it. The proper camera on the back is about as good as it gets. It takes detailed, well-coloured photos in standard mode. It does have a flash (but I hate taking flash photos) and will do a range of tricks like taking panorama photos and also attempt HDR photos. And the selfie camera on the front is more than adequate.
The phone has a full set of sensors. It's positioning system uses the Russian Glosnass system. The latest iPhone has moved over to this system as well, I've noticed, presumably because it does give better positioning. GPS pins me down to within a circle of about 20 metres radius. The circle of uncertainly for glosnass is only a couple of metres. Instead of showing that I'm probably in my garden, it shows which corner I'm in.
I'd not really heard of UMI, but it seems to be one of those huge companies. For the saving, and for the quality of this phone, and it's looks - the black one is genuinely beautiful - I think it's well worth having.

REVIEW_TITLE: A good device for your first steps into Vaping.
REVIEW:
This is an excellent kit, especially for those wanting to quit cigarettes or someone wanting to move-on from Cartomisers or ?cig-a-likes? and dip their toes into sub-ohm vaping and direct lung inhaling. The kit is really well made and the Tank performs well for its size etc.
Both the pre-installed coil inside the Tank and the spare are designed for use in Wattage mode and although this kit is capable of running Temperature Control coils, I strongly recommend that anyone wishing to use TC with a different Tank and Ni200 (Nickel) or Ti (Titanium) coils, takes time to learn everything they can about this before using the TC function. I have been vaping for well over 3 years and only extremely rarely will I use Ni200 or Ti coils in any of my numerous sub-Ohm Tanks.
When you get this, please check and fully charge the Battery. When mine was delivered, it was only a few percent from being fully charged but Li-Po or Li-Ion batteries do lose charge over time.
While this is happening, carefully remove the base and coil assembly from the Tank and ?Prime? the Coil by placing a few drops of your chosen e-liquid down the centre and to the wicking material that is visible through the 2 small holes in the side of the Coil. Carefully fill the Tank and replace the base/Coil assembly, taking care not to cross the threads. When the Battery is fully charged, turn it on by rapidly pressing the fire button 5 times. Make sure the screen on the device reads no higher than 20/25 Watts. When I first turned mine on, it was set at the maximum 40 Watts and may have damaged the new coil had I tried to fire it at this level. Now you can screw the Tank onto the battery. Make sure the airflow control ring is fully open and suck air through the mouthpiece 3 or 4 times without pressing the Fire button. This should help make sure the cotton wicking is fully saturated with e-liquid.
If you?ve followed the above procedure, you should not suffer any burning of the cotton or ?dry-hits?, as these are frequently called.
I used a 60/40 VG/PG mix e-liquid. I wouldn?t recommend e-liquids with less than 60% VG or higher than 80%. After taking a dozen or so vapes, I increased the power to 27.5 Watts and the Tank gave a good amount of vapour and plenty of flavour.
Pros:
Very well made and a fairly robust construction.
For its size (and price), the Tank in this kit gives good flavour and vapour.
2,200 mAh is a fairly decent capacity Battery. Battery life will depend on how frequently you vape and how high your Wattage is set.
The airflow control ring adjusts easily, but isn?t so loose as to move when using the device.
The complete unit is small enough to fit in a pocket or handbag.*
Cons:
Whilst bright, the font on the screen is rather small, specifically that showing coil resistance and the Voltage being applied.
The USB charging port is located on the base.**
Summary:
Please carefully read the instruction leaflet before using this device for the first time. The Kit is good value for money. It?s well made and appears robust. Filling the Tank is not difficult if your e-liquid is supplied in a plastic bottle with a fine point, as that allows you to place the point into either of the 2 filling ?slots?. It will be more difficult if your e-liquid is supplied in a glass bottle with a Dropper. If this is the case, Amazon sells 3 ml and 5 ml plastic pipettes, which are what I use.
*Always turn the device off (5 rapid presses of the fire button) and completely close off the airflow control ring if you plan to put the device in your pocket or a handbag.
**For charging, I suggest you remove the Tank and keep it upright because you will have to lay the Battery unit (or Mod) on its side due to the positioning of the USB port. At the very least, fully close off the airflow control ring if you have to leave the Tank on the device when you charge it.

Now, it covers several levels of vaping devices and implies that the kit gives you more or less everything you need, except e-liquid, to start using it the minute it's in your hands.
This kit would be ideal for intermediate vapers or those just starting out. It can deliver up to 50 Watts of power (when the battery is freshly charged) and the Tank in the kit gives enough vapour and flavour to satisfy those who never vape above 40 or so Watts. Vaping at 50 Watts with the device is going to impact battery life between charges.
The Mod and the Tank appear well made and solidly constructed. The device is really compact and fits comfortably in the hand. Wattage output is dictated by the battery's charge status and the coil resistance; the device isn't adjustable.
I love the device for the design, build quality and overall performance. My concern is that this device is claimed to be capable of Temperature Control which I believe it clearly isn't. Having said that, any experienced vaper will see this and I strongly recommend those new to vaping, do NOT try using Temperature Control until you have fully acquainted yourself with the principles and have a really good understanding of Ohm's Law. Pollux Vape Kit

Whilst I would not recommend it for experienced vapers, it is a good and very cost effective solution for anyone wanting to switch to vaping.
Pros for the Mod:
The Mod is very well made.
The screen is bright and legible.

My major concern with the Mod is that the charging port is on the base. To charge the battery, you need to lay the device on its side and if you do this, I strongly recommend that you remove the Tank.
Pros for the Tank:
For its size, the Tank produces a good amount of vapour and delivers plenty of flavour.
Changing coils is relatively simple.
The top-fill works well and is easy to use.
It is well machined and finished-off.
There?s plenty of airflow even though the bore of the coils is rather small
Cons for the Tank:
I strongly recommend that you do not use e-liquids with less than 60% VG, preferably 70%. I first filled the Tank using a 50/50 VG/PG e-liquid and the coil flooded and the tank leaked through the air flow control ring. The Manual does say NOT to use e-liquids below 70/30 VG/PG and I agree with this recommendation but I wanted to see what happened with 50/50 mixes. But from my personal experience, 60/40 works well too.
I would comment on the Tank?s capacity but as the TPD restricts Tank capacity to 2 ml, a bigger Tank wouldn?t comply with the Law.
Overview:
Although the Mod unit in my Kit was almost fully charged, I would recommend charging the internal Battery before using the device for the first time. I also strongly recommend that you take the time to properly ?prime? all new coils and to make sure all of the Tank parts are properly screwed together. Note; do not over-tighten as this can damage the ?O? ring seals.
The pre-installed 0.5 Ohm coil was reading 0.54 Ohm on the display and I set the Wattage to 30 Watts for this review. The coil will probably handle more power but, at 30 Watts, I got a satisfying volume of vapour and adequate flavour. 30 Watts should help extend your Battery life too. After discovering the leaking issue, I was vaping an e-liquid made by VapeWild, ?I?m on a Roll? (a Max VG mix) and then one made by Vapbus called ?Popcorn?, which is a 70/30 VG/PG mix. Even a maximum VG e-liquid (90%?) didn?t give me any dry hits.
Summary:
This is a well designed and manufactured Starter Kit that performs really well and is very good value for money. Spare coils are available on the Amazon website and cost around �12 for a box of 5, so they are not expensive. Please remember that very sweet e-liquids will reduce your coil life marginally, as will exceeding the maximum recommended Wattage.

It is essential to fully charge the Mod's built-in battery before using this device for the first time. It's also essential to properly prime the coil before filling the Tank. After priming the coil and assembling/filling the Tank with e-liquid, leave the Tank (after screwing it on the top of the Mod) for several minutes to make sure the coil is completely saturated.
The coils that come with the device are recommended for use between 15 and 50 Watts. If this is your first device, I strongly recommend starting off with the power set at the minimum, i.e. 15 Watts. Then, you can gradually increase the power until you find the vapor production satisfactory. Starting off new coils at the lower end of their recommended power range and only gradually increasing the power will help coil life and should prevent applying too much power which can burn the cotton, making the coil useless. Replacement coils are available from Amazon.

REVIEW:
I'm reviewing this based on the fact that it's a very simple AIO (All In One) kit designed for those dipping their toes into vaping for perhaps the first time and wanting to quit or dramatically reduce their cigarette smoking. I quit a 2+ pack a day habit, well over 3 years ago, literally overnight thanks to vaping.
I own other Auro products and they are all very well made. Operation is extremely simple, as there's nothing to adjust and no menu system to learn/navigate. I suggest that you put the battery unit on charge before you use this for the first time, just to make sure it is at maximum capacity. Always prime a new coil before vaping on it. Just put a drop or two of e-liquid onto the cotton which is visible through the wicking holes around the outside of the coil (4 holes) and a few drops down the centre. Once you've filled the Tank, leave the device so the cotton can become completely saturated for 10/15 minutes, to be on the safe side. It's far better to wait a while than risk burning the coil, as this will destroy it and give you a burnt taste.
Although the Tank design is very simple, it generates good vapour and great flavour too. It's also extremely easy to refill. It will work very well with 70/30 VG/PG e-liquids. Because of the coil design, I would recommend avoiding e-liquids sold as "maximum VG" as they are likely to be too viscous.
For the size of the unit, battery life is good, but if you are trying to replace more than 10/15 cigarettes/day you will need to charge it at sometime, as 1,600 mAh is unlikely to get you through the day. Mine charges at 1.0 Amps, so it's not as slow as some starter kits. I have been popping mine on charge for short periods during the day when I've not been vaping on it and then battery life isn't an issue, even for me, and I vape quite heavily.
Before doing anything, please read the instructions that come in the kit.
The kit is certainly worthy of 5-Stars but there are a couple of small issues! Firstly, the kit does not arrive fully assembled although it is extremely easy to do this by reading the Instructions that come in the box. Simply 'prime' the coil, screw it into the Tank base mounted on top of the 1,600 mAh battery, push the glass Tank firmly onto the top of the battery, fill the Tank with e-liquid (NOT down the centre of the Coil) and then screw on the top/mouth-piece. Secondly, the Amazon web-page currently says you get an additional top/mouth-piece, but this is not the case at the moment.

This e-liquid comes in packaging which clearly is NOT appealing to the very young. The entire box/bottle design is extremely well presented and very professional.
The e-liquid has a crystal clear pale tan colour and is basically a 70/30 VG/PG mix. This makes the liquid fairly viscous and able to generate very good amounts of vapour whilst rendering good flavour characteristics. The ingredients are clearly specified on the box, which is very encouraging and something many manufacturers choose not to do.
The flavour profile states that this is a Mint/Menthol e-liquid and I personally loved it. It is quite a strong flavour! However, flavour is massively subjective, so if you?re not sure, perhaps buy the smaller 30 ml bottle before buying this extremely economical 60 ml version. I never specifically recommend e-liquids based on flavour alone. The vapour/flavour balance generated within the 70/30 mix is very good but please remember that your vaping ?style? and the Tank you?re using will have a significant impact on your perception/enjoyment of ANY e-liquid. Personally, I haven?t used this in an RDA but should I do so, I will update this review at a later date if the results vary significantly from those reported here. Initially, I vaped it in a SMOK ?Brit? Tank at 45 Watts on the V8-X4 coil. These coils also fit the SMOK TFV8 Baby and TFV8 Big Baby Tanks.
If you?re an experienced vaper and have mixed your own e-liquids in the past, you may wish to do as I did and add some VG based Nicotine. I did this after doing my initial assessment of this product and personally, I thought it improved the vaping experience. I mixed sufficient 7.2% Nicotine to give me roughly 6 mg (0.6%) content. However, this is NOT something I recommend unless you know exactly what you?re doing.
Summary:
Personally, I really love the flavour and vapour production I achieved from this e-liquid, even before adding any Nicotine. I?ve since vaped it in a Uwell Crown III tank with a standard 0.5 Ohm coil running at 60 Watts, slightly below the recommended Wattage range (70-80 Watts).
FURTHER NOTE:
I also purchased the Chonburi 60 ml e-liquid from this Company. It's a totally delicious coconut and definitely something I will be buying again.

You then receive the call and you can hear the person giving their name. For example I had one last week- 'Its Jean from Sainsbury' (we had a problem with our online delivery so had called to complain, bananas were soft again).
If you wish to speak to Jean from Sainsbury you just then press a button and Jean is put straight through. Same for anyone not on your trusted list.
If however that call had been 'Bob about a compensation claim, we heard you had been in an accident and the insurer has already put money to one side for you' you can press 'Block' and Bob will never darken your copper telephone wire again (at least until he changes his name and number- we know he is really called something else and is calling from another country anyway).
Effectively what happens is dodgy Bob and his brethren don't even bother leaving a message as they know you won't believe it, and so you never get any call at all.
Perfection, I hate speaking to anyone on the 'phone when they are legitimate, never mind wide boys from all four corners of the earth.

REVIEW_TITLE: Not bad, one perspective on what caused Dewsburys downfall.
REVIEW:
Having grown up near Dewsbury (but not living there), I have memories when I was a kid of going to Dewsbury Swimming baths, the market and the shops as a kid, and it being a nice place. The town had all the usual shops, such as Marks and Spencer, and was relatively smart.
I knew it had become a run down and the home of Karen Mathews, but took my car to a tyre fitter there a year ago as they had a tyre in stock. Whilst my tyre was being done,I strolled through Dewsbury for the first time in maybe 20 years, and was shocked at what I saw, many of the shops and even McDonalds closed down. I saw a group of drunks fighting in the town square (middle of the day). I was approached by someone who appeared to have serious psychiatric issues. The people looked poor and dejected. Pound stores, ?never never? on the tick type shops and various Asian speciality shops seemed the order of the day. Even the market was a shadow of its former self and I heard just the other week that a famous Pork butchers had shut up shop after around 100 years or more. It was basically horrible, one of the worst towns I had ever walked though. How sad I felt.
I saw this book and wondered if it would cast some light on how a once nice town had become this. The rather quick death of the place had sort of passed me by, I would like some answers.
The book explains the cultural split in a Dewsbury with people living in alternate universe in places like Saville Town, and the lack of integration between communities. The author seems to think this is a big part of the town?s downfall. He also explains the political climate, and how certain entities ceased control and imposed an agenda, to the detriment of many Dewsbury residents.
Im not convinced the book is that well written and sometimes seems rambling and flitting between different subjects. However, it?s a decent read and offers on perspective on the problems Dewsbury most certainly has.

REVIEW_TITLE: Very interesting insight into Trump, even if it appears to come from the usual anti Trump perspective.

I read this back to back with 'Art of the Deal', and I feel both books tempered each other to some extent.
This book appears to be written with the usual anti Trump agenda, but it is still a good book. It fills in some more details on the Art of the Deal days (up to building the Atlantic City Casinos), but also misses out some of the very good things Trump has achieved.
Whether you love him or loath him, one thing does come out from this book and that is:
1) He is extremely clever, not a fool. The way he puts deals together, including acquiring different rights to build, and getting zoning etc, not to mention the financing deals he ties together, would be way outside the abilities of the average man in the street- those same average Joes who seem to delight in saying Trump is dumb.Yes he had a good start with his father backing him, but many others do and hardly any go on to make billions.
2) He is very hardworking.
3) He never gives up and continues to battle even harder in the face of adversity.
4) He seems to think a lot of his children.
5) He is not adverse to being a wheeler dealer.
6) When things don't go his way he never admits fault and is very good at putting shine on failure.
I think reading this and Art of the Deal it gives you a good idea of how Trump probably sees his presidency. Each problem is a 'deal' he has to win at all costs and he will keep on in an unrelenting manner until he gets what he wants or the deal is beyond redemption. This results in situations like North Korea- he will not stop until he gets what he wants. Is this a good thing? Maybe, maybe not.. One thing is for sure, Trump will do something. Only time will tell of the Trump way worked or is a disaster.

REVIEW_TITLE: The way to go for proper barbecue, and not grilling.
REVIEW:
Basically if you want to smoke, this is the best bang for the buck. There is a smoker called a Pro Q which is a bit cheaper but not as good. All the cheap ones are an utter waste or money as they struggle to maintain the low temperature required.
First some history. Weber is a high quality manufacturer of barbecues and grills. They started off by making buoys for water, and someone adapted one to a barbecue. These things are covered in ceramic and should generally last 20 years.
Next history of smoking. This is a barbecue. What you consider to be a barbecue is actually a grill and not true BBQ, it is what has become known as a BBQ in Europe. True barbecue was introduced to the USA by African slaves, where they cooked cheap cuts of meat in a pit. To break down the connective tissue and fat they had to cook it real slow- hence the low and slow phrase. This Weber Smokey Mountain (WSM) replicates the 'pit'.
So if you want to do real low and slow cooking and cook the big three - ribs, pork shoulder (pulled pork) and brisket, you need a smoker, a real barbecue, not a grill.
So how does this work? Weill it has 3 sections. The bottom is the fire grate. This has three metal vents on it. These can be opened and closed to control the heat. The coals sit on here (better to use coals as they burn longer for the long low and slow cooks) and you put a few wood chunks (apple, cherry etc) on top of the lit coals to impart the smoke flavour.
The middle section contains 2 grill plates, and a large ceramic covered water bowl that sits under the grates, suspended just above the coals. You fill the water bowl with warm water and it acts as a heat sink, regulating the temperature and keeping it low (it is not to keep the food moist). It also puts a heat shield barrier between the coals and the food on the grates. There are then two grates or grills, which are big enough to get a couple of chickens on or at least 4 racks of ribs when put in a rib rack vertically stood on the grill.
The top is the lid, with another vent on it. This should mainly be left open to allow venting and draw air in through the bottom vents.
The middle section contains a aluminium door. You can open this door to access the coal basket during the cook- either to top up with more coals as they can burn out on very long cooks (a brisket may take 12 hours) or to put wood chunks in, or even to refill the water bowl on a long cook as all the water may evaporate.
There are many good demonstrations on Youtube but essentially you get the coals going, fill the water bowl and use the bottom vents to regulate the temperature around 225- 250 degrees Fahrenheit (circa 110 celsius) and let your food smoke from anything from 2 to 12 hours depending on what you are cooking.
The Weber is so good it is regularly used by competition teams. It is superior to the cheaper ones as it keeps the low temps very well- the cheaper ones leak around the seals, allow in air and the temps shoot up- to the dread of the pitmaster. It is of very good construction and will not rust or fall apart, as stated it should last you 20 years. The only thing better than these for smoking is a ceramic komodo but good ones like Big Green Egg are at least �1k.
So if you want to do proper low and slow and turn out restaurant quality (and I mean a proper barbecue place that actually smokes, not a poor chain restaurant) barbecue which would hold its own in Texas or the Carolinas, this is the way to go. If you just want to grill (remember that is grilling, not barbecuing) then do yourself a favour and just buy a Weber Kettle, that is the best item for a straight grill. I have both but since getting my WSM, my kettle has not got a look in.
PRODUCT: Weber Smokey Mountain Cooker Grill

REVIEW:
The Coredy AC1200 (CX-E120) mini Wi-Fi dual band range extender comes nicely boxed with a user manual, a one meter RJ-45 networking cable and a reset pin in case you ever need to reset the extender.
The Coredy AC1200 range extender looks and feels well made and is quite small. It has four external antennas on top of it and two LAN ports on the bottom of it.
Even though the range extender has four external antennas it can easily be plugged into a double wall socket and have room for another plug to be inserted into the socket next to it.
Not only is this Coredy AC1200 a Wi-Fi range extender it can be used as a router or access point.
I personally have not used this product as a router I have only used the Wi-Fi extender and access point features on it so cannot comment properly on its router feature.
The Coredy AC1200 is simple to set up using a web browser or the WPS button on the front of the Coredy ( If setting the Coredy AC1200 up by WPS the device you are connecting the Coredy up to will also need to be WPS compatible).
Once the Coredy is paired to your router you decide how you are going to use it by selecting which function you want to use on the Coredy AC1200 with a small switch on the side of it.
When using this Coredy AC1200 as a straightforward Wi-Fi extender I did loose connection with my main router every now and again but I believe this might be to do with my router because it is fairly old and when I have used other Wi-Fi range extenders I have had the same problem.
Using the Coredy AC1200 as an access point and having it connected to my main router by a Ethernet powerline adapter and using either the Coredy?s 2.4G or 5G SSID Wi-Fi network gave me a lot more stable connection for all my Wi-Fi devices downstairs.
 If you look at the video or photos I have uploaded with this review you will see how much stronger the Coredy CX-E120_2.4G_EXT Wi-Fi signal is compared to the Blackstarnetwork Wi-Fi signal I usually use.
So helps greatly with my Sky HD box when downloading on demand programs.
Conclusion
A nice little Wi-Fi range extender that can be used as an access point or router.
If you need any of the above features I would give this Coredy AC1200 a try, if you don?t like it you can always get a refund.

REVIEW_TITLE: Good sound quality & wireless range a lot better than Bluetooth
REVIEW:
SHORT REVIEW
Good sounding wireless headphones that work well with all types of audio equipment and televisions I have tried them with.
Good wireless range on them a lot better than Bluetooth.
LONG REVIEW
The Artiste digital wireless headphones come nicely packaged.
Items included in the packaging are.
One set of rechargeable wireless headphones
One base unit stand to recharge the headphones
One power supply with a 183cm (6ft) power cord
One 190 cm audio cable with a 3.5mm stereo jack on one end and two RCA plugs on the other end.
One 3.5mm to 6.3mm stereo jack adapter.
One 3.5mm stereo jack socket to two RCA plugs cable.
Two AAA rechargeable batteries
One instruction manual.
These Artiste wireless headphones use 2.4GHz UHF/RF technology they are not Bluetooth so to use them the base unit needs to be plugged into any audio device or television that has a headphone socket or RCA audio output that the headphones are going to be used with.
With most audio equipment and televisions having a headphone socket or RCA audio outputs, there should be no problems using these wireless headphones with any equipment with these features.
The build quality of the headphones and base unit looks good but for �65 that these wireless headphones are selling for at time of writing this review I believe they could be slightly better but that's just my own personal opinion, don't get me wrong their not going to fall to bits when you pick them up, just some of the materials that is used in their construction could be a little better for the price.
The base unit and stand for the headphones is also the transmitter and charger for the headphones so the base unit will need to be plugged into a wall socket.
The headphones when not being used fit nicely into the base unit and look neat and tidy.
When the headphones are resting in the base unit they will start to recharge automatically.
I'm using these Artiste wireless headphones with a television in the bedroom with out any problems.
When using them with the base unit, stand plugged into the RCA audio sockets on the back of the television I can control the main volume of the television and the Artiste headphones independently.
If plugging the base unit into the headphone socket on the television the sound on the TV speaker becomes muted and the sound then comes through just the headphones.
Bare in mind some Televisions might allow the main sound on the TV speaker to remain on when you use the headphone socket but most audio equipment and televisions switch there main speakers off when using the headphone socket on them.
When wearing the headphones I found them comfortable to wear with a good quality sound to them.
For this review I also tried the headphones with a few other types of equipment, a Samsung Galaxy S7, a Hi-Fi amplifier and another Television without any real problems.
I couldn't get the headphones to work through the RCA audio sockets on the second television but I believe this is a fault with the television and not the Artiste headphones.
When listening to music from my Galaxy S7 the headphones produced a good clear sound, with a good bass to them, at high volume the headphones did not distort and the stereo on them worked well.
When walking around the house the headphones did not loose connection with the base unit with the music playing flawlessly a lot better than when using headphones with Bluetooth.
When using the headphones connected to any of the televisions I tried them on again they produced a good clear sound whether listening to a music channel, a normal TV programme or a news channel.
When listening to a news channel it sounded like you were in the studio and sound a lot better and clearer through the Artiste headphones than through the televisions main speakers.
Conclusion
An excellent set of wireless headphones, good sound quality and a good wireless range on them a lot better than Bluetooth.
Would I recommend them? YES

These attachments are a magnet, a small mirror and a metal hook.
The endoscope is around 5 meters in length, it has a camera at one end with six small LED lights and a micro USB plug at the other end.
The main cable of endoscope is semi rigid so can be easily bent to stay the shape you want.
TESTING
I have not tried this endoscope on a computer yet so can not comment on how well it works on one.
I personally am using the Wi-Fi endoscope with a Samsung Galaxy S7 with the endoscope working satisfactory.
The endoscope can be used over Wi-Fi using a app called HTwifi or can be plugged straight into a compatible smartphone like the Galaxy S7 and used with a selection of different apps.

When using the endoscope camera it could produce a adequate picture seen as though it is only a 2.0 mega pixel camera and the six small led lights around the camera are good at illuminating the surrounding area around the camera.
I found the endoscope camera seemed to display a better quality picture when plugged straight into my phone instead of using the endoscope with its Wi-Fi transmitter.
The LEDs around the camera can easily be dimmed or brightened by a control wheel on the small control box on the cable of the endoscope.
As mentioned above the endoscope also comes with three attachments to connect to the camera to help recover hard to reach items with the endoscope cable.
You can choose from a magnet, mirror or hook.
The endoscope camera has a waterproof level of IP67 so should be usable under water though I have not tried it out under water yet.
If I do decide to use the endoscope where the camera will get wet or go under water I will and would recommend sealing any joints around the camera with water proof tape.
I have had another endoscope that said it was waterproof to level IP67 and although it was ok in the water when using it a few days later when I came to use the endoscope again the lens of the camera was fogged over.
So better safe than sorry.
CONCLUSION
Overall I have found the Beva Wi-Fi endoscope to work satisfactory on my Galaxy S7 phone.
I also found you don't need to use the supplied endoscope camera with the supplied Wi-Fi transmitter, I used a different endoscope with the Wi-Fi transmitter with out any problems.
I'm afraid after a couple of days the Beva endoscope developed a fault on the USB cable making it only work if I twisted the cable so have only awarded this endoscope 4 stars.
If I get the endoscope replaced and all is working ok I will increase the score of the endoscope to 5 stars.

REVIEW_TITLE: Great smart watch, made and received calls without any problems, let down by bad apps
REVIEW:
The Mindkoo GT88 Bluetooth smart watch comes nicely boxed and presented.
Included in the box with the GT 88 smart watch is a charging cable, a user manual which isn't the best translation to English, a screen protector, a set of 4 spare screws and a small Phillips screwdriver.
The Phillips screwdriver is needed to remove the back of the GT 88 smartwatch to insert a micro SD and SIM card.
The watch will function perfectly well without a micro SD and SIM card but with out a SIM card you will only be able to make and receive phone calls and text when the GT smartwatch is linked to your phone.
When removing the Mindkoo GT88 smartwatch from its packaging you are greeted with a smart looking smartwatch that looks and feels well made from the main case of the GT 88 to its rubber wrist strap.
Some of the features of the GT 88 smartwatch are
Selection of different watch faces
Bluetooth
Phone when paired to a smartphone or stand alone if SIM card is inserted into the GT 88
Camera
Video camera
MP3 player when paired to a smartphone or stand alone mp3 player if micro SD card is inserted into it.
Heart rate monitor
Fitness tracker
Alarm clock
Stopwatch
Voice recorder
Simple calculator
Calendar
TESTING
Before I started using the Mindkoo GT 88 smartwatch I removed the back of the watch and inserted a 8GB micro SD card and a pay as you go SIM card which I found simple enough to do.
I also made sure the smartwatch was fully charged, this is done with the supplied charging cable that uses small magnets to attach itself to the power points on the back of the smartwatch.
I found the charging cable easily detached itself from the watch so you had to be careful not to knock the smartwatch when it was charging.
When turning the watch on with the power button on the right hand side of the smartwatch you are greeted to a good clear display.
I hand no trouble with the display even in bright sunlight.
The screen of the smartwatch is touch sensitive and I had no trouble using it even with my fat fingers, with the smartwatch switching screens with a flick of a finger.
PHONE CALLS
I couldn't make direct phone calls because the prepay SIM card I used had no credit on it but when trying to make a call and it directed me to the phone operator the GT 88 smartwatch did so with out any problems and I could hear the pre-recorded message perfectly.
I could receive calls and when I did everything again was perfect I could hear the caller fine and they had no trouble hearing me.
MP3 PLAYER
When playing music on the smartwatch, whether it was from the micro SD card or when paired by Bluetooth to my smartphone a Galaxy S7 the GT 88 smartwatch would always play the music through its own little speaker on the watch.
The speaker on the watch is good enough for having conversations on the phone but not really for music.
If you inserted a pair of earphones or wired speaker into the smartphone then music would be played through the speaker or headphones.
( I have reviewed another smartwatch and that did the exact same thing as this GT 88 smartwatch always playing music through its own small little speaker, though the GT 88 does sound a lot better than the other smartwatch.)
CAMERA
The Mindkoo GT 88 smartwatch can take videos or still images, videos and photos are of course not as good as a proper digital camera or smartphone but still good for that instant mess around snap.
FITNESS TRACKER HEART RATE MONITOR
The fitness tracker on the GT 88 gave around the same results as the fitness tracker I personally use all the time and with any fitness tracker you really need to use them with an app to monitor your progress, there are several apps for this GT 88 smartphone on the Google play store that have fitness software on them but a personal do not find them very good and let the GT 88 smartwatch down.
When using the heart rate monitor again it gave around the same results as my usual fitness tracker and built in heart rate monitor on the Galaxy S7.
APP'S
The one thing that let this smartwatch down was I could not find any good apps to download to my smartphone to support the smartwatch.
The user manual does tell you of an app to download and I am using it but it I don't personally find it very good with it not syncing the GT 88 to my smartphone all the time.
I did try a few other apps and they all seemed to be the same.
You also need these apps on your smartphone to send other apps that are compatible to the GT 88 smartwatch because there is no other way of getting apps onto the smartwatch that I have found.
I also could not find any way of transferring music from my smartphone to the smartwatch even over Bluetooth, I could easily transfer music files from the smartwatch to my smartphone over Bluetooth but like I said I couldn't the other way around.
The only way I have found to so far to put music files onto the smartwatch is to transfer the files onto the micro SD card before you fit it into the watch.
CONCLUSION
I really liked this Mindkoo GT 88 smartwatch it felt well built, it made and received phoned calls without any problems and the apps already on the smartwatch worked well.
The one thing that let's this smartwatch down is the software on the apps for it. If some clever programmer could start making better apps for this smartwatch like being able to transfer music files easier and a lot more different watch faces then watch out Android smartwatch's.
I'm not sure whether to give this Mindkoo GT 88 smartwatch 5 stars or 4 stars because of the bad apps and software holding it back, but the preinstalled apps and features all ready on the smartwatch are good so 5 stars.

This tiny action camera from Campark is really the dog's whats-its.
These camera have become incredibly popular in recent times, as they are tiny and easy to carry everywhere. They are usually described as 'action camera' as they have fast shutter speeds and good video quality to allow you to catch fast moving subjects in sports.
Most of these (cheaper) cameras I have seen have been ok, but stuck with 1080p resolution and cheap back screens with confusing buttons. This all singing, all dancing model is different.
You can take 4K video (only at 24 fps though), and the stills can go up to 20 MP. And best of all, the back screen is finally a touch screen, which makes navigating the menus so much easier.
The camera does not come with any storage on board, or an SD card, but micro SD cards are really cheap these days, so it shouldn't matter too much.
As I said, you can take still pictures up 20 20MP, which makes them great for landscape shots as you can zoom in with minimal loss of detail. The video quality is ok, but 4K at 24 fps is not as good as 1080p at 50 fps (in my opinion). I have tried to include a sample of both for comparison, but Amazon will only allow one video per review. The video of the dogs is 1080 at 50 fps. The photos are both 20 MP.
You get a nice semi hard case, plus a massive amount of accessories, mounts, sticky pads, and a fully waterproof case for shooting underwater. However, when the camera is in this case, you obviously cannot access the touch screen, but the button on the front allows you to cycle through all the modes, so minimal problems there. You also get a little remote control unit.
The battery with the camera is only 150 mAh, so it might be an idea to take 2 or 3 along for a day's fun. Other cameras I have tried of this type have come with a spare battery in the case, so a bit disappointing not to receive a spare here. Charging the battery took about 2 hours.
To get the photos off the camera, you can take the SD card out and stick it in your computer, or WiFi transfer is included. To use the WiFi with your phone is a bit complicated (well it was for me anyway). You have to create a new wifi connection to the camera, then download the 'CamKing' app (for Android, not sure about iOS), and view your pics on your phone. You can then download them to your phone, and finally I uploaded them to Google Photos to access them on the computer. Long winded, but once set up it works ok.
A really nice camera, good quality capable of some very good shots/videos, and small enough to take around in your pocket.

The unit is designed very well, with a long cable to plug into your 12V socket (any higher will burn the motor out, so check your car's voltage if not sure) and a sturdy air hose with a locking-type adapter on the end that means you don't lose too much air from the tyre when removing it - a feature in almost every other compressor I have used. The unit has a very clever recess path built into the back that stores everything away neatly.
Using the unit is very easy; press any of the three buttons on the front, attach the air hose to the tyre inflator and the pressure (defaults to PSI but can be changed to other units by pressing the 'R' button) is immediately displayed; press the + or - button to set the desired pressure, switch the pump on and the tyre will inflate to the set pressure and then automatically switch off. Simplicity itself.
Instructions and a set of adapters (for bikes and air mattresses etc) are included. The unit also has a built-in LED light for working in the dark.
The compressor is loud but not unbearably so. If I have one criticism, it's that the air hose could maybe be a bit longer, but then it probably wouldn't fit quite so well into the unit.
An excellent little device, should be in every car.
Thanks for listening.
PRODUCT: Digital Tyre Inflator,AUPERTO 12V Car Tyre Compressor Pump with Adapter to 150 PSI

REVIEW:
The size of power banks seems to have reduced dramatically in the last year or so. I have 10,000 mAh banks that are at least twice the size as this one from a couple of years ago.
This is good news for us of course, they are far easier to carry around. They are necessary due to the poor battery life of most devices, a full day if you are lucky in most cases, if you are going out for a weekend, then a power bank with a decent capacity is a must.
This bank from VIVIS is 15,000 mAh, capable of charging most phones about 4-5 times before it runs out of juice. Charging it is easy, takes around 6 hours with a 2A charger. The bank is capable of charging at up to 3A, so if you have a phone with fast charge (as long as it's not QC), then your charging time should be reduced. My Galaxy S8+ is QC enabled, so it didn't register a fast charge with this, but it did reduced the charging time by about 30%.
This also has a built in charging cable, micro-usb, which is quite handy (if your device charges via Micro-USB). You also get a lightning adapter for iPhones, this would be great except that there is nowhere on the device to store it. A little recess would have been a good idea. But still nice to have a built in cable.
There are the usual four LEDs on the side next to the power button. These each signify roughly 25% charge (4 lights lit = fully charged).
Some people mark these things down as they don't come with absolutely every cable for every possible device out there! Use your original cable, it's not rocket science!
A nice power bank which could be improved with a recess to store an adapter for the cable.
Thanks for listening.
PRODUCT: Power Bank 15000mAh, VIVIS Portable Charger Built-in Micro usb cable and Lightning Connector, Phone Stand Holder Li-Polymer External Battery Charger for iPhone, Samsung, Tablets etc

REVIEW:

And that was with a flat screen. All the other cases I have seen for the S8+ have had the screen protector removed, as it must be much more difficult to fit a curved screen precisely. However, I-Blason seem to have done it. There is absolutely no gap between the case and the phone screen, it's as if the protector isn't there, it follows the contours of the curved screen perfectly.
The case comes well protected with a polystyrene block inside, and the back and front screens are protected with plastic films. It goes without saying that you need to clean your phone thoroughly before inserting it into the case, as a tiny speck of dust can ruin the look of it. Simply press your phone firmly into the front, and than push on the back. You then need to go around all the seams making sure they are pushed into place. What you are left with is slightly bulky, yes, but your phone is COMPLETELY protected. I am happy with the compromise.
Other reviews have said it is impossible to remove the case once fitted. I don't really understand why you would WANT to remove it, but I found little difficulty getting the case off. The bottom right hand corner has a little gap that allows some leverage to remove it.
The case is surrounded with rubber for drop protection. I am happy that my phone would survive a fair drop with the case on. I am very happy with it and recommend it.
Thanks for listening.

REVIEW:
I have tried quite a few different fitness trackers, but I have always been left disappointed...until now.
I wanted one that doubled as a watch, but all the ones I have tried have the time displayed vertically. It may seem like a small insignificant thing, but it was important to me, and this one from YAMAY fits the bill perfectly as it displays the time 'properly', i.e. horizontally.
The unit comes already installed into the band, but it easily pops out and plugs directly into a USB port to charge. Charging time is about 2 hours, and I got 2 days of moderate use before recharging.
The device is paired with an app that can be found by scanning the QR code on the box, and you can download for Android or iOS. The app is very good and allows you to configure the watch and track all your fitness activities, and even includes some exercises to follow.
The screen of the unit is not touch sensitive, rather there is a touch sensitive button at the bottom of the display that is used to cycle through the options. There are 'standard' options such as a step counter, calories burned etc, but you can also track your sleep, and the unit also includes a heart rate sensor in the back. I am not sure this is all that useful, as when the watch is worn on the wrist, it doesn't pick up the pulse. You have to position your finger on the sensor for it to pick up (at least this is how mine worked), therefore you have to take the watch off. A minor point though.
You can also use the unit as an extension of your phone, with options for phone ring alert, message alert, an alarm to sound when you leave either the phone or the watch apart from each other, and also one I've not seen before, WhatsApp alert. I use WhatsApp most of the time rather than messaging, so this is perfect for me.
The unit is very lightweight and comfortable to wear. My only criticism is that the date is displayed in the American format, i.e. month first then day. Again, this may seem a minor point, and it isn't enough for me to knock a star off, but I still would have liked an option to change it to the British format.
So I am very happy with the unit and recommend it, certainly a lot cheaper than a FitBit.
Thanks for listening.

REVIEW:
The Rainbow 2 is a budget smartphone from Chinese maker Cubot. I already have the Cubot Manito and this is an upgraded model.
In the box you have the phone, USB charging cable, Quick Start guide, a UK power adapter (if buying in the UK) and you also get a clear plastic case included. The screen also comes with a screen protector already attached, these can be a nightmare to install so it was nice that this was already done.
The screen is 5 inches, so it is comfortable to hold in one hand. The back is made of smooth plastic, and in the case of the black version, looks very smart and shiny (although inevitably it is a fingerprint magnet). On the front screen at the bottom are the 3 'standard' Android buttons; Menu, Home and Back. On the right side of the device are the power and volume up/down buttons. On the top of the device you have a 3.5mm headphone port and the micro-usb charging port (a lot of the 'budget' phones favour the charging port at the top, not sure why). The left side of the device is blank, and on the bottom you have what at first appear to be 2 speakers (?stereo sound), but only one is a speaker, the other is a microphone. On removing the back cover (which is quite stiff and difficult), you are presented with a non-removable battery, 2 SIM card slots and a Micro SD card slot. The phone is 3G only, 4G is not supported in either slot.
The phone sports a 1.3 GHz processor, a motion coprocessor, 1GB of RAM and 16GB storage, which isn't a great deal but you can add up to 128GB of SD card memory. The 1GB of RAM was a bit of a worry but the phone seems to run smoothly (most of the time). Wireless and Bluetooth are also supported, but no NFC and no fingerprint reader.
The phone runs Android 7 (not 7.1), a fairly basic version with no bloatware installed. A software update was available right away, a 1GB download so if you don't have super fast broadband, it could take a while.
Upon switching on, you are presented with a nice bright, clear screen, 720p resolution so nice sharp easy to read text and vibrant colours. The phone has a software trick called Miravision, which adds dynamic contrast and 'vivid' colours, so the screen can look pretty decent when all the tricks are set. Upon checking the settings, all the usual suspects are there, along with a few tricks called 'gesture settings'. These allow you to use the front camera to do things like wave your hand over to move between pages or photos, wake up your screen or reject a call etc. You can also 'write' on the screen with your finger to wake it up into a particular app, eg draw a 'c' with your finger to automatically start the camera, that sort of thing. I guess it's useful if you like that sort of thing.
The camera is the main distinguishing feature of the Rainbow 2. It is a 13MP back camera, with a 5MP front camera, however the back camera has 2 lenses. Cubot says that this allow for better pictures, and it is true that pictures taken with the Rainbow 2 are superior to those taken with the Manito. As other people have said (and as is pointed out on Cubot's web site), you can also take photos with 'depth of field' This essentially means that when you take a picture, you can have the foreground blurred and the background in focus (or the other way round) and you can select between them. My Galaxy S8+ can also do this and it does actually work well. When you tap on a certain area of the photo you have taken, it is brought into sharp focus and the rest of the shot blurs accordingly. However, I may be missing something, as I can not get it to work at all, and there is no mention of it in the Quick Start guide, or in the 'Gallery' app. Maybe it's just me, but I was disappointed with this feature.
Using the phone in Android 7 seems fairly zippy, with minimal lag. The touchscreen, however, leaves something to be desired. There seems to be at least a half a second delay between tapping an icon and the corresponding action being taken, at least in my device. The screen feels 'spongy', and with the delay you are often wondering if you tapped properly in the first place.
Performance in games seems quite good, despite the 1GB of RAM. I usually test the phone by installing a game called 'HayDay', which features an isometric viewpoint of a farm you build and maintain, and the game is quite graphically intensive. When scrolling around the viewpoint, there is no noticeable lag, so it seems performance is not an issue.
If these issues were present in a phone costing �500-�600, I would be quite disappointed, however you have to remind yourself that the phone is less than �100, quite cheap these days, so these 'faults' can be forgiven. The quality of the pictures taken with the camera are actually quite good, and definitely better than the Cubot Manito. The last 2 pictures were taken with the phone, indoors in good daylight.
So, if you are on a budget, you could do a lot worse than this phone, in my opinion.
Thanks for listening.
PRODUCT: Cubot RAINBOW 2 Android 7.0 OS 3G Dual UK SIM-Free Smartphone - Black

REVIEW:
I have used many screen protectors over the years, and recently I decided that I would no longer use the plastic kind, preferring instead the tempered glass variety. These go on with absolutely no hassle and no bubbles.
All was going well with this until I got my Galaxy S8+. As the screen is curved, tempered glass protectors suddenly aren't as easy as they used to be. There are quite a few about, but the ones I have tried have a lot of trouble sticking (or staying stuck) to the edges.
So I looked at plastic ones again, and recently I have discovered that there are ones that go on 'wet'. I was intrigued, so I chose this set from Surwell. In the box you get 4 protectors, and 4 sets of installation tools, making great value.
The procedure is straightforward;
1. Clean your screen thoroughly with the alcohol swab, dry it with the cloth and pick any dust off with the stickers
2. Peel back the first layer of the protector and spray the water solution all over the back (sticky side) of the protector.
3. Line the protector up with the speaker, home button etc until it is perfect.
4. Now the clever bit: Using the squeegee card wrapped in a cloth, you hold on to one side of the screen and gently 'squeeze' the water out by rubbing the card smoothly from centre to edge until all the bubbles have gone. Repeat this for the other half of the screen.
5. Now you have to let it dry for a couple of hours, as if you try to remove the second film too soon, the whole thing will come away. Be patient!
When I did remove the second film, there were a LOT of bubbles still visible. The instructions say give it 48 hours and the bubbles will disappear. I was sceptical, but followed suit.
The application I did on Friday; it is now Monday and ALL but one tiny bubble have gone, like magic!
I am well pleased with the result; Normally plastic protectors are cheap rubbish but clearly a lot of thought has gone into this package. All the tools required are there, and if you do mess it up, there are 4 in the box. What more do you want?
There are numerous videos on YouTube detailing the above procedure, and if you follow it with care it is very easy to do.
Thanks for listening.
*24 hours later, and even that small bubble is gone; the screen is now completely clear!
PRODUCT: Galaxy S8 Plus Screen Protector - Surwell Samsung Galaxy S8 Plus Wet Screen Protector Not Glass Anti-Bubble Case Friendly (4 Pack,Clarity)

REVIEW:
I really like power banks, and I have quite a collection now. No excuse for running out of power!
They all vary in size, shape, capacity and features, and I am always on the lookout for unusual features.
This bank from EC Technology is 10,000 mAh, a good mid-sized capacity, and it will charge most phones 2-3 times before running out of juice itself.
This has 2 different features; first, it can be charged via the sun, thanks to one side of it being covered in solar cells, and second it provides a flashlight. Not the usual single LED flashlight you usually get, but 32 (yes, thirty-two) LEDs covering the other side. As you can imagine, 32 LEDs provides quite a bright light.
All the other usual features are present, 2 USB outputs which are 'smart' (ie they identify your device and pump out the highest charge possible, up to 2.1A), 4 blue LEDs to signify charge level (and a green LED to signify that solar charging is taking place) and a micro-usb input for charging the power bank itself. You are advised to charge it via the mains, and only use the solar for 'topping up', and as I live in the UK with our summers consisting of 1 and a half days of sunshine, this is sound advice. You are unlikely to be able to charge the device fully from the sun alone, unless you live in the Med or something. To charge the device from empty via the mains took about 4-5 hours, depending on the output of your charger.
You also get a rubber case to keep the bank in, which is open one side and has 2 flaps on the other. I thought this was a bit odd, as you would really want the solar cells AND the LED torch exposed at the same time, instead of choosing between them. Maybe that's just me though.
A really nice power bank, and one that I am happy to recommend.
Thanks for listening.

REVIEW:
I was initially a little confused when I received the product, as it had 'milk mixer' written on the box, it seemed to be some kind of mixer for making bottles of baby milk.
However, this is not the case. It is in fact, a really good water dispenser. The reason it is described as 'for babies' is down to the features.
The first thing you do is flip open the lid and fill the container with water up to the 'max' line. It holds about 2 litres.
Then press 'boil'. The water will be heated to 100 degrees Celcius, confirmed by the large easy to read display. It takes 5-10 minutes to reach 100, this might seem slow but remember you will only need to do this once or twice a day.
Once the water has been warmed, it automatically enters 'Insulation' mode. This means that the water is maintained at your chosen preset temperature, constantly. So if you set it to 80 degrees, once boiled the water will cool to 80 degrees, and then be heated automatically to maintain that temperature (give or take 10%). So whenever you want a hot drink, all you have to do is dispense the water, rather than wait for it boil. Clever eh?
But suppose you want cold water? Not a problem, simply press 'fast cool' and the water will cool rapidly. And you can also choose any temperature to heat the water, hence the reason it is described as a 'baby milk mixer', as you need to be quite precise when making up bottles.
There is also a 'Chlorine remover' mode, which constantly boils and cools the water for around 5 minutes, as this process apparently reduces the amount of chlorine in the water. I can't say I've noticed a difference, but it's a nice feature.
The unit is aesthetically quite attractive, in kitchen white, and the large digital display makes it very easy to use.
In the package are a sheet of instructions (very good ones, too) and a little clip-on cup rest.
I really like the unit; if like me, you drink a lot of coffee, it is nice to have instant hot water available instead of waiting for it to boil.
The lid detaches for easy cleaning, and the surface of the heater does not get too hot to touch.
All in all, a great idea and I am happy to recommend it.
Thanks for listening.
PRODUCT: Haier HBM-F25 2.0 Liter Water Boiler and Warmer with LED Digital Display Screen - White

REVIEW:
Dash Cams are fast becoming essential in-car tech. Like Sat Navs before them, they aim to make our driving experience easier, in this case by recording people being naughty, and providing evidence in accident situations.
First the good;
It's made by Anker. Despite having the name 'Roav' on it, you have Anker's fantastic build quality, expertise and second-to-none customer service.
The unit has a very small footprint, approximately 6x4 inches, and quite slim. In the instructions, you are advised to position it behind your rear view mirror, and I found this to be the ideal spot. The shadows in the video are down to me not checking the position carefully enough, I just need to move it down and to the right slightly, then you get a lovely wide-angle high quality view.
The buttons are easy to learn, but it is not a touch screen device and I think it would be a lot easier to use if it was. The power button on the left side is ridiculously sensitive, and I had managed to record six videos just by handling it before I knew what I was doing.
It does take a thorough read of the instructions and several field tests to become familiar with it's use. You have a lot of options in the menus, from video quality to auto power off. I opted for 720p resolution at 60fps, as I prefer smoother video to high quality, and as you can tell from the video, the quality is still excellent.
Installation in your car can be a bit of a nightmare. The cable you get is nice and long, and plugs into the provided cigarette lighter adapter. You get a 'trim lifting' tool, but be careful with it as you could easily damage your car's aesthetics if you are not careful. I managed to run the cable from the cigarette lighter adapter, across to the console, up onto the dashboard, across to the right hand side of the screen, up the screen and along the top of the windscreen to the mirror, and I still had cable length to spare. How you position it in your own car is obviously down to your car's logistics and preference, but you should be able to find a good setup.
Once installed, the unit automatically starts recording when the engine starts, and records in three-minute sections until you stop (or run out of space on the sd card, in which case it starts to overwrite old files).When you stop the engine, it carries on recording for another 30 seconds then automatically powers down. You also have the option to start recording in the event of a 'jolt', ie if someone is trying to steal your car. This is an excellent addition.
So, a good, small, easy to use dash cam.
Now the bad;
As already mentioned, the power button is VERY sensitive. Be prepared to curse a few times as you record unwanted footage whilst setting up.
To review your recorded files, you either remove the device from the car and access the sd card on your computer, or you can download the 'Roav' app (Android and iOS). To use the app, you have to create a wi-fi connection between the unit and your phone, but in order for the app to 'pair', you have to switch the wi-fi option on in the menu. As I have mentioned, the menu system is a bit awkward, even more so when the unit is fixed in position behind your car's rear view mirror. Worst of all, the wi-fi keeps switching itself off, so you have to go through the pairing process every time. Not ideal.
Also be careful with SD cards. I managed to fry two of them whilst setting up as it does NOT support plug-n-play. Insert an sd card whilst the power is on (even though the unit asks you to) and you will destroy it. Oops.
Apart from these fairly minor points, this is a good small dashcam that produces very good video and could save you a lot of hassle in the event of an accident., and I am happy to recommend it.
Thanks for listening.
