I recently bought a SamSung Galaxy S7 edge, and whilst it is a fantastic phone, I have been wondering why it is so expensive. I started looking around at some of the cheaper Chinese phones that use Android, and I came across this one.
The phone is very well packaged, with a screen protector already applied with no bubbles whatsoever, and it comes in a nice clear plastic case that has 'bumpers' in each corner that protect it if it drops. In the box you also get the charging cable and a UK plug, along with a sheet of basic instructions.
On the top of the device is the charging socket (micro-usb), this seems to be a fairly common trend in the cheap phones, to have the charging socket at the top, I don't know why but it doesn't make any difference. You also get an earphones socket. On the right side of the phone is the power key and the volume up/down keys. The left side is blank, and on the bottom you have the microphone. On the back of the phone, is the camera lens and a single LED flash. The speaker is at the bottom. I charged the phone before I used it (it was at 55%,and it took about 2 hours to get to 100%). Wireless charging is not supported, but there are adapters available that work brilliantly.
Upon switching on the phone, I was pleasantly surprised at how bright and clear the phone is - it is 'only' 720p resolution but you wouldn't know it, text is very sharp and clear. It comes with 'Miravision', a software trick which improves the quality of the display and it works well.
The phone has a 1.3GHz Quad Core Processor and a separate GPU, and 3 Gb of RAM, and 16Gb of ROM. This should be enough for most people, and you can also add an SD card if you wish, up to 128Gb which again is unusual for these cheap phones, usually you are limited to 32Gb. It runs Android 6.0 and there is a software update right away. I am not sure if Android 7 is going to be supported. The phone also supports WiFi, Bluetooth, A-GPS and dual SIM cards (only the one in slot 1 can be 4G, the other slot only supports 3G). There are no physical buttons on the front, only the touch-sensitive menu, home and back keys.
The phone is certainly speedy at zipping through menus, I couldn't detect any lag. The Play store is already installed, and there were plenty of updates waiting. Installation times were very quick.
Most games and apps seem to work perfectly well. The only game I had that stuttered a bit was HayDay, whereby you create and maintain a farm, and I think it is quite graphically intensive, and when scrolling around the isometric viewpoint, there was some slowdown. It didn't make the game unplayable, and I didn't see any crashes, but it was a bit slow. But all my other (less graphically intensive) games worked well.
Call quality was very good, and the speaker is nice and loud and clear. There was no hiss and no problem for the other party in hearing me.
You get a 8Mpixel camera at the back (interpolated to 13Mpixel), and a 5 MPixel camera at the front (interpolated to 8MPixel). In good light, the pictures are not too bad, but in low light levels they do suffer. The last two images are photos taken with the phone. There are a couple of software tricks installed, such as beauty mode and smile shot etc.
I am actually really pleasantly surprised with the performance of this phone, considering the price (currently about 92 Pounds on Amazon UK). With the exception of HayDay, I had no issues running any of my software, the battery is not the biggest but I got a full day with it before recharging.
If you are looking for a budget phone, I would have no hesitations in recommending the Cubot Manito.

On the front of the device is a large sensor, which allows the camera to 'trigger' and start recording when it senses movement. That way, you don't waste hours filming when nothing is happening, although you can set the camera to record continuously if so desired.
The lens arrangement is on top of the device, and it swivels 180 degrees, so you should be able to get a decent angle to film from, wherever you decide to place the camera.
On the bottom of the device are the few controls. These are an on/off switch, audio on/off slider, play and record switch. The camera records to a micro-sd card, you can use any capacity but the faster the card, the better quality the video will be.

The recorded video is reasonable quality, and it does record quite well in the dark, it's just a bit fiddly to use. For me, the biggest drawback of the device is the lack of a screen to see what is happening. There is no 'live' feed of what you are doing, and you can't see the result of your work until you can get the SD card into your computer, so it lacks the 'instant' nature of digital cameras in this respect. Obviously a screen would make the camera larger, so it wouldn't be the same 'micro' device any more, but I think I would have liked the device more with a screen
To set the date and time, you have to connect the camera to your computer via the micro-USB slot and alter a text file; again not ideal when all you want to do is record some video.

After a year of incessant publishing of 'thisishygge' books trying to sell unsuspecting not Danish people the way to be happy, Danish style it is SUCH A RELIEF to finally, finally read a Hygge book that is truly portraying Danish Hygge. REVIEW:
Waited a long time for GT5 and.............its a bit bland and a a bit boring. The vehicle physics do not provide enough feedback, as in previous installments the race series do not provide enough AI making it all too easy.
The new cape ring track is dull, there are not enough cars (too many duplicates of JDM cars). License progression is pointless, B spec is unneccesary, the rally sims are aweful - the feedback from the loose surfaces is non existant with zero progression.
As a stand alone driving sim it is OK, as a race environment it isn't. Perhaps the GT4 time trials should have been kept to remove the AI issue, drop the B spec, add a few more RM car derivatives, develop a more realistic braking and wheel slip algorithm.
Viewing it through my eyes as a race driver and vehicle engineer it doesn't come anywhere near living up to the hype, as a gamer it is worth having, it is entertaining but it doesn't grab you and force you to keep driving
PRODUCT: Gran Turismo 5 (PS3)

REVIEW:
Waited a long time for GT5 and.............its a bit bland and a a bit boring. The vehicle physics do not provide enough feedback, as in previous installments the race series do not provide enough AI making it all too easy.
The new cape ring track is dull, there are not enough cars (too many duplicates of JDM cars). License progression is pointless, B spec is unneccesary, the rally sims are aweful - the feedback from the loose surfaces is non existant with zero progression.
As a stand alone driving sim it is OK, as a race environment it isn't. Perhaps the GT4 time trials should have been kept to remove the AI issue, drop the B spec, add a few more RM car derivatives, develop a more realistic braking and wheel slip algorithm.
Viewing it through my eyes as a race driver and vehicle engineer it doesn't come anywhere near living up to the hype, as a gamer it is worth having, it is entertaining but it doesn't grab you and force you to keep driving

REVIEW_TITLE: Very nice Pistachios - clean, sound and tasty. Unshelled, Unroasted and Unsalted. Just what I was looking for.
REVIEW:
At Last! A kilo bag of unroasted, unsalted, unshelled Pistachios at an affordable price.
At the moment, these seem to be as rare as hen's teeth. Most Pistachios I've looked at which are still in their shells seem to be salted.
Most of the unsalted ones seem to have had their shells removed.
That's no good for me - if they're naked, I'll mindlessly scoff my way through an entire packet while watching TV - having to take off the shell gives me something to do while I'm eating them (under the pretext of shelling some to use for cooking), but I don't want them covered in salt.
So I'm very grateful to have found these, and they're nice Pistachios, too. Clean, sound and tasty.
Unshelled, unroasted, unsalted.
Have a provenance, (Iran), have a batch no. and a BB date (late 2018), so all is as it should be.
These arrived in a resealable Kraft baggie, all of them in very good condition.
I just hope I manage to keep my mitts off them long enough to at least have some left for Christmas.

REVIEW_TITLE: Delightful vintage stoneware 'Puddings' jug. My favourite.
REVIEW:
I think this jug is absolutely charming - has a vintage ' Treacle Sponge' illustration on one side, and the other side has "Spotted Dick and Custard" depicted in the same retro, vintage style. The transfer is cleanly done and the attention to detail is spot on. Lovely bit of distressed imaging round the rim and base of the jug.
Base colour is a good, solid antique cream, glaze is smooth. Jug is 5" tall, 3.5" diameter across the base.
It holds a volume of 500ml - or just under 1 pint.
Lovely, solid little stoneware jug, well made, with a good handle and an easy pour lip.
It'd be fine for holding flowers, but for me, this is a much loved jug for custard, or for cream, to go on the table for people to help themselves.
Everybody adores it, and so do I.

REVIEW_TITLE: Good tasting, well cooked Chestnuts. Versatile and Squirrel proof.
REVIEW:
I usually pick this brand up in Sainsburys but when I spotted a bundle pack of six of these for six quid with Prime on here, I couldn't press 'one click' fast enough.
These are exactly the same as the 180g bags sold in the Supermarkets, really long shelf life while unopened, (this order in November '17 is good until August 2019) these are simply cooked, peeled and packed. Nothing else added.
Cooked soft, but still retaining their structure, these are sweet and nutty. Excellent for sprouts, stuffings, puddings and cakes.
Each pack contains the equivalent of a mugful of cooked chestnuts - if you were going to make this amount from fresh chestnuts, you'd need to start off with about 2lb chestnuts, because by the time you've boiled them, shelled them, taken off the 'paper' and removed the inevitable discoloured or dodgy bits, this 180g is about what you'd end up with. I know, because in the years that the squirrels actually leave me enough sweet chestnuts for my own use from my trees, this is about what I get.
It's easier to leave the squirrels to their thievery and buy these.
PRODUCT: Merchant Gourmet Whole Chestnuts 180 g (Pack of 6)

They're smallish - it's quite clear they're 50 litre sacks, not the big, 120 litre dustbin sized ones. I got these for lining a 40 litre Simple Human kitchen waste bin and they fit the oblong pedal bin perfectly. These are a fifth of the price of the branded liners designed for the bin.
These are gusseted, with tie handles, not drawstring tops. They're not seriously heavy duty in the same way that the 'garden waste' bin liners are heavy duty, but they're easily strong enough for lining a domestic kitchen bin - I don't need very heavy duty sacks for an indoor bin.
There's less plastic waste, the tie handles are fuss free, and 100 liners at current prices represents very good value for money.

These are a decent standard size, not jumbo but that's fine for me - they're premium cashews but at a reasonable price for a good product.
I like that they're not roasted or salted, haven't had anything done to them, so are perfect for snacking as well as cooking.

REVIEW:
Monster Christmas puds..... almost 1kg each, and there are two of them! Currently on for an excellent price for the pair, I was expecting them to be nearing their 'best before' date - but the BB date on these is April 2019.
I usually make my own Christmas puds as they're far nicer than shop bought, but home made take hours and hours to steam and now I've run out of time if the puds are going to be able to mature. So I looked online.
What attracted me to this particular make were the very positive reviews from other purchasers, and the ingredients in the puds - plenty of fruit, nuts and booze.
When they arrived, I did undo one and had a little peek, - they're beautifully presented in a plastic bowl with a shrink seal lid, well wrapped and only need to be heated up, either steamed for a couple of hours or two minutes in a microwave.
Having opened one, I took a teaspoon and dug out a little taster...
Delish. Very rich, fruity and dark, with a gorgeous Xmas pud fragrance, succulent and although not over boozy, I can taste there's been a bit of booze added. These are luxury puds. The description is accurate.
All I've done with these is to spike a few little punctures in them, added a tablespoonful of brandy to each one to soak in, replaced the seal top with clingfilm and now I'm going to leave them until Christmas.
Then when I serve them up, I'm just going to smile benignly when everyone says how fab my home made Xmas puds are, and where on earth do I find the time.
If I don't get found out and strung up for a liar, I'll be back to update. In the meantime, if these are still on for around sixteen quid for this pair of brazen beauties, grab them, quick.
You don't need to add any extra booze. I only did because I'm clearly a very bad Maggie.
PRODUCT: Matthew Walker Luxury Christmas Puddings, 907g, 2 puddings

REVIEW_TITLE: Good sized, clearly labelled. Laminated surface wipes clean. Misses a couple of teaching opportunities, but generally very good.
REVIEW:
Large, poster sized, well printed wall chart of the skeletal anatomy of the goat, well laminated and tough enough to withstand highlighter or marker pen and will wipe clean. Metal rivet holes in corners for hanging, mine also had strong, double sided adhesive pads to adhere directly to a smooth surface. All skeletal parts appear to be correctly labelled and can be clearly seen.
I would have liked a closer diagrammatic inspection of the frontal bones of the skull where the areas of horn growth occur, and the correlation with the frontal sinuses (not labelled). Many domestic goats are disbudded when very young and incomplete or incorrect removal of the bone 'bud' and cauterisation of the surrounding tissue can result in significant problems later on - in my opinion the omission of this significant skeletal and anatomical area misses a key teaching point.
I'd also like to have seen closer diagrams of the structure and anatomy of the feet and legs - they've documented this on the Bovine and Equine wall charts, but not on this one. A detailed knowledge of the structure of the foot bones and hooves of goats and sheep is essential when assessing conformation, mechanics of movement and possible disease processes. Omitting these misses some important teaching opportunities.
But as a teaching and learning tool for educating students and those interested in the framework of Caprines, this is a very good wall chart.
Good sized and clearly labelled - much more useful and informative than diagrams and illustrations more commonly found in many books, this wall chart has plenty to teach.
PRODUCT: Dbios Educational Digital Printed Skeletal Parts of Goat Anatomy Wall Charts

REVIEW_TITLE: Fishing Tin - nicely made with good attention to detail. Great gift. Shame about the biscuits.
REVIEW:
Great tin, well decorated and embossed on all sides (not just the lid). Proper suitcase style with hinged lid, central clasp closure and a hinged plastic carrying handle. Measures 10" long, 7" across and 3" deep.
Just right for a bait tin, a lunchbox, sweet/treat tin or to hold tied flies once the biscuits are eaten. Fairly robust, but not heavy duty, this is a decent novelty item.
Should have been a five star product, but for the fact that the biscuits weren't protected well enough inside the tin, They'd shaken loose from their sections and the debris from the broken ones had spoiled the look of the ones that had survived. Bit of a mess.
An extra piece of corrugated or padded card inside the packaging might have helped them survive transit better - other manufacturers of biscuit tins manage it.
The tin is still the reason I bought this product. I ate the biscuits (they were really good ones, big, crunchy and delicious, such a shame) and replaced them with a mixture of wrapped biscuit bars because I like this tin - it's got a bit of character and makes a lovely stocking filler.

REVIEW_TITLE: Uncomplicated, reliable and inexpensive analogue alarm clock.
REVIEW:
Inexpensive, pocket sized Alarm Clock measuring 5.5cm x 5.5cm x 3cm deep. Plastic shell. Large, clear numerals and minute/hour hands with luminous coating. Sweep second hand plus hour alarm indicator. Really simple to set up. Insert the AA battery (supplied), set the time from the winder on the back which has two positions - pulled slightly out to change the time, pushed in to change the alarm time. Button on top of clock pushed to 'up' position to set alarm on, 'down' position for off.
I first had one of these when I was a schoolgirl, and it woke me dutifully every day, for many years. And I took some waking, like most kids. It lasted forever. Very sturdy and survived being swept off bedside tables, knocked over and thrown. This one is pretty much identical.
This has a clear, insistent, repeating chirrup of an alarm call, but other than that, the clock is virtually silent.
Battery will last a year or longer.
This comes properly boxed, with all the paperwork for instructions, guarantees, etc.
I got this for the car, as the internal car clock has clapped out, but this is an ideal little analogue clock that will fit in discreetly just about anywhere..

REVIEW_TITLE: Light in weight, adaptable and comfortable for general use. Limited use as a wheelchair pad.
REVIEW:
A light, 2" thick cushion (18" x 16"), the padding comprises 2 x 1" sheets of foam inside a zipped vinyl cover which has vinyl ties for anchoring to the back. I got this for adding extra cushioning to an office chair to make it a bit more squidgy for sitting, and for the money, it's very good, fits well, doesn't slip and definitely adds to the comfort when sitting down. This is also really good as a bit of extra cushioning on a car seat for the same reasons, especially on a long drive.
This cushion rolls up and fits into a carrier bag - worth getting if you're going to the pictures and it's a long film - those Multiplex cinema seats give me a terrible numb bum and this makes a huge difference.
As for use in a wheelchair, this would be okay, but for light or occasional use only. The foam isn't high density, so is probably best used over some existing padding if the occupant is going to be sat for hours. The vinyl cover is thin and unlikely to be able to protect the foam if the user may have continence issues - the stitched edges aren't waterproofed.
The foam does collapse a bit with extended use - it's fine for me because I don't have restricted mobility, but if it's the sole means of support and cushioning for someone who isn't able to move about, I'd say get professionally assessed by a physio as everybody's needs are different.
This looks like a pro-pad, but it isn't. It's inexpensive and just the job for everyday extra cushioning, but it's not a specialist item.
PRODUCT: Aidapt Vinyl Cushion 18 x 16 x 2 inch Memory Foam (Eligible for VAT relief in the UK)

Fits well but not over generous, so might be worth getting a size or two up if you like these cardies as a relaxed fit or wearing over a thinner sweater.
Lost a star because I prefer my cardies a good, bottom covering length - this covers my tailbone, but it would have been better a couple of inches longer.
Colour is good, it machine washed well on a 'wool' wash without noticeable colour run, shrinking or pilling but needs drying flat, not tumbled.
Nice cardie for casual wear - more High Street than High End, but it's a decent cardie for all that.
I like mine and if it had been just a bit longer, I'd have bought more in other colours.

REVIEW_TITLE: Good, strong antimicrobial. Use with care.
REVIEW:
Very potent antimicrobial, and this will sting like mad on broken, or sensitive skin if it isn't well diluted in a carrier, or if in a bath, some dispersant. My OH puts a few drops of this along with a few drops of Cinnamon Bark Essential oil in a deep, hot bath as a change from Tea Tree when he feels like his sinuses are blocking up or he's getting Man Flu - the steam is strongly antiviral and antimicrobial, warming and richly herbal. He likes the decongestant effect and the warming effect on tired, sore muscles.
I'll use it too, but prefer it mixed with Lemon Myrtle (another strong one) to lighten up the fragrance without compromising on the therapeutic properties.
Red Thyme has loads of uses. In diffusers in the greenhouse to repel pests it's really effective, and it'll clear up fungal infections of toenails as effectively as Oregano when painted on the nail two to three times a week and left.
This one seems to be unadulterated and undiluted with any 'sauce' though, so needs care in use.
Only lost a star because I'd have liked to have had the chemotype (CT) stated so I could use it in different applications.
PRODUCT: Mystic Moments | Thyme Red Essential Oil - 50ml - 100% Pure

New season's (2017) harvest of raw California almonds, and these have a long, 2 year shelf life. These almonds are good quality, clean, undamaged, very little scratching from the sheller run, around 23/25 per oz size, though there are a few doubles. I reckon we're lucky to have fresh almonds at all, given the devastation the recent fires caused in California this year. These are good, crisp and clean tasting.
I use raw almonds to make nut milk, and these have their quality and freshness reflected in the taste of the nut milk. Good product.
PRODUCT: New Harvest Raw Whole Almonds, GMO free, collected from the organic area (700gr)

REVIEW_TITLE: Good, big chair. Roomy and comfortable when spending long periods behind a desk.
REVIEW:
Bought the Standard chair, and it's very comfortable - much better and more comfortable than the typist's chair I'd been using for years.
This is exactly as pictured in the product photo, well made, supportive. Height is adjustable with the lever down on the right hand side, and the button on the side of the seat pad depresses to let you lean back in an over 45 degree tilt. Depressing the button again brings you back upright.
The seat is wide enough to comfortably support large bottoms, and the padded armrests are 'floating' so there's no upright to dig in to the sides of your legs. Even if you're big, or tall, getting in and out of this chair is easy. This chair will comfortably support a big, 25 stone man.
The chair doesn't creak or squeak, it spins on its axis smoothly and the wheels are sturdy and strong. The chair moves around effortlessly on carpet.
The reason this chair lost a star is because the instructions for putting it together were awkwardly written, and I'd have liked the seat padding a bit more squishy.
But it's a very good chair. Roomy and comfortable whether you're spending hours behind a desk or busy at a desktop PC.
PRODUCT: Executive Recline Extra Padded Office Chair (Standard, Black)

REVIEW:
Good quality card, lovely artwork done by the animal cartoonist and artist Alison Lingley.
Card is around 8" x 6" and comes complete with a decent envelope, all wrapped in a crystal plastic wrap. Blank inside.
It's not easy to find just the 'right' card for people, but this one is perfect for someone I know who raises pheasants and is a Land Rover enthusiast. These must be his birds. No wonder they're in a flap.
PRODUCT: A panic of pheasants - Humorous Pheasant themed greeting card

REVIEW_TITLE: Good quality 1m offcut lengths, festive designs in different widths and materials. Delightful ribbons.
REVIEW:
These Christmas themed ribbons arrived neatly folded in a branded, sealed 7" x 3" crystal poly bag. 10 x 1 metre lengths, all different festive Xmas designs. Mine were all good quality, mainly Grossgrain, but there were a couple of satin and organza ribbons too.
Half the pack was 5mm - 10mm width, the other half 10mm - 20mm wide with one being 25mm.
Super little offcuts for enhancing gift wrap, festive bows, decorations or hair styling as well as crafting onto paper, card, or sewing trims.
Good, inexpensive way of buying small lengths of soft, unwired ribbon for pretty, festive trims in a broad range of designs.
PRODUCT: Ribbon off cut bundle - Xmas Theme - contains 10 different 1 metre ribbons

REVIEW_TITLE: Good selection of sizes, nicely made jingle bells for crafting and decorations.
REVIEW:
Over 200 metal jingle bells in green, gold, red and silver. About half the pack are 10-15mm by weight, the other half 20-25mm by weight, so a fair distribution of sizes. 10m of gold braid thread is included.
All the bells jingle except the very tiniest ones, all of them have an unbroken metal loop on the top for threading. I'd suggest 4-5mm ribbon if you prefer ribbon to the thread.
These were excellent value for money and nicely presented in a resealable poly bag.
They're just right for adding to ribbon wrapped gifts, home made decorations and crafts.
PRODUCT: 208 Pieces Craft Bells Christmas Jingle Bells with Golden Silk Thread for Holiday Party Decoration, 10, 15, 20, 25 mm, Assorted Colors

REVIEW_TITLE: Robust, excellent quality jute sack. This one's an XXL, straight out of Santa's grotto.
REVIEW:
Really strongly made, and very large - 26" wide, 46" tall. Capacity around 120 litre volume which makes it around the same size as a large dustbin liner.
Some types of jute or hessian sacks are thin, flimsy affairs, but this is much better quality.
I usually buy hessian sacks for storing root veg, but this one is for a large "Santa" sack. It's big, strong and robust.
It accepts Stencilling for decorating, and it's really easy to attach metal "jingle bell" ornaments and wired decorations such as pine cones, festive bows, etc. on the outside. A thick string closure is simple to thread through with a trussing needle, and the top can be folded back neatly if it's not going to be filled completely.
I was looking at the natural fibre Santa sacks on Amazon, but most of them were around 19" x 28" which is pillowcase size, ok for stocking 'fillers' for the kids either under the tree or at the end of the bed, but not big enough to stash boxed gifts, and the bigger, pre-stencilled ones were a bit too expensive.
This is huge - a big, strong sack which is versatile enough to be multipurpose, to hold loads of small gifts for a ward full of poorlies, a classroom of kids or a family sized collection of boxed gifts.
As well as around 50kg spuds.
PRODUCT: Nutley's 66 x 116cm Extra Large Hessian Potato and Vegetable Sack

REVIEW_TITLE: Just the right size for scooping Muesli and other dry Storecupboard items.
REVIEW:
Basic pair of lightweight metal scoops and the right sort of kitchen size I was looking for - scoops either seem to be far too tiny, or massive.
These scoops hold around 70 - 75g muesli, about the same weight of dog food kibble, dry almonds, or about 100g flour, granulated sugar or rice.
Scoop barrel measures around 4" long, 2.5" wide at its widest part, graduating to 2" at the end, averaging about 1" deep. Handle is just over 3" long with a diameter of 0.5," soldered on to the barrel and capped off at the end. The finish on mine is as illustrated in the product pic, not roughly done, functional, but no bells or whistles. The product description says they're stainless steel but these feel more like a light alloy, and I wouldn't put these in a dishwasher - the finish on them wouldn't survive.
They probably would scoop ice cream, but only if the ice cream is 'soft scoop' - there isn't a lot of substance in the construction of these scoops.
With everyday light domestic use these should last a lot better than the empty yoghurt pots I'd been using as scoops, as well as looking a lot smarter.
I'll update on their performance over time, but for now, three stars, which I'll upgrade to four if they last reasonably well.
PRODUCT: 6 Ounces Ice Scoop Stainless Steel Bar Dry Bin Goods Scoop Candy Spice Scoop, 2 Pack

REVIEW_TITLE: No Rinse Formula. Massage in, brush out. No powdery residue, no mess. Cleans and deodorises.
REVIEW:
Several different products seem to be under review on this page, so for the sake of clarity, this review is for the "No Rinse" formula.
Order comprised 2 x 240ml bottles, so a good amount of product for the current price. It's very easy to use.
The pump action top delivers a mousse style handful which is then applied to the dog's coat, and worked down into the coat with fingertips.
The foam is applied to a dry coat, but if the coat is a bit damp anyway, it won't matter.
I used this on a long coat GSD, so I ended up using about 100ml, or about half the bottle in total. That was enough to get through his whole coat, nose through to tip of his tail without being over-generous, but on a smaller, or shorter coated dog, you wouldn't need to use so much.
After application, the dog's coat is supposed to be given a rub with a towel, and given a good brush. Easy.
After I'd worked it into his coat, my hands had product on them, but it didn't feel particularly sticky or greasy, and neither did the dog's coat. It brushed out easily, and he definitely looked more bouffant and cleaner, and subsequent brushings continued to bring him up looking nicer than standard grooming alone.
I don't 'wet shampoo' the dogs as they take days to dry properly, but their coats do ming a bit if they're not kept relatively clean. I used to use Quistel spray, which is a great product, but it's really expensive when you've got Sheps.
Some products can leave the coat feeling a bit sticky or greasy, and some are just plain useless. This seems to be effective, and leaves the coat feeling clean and it was definitely easier to get the brush through, even on difficult areas like under his tail and between his back legs round his baccy pouch. Really quick to use and seemed to do a good job.
This product deodorises his haircoat effectively without making him smell like an overpampered baby.
Which he is, but I'd never tell him to his face.
PRODUCT: Wahl Smartgroom Shampoo No Rinse for Pets, 240 ml x2

REVIEW_TITLE: Great Quality, Genuine Elemi Essential Oil.
REVIEW:
This is lovely quality - Elemi has loads of uses as an anti-inflammatory, gently antiseptic oil with a slightly spicy, frankincense like fragrance. It's mainly used in expensive cosmetics - I use a few drops in rosehip seed oil for facial use or added to a moisturiser for all over - it's soothing and healing, smells and feels lovely, sinks in with no oily residue.
Good too, blended with Styrax Benzoin in a bit of my Calendula oil for repairing chafed skin and healing moisture lesions.
A mix of Elemi, Benzoin and Eucalyptus in a vapouriser or as an inhalant is a specific for head colds or respiratory virus infections as well as smelling lovely, suitable for all ages.
Elemi is superb all year round, but it's one of my absolute essential for winter use.
This is a really well sourced E.O. from a reputable company and it's one of the best.
PRODUCT: Elemi Essential Oil 10ml

REVIEW:
Total length 10.5" - Total height 7.5" Footprint is 6" x 5.25" excluding the forward slope if it's sitting as shown in the product pic.
If you're storing flour or other bulky dry goods such as cereals, biscuits or cat/dog food kibble and want to max out on the 5 litre volume capacity, this also sits securely on its back end on a total footprint of 7.5" x 6"
Stood as shown in the product pic, the capacity is 5 litres in total, but only 3 litres to the flip top porthole in the lid.
It depends on the density of what you want to store as to how much you can get in one of these and whether the container is parked as shown, or on its end, but 2-3kg muesli, same for nuts, seeds, kibble, flour, sugar etc. But maybe only 750g Rice Crispies or Cornflakes etc.
Six clips hold the entire top on firmly. There's a blue sealing gasket round all inner rims to keep contents secure, damp proof and relatively air tight.
Top has a built in flip top lid which stays open when pushed back and the porthole opening is 3.25" x 4.5" - big enough to get your hand inside, or a measuring scoop.
It's been designed to be versatile and it's been made from strong plastics, freezer proof and dishwasher safe. Good product and will keep all sorts of dry goods safely stored.
I'm using mine to store home made muesli in, and it does a terrific job of holding 3kg at a time with room to spare.
This'll last many years.
PRODUCT: Lock & Lock Kitchen Caddy with FlipTop Lid - Clear/Blue, 5 L

REVIEW_TITLE: Good stuff. Completely removed ingrained stains in a wool carpet that I thought were permanent.
REVIEW:
I've used Vanish carpet products for years on the wool carpets in my holiday cottage - the foam is good for general high traffic areas, but there've been some more difficult stains that have been a bit of a problem, more recently a rather anonymous splat which someone had wiped up and it had dried in - I'd no idea what it was, but the other spot cleaners hadn't touched it, so I got this Vanish Gold, more in hope than expectation.
This product cleared it completely. Gone. Wouldn't have known anything had been splatted.
So I gave this a go on another old carpet stain which had been around for a long time - I occasionally have another run at it and it's barely visible, but I know it's there, and it bugs me, so I gave it a go with this. Gone.
I did give both stains a good dosing - not to soak the carpet entirely, but a generous application. Gently scrubbed it in and left it overnight - the instructions say 5 mins max but I got waylaid. Revisited it next morning and there was nothing there, and the carpet fibres hadn't suffered any colour loss or damage.
This is also really effective on anonymous stains on the upholstery of sofas and chairs where I haven't got time to, or can't, remove the covers for washing on changeover. These are mostly hot drinks the guests have accidentally slopped on the sofa, or a dog has slobbered. Or something - but it gets rid of them, too and the upholstery is pristine again ready for the next assault.
I've used this in my own house for the greasy tide mark left by my own GSDs when they've lain on the floor up against the sofa, or wiped their whiskers on the chair backs, thinking I won't know. I don't normally fuss about the grime my own dogs make in the house, but I'm a bit fussy about the cottage, and I'm well pleased with this. Good stuff. I've got some more of this ready for the next 'emergency.'
PRODUCT: Vanish Gold Carpet Stain Remover Spray 500 ml (Pack of 2)

REVIEW_TITLE: Well made and nice to hold. The Launch Party is still out, though.
REVIEW:
Gave this four stars because of the construction - strong, well made from good quality plastics and silicone. Ergonomic, comfortable and non slip handle, 25" long with a robust cup. This won't snap or break like the cheapies.
Lost a star because, even with all the technology, it's still a bit rigid and I like a bit of flexibility in the wand to get a good fling on the ball.
This does fling, but the technique has to be slightly different - it works better if held out to the side and then flung forwards and up at around 45 degrees and it takes a bit of practise to get the wrist flick right, whereas the cheapies are more flexible and lob quite easily.
This does a better job than the Chuckit! pocket launcher which is so stiff and short it's impossible to get the ball to go any distance at all - I couldn't get on with that one at all, neither could my OH, and he serves a Masterclass in lobbing.
The ball that came with this wand is a genuine Chuckit ball - quite tough, but not indestructible and the cup is a standard size so will take most standard tennis balls, or any ball with around 2.5" diameter. I like the Chuckit Whistler balls - they're mine and the dog's favourite in this range.
Worth the money? Here's the bottom line. The cheapies do a better job if you're used to the cheapies. But they often break, and these don't, plus these are much nicer to use, once the technique has been perfected. But you have to get used to the different technique. My OH gets on well with this now, but he did have to practise with it.
Me? Jury's still out to launch on this one. I might ask the dog to buy me an extra long one for Christmas.
PRODUCT: Chuckit! Ultra Grip Ball Launcher, Medium, 64 cm

REVIEW_TITLE: Absolutely worth the wait - these are beautifully constructed bouquets, lovely quality 'blooms.'
REVIEW:
Beautiful, romantic swathe of fabric peony flowers, central main stem with about a dozen long, offshoots with fabric leaves, each offshoot has a large, 3" - 4" peony head, colours mainly pale, dusky pink/pale lilac petals with deeper tinted edges, darker centres, masses of curled petals in each mophead bloom.
One or two variants, a spike of meadowsweet here, a seedhead there for texture. All the flower stalks are bendable, so the display can be arranged easily.
Two or three of these bouquets will fill a large, shabby chic pitcher. The more generous you are, the better the display will look
I don't usually like fake flowers at any price, but these are beautifully made, soft, well constructed, utterly retro, beguilingly shabby chic.
Mine are in a Victorian style, tall cream jug, decorating a cast iron grate in a disused inglenook fireplace.
It looks absolutely stunning.
Even my OH, who normally winces at artificial flowers, says the peonies have transformed the plain, cold fireplace into something that looks really lovely.
PRODUCT: HuntGold 1X Artificial Peony Silk Flowers Bouquet for Wedding Party Bouquet Decoration(cameo)

REVIEW:
Got this pair of turkeys to augment the six racing penguins in a set of Christmas crackers to add to the general chaos of post-Christmas dinner silliness.
This daft looking pair are each about the size of a tennis ball, wind up at the side and their clockwork feet take them pottering along (not always in a straight line) along the race track in a race with the penguins - but it would be easy enough to make them their own track from a piece of cardboard box, and competing with other clockwork creatures available on Amazon - there's loads.
These don't go very far.... fully wound, they scuttle along drunkenly for about 12" - 18" before running out of steam.
I had hoped, being a bit bigger, they'd have a bit more about them. I'm tempted to buy the Grandma & Grandpa racing figures and give the turkeys a head start.. see if the Gramps can catch them up on their Zimmer frames.
The possibilities are endless.
PRODUCT: Racing Turkeys

REVIEW_TITLE: Lovely, timeless portrayal of Dartmoor and the Dartmoor pony.
REVIEW:
Bought this DVD as a bit of local interest for holidaymakers at the cottage, along with some other DVDs about Dartmoor, and I can tell it's been watched, a lot, over the years.
Our native ponies have been under threat for many years - this DVD investigates some of the reasons why, and honours the Moor people who have owned and managed their ponies, breeding into them the hardiness and strength to survive on the different areas of Dartmoor where different challenges need slight variances in breeding policies for these ponies to flourish in their particular locations.
It's an old film now, but the Moors are still as timeless and beautiful as they have been for centuries and the Dartmoor pony has been sensitively and sensibly portrayed with a sympathetic narration, along with glimpses of the lives of the folk who own them and run them.
An absorbing and warming film, about an hour or so long, covering a year in the Calendar of the Dartmoor pony, the simple camera work tells a simple story.
A classic, and still worth watching for the beautiful Dartmoor scenery, the ponies, and an ancient way of life.
PRODUCT: The Year Of The Dartmoor Hill Pony: The Story That Must Be Told!

REVIEW_TITLE: Good Hyacinth Fragrance Oil. Loads of applications in fragrancing.
REVIEW:
Good, Hyacinth fragrance with a very natural smell, not chemical. Good in a bicarbonate of soda 'shaker' as a carpet freshener or on a tissue inside the Vacuum cleaner dustbag to stop any niffs when you're vacuuming - a few drops are all that's needed. The fragrance is synthetic, but it is very close to natural Hyacinth. A few drops on an aroma stone, or in the dish of an Airwick wax melter (without any messy wax) fragrances the whole room.
I use this in a reed diffuser after the original contents have evaporated. Half fill the diffuser with vodka, add half a bottle of the fragrance oil and a drop of liquid soap as a dispersant. Mix well and stick the reeds back in.
I use the recycled reed diffuser in rooms that aren't being used much to keep the air sweet and deter any bugs.
Lasts weeks, just as good as the expensive replacements and much cheaper than any plug in.
PRODUCT: LiveMoor Pure Fragrance Oil - Hyacinth - 25ml - Paraben Free

REVIEW_TITLE: Strong, light, flexible and easy to use. Multipurpose lifters
REVIEW:
I bought the set of 3 with the wooden handles - very pleased with the strength, lightness and flexibility. The tang on the 8" one is fitted down the wooden handle to a good third of the length of the handle, two rivets to hold it secure. The 6" spatula is similarly fitted, the 4" one has the tang a good half the length, again, two rivets. All three have a drilled hole for hanging (no loop).
They're pretty secure. Not meant to be immersed in water for long, or put through a dishwasher, they still clean up well and have been really versatile. I've been using these for all sorts of purposes.
They're really good at lifting wedges of flan or pie from the dish; for lifting traybake slices such as brownies or flapjack, or for extracting slices of pizza, lifting slices of cake or cheesecake from the plate/stand - and do a much better job than a broader fish slice (previously the nearest thing to hand) and live quite happily in the utensils jar along with all the other paraphernalia. They're pretty much my 'go to' gadgets.
The design is very good, and the offset makes them particularly useful as lifters, but they're well balanced enough for distribution of icings and frostings, and as a flat finishing tool if you're short of a dedicated float.
The materials used are basic s/steel which will pit, eventually, and the wooden handles, if exposed to a lot of steam or extremes of temperature will deteriorate. But as inexpensive, useful kitchen utensils that will last well for years with a little care, these represent good value for money at current rsp of under a tenner. I like them and they're good at what they do.
PRODUCT: Puckway Offset Cake Icing Spatula Set of 3 Professional Stainless Steel Cake Decorating Frosting Spatulas (4"-6"-8" Flexible Resistant Blade)Angled with Wooden Handle For Easy Grip

REVIEW_TITLE: Excellent domestic kitchen scale. Reliable, fast and responsive. Large, clear display panel.
REVIEW:
These kitchen scales are arguably the best I've ever used for the price paid. The circular weighing platform is polished metal, just under 7" diameter so it's able to support large containers and jugs as well as most bowl sizes. It's fast and accurate - measures weight in units of grams and/or pounds and ounces; plus volume in units of millilitres and/or fluid ounces.
The LCD screen is a good, big size at nearly two inches long and almost an inch high. The unit system (grams, lb:oz, ml or fl.oz) is clearly displayed along the bottom - and you're able to switch between . The displayed weight numerals are large, well spaced and clear.
It's not backlit, but a big plus is that the display is on a slant, so it makes it even easier to see.
Clear icons show when you're weighing using the Tare function.
Gives you a good two minutes before it turns itself off, so you won't have to worry about having to rush off to fetch a bit more of something, only to find the machine has turned itself off already.
Buttons for Unit (lb:oz, etc.) and On/Off and Tare are large and well separated either side of the display panel.
It will turn off straight away if you press the on/off button.
Two AAA batteries (supplied) are easily fitted into the compartment on the underside - much better than fiddly disc types.
The whole scale measures 7" wide x 8.25" long, so it's not cumbersome.
Plastic and metal construction is easy to wipe down, and the box is no bigger than the average hardback cookery book, so its easy to store when not in use.
PRODUCT: AmazonBasics 5kg LCD Digital Kitchen Scale

REVIEW_TITLE: Digs out the Myths surrounding the Veggie garden and composts them. Worth forking out for.
REVIEW:
Excellent little hardback book from the 'No Dig' specialist and gardening guru Charles Dowding. About 100 pages long, it debunks the folklore, myths and superstitions that many gardeners have been deluded into believing to be gospel. It's mainly aimed at vegetable growers, but it'll be of interest to anybody who enjoys gardening but wonders about the real truth which belies all that traditional hard work and slog...
Written in a gentle, easy to read style, well laid out and delightfully illustrated in an old fashioned style, this book also has a marker ribbon to keep your place whether you prefer to dip in and out or if you want to refer back to a particular part.
The common myths and misconceptions regarding Sowing and Planting, Watering, Veggie garden planning and design, Vegetables, Trees and shrubs, Manure and fertilisers, Compost making, Soil structure, Pests, diseases and weeds are all discussed and the myths surrounding them explained and in many instances debunked altogether.
This book is a great little gift for any plot or allotment holder who's interested in growing their own veg, but a bit put off by all the old, often outdated advice that things absolutely "Have To Be Done A Certain Way."
I've grown veggies for the house most of my life and I've often questioned some of the traditional practices - it was great to read from someone who also raised the same questions, done the science and laid much of the folklore to rest where it belongs and written about it in a sensible, pragmatic way.
One of the clever things about this book is that it's a good intro to wanting to read more by this author. I haven't yet read any of Charles Dowding's other gardening books, but I will, as I like his take on things. This is a super little companion book, ideal for a grower, or anyone interested in gardening.
PRODUCT: Gardening Myths and Misconceptions (Wise Words)

REVIEW_TITLE: Big, Beautiful, Chocolate Pound Coin. Put your money where your mouth is!
REVIEW:
Exactly as it looks on the product photo, this oversized, gold foiled Belgian milk chocolate coin measures 5" diameter and is a quarter of an inch thick. Weighs 90g and has minimum 28% cocoa solids - so there's quite a bit of choccy here, and if we're counting, this will give you around 450 calories. Eeek.
Gold foil wrapping is strong and the embossing (both sides) is excellent. Good colour, similar to the cash coins and this comes nicely gift wrapped in white tissue with a scripted label, so it all looks quite posh.
This is a stocking filler for my OH, so I can't comment on the taste of this coin yet - but I have had chocolate from this Belgian chocolatier (Albert Premier) before, and it's decent chocolate, smooth and sweet. Not luxury quality - but then again, this was bought as a novelty product, and as such completely fulfils expectations.
The Best Before on this (bought in November '17) is end of June '18, but it will probably have been eaten before Boxing Day!
PRODUCT: Giant Belgian Milk Chocolate Pound Coin

REVIEW_TITLE: Soft, warm and light. Beautiful Pashmina style multi-purpose wrap.
REVIEW:
Soft, silky, cosy and very light, this pashmina sized wrap is 6' long (not including the 3.5" tassels either end) and 28" wide.
Charcoal black background on mine with a wine red poppy design which has the background colour woven through the petals to give the illusion of texture and depth. Poppies are approximately 3" diameter, subtle, muted and very pretty.
Can be worn reversed so it shows a red background with black poppies if you want a bit more impact. The hemming is nicely done and the tassels have been tied.
This is a lovely shawl, perfect to wear to keep your head warmly covered, as a wrap around your shoulders, or simply as a scarf.
I bought mine for commemorative reasons this November, but it'll be lovely to wear at any time of year, particularly on chilly days.
Made from an acrylic/viscose mix, it's hand washable (30c), dry flat, cool iron.
Mega good value at current price and worth every one of it's five stars.
PRODUCT: New Fine Pashmina Soft Black Red Poppy Poppies Print Scarf Wrap Gift

REVIEW:
Six little nylon mesh bags each containing nine gold wrapped chocolate 'coins' of three different sizes - 2 coins of 38mm, 2 of 28mm and 5 of 22mm diameter. That's about an inch and a half, an inch, and three quarters of an inch, if you're still working in Old money, as this Pirate Treasure undoubtedly is.
All coins are the same thickness, 4mm. Wrapped in strong, gold foil, embossed with Pirate logos on both sides and with ridged edges.
They're pretty tough, and will withstand being slammed around, bartered for Haribo jewellery, stolen, fought over, trodden on and buried in pockets.
And that's just the Adults.
Little ones might need an adult's help to get the foil off, but the foil is put on in two halves, so peels off cleanly round the edge of each coin.
Net bag is sturdy and securely tagged with a cartoon Pirate.
The chocolate is sweet and cheap, as you'd expect, but very few young Pirates will complain.
Just don't let them near your Rum.
PRODUCT: Six 25gr bags of Gold Pirate treasure Chocolate coins

REVIEW_TITLE: Well designed, efficient in use. Durable and should last for years.
REVIEW:
Good, strong, mirror polished 4" steel wheel, bevelled edge, sharp. Central pivot secured with two steel washers with sturdy nut and screw fixing, designed for a Phillips, but versatile enough to accept adjustment from a rounded knife tip if and when the wheel needs a tighten and you can't remember what you did with the screwdriver.
Sturdy tang is fixed firmly down inside the chunky, ergonomically designed plastic handle.
This cutter is 9.25" long in total, so it's a good size - cuts and wheels through deep fill pizza without pulling or tearing at the toppings like a standard knife does and there's absolutely no chance of this gadget seizing up as there is with other makes of wheel that have only been riveted.
It can also wheel through flans, flapjacks or other traybakes without ripping at the surface.
It could have done with a protective sleeve for storage in the gadget drawer, or a loop to hang it up with so it's safely out of the way when not in use. Mine's kept in an old sock, but it does the job of protecting the blade.
I'm glad I got this wheel. Very useful and sturdy, dishwasher safe, sharpens up with the 'pull through' knife sharpeners and should last for years.
PRODUCT: Pizza Cutter, Large 10cm Professional Heavy Duty Stainless Steel Wheel, Dishwasher Safe, Non-Slip Handle

REVIEW_TITLE: Discreet and charming Poppy lapel brooch.
REVIEW:
Pretty, discreet little lapel pin measuring just under 1.5" tall and an inch across. Covered with tiny, gold outlined, enamelled red poppies with black rhinestone centres on the upper surface. Plain on the reverse with a fastener which has a securing clasp.
Presented in a cellophane packet inside a red plush drawstring baggie.
Almost lost the fifth star as the fastening feels a bit dainty to my fumbling fingers, but it's got the benefit of the doubt, for now.
I like the style of this little brooch - the message is quite clear, without being OTT.
There isn't any donation from the sale of this brooch to the British Legion's charity.
I tend to put some money in the collecting boxes anyway, but I don't care for the traditional poppies, so I don't take one - then my poppy wearing colleagues gang up and accuse me of ignoring the appeal.
This attractive little brooch will do a good job of keeping the naysayers off my back, and I bet they'll all be wanting one.
PRODUCT: NEW 2017 Design Gold Red Black Rhinestone Ribbon Poppy Brooch Pin Remembrance Day Awareness UK Seller

REVIEW:
I like to give my GSD a chew treat occasionally when I want to keep him occupied and give him something to do - he isn't interested in fake bones, chew toys or Kongs, it has to be a food item to engage him for more than a few minutes. He's raw fed and I didn't want to give him a natural bone as they form part of his diet anyway. I usually get natural 'chews' from Zooplus, but they're gone in a matter of seconds, and I'm not keen on rawhide chews or leathers because of the chemicals often used in processing.
These are made from Yak's and Cow's milk compressed into very hard bars, each weighs just under 100g and measures 1" x 1" x 5" long.
He absolutely loves these - gets right into them, and they give him a good, long chewing session of around 45 minutes non-stop gnawing, which is quite an achievement - the dog has the jaws of a Hyena. I haven't found any other 'natural' chew that will keep him so totally engaged for the best part of an hour until the very last crumb is gone
These haven't been messy, haven't left a mark on the carpet, and haven't upset his stomach.
After a session with one of these, he has a long drink and then totally crashes out, exhausted, content and evidently very pleased with himself.
This order of 5 pieces comes in individual, airtight bags each with a desiccant sachet. Each bag has a date of manufacture printed on the outer. The Best Before is three years from date of manufacture. The chew is odourless - maybe just a very slightly sweetish fragrance.
It's a very good product, well presented. Expensive, but he's worth it, he tells me.
PRODUCT: 5 Piece Pack Large Dogs 100% Natural Dog Chews, Made from Yak and Cow Milk, (Large Dogs)

REVIEW_TITLE: Very blunt and the wheel completely seized on first use.
REVIEW:
Bought to slice through 'Deep Pan' and deep filled large pizza - ordinary knives pull and tear at the toppings, so a wheel is a useful piece of kit.
This one, although a good size and having a thumb guard, was very blunt, not even sharp enough to cut, let alone give a clean slice.
Not that it even got that far. Halfway through its very first use, the wheel seized up completely. There wasn't any way of adjusting it, as it just has a central rivet - it can't be freed up once seized.
Absolutely useless and I was back to using the Mezzaluna to finish dividing the pizza.
Back on here to look for a decent one.
PRODUCT: HeyLR 4 inch Premium Stainless Steel 18/8 Pizza Cutter Wheel Pizza Slicer - Strong and Best Sharp Blade Pizza Cutter Wheel

REVIEW:
Six large, gold foil crackers with proper tartan ribbon trims, each containing a snap, a paper crown, a motto and a cellophane wrapped, numbered clockwork penguin.
The racetrack is a flat, printed board, 11" wide x 12" long, and will sit on top of the box if you want to play without clearing the table.
The plastic penguins have a winding mechanism on their sides, they're about 2.5" tall, 1.5" wide, and about an inch from front to back.
Wind them up, set them down on their numbered track lane, and off they waddle - stumbling, going round in circles, falling over.. sometimes they might even go straight long enough to get to the finish line.
Fully wound, they trundle along for a couple of feet, so if they fall over or crash into each other, there's enough clockwork to set them off from the start line to give them another chance without having to rewind them..... if you can stop laughing long enough...
They're a smart black and white, clearly numbered on the back, and quite nicely detailed with daft expressions
Great fun and lasted well.
PRODUCT: 6 Penguin Clockwork Racing Christmas Crackers

REVIEW_TITLE: One doesn't fit, the other one drips. NBG.
REVIEW:
Bought a pair of these pump dispensers to give accurate measures from 5l containers of laundry detergent and conditioner.
Both 5l containers were standard size, with 38mm openings.
Theoretically, these should fit - all you have to do is to affix the tubing to the pump, then screw the pump onto the container in place of the cap, then prime the dispenser by depressing the plunger a couple of times.
One dispenser fitted, the other didn't. Swapped them around, in case it was the container, but it wasn't, the fault lay with the dispenser. Maddening.
The one that fitted, drips. You have to lock off the pump by pushing it right down and twisting, which is a pest if you've already dispensed what you need from the container, and it still wants to have the last drip, even then.
I've been looking on Amazon for other "Pelican" type dispensers, because I don't want to have to keep decanting from 5l containers into smaller ones, it's too much faffing around.
So far, all of them look pretty much alike. If I find a pair that are any good, I'll revisit this review and give you a steer, but I couldn't really recommend these. Doesn't matter how inexpensive these get, they're still nbg if they're nbg.
PRODUCT: Pack of Two 38mm Pump Dispensers to Suit 5 Litre Containers - Dispenses 30ml Dose - White

REVIEW:
I was glad to see these particular almonds back on sale, so I grabbed a few packs - although they're a bit smaller than the usual premium sized almonds and the packs do contain a few doubles, these seem to make better Almond 'milk' than most.
These give a really good, creamy milk with a delicious flavour which is quite noticeably sweeter, creamier and fresh tasting.
They're currently on for a very good price and are well produced, with no diseased nuts or brown spot, very few scratched or chipped ones in the packs, hardly any damaged ones. I don't think they're the new harvest for this year, but they're still crisp, clean and good tasting.
I'd have given them five stars, but the bags still don't carry any provenance or a harvesting date.
But the milk they make is just as good as ever. I make mine by soaking about 200g in cold water overnight, then rinsing and putting in a blender with a teaspoonful of sugar (optional), a pinch of salt and a 1.5 litres of water. Blitz for a minute or two, then pour into a nut milk bag and squeeze the 'milk' out into a bowl, then decant into a 'lock and lock' style fridge jug and use within 2 - 3 days. It does separate a bit with standing, but easily shakes back up. Lovely on cereal or porridge, really creamy and tasty, and these are the best.
PRODUCT: Vie Nutrition Quality Whole Raw Almonds - 750g

REVIEW_TITLE: I shall be living off Beans on Toast for the rest of the week.
REVIEW:
Bought the large size as an indulgent birthday present for my GSD. He loves anything creamy, or milky and I thought he'd be interested in this as it's made from Yak's and Cow's milk - it actually reminded me of a piece of hard, whey cheese, like a Mysost, only much firmer and denser.
Compressed into a bar, this chew weighed just under 100g and measured 1" x 1" x 5" long.
Comes in an airtight bag with a dessicant sachet, this has a date of manufacture printed on the outer. The Best Before is three years from date of manufacture. The chew is odourless - maybe just a very slightly sweetish fragrance. It's a good product, nicely presented without any fanfare.
My dog loved this.
He's raw fed, so very experienced in chewing through meaty bones and carcases and I was curious to see how long this would last.
Well, he really enjoyed it. Every morsel. He had a wonderful chew and really got into it. It lasted 45 minutes, start to finish.
Afterwards, he headed off to his water pail, had a good drink and then came over and gave me that slow wag of his tail and smiling, like he does when he says his doggy equivalent of "Thank You."
Then he went and crashed out by the sofa.
Eating the whole chew didn't cause any digestive upset and there wasn't a mark on the carpet or a crumb left uneaten.
Money well spent, but I can't afford to buy him these very often, though I did notice that these are also sold in packs of five at a slightly better unit cost.
Old hyena jaws isn't interested in chew toys, kongs or nylabones - it has to be a food item to engage him, and this is the first food 'chew' that he hasn't demolished in under two minutes. So I'll definitely repurchase, but for "Special Occasions" like Fireworks night (to keep him occupied), Christmas and the like.
That dog eats better than I do.
PRODUCT: 100% Natural Dog Chews, Made from Yak and Cow Milk, 1 Piece High Protein Content Dog Chew, Organic Dog Chew/Treat (Large Dogs)

REVIEW_TITLE: Plump and succulent fillets, no dry bits. Natural and delicious.
REVIEW:
These are delicious fillets of herring, beech/oak wood smoked into traditional kippers, no dye. This order of 2kg contained 10 packs, each pack containing two (double) fillets, each fillet measuring about 4-5" across, about 6" long. Each pack weighs a minimum of 150g and the fillets are plump and succulent.
These arrived in double quick time, by courier, in a chilled state, boxed and with chill packs to keep cold. They're ready for use in their 'boil in the bag' packs, or can go straight in the freezer.
I don't like kippers very salty, so I don't do 'boil in the bag.' I like mine better decanted from their packs into a pan and poached for a few minutes in a little water, then lifted out and served with a dollop of butter and a big chunk of freshly baked bread. The poaching takes out some of the salt, but doesn't spoil the flavour.
These have been well filleted, very few pins. Bigger and much nicer than the yellow offerings in the supermarkets, and better tasting.
I prefer fillets to the whole kippers as they're easier to do in a pan (or under the grill) and there aren't any dry bits or skeletons to dispose of.
It's hard to find really good kipper fillets, these are lush and I'll definitely order from here again.
PRODUCT: Port of Lancaster Lancashire Kipper Fillets - 2kg box

REVIEW_TITLE: Things that go squeak in the night.......
REVIEW:
This squeaky squirrel measures 9" from nose to root of tail, tail itself is well stuffed and stitched to halfway up the back of the main body. Ears and all four legs are distinct from the main body, eyes are patches. It looks pretty much anatomically correct, with a squeaker in the tail and another in the main body. All the stitching is secure and the stuffing is firm. Really good detailing. Too much, possibly.
A serious chewer will dismember and disembowel this creature in short order, legs and tail are just begging to be chewed off, but a dog who isn't hard on his or her squeakies may well be very gentle with this.
My German Shepherd's life ambition is to capture a real squirrel - in fact I can't even say the word 'Squirrel' without an excited dash to the door.
But he's very mindful of this toy and even seems to be very caring of it.
I, on the other hand, wish he'd rip it up, because it feels just like a dead rodent when I pick it up - it's the exact size of a large, dead, tree rat.
Even more so when it's wet from being licked and cuddled up to.
I'm not squeamish, but there are limits, especially when I trip over the thing in the dark, in the middle of the night.
PRODUCT: All For Paws Squirrel Dog Toy wih Squeaker, 9-inch/ 23 cm

REVIEW_TITLE: Delicious Umami. A staple ingredient for winter casseroles, pot roasts, sauces and stuffings.
REVIEW:
This order comprised four bulbs of black garlic, each separately boxed. Each bulb is a good size and the cloves have been well aged, all in excellent condition, no duff ones.
I love the taste of black garlic, it's nothing like raw or fresh garlic. I can quite happily eat a clove like a sweetie and not be breathing garlic fumes over everybody for the rest of the day.
Tastes like caramelised onion, sweetly balsamic, hint of aniseed, slightly treacly. These cloves are soft and fudgy, good, dark colour. These are soft and pliable, slice well, mash well, can be blended with oil to add terrific umami to dressings or mayo.
I like them in all sorts of savoury sauces and a clove or two,sliced, in scrambled eggs lifts the eggs onto another level altogether.
Delicious added to stews or casseroles, either whole or sliced, and give a real umami to pates and terrines.
An absolute 'must have' to add to lamb dishes, risottos or anything with mushrooms.
There's loads of recipes where black garlic can really add to the flavours of food.
I used to buy the paste, but these cloves are really fuss free, easy to use and this order (bought in October '17) has shelf life of over a year.
Definitely putting these on the regular order list as I don't want to be without these, especially for winter casseroles and pot roasts.
PRODUCT: Black Garlic Single Bulb, Whole Head of Black Garlic, Unpeeled Black Garlic Bulb, Pack of 4 Black Garlic Bulbs.

REVIEW_TITLE: Very useful 100g grip leads which sit hard on most tides.
REVIEW:
My OH particularly likes these for estuary fishing when he's going after Bass and Bream. These are well made 100g leads, very hard to find at this weight.
He says 4oz leads are just slightly too heavy, but these are perfect for estuary fishing where they grip the estuary mud.
These sit hard on the bottom on most tides which is exactly what he wants.
These have been coated in a corrosion resistant finish, so should last well if he doesn't lose too many.
He's well pleased with these. Recommended.
PRODUCT: Zfish Grippa Lead 100 g (Pack of 10) Lead, Black, S

REVIEW_TITLE: Good, robust rubber construction. Fits well in most throwers.
REVIEW:
This pack of 2 mid-sized balls are quite tough rubber, but not too heavy to make pick up and retrieve difficult. They fit well in most standard sized throwers, and with a decent thrower, the weight and balance of these helps the ball go a good distance.
The 'whistle' is more of a Sci-Fi "Whooooo" - looks a bit silly written down, but you get what I mean.
Balls bounce on landing, acting like a normal tennis ball. Because they're not fuzzy, they don't get too slobbery and can withstand a sneaky gnashing on the retrieve.
What lost them their fifth star was the colour - these easily get lost in grass, they could do to be a bit brighter for us humans to find them if the dog has got distracted. They're unlikely to survive the attentions of a serious chewer for long, and this size could present a choke hazard for a large dog, so I think, like tennis balls, they need to be used with supervision.
I like these better than tennis balls though, they're well made and robust.
PRODUCT: Chuckit The Whistler Dog Toy, 6 cm, Medium, 2-Piece

REVIEW_TITLE: Rigid and inflexible. Didn't 'throw' well at all.
REVIEW:
Couldn't get on with this. It's too rigid - no flexibility in the throwing wand meant that the ball being launched didn't go any distance at all.
There is a knack to these launchers and I'm a bit rubbish at the best of times, but even my OH, who is an expert in the technique of using throwing wands, didn't like this thrower either.
Said it was too short, too inflexible - at best, the ball launched 10 - 15ft; which would be okay for a little dog or a puppy, but useless for a bigger, more energetic dog who likes a good chase. He says he can throw the ball further than the launcher.
The ball that comes with it is sturdy, and survived a good gnashing - but it looks like I'm still on the hunt for a decent thrower.
Shame, really, as it was quite expensive and I was hoping that it would live up to expectations.
PRODUCT: Chuckit! Pocket Ball Launcher (Colors Vary)

REVIEW_TITLE: This offer represents better VFM, but for a brand leader, it's not all it's cracked up to be.
REVIEW:
I usually wait for Ariel to be on offer at the supermarket before buying any, as I think it's overpriced.
I didn't have any hesitation about sending off for this 3 x 2litre bottles though, because it does represent reasonable value for money at eighteen pounds for the three bottles, as opposed to the rsp of thirty in most supermarkets. I get through industrial quantities of laundry detergent during the holiday season when I'm doing tons of heavy, white cotton bedlinen every week, and I need to have the linen spotless.
Each bottle will do up to 40 washes, depending on how hard or soft your water is, plus your machine size.
A 6-8kg machine load needs 75ml, plus another 25ml if your water is hard, or your clothes are very grubby or stained. It's an effective detergent, but if you're using 100ml (about half a cupful) of Ariel for each wash, then the bottle will only do 20 washes.
I'm not keen on this dosing cap. The idea is that you pour the amount into the cap and put the cap, with the detergent, into the machine with the clothes. I always end up losing the cap, but if I don't put the cap in the machine then I've got to wash the cap before I can replace it on the bottle..
The bottle usually ends up getting runs of detergent down the outside anyway because the inner cap hasn't been very well designed, and as the liquid has been described as being possibly irritant, that's not good if you get neat liquid on your fingers.
So, all in all, a bit of a thumbs down. Ariel has got reasonable stain removing power, but it's expensive and these bottles are messy. I prefer Lidls Formil, which is vastly cheaper, has a much better designed cap and IMO just as good. If I've got whites that need an extra boost I'll put a measure of Astonish in with it. This Ariel isn't great for coloured clothes, it does tend to fade them after a few washes.
I used to really like Ariel back in the day, but I don't think it's all it's cracked up to be these days.
PRODUCT: Ariel Washing Liquid With A Touch Of Febreze 120 Washes (3 x 2L pack)

REVIEW_TITLE: Wear with pride. The ultimate in a comfortable, well fitting and unobtrusive 'sensible' bra.
REVIEW:
Wow! This is quite a bra.
Had to wait a while as it came from N.J. in America... "Look!" I'd said to my OH. "New Jersey!"
"Really?," he said. "Thought it was New Bra."
It's certainly a sturdy bra. Fits like a glove. But.... and here's the thing. It's a strong bra, so if you're between sizes, go for the next size up as the under band might be a bit tight, it's important to measure yourself under your boobs accurately. Ordinary bras are a bit more forgiving. Cup sizing is perfect. Strong, properly padded straps are really comfortable, don't slip. There is some leeway for adjustment, but not enough for bouncing around, and is unobtrusive under tops and tees.
Full coverage keeps everything safely gathered in while giving uplift and shape. Wide side panels that stretch, but keep you well supported.
Four hook and eye fastenings at the back in three positions for maximum comfort. Good, wide band under the bust, really comfortable, no ride-up, but for maximum comfort you'll need to have measured properly.
The construction is polyester, with some nylon, some spandex, interlined with cotton in the banding. Beautifully made. Big, fully supportive and comfortable, but very light to wear. Hand wash, hang up to dry.
This is a big, beautiful bra. Bridget Jones would go crazy for this. Buy it and wear it with your granny pants. Steal the show.
PRODUCT: Playtex 18 Hour Women`s Original Comfort Strap Wirefree Bra - Best-Seller

REVIEW_TITLE: Rich, full flavoured and well balanced blend. Can't believe it's Decaf too.
REVIEW:
This blend of different Arabica beans makes delicious coffee, and it's been decaffeinated without chemicals, so I can drink it all day without getting wired. Made in an Aeropress it's almost as quick as a cup of instant, but it's light years better. Lovely, rich, intense coffee, no bitterness, very low acidity. I do mine espresso strength, topped off with hot water and a splosh of frothed milk. Done in a minute.
The decaffeinated processing hasn't taken anything away from the flavour of the coffee, really good tasting blend.
I've made this in a French Press, and it's excellent in that, so it's a pretty versatile coffee.
Grind is quite fine, like an espresso grind, but I haven't got an espresso machine, so can't comment on any crema.
I like the idea of two metal, sealed tins, one kept absolutely fresh while the other one is in use. Opened, the coffee still retains its freshness without any noticeable deterioration for about a fortnight, but I'm using this a bit faster as it's such nice coffee.
Definitely one that I'll be ordering regularly.
My OH doesn't drink caffeinated coffee, but he really likes this one, so it's nice to be able to share.
PRODUCT: Premium Decaffeinated Ground Coffee - Caf� Saula's Award Winning 100% Arabica Spanish Espresso Blend 500g (2x 250g)

REVIEW_TITLE: Unusual, original and different way of telling someone you love them.
REVIEW:
I was looking for something a bit different for my OH as it's our anniversary coming up and this is ideal.
For starters, the card is a really good presentation quality, inside a glossy board outer envelope.
Open it, take out the card, and there's a smaller, folded tag inside for your message. Tucked into the pocketed right hand side of the card is an 80g slab (postcard sized) of Belgian chocolate, slightly thicker than chocolate Neapolitans with the message. It's all clearly printed in an edible food dye and sealed in a cellophane wrap. It's all been beautifully done and well packed to protect the chocolate message.
Wording is suitably sentimental, but without being slushy, so he might well get another one next February for Valentines.
I make an effort to find him something nice. He gives me the same card every year, and secretly retrieves it to give it to me again the following year. He thinks I don't know.
No chance of me doing the same thing with this card - he'll have scoffed it by the end of the day.
UPDATE: Well, he ate the chocolate when I was at work so I didn't get to share any... when I asked him what the chocolate was like (for the purposes of this review), he said, and I quote, "Well, it wasn't all that nice, actually. It was okay, but not as nice as some of the stuff we've had."
Note to self. Find a similar card with Laxative chocolate next time.
PRODUCT: Love is not finding someone to live with, it's finding someone you can't live without - Chocolate Card (80g)

REVIEW_TITLE: Good way to sample Monty B's decadent, luxurious chocolate truffle varieties.
REVIEW:
These "Pick and Mix" Monty Bojangles chocolate truffles didn't arrive in a fancy package, but simply bubble wrapped in a plain cardboard box outer, protecting a ribboned cellophane bag containing 49 individually wrapped chocolate truffles. Each coloured wrap denotes the flavour of the truffle inside.
If you're looking for gift packaging in the branded boxes, that's not how these are packed.
This is a good selection of the different flavours of MB's truffles, and they're all really high quality chocolates, very rich and decadent. I like these better than Thorntons, although it hurts me to say that.
Each individually wrapped truffle flavour is roughly cylinder shaped, about an inch tall and weighs around 7 - 10g. Just the right size for a choccy hit.
Buying Monty B's truffles like this is a slightly less expensive way of getting these chocs, which in my opinion are some of the best on the market.
PRODUCT: MONTY BOJANGLES CHOCOLATE TRUFFLES - 7 VARIETIES (49)

REVIEW:
This cartoon card by Alison Lingley of a black Lab doing the washing up is beautifully done - the artwork is lovely and the card is printed on good quality board, measures 8.25" x 6" and blank inside. Decent envelope and cellophane wrapped.
I know someone who has a Golden Retriever who does this all the time.. I fell about when I first saw her doing the dishes but my friend didn't turn a hair, which made it even funnier. This card is a 'must have' for her - just wish I could have found one depicting a Goldie, as this illustration comes as coasters and chopping boards as well as the card. Great gift.
PRODUCT: Alison's Animals Pre Wash Dog Blank Greeting Card

REVIEW_TITLE: Middle Age Spread - To be taken with a pinch of salt.......
REVIEW:
This made me laugh when I saw it, so it was a bit of a no-brainer to buy it as a token gift for a mate of mine who enjoys the quirky humour of Simon Drew.
The pot stand isn't just funny - it's well made, too. Tough melamine surface with a robust, compressed cork backing a quarter of an inch thick, this pot stand measures 6.25" x 6.25." The melamine is resistant to temperatures of 145c, and cleans up with a wipe from a damp cloth. It's not to be immersed in water or put in a dishwasher.
Comes well packaged, so all I've got to do is to wrap it in some fancy paper.
When I've stopped giggling, that is.
PRODUCT: Custom Works - Simon Drew Pot Stand - Middle Age Spread

REVIEW_TITLE: Powerful laundry liquid without fancy pricing. Cleans more than just the washing.
REVIEW:
This biological laundry detergent is a good, concentrated one. Most laundry liquids contain 5 - 15% surfactant, this contains, surprisingly, a whopping 35% - plus the same enzyme activity to dissolve organic soiling as the much more expensive brands. This also contains the same optical brighteners.
It's got a clean fragrance, smells fresh, not of chemicals. Doesn't make much in the way of suds or lather, so fine for all types of machines, or for hand wash - but if you're hand washing anything you only need a tiny bit, because this is concentrated detergent.
It can be used as a pre wash soak for stains that have set in.
You don't need a big volume for machine wash either - for a 7kg load of dirty clothes in soft water, 35ml is plenty. If you live in a hard water area, an extra 15ml will do a good job without scum. Rinses easily.
I usually use Ariel for white cottons that I want to look absolutely spotless, and this seems to do just as good a job on a 60c wash, but then Formil from Lidls is a good detergent too.
The only real difference I can see between this and the expensive laundry detergents (apart from price) is that the expensive brands are often thicker. This isn't particularly runny, but it's not thick and gloopy, so is fine for cold wash and quick wash.
Good, all round liquid detergent - I can't say if it might be irritant to sensitive skin - being a biological detergent, it may well have some irritant properties, same as all of the enzymatic laundry liquids, but it didn't make my skin itch when I used some to scrub the kitchen floor - where, incidentally it did a really good job on the grungy tiles. And on the paintwork where the dogs come in through the back door and leave a greasy tide mark along the wall.
I felt like the woman in the Adverts, except I was grumbling about cleaning instead of smiling brightly.
I don't think there's a laundry liquid on earth that has the power to make me smile brightly.
PRODUCT: Proline Lux+ BIO Spring Linen Laundry Liquid 5 ltr 142 Washes

REVIEW_TITLE: Two Pages per Day. Big, Robust and strongly made. Good Quality.
REVIEW:
Excellent diary. Two full pages per day, lined down to the bottom of each page, with only that month and the next month laid out in a line along the footer, not grid, so nothing is taken away from the page space. Saturdays and Sundays still have two pages each.
A big, heavy diary like this has to be very strongly made, and very robust, and this one is. Strong board covers and spine, well covered, the pages are good quality, not flimsy and have been well sewn. It opens up fully without cracking or splitting anywhere, and there's a good ribbon tape acting as a page marker.
There's all the usual additions for a diary, year planner, pages for accounts, high days and holidays etc, but nothing extraneous or wasteful.
