I usually buy a cheaper A4 "two pages for each day" diary from Amazon every year, but I have had problems with getting the right type, being sent "two days to a page'' when it's been advertised as "two pages per day." Even been sent the wrong year!
So to save myself any further hassle, I got this one, as it was quite straightforward and unambiguous in being what it said it was.
I'm glad I spent the extra money, because the cost is reflected in the materials used and the robustness of this diary. It's a superior product.
It's for 2018, so I'll update on how well this Collins diary performs, but at first manhandling, it seems to be well up for all that will be expected of it.
PRODUCT: Collins A4 Desk 2018 Two Pages a Day Diary - Black

REVIEW_TITLE: Edible Birthday Card for Pampered Pooches.
REVIEW:
My dogs are spoiled rotten, they get birthday presents as well as doggy advent calendars and Christmas prezzies. So when I saw this card... well, I just had to. Even if it's only ever a one-time thing.
This edible card is 4.5" x 4.5", two pieces of parchment-thin rawhide. Red coloured rawhide strings hold the pieces together like a card,
"Happy Birthday" is punched out on the front, and is decorated with a bone shaped piece of rawhide with a coloured rawhide strip imitating a candle - all attached with another rawhide string to hold it all in place.
A black cardboard 'pillow' envelope with a cream coloured panel to write in completes the ensemble, and a slip of paper to write your greeting - so this can be posted - either to your dog via the postie, or to send through the post to another dog - a friend's dog, or to a dog whose owner you want to impress... I'm always well impressed if a friend gives me a present that's meant for my dogs.
I'd love it if I got one of these through the post for one of my mutts.
But rawhide can be tricky, so I wouldn't let one of my dogs just take this off and scoff it somewhere hidden, it'd have to be enjoyed in plain sight like pig's ears or other things that have the potential for bits to get stuck, and I wouldn't give this to a puppy or a dog that was very possessive over a food item. But for my soppy GSDs this makes a fine gift.
PRODUCT: Happy Birthday Card for Dogs made with Edible Rawhide - "Greet Me Eat Me" from Reg and Ruby (Small)

REVIEW_TITLE: Cheerful tablecloth, good colours. Cotton seersucker is a bit thin - better as a slip cloth when layering.
REVIEW:
Good, 100% cotton tablecloth in a seersucker weave. This is nicer in the hand than on the product photo - the colours are a cheerful daffodil yellow, and a warmer, more dandelion yellow in the main colour panels, intersected by a stronger, marigold stripe. There's a subtle cream running through the weft, all of which overlie a crisp white background.
What lost it a star was that the cloth is a bit thin, but it's perfectly good as a slip cloth on top of a plain cloth, either as a layered diagonal, or over a felting cloth so it won't slide around.
This light cotton shows every mark, but happily it can be washed at 60c - cool tumble or hang dry, non iron.
The cutting is accurate, and it's been decently hemmed. Great value at current price.
PRODUCT: Yellow Check Seersucker Tablecloth 50/50"

REVIEW_TITLE: Stunning occasional table. Solid wood with bags of character. Strong and well made.
REVIEW:
Strong enough to sit on, this lovely table has multiple uses and fully deserves its five star rating. Sturdy, solidly made from hardwood (Indian Rosewood) the grain in the wood shows beautiful flaming and striping. It's been given an antiqued stain and waxed for a natural, satiny lustre. Mine is a very attractive deep chestnut colour similar to antique pine. Metal banding on the corners and studding on the top of the table complements the table and gives it bags of character.
This table comes already assembled, all that needs to be done is to screw the legs into the pre-drilled holes in the corner blocks on the underside of the table. Took me two minutes as the legs already have the bolts in place.
The cylindrical, carved legs are a sturdy 11.25" tall and have a diameter of 2.75".
The table top is 17.5" x 17.5" including the chamfered edges, and the side panels have a depth of 4.5" - the wood itself is about an inch thick, so it's a sturdy, solid table. Overall height 16" approx.
There aren't any protective pads on the bottom of the legs, should be okay on most surfaces, but if you have laminate, it might be worth sticking some circular furniture protector pads on the bottom of the feet.
I'd been looking for ages for a strong little table with a bit of character that didn't cost a fortune, and this one is perfect.
PRODUCT: Mercers Furniture Indian Jali Lamp Table - Indian Rosewood, 45 x 45 cm

REVIEW_TITLE: Delicious nutty, luxury chocolate truffles, seriously chocolatey, seriously good.
REVIEW:
I love Monty B's truffles (they're like the posh cocoa dusted deluxe ones from M&S). This nutty one is a good, smooth tasting and very rich chocolate truffle with tiny pieces of toasted hazelnut which complements the chocolate beautifully.
Each box contains a foil pouch with around 25 cocoa dusted truffles inside - each chocolate is about an inch tall and an inch across and weighs 7 - 10g so just right for a choccy hit.
These are richly chocolatey - dark and not over sweet, but not bitter chocolate. The toasted hazelnut flavours the whole truffle and gives a bit of texture.
These are chocolates for grown ups in a funky box. Two or three pieces are just enough for a good, chocolate hit without overdoing it. They're a real treat.
Bought in October, these have a long shelf life until June 2018, but this twin pack of truffles hasn't got a snowflake's chance in hell of getting past Christmas. In fact, I'll be lucky if they last till next week.
PRODUCT: Monty Bojangles Scrumple Nutty Cocoa Dusted Truffle Gift 200g x 2

REVIEW_TITLE: Good, strong Old Fashioned quality tea towel made from Linen/Cotton mix. Will last for years.
REVIEW:
Excellent quality tea towel. Made from 55% linen, 45% cotton, it's been well made and the fabric is weighty and hard wearing.
It measures 29" long, 19.5" wide.
All edges strongly hemmed and properly sewn. Strong hanging loop.
Illustrations are clearly printed, strong colours.
This is deffo a tea towel that Daffy Tottering would be delighted to put her name to.
One of the best, it's funny, quirky and a brilliant gift for a Tottering fan and dog owner.
Excellent value, robust and will last for years.
PRODUCT: Tottering By Gently Tea Towel - Dog Rules

REVIEW_TITLE: Inexpensive, lightweight polyester tablecloth - perfect for layering. Resists spills.
REVIEW:
Got the green gingham 36" square as a diagonal overlay on top of an existing tablecloth - I like the layered look, and this looks very pretty.
Faults? Well, the polyester fabric is a bit fine, - think 'headscarf' or lawn handkerchief - and if it's overlaying a bare table or another polyester tablecloth, it will slide about. It sits better on cotton or damask where there's some fibres to anchor it.
I don't think it's heavy enough or substantial enough as a stand alone tablecloth unless it's going on top of one of those non-slip table protectors.
Good bits? Its not as dazzling green as in the product photo, green is paler, more subtle, less busy. It's been well cut, and the edges are well sewn.
The other thing I like is that this polyester is resistant to spills and washes up spotless on a 40c wash, doesn't need ironing.
Is it alright to confess that as I was putting this cloth on, I accidentally knocked over a coffee mug and the dregs went all over this cloth?
The coffee just stood in puddles on the cloth and I was able to flick them off quick. Didn't sink in or leave a mark. Phew.
PRODUCT: Gingham Check Square Tablecloth Dining Room or Kitchen Table Linen 36" x 36" (Green)

REVIEW_TITLE: Basic chocolate truffles. No massive chocolate 'hit' but they're decent loose chocs with no frills.
REVIEW:
These are three star, no frills chocolate truffles - the chocolate shell enrobing the soft, milk chocolate and caramel truffle middle is a bit over-sweet and isn't of the quality of, say, Thorntons, - it tastes a bit like Mars chocolate.
The truffle middle isn't liquidy, but it is very soft, and has a rich, unctuous mouth feel. Very nice and velvety, like a proper chocolate truffle should be.
For under twenty quid for chocolate truffles weighing 1kg and giving you over sixty chocs, this product represents fair value for money.
I got these to stash away for Christmas, but me and the OH have already broken into the box to give them a trial run as it said "orange parfait' on the small label on the box and we didn't want them for Christmas if they were the wrong ones as neither of us are keen on orange flavoured chocolate. But it was just the label.
The packaging is a straightforward, plain cardboard box with two layers of chocs straggling along flimsy inserts. But that's fine for us, it's the chocolate we're after, not fancy packaging. The BB date said 200/2018. Not sure what the 200 meant, but the chocs should see us through Xmas.
If you're a chocolate connoisseur, then you'll probably be better off paying a lot more and going up-market, as these are basic chocolates.
That doesn't mean they're not nice, they are. They don't have the chocolate 'hit' of Monty Bojangles, but they're cheap and cheerful.
PRODUCT: Loose Chocolates - A kilogram box of 'Melissa' a runny centred caramel and milk chocolate truffle.

REVIEW_TITLE: Perhaps not quite so Comforting as first appears.
REVIEW:
I usually use Lenor, but when I spotted this Comfort at a good price I got it.
It's got a pleasant fragrance - a citrusy bergamot, but it doesn't stay in the clothes long with drying - the super concentrated ones win out hands down for lasting fragrance here.
This isn't a concentrated fabric softener - with this one, they recommend 140ml for a 6-7kg load. This 5litre bottle will do 45 washes.
With standard Comfort, the recommended dose is 55ml for a 6-7kg load, and a 1.5litre bottle will do 42 washes.
With the Lenor the recommended dose is 35ml for a 6-7kg load, and a 1.9litre bottle of Lenor 4X will do 76 washes.
This 5litre bottle at current prices works out about two quid a litre, so it's not quite the bargain it first appears as the other, stronger conditioners are around the same price per litre and do twice as much.
Having said that, I tend to use far too much conditioner anyway - I'll fill up the fabric conditioner dispenser drawer in the washing machine regardless of recommended dosage, and my machine's fabric conditioner drawer takes 100ml, so by using this Comfort, I'm probably being a lot less wasteful.
PRODUCT: Comfort Fabric Softener Sunshine 5LT Litres Professional Brand New Formula (Packaging may vary)

REVIEW_TITLE: Washes amazingly well on a 40c, non iron. Improves with laundering. Well made and excellent value.
REVIEW:
Very closely woven polyester yarn is what helps give this tablecloth its spill repellent properties, and it washes really well. I usually buy cotton or polycotton tablecloths, but it's hard to get greasy marks out, even with a pre-soak. This one will go in on a 40c wash, even quite mucky and it comes out spotless. It doesn't crease up, so I only have to show it a cool iron - I could easily get away without ironing it at all.
This is a good colour - described as Sage green, I'd argue it doesn't have enough blue in it for Sage, it's more like an olive green.
It isn't a shiny polyester thank heaven, although it has a Satin Stripe in the weave which is.
The material does look initially quite fine, but the fibres get softer and thicken up a bit with washing, so it improves the look, handle and feel.
This cloth has been well cut, nice and straight, and the hemming is well done, secure and perfectly straight.
Very decent tablecloth for the money and I'll get more of these now my old cotton ones have got a bit past it.
PRODUCT: VEEYOO 152 x 213 cm Striped Rectangular Oblong Polyester Waterproof Spill proof Tablecloth for Restaurant Kitchen Dining Party Decor, Sage Green

REVIEW_TITLE: Another seasonal vignette from Daffy Tottering.
REVIEW:
I love the satire of Annie Tempest's Tottering-By-Gently characters - Daffy Tottering has a quirkily pragmatic view on life and a superb sense of irony - the sketches and cartoons make me chuckle and there's always something to identify with - it doesn't matter if you're a titled, landed aristo or a peasant, the social commentary is pretty much a world view. I identify with Daffy, if only for the quilted green jacket and muddy wellies we both seem to live in and that we can both laugh at ourselves.
So here she is, in Christmas Card form. Still wearing her green quilted jacket with a dog or two under her feet and having overdone it again.
This set of five cards (with wine coloured envelopes) will appeal to the Daffys that all of us know, as much as established Tottering fans.
PRODUCT: Humorous Christmas Cards (PHB1109) Drunk Too Much - Tottering-By-Gently - Pack of 5 Cards and Envelopes - In Aid of Combined Charities Christmas Cards Association representing over fifty medical research, hospice and children's charities.

REVIEW_TITLE: Beautiful artwork on high quality board. Much more than just a 'greetings' card.
REVIEW:
Lovely set of eight cards on high quality board, each measuring 6.25" square, with white envelopes in a strong cellophane pack. 50p per pack donated to the Stroke Association.
Artwork on these is by S.R.Badmin - snowy winter fields, woods and distant images of people tobogganing down a snowy hillside. but the magic in the imagery is in the cold, blue outlines of billowing clouds and timeless landscape. I particularly love the depiction of the wary hare in the bottom left hand corner, the starkness of the dormant, snow laden treescape, softened by shadows and light, and the almost Lowry-esque late arrivals to the afternoon's fun.
This is a card that tells a story as much as sends a greeting.
Wording inside is a simple, secular "Season's Greetings" in gentle script.
Beautiful card, and a worthy Charity, of which there is a little more info on the back.
PRODUCT: Charity Christmas Cards (ALM1216) Tobogganing - Pack of 8 Cards - Sold in Aid of the Stroke Association

REVIEW_TITLE: Stunningly beautiful photograph printed on high quality board.
REVIEW:
These really took my eye. Beautiful photography of winter sun through pollard Ash trees, their shadows falling on frosty pasture.
Printed on high quality board with a slightly glossy sheen, a secular Winter greetings card with a simple "Seasons Greetings" in spiky script inside.
The inside isn't coated, so easy to write on. Card measures 6.25" square.
Back of the card gives another, smaller photo of the trees and some info on the Woodland Trust, who receive 50p donation from the sale of this pack of 8 cards, all of the same design, and 8 white envelopes.
The card is a slightly deeper, orangey-gold 'in the hand' than the lighter gold depicted in the product photo.
Stunning card, really stands out.
PRODUCT: Charity Christmas Cards (ALM1377) Winter Tree - Pack of 8 Cards - Sold in Aid of the Woodland Trust

REVIEW_TITLE: Discreet, comfortable to wear and stay put.
REVIEW:
These are the first In-Ear headphones I've used that have actually stayed put.
I like to use headphones when I'm listening to my Kindle so I don't disturb anybody else but got fed up with In-Ear ones which kept slipping or falling out, so I've usually used over ear headphones which are uncomfortable if I'm listening in bed.
These come with a selection of little neoprene spongy caps for the earbuds for best fit and comfort and a microfiber baggie to keep everything safe.
There is a knack of hooking the little cables over your ears, but once they're on, they stay on.
The length of the lead from the earpiece to the jack is over a metre, so enough length but not enough to get in the way or tangle up.
An adjustable rubber clasp allows you to have the separate ear leads diverging at a comfortable distance to suit your headspace.
A small slider near the earpiece allows pause or replay.
There's no leakage of sound to irritate anybody nearby, and I'm not disturbed by external noise when I've got these on.
Only lost a star because I'd have liked a bit more 'body' to the leads where they fit round the ears - they're shown on the product pic, but not on the actual product - but it didn't really matter too much as they don't tend to fall off anyway, once you've got them on.
These are a good product, discreet and comfortable to wear.
PRODUCT: AmazonBasics Sport In-Ear Headphones

REVIEW_TITLE: Well made, branded and tagged microfibre fleece bottoms. Comfortable and well sized.
REVIEW:
Fleecy, soft, warm and extremely comfortable winter PJ bottoms or lounge pants. Polyester microfiber fleece, no static or cling. These have a wide, elasticated waist with drawstring tapes for extra security and - Hooray! - two large, deep pockets in the outer seams.
Well sewn throughout.
I got the 2XL size - They come up nice and high though the waist, not skimpy. The inside leg measurement on these is 32". Outer leg measurement is 48" from waist to ankle.
These wash well (inside out) on a 40c wash. Not recommended to tumble dry, but these fleece bottoms will dry fast just hung up.
Excellent value for money.
These branded, tagged pants are presented in a decent poly bag with branded card insert and are well worthy of their 5 stars.
PRODUCT: Mens Classic Checked Polar Fleece Lounge Wear Pyjama Trouser Bottoms Sleepwear Nightwear (XXL, Red Checked)

REVIEW_TITLE: Lovely replica of a genuine antique at an affordable price.
REVIEW:
This is an absolutely cracking mantel or shelf clock. All metal construction painted in a distressed, dark charcoal grey, hooked fish is slightly paler to highlight the detailing on fins and body shape. Lots of three dimensional detail including an old fashioned reel complete with line handle.
Graceful curves and lines give a lovely, balanced look to this clock - pure Victoriana.
The antiqued, distressed clock face has roman numerals and Victorian style hour and minute hands, the clock casing is properly protected by a glass front.
The clock is 14" tall at its highest point, 10" wide, 4" deep. Weighs 500g.
Powered by 1 x AA battery at the back. There is an audible tick, but it's a soft, gentle old fashioned 'tock,' not loud or intrusive, but might not be suitable for a bedroom if the sleeper likes total silence. Perfect for a lounge, fishing room or study.
This is a gift for an angler who likes old fashioned and vintage style pieces and I know he's going to be surprised and delighted by this unusual timepiece. It's a lovely replica of a genuine antique at an affordable price. I'm really pleased I found this.
PRODUCT: Old Fashioned Vintage Retro Fishing Mantle Clock Ornament

REVIEW_TITLE: Beautifully constructed WW2 Admiralty Chart clock. Vintage inspired, clean lines.
REVIEW:
I'm delighted with this product - really unusual clock, framed 9" x 9" x 2" deep with protective glass face over a section of a WW2 Admiralty chart map covering the area of Dartmouth, Devon.
Clean lines, sturdily made, but not clonky, will hang on a wall or stand on a shelf.
Vintage inspired, the clock is powered by an AA battery. Silent running, clearly seen, contrasting hands, sweep second hand, numeral free so the fine detail on the accurate mapping isn't occluded.
Lovely bit of local interest for my guest cottage.
There's loads of others in this Coastal Clocks range, I was well made up to find several more very local to me, as well as many featuring coastlines and river estuary approaches throughout the South and South west peninsula.
These have been carefully constructed, well made and a real talking point for people interested in our Coastal heritage.
Would make a great gift too as they're presented in a gift quality box with secure wraps.
PRODUCT: DARTMOUTH Devon Nautical Sailing Chart Design WALL CLOCK, Sweeping Seconds Hand, Glazed Shadow Box Frame 23 x 23cm Coastal Clocks Ideal Gift for Him or Her

REVIEW_TITLE: Skimpy, thin, see-through polyester. Badly cut, sizing is way, way off.
REVIEW:
I was really disappointed when these finally arrived. They're horrible - not only seriously undersized, but seriously 'low rise'. These would barely cover your essentials. If I wore these and bent over, I'd straighten up to find someone had parked their bike.
These were XXXL - they're actually clinging and revealing on someone size 10-12, while at the same time being too long in the leg.
The material - I was expecting something like yoga pants from M&S or similar - is a thin, stretchy, polyester blouse-like material so flimsy you can see straight through if you hold it up to the light.
These are currently on for around the same price as decent yoga pants. Unbelievable.
Poorly made pants, substandard in all respects. I bought a couple of pairs, they took ages to arrive and the colours weren't as ordered, either.
These got my attention, but only to ensure I never, ever make the same buying error again.
They're nothing like the product pic. Dreadful.
PRODUCT: HOEREV Women's Soft Modal Slimming Lounge Pants Yoga Pants Pajama Pant

REVIEW_TITLE: Comfortable, warm fleece lounge pants and top.
REVIEW:
Bought the XXL. Inside leg on the pants part measures 32". Elasticated waist is roomy, comes up high over the waist and covers a multitude of sins. Fleece is polyester, soft, quite thick. Warm to wear and soft. Doesn't attract static.
V neck top is good, non constricting, relaxed fit, true to size. Long sleeves 28" from shoulder insert, plenty of room for upper arms and it's a good length - you won't get cold kidneys or a chilly midriff.
Not inclined to pill or to shed, didn't appear to lose colour in a 30c wash and cool tumble, didn't shrink.
Stitching is nicely done.
Doesn't look like a pair of PJs, just like casual top and bottoms, would be perfectly okay to be seen in these, you won't look like you're just about to go to bed, and these aren't just for the boys. These are really easy to wear and dead comfy.
Might not quite have the style of something from an expensive fashion house, but I'd trade fashionista for comfortista any day.
And....Bonus - it means that I can get in from a late shift, get into these and not whinge about being cold.
Because my OH says there is absolutely zero chance of the heating being put on until we've had at least three consecutive frosty nights.
But we'll see. I got these for him, but after that remark, I kept them for me, so we'll find out who crumbles first.
PRODUCT: Men's Harvey James Thermal Top, Polar Fleece Pant Pyjama Sets. (Navy) (XX-Large)

REVIEW_TITLE: Uncomplicated, leather RFID protected purse. Really well made and excellent VFM.
REVIEW:
I like Lorenz purses - for inexpensive day to day use they're really well made and good value. The colour I ordered looked like an antique saddle brown leather on the pic, but the purse that arrived is actually what I'd call ox blood, a very dark, blackish claret, good colour, I like it.
Purse has one main zipped compartment with four sections and a central zipped coin compartment. Good quality zips, all the compartments are fully lined and faultlessly stitched, no weak areas or missed bits.
Studded opening on the wallet part reveals a capacious note compartment - easily big enough for �50 notes (not that I have ever seen many), �20 and �10 without having to fold them in half, and the pocket is deep enough to tuck them right in without the edges of the notes on view.
There are three easy access pockets for cards, two concealed pockets for secrets, and a zipped pouchette. A smaller fold out windowed ID pocket with two more card slots on the reverse.
The purse is RFID protected.
I don't want a great big purse with hundreds of card slots, or loads of zipped compartments to confuse me and this one is just right.
This purse measures 5.5" long, 3.5" height, an inch thick. Everything has been strongly stitched, sturdily built of quality materials and it should last for years.
PRODUCT: Lorenz Ladies Leather Purse/ Wallet Zip Around - Colours

REVIEW_TITLE: Only useful as a stopper for bottles with an opening of less than 18mm. Most standard bottles etc are just over 18mm.
REVIEW:
This is a nice product, and a lovely idea, but you'll need to measure the diameter of your bottle mouth carefully if you want the cork to grip the inside of the bottle it's intended for - standard wine bottle mouths are three quarters of an inch (19mm diameter).
The bottom end of the cork on these measures 16mm, graduating to 18mm - the widest bit of the cork is fixed inside the wooden peg so although the stopper will sit inside a standard bottle, there won't be any grip, and it certainly won't be leakproof or airtight.
This gadget will only be useful for stoppering a bottle with an opening of under 18mm - that couple of millimetres really does make all the difference between this product being any real use, or just ending up gathering dust in the clutter drawer.
It's a shame the makers couldn't use a cork the next size up, then it'd be great for stoppering wine, oils or vinegars and it'd probably be a five star product.
PRODUCT: OLIVE WOOD CORK BOTTLE STOPPER by Mastro Leonardo - Handmade in Italy (Set of 2)

REVIEW_TITLE: Attractive, decorative, Vintage style metal jugs.
REVIEW:
Very attractive vintage look metal jugs with a decorative, sealed coating which resembles distressed enamelling - the coat seems to be a plasticised compound skin which has been bonded on. The metal base is a light alloy which resembles zinc.
I bought one of each of these jugs - I like the Chair one and the Bike one best - the illustrations are nicely done and look quite authentic - I thought the Birdcage one looked a bit more wishy washy.
I wouldn't expect these to hold any water - I think they'll deteriorate and rust out too fast - these are meant to be kept out of direct sunlight and to be kept dry to preserve their decorative looks.
The body of the jug is 7" tall, top opening is 3.25" diameter (base of jug is 5" diameter) and is absolutely fine for fresh flowers if you use a liner such as a suitably sized cylindrical jam jar or tumbler about 6.5" - 7" tall, with a diameter of 3". I put a fold of kitchen paper in the bottom of the jug to absorb any drips and help protect the metal.
An 'aqua bouquet' works well with these jugs - I settle an open freezer bag into the jug, add a bit of water, arrange the stems of the flowers into the poly bag, tie the neck of the bag round the stems with raffia to cover up any plastic that might show and top up the bag with water through the centre of the arrangement. Saves faffing about looking for a vase or jar the right size and shape and looks really pretty if you can conceal the freezer bag with a few strategically placed blooms or leafy stems.
But these jugs will hold all sorts of oddments and implements, bunches of dried flowers, etc. I try to keep mine for fresh flowers, but they're a magnet for all my clutter.
PRODUCT: Shabby Chic Jug Vintage French Antique Flea Market 3 Styles Cream Dusky Green (Bicycle)

REVIEW_TITLE: Multipurpose baggies, good size, well designed.
REVIEW:
Bought the multipack of five - small softgrip overlay panels texturise the polyester (which feels similar to good swimwear fabric), inner has a soft nap surface which affords some protection as well as a polishing cloth. Bigger than I thought, these multipurpose drawstring baggies measure 7.5" x 5" there or thereabouts, they're very light and strong, well made, no faults in the machining or the fabric.
I originally got these as keepers for my cheapo 'ready readers' specs, but they surprised me by being big enough to comfortably hold and protect some oversized sunnies and my night driving glasses that I keep in the car as well.
Drawstring baggie means that I can fix them up near to hand and don't have to grope around trying to find them while I'm driving. Bonus.
Different colourways on the baggie helps differentiate the respective contents.
These are big enough for all sorts of items you want to stash, from specs and small valuables such as watches or keys, to mobile phones and change for the car park. They're a good idea. Glad I got them.
If they get grubby, they clean up well with just a quick swizz in water and they're dry in no time.
PRODUCT: Ed Hick's Sacculi Drawstring Microfibre Sunglasses Case Bag & Glasses Pouch. Helping you Store, Find & Clean your Glasses Easily and in Style. (Pack of 5 Multi Pack- 1 Pink, 1 Red, 1 Turquoise, 1 White, 1 Rainbow)

REVIEW:
I usually get these in Sainsbury's, but I haven't seen them for ages. I like them better than trackie bottoms or joggers as they fit nicely, look light years better and they're dead comfortable to wear. Good, high waistband covers a multitude of sins, decent length, very forgiving. Light, but still warm, stretchy but not baggy. Wash and dry like a dream.
I haven't got a Marks and Sparks anywhere near where I live, but now I've found them on here I'll be back for more.
PRODUCT: marks and spencer Ladies Flat Front Straight Leg Jogger Trousers Sport Active Gym (22 Medium, Navy)

REVIEW_TITLE: Nicely made bra, well cut, good value.
REVIEW:
This is a nicely made bra - can't find any faults in this. Adjustable straps are almost an inch wide, enough stretch for comfort, but not enough to turn me into a human catapult. The band at the bottom of the bra is three quarters of an inch wide, comfortably faced on the inner surface with fleecy polyamide, as is the panel where the fastenings are. Doesn't ride up or dig in.
Side panels are stretchy, but nice and deep, so you wont get a muffin top under your arms. Don't laugh. This stuff is important!
I did wonder if the cups were going to be staunch supporters of order and shape - I don't want to knock myself out (or trip myself up, come to that) - and if you think that's all "just too much information," well, you're either beautifully put together, or not yet matronly enough to warrant needing an 'over the shoulder boulder holder.'
Happily, these cups are supportively cut and stitched - and the bra is comfortable to wear.
Mine didn't have any washing instructions as the labels had been removed, but it's been through the machine a few times on a 40c and hasn't fallen apart. It's a good bra. You don't have to be a granny to like comfort and I've never been a fan of underwired underwear.
PRODUCT: Ex Store Non-Wired Full Cup Total Support Bra Black 44 B

REVIEW_TITLE: Well made set of five retractable tape measures. A pleasure to use.
REVIEW:
This pack of five retractable tape measures currently represents excellent value for money and the measures themselves are of decent quality.
Measuring 2" diameter, 0.5" deep, the housing has a central push button for retracting the tape.
There is a ratchet on the internal mechanism which allows you to pull out tape in an easy, but controllable way, and the central spring ensures a swift return. Releasing the retract button halts the tape.
Tape is 60" long, made from soft, flexible plastic. Tape is quarter of an inch wide. Clear markings show inches (with divisions of sixteenths), Centimeters (with mm divisions) on the other side.
Tape end tag is plastic, and it is very stoutly bonded on.
I have twisted, pulled and tugged at both the tape and the tape end. The tape itself remains accurate and non stretch.
The tape end has refused to be pulled off,
All five tapes are consistent in build and quality. Wipe clean tape and housing in a clean, neutral colour.
Good to have a set of five, because I'm always putting one down and forgetting where I left it, and all of these are good ones.
This set of five has been properly made, work well and I'm very pleased with this order.
PRODUCT: eZAKKA 60 Inch Push Button Retractable Tape Measure,5-Pack

REVIEW_TITLE: Not as intense as the darker 'Extra Brute' no 3, but still delicious in all baking, puds and Hot Choc drinks.
REVIEW:
This is very good cocoa powder and I'm using it for all sorts of baking and chocolate desserts, as well as rich, chocolatey cocoa hot drinks. It's been alkalised, so although the purists might say cocoa loses some of its antioxidant properties during the dutching process, I think it gives a better, more chocolatey hit.
This one is slightly paler in colour and less intense than the 'Extra Brute' which, regretfully, loses it a star, as I prefer the 'strength' of the darker variant, but that's just personal preference.
People who find the darker No 3 a bit too intense will probably prefer this.
As with the Extra Strong, this one mixes like a dream, dissolves quickly, cooks really well - nothing not to like.
If I'm making a Hot Chocolate with this, I just add a bit extra powder - tastes lovely, no powdery residue. Top cocoa powder. Recommended.
PRODUCT: Cacao Barry Alkalised Cocoa Powder Plein Arome 1Kg

REVIEW_TITLE: Sturdy, reliable 2 socket, 5 vertical port desktop charging station. Good safety specs. Long cable length.
REVIEW:
Good length of cable from plug to unit - measures 58" (4'10") or 147cms. Plug is a safety standard with reinforced collar; more reinforcing where it enters the non-detachable unit. Unit has a footprint of 5" x 5" with four small rubber discs on the bottom corners to stop it slipping on the desktop.
It's 2" tall at the front edge where the two sockets are, 3" at the back where the 5 usb charging ports are. Useful 0.5" channel for supporting gadgets in front of the usb ports while they're charging.
On/Off switch located adjacent to the cable - this switches the whole unit on or off. No individual On/Off switching for the sockets.
This hasn't been designed to be mounted on a wall or vertical surface.
There aren't any LED lights to indicate whether anything's on standby, only the faint blue from inside the usb ports, so it won't disturb your sleep if it's being used in a bedroom.
All safety specs as per the product description appear to be accurate, and everything works well.
I bought a very similar gadget about 18 months ago and it's been in permanent use 24/7. Never had a moment's worry with it, so I bought this one to go in a different room (my other one was 'unavailable' when I looked).
This seems to be exactly the same.
I seem to be using more and more gadgets that want charging from usb ports - I like that these are 'smart' ports, and I like that they're vertical ports - it's easier for me to put the charging leads in.
Two sockets is enough for my needs along with the ports, and this whole thing is discreet, neat and tidy.
UPDATE: This has been in constant use for the last three months. Everything is working perfectly, absolutely no probs.
PRODUCT: ISELECTOR 2 Socket Extension Lead Surge Protector with 5 USB Mains Plug Power Strip Charging Station

REVIEW_TITLE: I've had better retractables from an Xmas Cracker.
REVIEW:
60" long tape measure (soft), a quarter inch wide. Inches and marked sixteenths one side, Centimeters and mms on the other. Nice, clear markings when new. Small metal end tag - TIP: you'll probably need to secure this better before you use the tape (or suffer the consequences!) A drop of Superglue should do, or even a stitch or two. Housing is a 2" diameter case with small, central button which you press to retract the tape. The tape should pull out and stay out, until you press the retract button, but the longer the length you pull out, the more likely the internal spring is to start having a hissy about retracting. Trust me.
What's likely to happen is that the end tag flies off when you retract the tape and the tape disappears inside the housing. You can't get it out without breaking into the case, which wasn't designed to be broken into. Once you've broken into the case, retrieved your end and tried to close the case (it won't, not properly), then the coiled spring will unravel, suddenly and dramatically, because you haven't been able to put the retract button back on properly (that's come off, too, while you've been doing surgery on the case).
You wonder if it's just you being fumble fingered. Well, no. You're not fumble fingered. This housing is a piece of C**p.

REVIEW_TITLE: Helps settle and comfort anxious or stressed dogs at all life stages.
REVIEW:
I usually have a bottle of DAP on hand for stressful times for my dogs - sudden or unexpected disruptions to their daily routines; thunderstorms, car journeys, and of course fireworks night (which is more like fireworks fortnight nowadays). Some dogs don't seem to be affected at all by DAP, but many dogs, including my own, do display more settled behaviours which is why I keep a bottle around. I got this new bottle as it's coming up to fireworks. My dogs are sensitive souls. I think they probably worry about how fireworks make me react as well as hating the screeches and bangs themselves - but anxiety is anxiety, whatever the cause.
DAP for the dogs - Whisky for Maggie. Except not, as I'd probably just end up fighting the neighbours.
These bottles of spray can be a booster when used in conjunction with a DAP plug in, or they can be used on their own. The 'reassurance' pheromone contained in DAP spray is in a volatile compound which needs to evaporate before the dog can properly detect DAP, so I spray a few puffs ten minutes or so in advance - in the car before a journey, or round their bedding/denning areas (storms or disruptions) or on my clothes and a few squirts into the air when it's fireworks. The calming effect should last a good couple of hours and you don't need much - dogs can pick up on just a few molecules in the air, and that's enough.
A bottle lasts ages and has a shelf life of years if kept in its box.
Online prices can differ, so it's worth shopping around - but get it from a reputable seller on here, as fakes do occur.
PRODUCT: ADAPTIL Spray, 60ml

REVIEW: This book is a well written insight how things functioned immediately before, and straight after 11th September 2011 when the USA planned to retaliate against Al Qaeda and the taliban. The author had good access to the Bush cabinet as well as Bush himself to get good accounts of what was said, and what happened. It gives you a good taste of how running the country and planning a war can be difficult. The book is a litte short and can sometimes be light on detail, but is a good journalistic account of the time.
PRODUCT: Bush At War (Bush at War Part 1)

REVIEW_TITLE: Good all round protection with additional front screen cover
REVIEW: It took me a long while to settle on a case for my iPhone 3 and I went through a lot of cases. So when I got an iPhone 4 I was worried I would have problems with finding a case. Thankfully I got this case straight away and there have been no problems. This is a snap on case where you put the iphone between the layers. The ends clip on securely and have not slipped off. There are areas on the shell which are empty for the camera/charger port/buttons etc. for easy access. The shell itself has a built in screen protector (so no more stick on layers). The shell is quite durable and the phone has survived a few drops already. I haven't found any faults. Highly recommend for a new iphone 4/4s case.
PRODUCT: Gear4 Black Ice Hard Plastic Case for iPhone 4 4S IC402

REVIEW_TITLE: Intriguing book on how separating military from civilian life has caused problems with US military power
REVIEW:
I read this book as I had nothing to do during the holiday - however I do recommend reading this as it has an interesting central idea: namely that the US has been moving to separate civilian life from 'martial life' which has caused problems in a wider range of US politics. Without going into too much detail it spends a bit of time coming from the US constitution how all wars should be fought with civilians to allow the people to know what they are fighting for (loosely paraphrased). It spends a bit of time showing how various legal manoeuvres have ensured that civilians are not involved in understanding what the military does any more so that they are not involved in what is presented as major policy issues.
It gives a summary of why this has happened, and it shows the rise of private military contractors. The methods that successive US presidents have used to unilaterally declare war, or even what it sounds like illegally or clandestinely conduct 'wars' is quite scary. The descriptions of the private contractors as worrying suggesting that the US can "outsource" the war without taking responsibility, and there is sections suggesting that these contractors are immune from laws, and seem to not actively help the military but also contribute to sexual slavery if not outright paedophilia.
I'm not sure what the only other current review that is 1 star is on about because it doesn't even seem to review the central thesis of this book. I would state that it is better to actually read the book (lend it from a library if you need to) than fall into the right wing/left wing trap.
The argument seems to be well written down, and seems to suggest that the US needs to connect their people again with the idea of war so that wars are waged for the right reasons and everyone is behind it rather than paying mercenaries to wage war by proxy.
I highly recommend this interesting book to read. It is at least thought provoking even if you do not agree with its idea.
PRODUCT: Drift: The Unmooring of American Military Power

REVIEW_TITLE: Great Networked Attached Storage - extendable and useful
REVIEW:
The Synology DS212J is a great network attached storage unit (NAS). To actually review this I have to explain a few things, especially as the differences between the types of NAS are quite difficult to see.
What is a network attached storage unit - It means that instead of having a hard disk you can plug into the computer to save or backup documents, you plug it into the network so it can be accessed from any computer on your network. When I say network this is useful into your wifi router.
Why do this? - It means that you can share files between computers easily. Also with modern computers you can automatically set them up to backup to the hard disk in the NAS
Why the Synology NAS? - Because it seemed to be the best reviewed on amazon, the register etc. on looking at reviews (which you can also see on synology's website). Another recommended manufacturer was QNAP. Another reason was that I didn't trust the hard disk manufacturer's offerings that you can get through PC world etc. after having bad experiences with some of their products. Also the machine runs it own mini-operating system so you can load in additional packages to extend the basic functionality to do things like backup, run your own website, run your own email server, stream music and video to your tv, share photos, as well as making your own 'cloud' (like dropbox or google drive) that you can access your data from anywhere
What's the difference between the different NAS types from synology? - i write this as it took me a long time to understand the model numbers for synology. The last 2 numbers are the year it was made, and the number in front of this is how many spare hard drive bays there are to fill - so 212 means that it is the 2012 model with 2 bays. Apart from this models are termed with no suffix, with a plus ("+") to indicate a more powerful model, or "J" to indicate a more consumer focused model
So it comes with a hard disk? - You can buy it with hard disks but I bought the basic roughly �160 model with no hard disk as I had a spare 1TB hard disk. You need to have (I think) a serial ATA type of disk. But you can put in as much hard disk as you can afford. It means that I also have a spare bay to add more capacity later
What can it do? - I haven't done very much with this yet. I have done basic backup, file sharing, and got it to stream things to my computer, and to the playstation 3. You can easily set it up so that any video on the disk can be streamed to 'DLNA' compatible machines so that you can see it anywhere in the house. Since smart TVs can do this it means you can view your videos etc anywhere. I have also moved data from an old hard disk via the usb port on the synology onto the machine itself
What pitfalls are there? - You need to have a slight bit of elbow grease to get things going to actually click the hard disk in place, and then to set it up. The one thing that I need to share is that whilst the machine works well in itself, sometimes spending too long accessing the machine via the web interface seems on my machine (maybe I am unlucky) to make it crash, however accessing it other ways the machine is stable. Once it is set up it chugs along fine.
What do you still need to do? - I need to set up the backup so that I can use my mac's time macine function to backup data to the machine. Also there are approved applications for the machine which you can get from synology to do other things but I think i'll try them slowly in the future.
Should I get one? - if you want to backup data properly this is great, although you should also keep off site data if you truly want to keep all those memories safe. there is a bit of an upfront expense in getting this but I certainly recommend it. you even keep control of your own data rather than putting it on some of the online sharing sites
I will try and update this as things go by

REVIEW_TITLE: 4th Edition - good update to great handbook
REVIEW: The new 4th edition of the Oxford Handbook of Emergency Medicine (Oxford Medical Handbooks) is a great update for anyone working in an emergency department. The book is an update to the old books, but contains updated protocols. It is not the most comprehensive book, but then again it does not claim to be so as it is a handbook. It contains all the basics and is still in the same small format. I cannot find any fault with the book. Recommend
PRODUCT: Oxford Handbook of Emergency Medicine 4/e (Flexicover) (Oxford Medical Handbooks)

REVIEW_TITLE: Warts and all history of the papacy
REVIEW: I have to say as a general interest history book this is quite fantastic. The book is a history of the papacy from the earliest recorded times. It actually deals with how the papacy was actually formed and the power and money struggles as well as the intrigues of how everything worked. It was quite an eye opener in how the early papacy wasn't really "holy" and how a lot of things were done for money. Some of the really shocking tales are of the selling of indulgences, and the massacres of the Cathar population. The book is quite easily readable and will take a week or two reading chapter by chapter. Overall quite a nice easy reading book for general knowledge. Recommend!
PRODUCT: Absolute Monarchs: A History of the Papacy

REVIEW_TITLE: Great story on how common sense isn't actually true and using statistics to succeed at baseball
REVIEW:
The title says it all. The book is a story of how statistics was used in baseball to try and succeed in the game. It defies the "old conventional wisdom" on what makes baseball success, and on what people used to look for, and then explains what actual measures in baseball actually lead to success. The book is highly recommended by many and I was interested on what it actually said.
Boiling it down it is a story of how many old style baseball managers and fans have outdated views of what makes success, and how by measuring individual players movements and comparing them to how often they win, the manager made a team which beat the odds. By essentially buying low and selling high the manager managed to gain the team success over the course of a few seasons.
The book does have an interesting parallel to football in the UK as money here does seem to buy success as in the USA. The book is a great supporter of using performance measures to make the best team, however in the end it does seem to state that you can beat the odds over a long season but in individual games luck does seem to play a part.
Overall it is a very interesting read, albeit I had to look up some of the baseball terminology every now and again. Highly recommend.
PRODUCT: Moneyball: The Art of Winning an Unfair Game

REVIEW_TITLE: Okay story for Tom Clancy fans but quite stagnant plot otherwise
REVIEW: I do like Tom Clancy however I just feel that while there is no major change to his writing, the whole "story-world" that he creates is stagnating. The book seems like an obsessives guide to current military equipment and there is nothing really outstanding about the book. He does try and bring current politics into the book again to frame why the story as it is. Again the story seems to be one of a secret US spy agency trying to prevent further middle east terrorism. It is not a bad book and for fans of the genre it will be a good read, however if you are not interested into this genre I would avoid.
PRODUCT: Locked On (Jack Ryan Jr Book 3)

REVIEW_TITLE: Sobering autobiography of an underrated wrestler
REVIEW: Walking a Golden Mile is a great autobiography. It gives you a good insight into the life and career of 'William Regal', but also delves into the background of pro-wrestling and what it took for him to get to the top. This also has a good insight into the horrors of drug abuse that he faced, and why he hasn't quite lived up to his potential. I always wondered why this guy hadn't been given such a prominent role and this book does reveal what had happened, but how he has also had lucky breaks. A good read for fans of this wrestler.
PRODUCT: Walking a Golden Mile

REVIEW_TITLE: Only worth buying for multiplayer; wait or rent for average singleplayer
REVIEW:
It's very difficult to review this game - to get a feel you must have played Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (PS3). There has been so much hype around this game, but to summarise it is a sequel to Modern Warfare 2 with a follow-on story and slightly different graphics. It plays the same, which is no bad thing as MW2 was an excellent first person shooter. The problem however is that the single player whilst wrapping up the storyline is atrocious in its length - it can be completed in less than 5 hours easily. There doesn't seem to be the same challenge as in the previous game. The good thing is that there are further "special ops" missions which can be played with a friend on the same machine which makes the game a bit more fun although again it doesn't have the same challenge as MW2's special ops missions. However compared to MW2 I feel that it just doesn't have the same length or fun on single player. This certainly isn't a bad game, and although I've rated it an average 3 stars, this is mostly for the short length of the singleplayer. MW2 set the bar so high this doesn't reach it. However it is better than Call of Duty: Black Ops (PS3). Versus other FPS games this is actually a very very good game. I can't compare it to Battlefield as I haven't played it.
I can't say that much about the multiplayer as I don't have time to put in big sessions. It doesn't seem much different from MW2. However multiplayer is only for those that have time to put into it as all the bonuses come with gaining experience from playing, so its not great for new or casual players.
I would say if you are wanting this for single player only I would wait for the price to drop or to rent it. I'm only going to put a few more days into my copy and then trade it for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (PS3) which seems it would be a longer challenge.
PRODUCT: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 (PS3)

REVIEW_TITLE: Essential beginners book for anaesthetic trainees
REVIEW: A short review, this book is essential bedside book for anaesthetic trainees. It won't give you the background basic sciences, but it covers all the important clinical topics that you will need on a day to day basis. The handbook itself is quite a thick book so is not as 'pocket sized' as say the Oxford Handbook of Clinical Medicine. However there is great value in this book as a basic primer, but be sure to get other books to back up all this knowledge. Also be aware there are phone versions of this book to allow you to carry it on the go. Recommended!
PRODUCT: Oxford Handbook of Anaesthesia (Oxford Medical Handbooks)

REVIEW_TITLE: Promising title but overall package is just average
REVIEW: Looking at everything in the description this CD was quite promising - a combination of video game music performed by an orchestra. I can't doubt the musical excellence here but I just feel the overall concept falls a bit flat. While this may work as a live orchestra piece, I just can't see this being something I would pop into a CD player on a whim. The music selection is up for debate, but certainly has some of the best musical pieces from video games. It is translated well into orchestra format, but I just feel there is no joy for me listening to video game music without the video game. Combined with this the premise of different video game's music has the whole CD sound a bit disjointed. Some of the selections just stand out as probably not suited to an orchestra, whereas others were more written for an orchestra originally. I can't criticise this musically, but whilst the premise was good I think in reality it just is not suited to be replayed on CD.
PRODUCT: The Greatest Video Game Music

REVIEW_TITLE: Not a bad film but if you've seen the first Hangover you've seen this
REVIEW: The Hangover Part II isn't a bad film by any means. Building on the success of the first film this is a film about another stag-do with the same cast. However the plot of the film is pretty much the same as the first one, just in a new location. The film itself isn't that bad, and it is eminently watchable, but my warning is don't get your hopes up for much new. Recommend only to people who liked the first hangover.
PRODUCT: The Hangover Part II - Triple Play (Blu-ray + DVD + Digital Copy) [2011] [Region Free]

REVIEW_TITLE: It is laugh out loud only if you're not easily offended
REVIEW: After watching a lot of Frankie Boyle material I though I'd read his book. It actually is quite laugh out loud funny at points, and is actually an autobiography of sorts, mashed in with random diversion in his story. It actually feels quite rambling at times. The book is quite offensive so I would only read it if you can stomach his brand of comedy. Why 3 stars? It is quite rambling and I don't know if I'd have read it or even finished it if I didn't like his comedy. On the plus side I read it start to finish (an achievement for me!) plus at times it was actually laugh out loud!
PRODUCT: My Shit Life So Far

REVIEW_TITLE: Easy to set up, good music streaming but a bit pricey
REVIEW:
After buying the Apple Airport Express router I have to say I am quite pleased with my purchase. I bought this as a replacement for a old router, but the main aim was to get something that would be easy to set up and maintain. Looking at other router reviews this seemed to be a problem - you can get a �20 router but this probably would not suit.
The Airport Express router is a fantastic bit of kit. It is easy to set up, although it uses custom software instead of a web based interface. It easily connects to a network and the signal is fantastic. On top of this the router is small. The audio out port works with itunes well and gives good quality sound. I can't comment on the printer functionality as I have not used it.
I highly recommend this as a replacement router. It is a bit pricey but for the ease of use and set up it is excellent.
PRODUCT: AirPort Express Base Station w/ AirTunes (802.11n)

REVIEW_TITLE: Novel viewpoint of zombies, as well as a good futurist geopolitical exploration
REVIEW: I picked this up after hearing of the filming of World War Z in the UK. Reading this book is very interesting not really taking one single viewpoint. It makes a decision to make a book on zombies as a fictional 'report' of people's experience. The viewpoints are fairly short, but overall give you a good overall view of the story. In the book whilst the zombies are the background, the more interesting parts are the background geo-political context of the wold. I have reservations how they can make this into a movie, but the book itself is quite readable.
PRODUCT: World War Z

REVIEW: I have to heartily recommend this case. The case is a hard shell with a leather covering. It provides excellent protection especially if you're prone to dropping phones. This is in fact my 2nd Elan Form case, the first one with the leather peeling off. The case comes with a screen wipe cloth and a plastic screen protector. For �[] I highly recommend this case.
PRODUCT: Griffin Elan Form with Easy Dock for iPhone 3G -Black

REVIEW_TITLE: Secure and spacious bag for touring
REVIEW:
Pacsafe's products are quite niche, but very useful, in that they have a set of security travel products useful for those going to places with pickpockets etc. My first introduction to pacsafe was years ago with moneybelts with slash-proof features.
The VentureSafe 150 is a more spacious bag. It is a cross-body rucksack that can be worn face forward, or face-backward (i.e. like a normal rucksack). Face-forward allows you to see where it is at all times. It is quite spacious and carry a reasonable number of items securely at the same time (e.g. phone + wallet + digital camera + passports + guidebooks). The security part comes with the slash-proof belt and material to make the pack itself. Further features include a second compartment within the main compartment to hold back-up items (e.g.passport, credit cards). The design also has the zips of the main compartments fitted in a locking fashion so that someone cannot just open the zip, they need to unlock it which is noticeable. The bag itself has 3 zipped area accessible from the outside. It is also quite comfortable to wear.
The downside is that this is quite expensive. However for the safety features and to prevent losing money etc. in tourist areas I would mention that it is worth it. It is also lighter than a traditional rucksack, but trading off space to that.
I would highly recommend this product to security conscious tourists. It might be also worth looking at PacSafe's website to see if there are other products which can help with secure travel.
PRODUCT: Pacsafe Venturesafe Cross Body Pack - Black

REVIEW_TITLE: Good read with typical James May humour (though might not have anything useful to teach)
REVIEW:
My review is of the audio version of the book How to Land an A330 Airbus: And Other Vital Skills for the Modern Man. It's the full version of the book read out by James May himself.
The book is quite hilarious pretending to be a to-do manual of things men should know how to do, except with esoteric subjects. In truth nobody will ever need to do any of these, but James May presents it in a light hearted but quite informative way, talking around the subjects. The only chapter I missed is one regarding eating your dead friend, but I just couldn't bring myself to listen to that, other people might find it funny.
This will appeal to James May fans, as well as people who want a quick light hearted read. It doesn't teach you useful skills. The audio version is quite pleasant to listen to on a card drive. Recommended.
PRODUCT: How to Land an A330 Airbus: And Other Vital Skills for the Modern Man

REVIEW_TITLE: Good clinical reference for MCEM part C
REVIEW: It has been difficult to get books that specifically have been written for the College of Emergency Medicine MCEM exams. This book has been specifically written for MCEM part C, and it provides sample marking schedules for stations, as well as suggestions for possible clinical scenarios. It is full of tips for the exam. Highly recommended!
PRODUCT: Mastering Emergency Medicine: A Practical Guide: A Comprehensive Guide for MCEM

REVIEW_TITLE: Short introduction, but less information than a wikipedia article
REVIEW: This book is a more short introduction to World War II, and very superficial details behind it. I suspect this is more of a primer for teenagers who can then jump off and read more into World War II. However you could probably get more information from the Wikipedia article than this. It reads well, and is free, but you can get much better information elsewhere.
PRODUCT: World War II 101: The TextVook

REVIEW_TITLE: One of the funniest British films made
REVIEW: The Carry On films are like marmite - you either love them or hate them, in their bawdy humorous kind of way. This is one of the best Carry On films produced and stars most of the usual carry on team on a trip to an island holiday, parodying the typical Spanish jet set holiday you could get. The comedy does come think and fast in various set pieces. Some of the scenes are actually so full of double entendres you may actually miss them the first time you watch this. Whilst having quite understated British sexualised humour, it is never overt as in many films made recently (evidenced by the fact that you can see these films sometimes during the day on television). The film is funny enough to be seen on multiple occasions. I would highly recommend getting this DVD.
PRODUCT: Carry On Abroad [DVD] [1972]

REVIEW_TITLE: Good airplane book: if you only have '59 seconds' just read the conclusion
REVIEW:
You can interpret my review on how you want to approach this book. If like me you are reading this out of general interest, and on a place, you can get through this in a few hours, and it's a good read on the topic of how to change your situation quickly. The chapters have a lot of background to the message, and have exercises to do to help you.
If you really want a self help book, this is probably not it as it will not provided the depth you are looking for, and if you want quick fixes the best if just to turn to the conclusion and read that only.
Overall this is a good book if you're travelling and for general interest only.
PRODUCT: 59 Seconds: Think a little, change a lot

REVIEW_TITLE: For guys as well - useful on planes/travelling
REVIEW: This mini atomiser is an amazing aid for travelling around. It can refill itself from any aftershave which has a removable pump head and there are instructions around on the web on the best way to wash it out if you want to change aftershaves or perfumes. The best thing is the ability to take it anywhere, and not relying on the miniature aftershaves you can get. The atomiser itself can easily be taken on a plane. One of the best features is the 'window' on the side which allows you to see how much is left. All in all this is a fantastic bit of travelling kit for guys and gals. Recommended.

REVIEW_TITLE: Worthwhile read on the use of checklists and teamwork in healthcare
REVIEW: Atul Gawande presents a short, but interesting, account on how he developed and promoted the use of checklists in healthcare. He compares modern healthcare to complex systems where individuals cannot know enough and be relied on to do everything correctly in complex situations. He has a good comparison to early Boeing planes which became so complex a checklist was developed for it. He continues with this comparison throughout the book, even going on to describe checklists and how team members relate to each other in modern airplanes, and how this was helpful in the "Miracle on the Hudson" where checklists and teamwork helped safely evacuate the plane. He also stressed that the checklist helps as an aide memoire but also as a system of promoting a safe team culture. Parts of the book are good at demonstrating how the checklist was trialled and implemented, and how checklists are also used in investment banking as well as in construction. The book is a good read in describing a way of making modern health care safer, and how difficult it is to implement. I would recommend this book for anyone interested in safety in modern medical systems.
PRODUCT: The Checklist Manifesto: How To Get Things Right

REVIEW:
I got Omar Khayyam's Rubaiyat to read on the go on my kindle - as poetry it consists of multiple 4 line verses translated from Arabic. I find this a fascinating book to see the translation and I find reading this quite relaxing. It is a window to the translation in the past as well. The poetry is accompanied by quite volumes notes on the poetry and its translation. Reading the actual poetry itself is quite relaxing.
The only downside to this is the 'print' quality. Compared to other Kindle books that I have the text (whilst amazingly readable) has a 'scanned' quality about it rather than the crisp text of other books - some people may mind this.
PRODUCT: Rub�iy�t of Omar Khayy�m (Oxford World's Classics)

REVIEW_TITLE: Good basic introduction to John Wooden's life and phiosophy
REVIEW: This is quite a good, but short, introduction to John Wooden, his life and his philosophy. The book itself is more of a springboard to reading other books on John Wooden, or perhaps interesting someone else in exploring the full history behind this book. It does contain some interesting quotes. It is a very quick book to read, taking about 15 minutes. As a free book, I highly recommend it, although if I had to pay for it this would not be a good book at all.
PRODUCT: John Wooden's Winning Ways (Insights From Great Business Minds)

REVIEW_TITLE: Best espresso system for the home - excellent machine
REVIEW:
I got this machine as a coffee (or more accurately) espresso machine for my house. I was fed up with the 'barista' type machines with the steam nozzles for making cappucinos as they were difficult to use and to clean, and in my house would not be used due to the time consumed in using them. Nespresso has created an excellent system of making a quick, proper coffee.
The coffee is much better than instant. However the capsules needed for the machine are slightly expensive (c.20-30p depending on type) however it is good coffee and you have to consider if you bought this coffee at a shop it would cost at least �1.50 if not more. Purists may also argue that using a traditional machine or one of the coffee presses might make better coffee, but I don't have the time or inclination to go down that route.
The machine is simple enough. There are two automatic buttons which you can program with the amount of coffee that you want to put in a cup. Fill the tank with water (again a much simpler system than the traditional coffee machines you can get from other shops), put in a capsule, press the button and you have a good coffee. You can make volumes from espressos to full mugs, but note that if you run water through a capsule for a second espresso it tends to be a bit weaker. If you want you can even use this as a stand in for a kettle if it's already powered up by just running water straight through.
The aerocinno mug that they give is also quite good. It is a magnetic whisk system for hot and cold milk so can make lattes or cappucinos effectively. You can even use it to whisk milk for a hot chocolate!
I chose this machine as it was the basic range of nespresso machines (i.e. also the cheapest), plus it was the automatic version (the manuals you need to hold the button down), and it came with the aerocinno accessory. There are other models which have stunning designs, and have other features, but they also come at a price - but could be more suitable for other people's requirements.
Capsules need to be ordered direct from Nespresso, but they offer to give you a speciallly designed capsule order with your first order.
Overall I love this machine. I can press a button and have a coffee waiting for me after I get out of the shower. I would recommend this machine for those who want a good coffee once a day.
PRODUCT: Nespresso by Krups XN2003AP Essenza Manual Coffee Machine Bundle With Aerocinno , Black

REVIEW_TITLE: Excellent resource for the starting anaesthetist - basics and more
REVIEW: Fundamentals of anaesthesia is an excellent resource for those starting out in anaesthesia. It is a well written book, well illustrated and divided into sensible sections detailing all that is needed to know for those starting out. Basic principles are explained well, as well as the practical concepts around these. The book also goes into the physiology, pharmacology and physics behind anaesthesia to allow one to deliver a safe anaesthetic. The book is quite long however this is not more so than other basic textbooks. For a starting point this is excellent. As a bonus there is a separate kindle edition for those on the move, although all I have read is the sample, the contents are the same.
PRODUCT: Fundamentals of Anaesthesia (Cambridge Medicine (Paperback))

REVIEW_TITLE: Excellent product for the price, wireless prints and scans on Macs
REVIEW:
I purchased my new HP Deskjet 3050 all-in-one and for the price it is amazing! Considering what separate printers and scanners used to cost, this all-in-one is cheap, and works perfectly. For my needs it is good and works with Mac OS 10.6 easily. And on top of printing wirelessly, it scans wirelessly as well. The only downside as with all printers nowadays is the ink is expensive and the cartridge type doesn't seem to have cheap re-manufactured equivalents of a re-filling kit yet (note Amazon sells the big size replacements for quite cheap).
To start off I bought this to replace another Hewlett Packard (the 720c) which would not work with my mac. I chose HP for their excellent quality, the fact that my deskjet is 11 years old (and still going strong) and that I also have a HP LaserJet, I trusted their quality. The printer comes in a fairly light box, and the machine itself is very very light compared to my old printers.
Setup for the mac was easy enough, and needed the installation of the software on the CD and the USB cable to allow communicating to the printer the wifi settings. After that everything has been working fine. I can switch the machine off at the mains and then turn it on again as needed and it remembers the settings. Printing and scanning wirelessly from Mac OS 10.6 (Snow Leopard) is easy - print as you would, and you can scan by putting a sheet in the machine, pressing a button and selecting the relevant machine to scan it to. It seems to use Apple's Bonjour (AKA ZeroConf) for scanning. The only downside is that scanning does take a long time, but the only machines that I have ever seen scan fast are business machines (i.e. the more expensive ones). Also note there is no automatic document feeder for the scanning.
Print quality is good for home use, but I don't think this machine is advertised for photos, but then again at the price it's not my main concern.
I have not tried this with a windows machine yet so cannot advise on this.
All in all this machine is great at the price, and is excellent value. If you are looking for a wireless printer-scanner I would go for this machine.
PRODUCT: HP Deskjet 3050 All-in-One Printer

REVIEW: This is a good basic pulse oximeter for daily community healthcare. The manufacturer Nonin is well known in the medical community for making higher end kit, and it is good to see that they have made a cheaper home version. The fingertip pulse oximeter is well built, only runs on one battery, and automatically functions when a finger is put in. There is a back light for dark situations as well. The machine is quite sturdy and can fit into a pocket or case. The only downside is that a case is not provided with the machine, considering the price. Another (relatively small considering what the machine does) downside is the choice of colours: blue/orange/green - sometimes you do wish for a basic black model, but the blue is quite a dark blue. The machine doesn't have the higher end waveform functions of its more expensive brethren, nor pulse oximetry tracing, however unlike what seems like the cheap/dubious import oximeters which seem to have colour screens and recorders, having reliable oximetry is the key which is why I originally went for the Nonin Go2. REVIEW:
This is a great post-apocalyptic novel from Dmitri Glukhovsky. I will confess I only read this after starting to play the game Metro 2033 (PC DVD) which is based on this book. It is a fairly standard post-apocalyptic novel with similar themes, although it has reflections and themes based on what happened on the Second World War from a Soviet/Russian perspective. The book follows a fairly young inexperienced traveller trying to save his "home" metro station from unidentified attackers - and allows him to experience what has become of Russian society after a nuclear attack. It is interesting as we can see his naive reactions to what has happened to the inhabitants of Moscow, which reflects some of the previous factions and history in Russian society.
It has been interesting as I have never read a modern Russian author before, although I cannot tell if anything or not has been missed in the translation. One thing that may be unfamiliar in this book is the use of Moscow Metro station names - it is easy to get confused with the names and being unfamiliar with them I have no way to tell if there was some underlying meaning to the use of the station names.
Overall this is a good science fiction novel and well worth reading, especially if you enjoyed the game.
