REVIEW_TITLE: A potentially great player - if you're lucky
REVIEW:
I've had two of these, the first unfortunately going into the washing machine just days after it was purchased, thus I bought a second.
It appears from reviews here and elsewhere that buying this you take pot luck. It may be fantastic and work well for years...... or you may be like me, and have nothing but trouble. First the good though:
The screen is clear and navigation is pretty easy. Files can be uploaded via Windows Explorer and the MP3 player sorts them without further intervention. Volume is okay, though if you are getting a bit long in the tooth, it could be louder when cutting the grass say. I used it principally for podcasts and audio books, for which it was well suited and automatically bookmarked your progress, which surprisingly few players do.
Now the bad. From the outset, the player would switch itself off at random, or simply freeze up. There is no re-set button, thus it is necessary to hold down the power button, sometimes for minutes at a time, until it clears itself. Attempts to upgrade the firmware failed - it appears the Sansa Firmware update is either corrupt or does not work with Win 7.
Sandisk customer services could give lessons to British Gas in obstruction and Amazon washed their hands of the issue when I tried to return it in the first few weeks. Sandisk will only respond to a warranty claim if the serial number can be quoted. Given that this is printed on top of the clip in characters less than 2mm tall, this would be a tall order for anybody with 20/20 vision; a photo of the numbers (illegible I fear) produced a response that - you've guessed it - the serial number is required.
I have spent 18 frustrating months with this thing and it has now failed completely.
It is worth noting the literally hundreds of these for sale on eBay as "manufacturer refurbished". Now call me a baboon and paint my bottom orange if I'm wrong, but I suspect that these are all returns from dissatisfied customers - presumably with better eyesight than mine - who have returned the player to Sandisk. This does suggest to me that when buying this, one is taking a gamble whether it will be a good 'un or a dodgy one. Personally, if I want to gamble, I'll go to William Hill.
I'll not be buying a third one.
PRODUCT: SanDisk SDMX18-004G-E46K Sansa Clip+ MP3 Player - 4 GB, Black

REVIEW:
I am doubtless going to offend by stating that I thought this "cult classic" a load of rubbish.
The film appears to have no storyline - it is interesting to note from another reviewer this was developed from 3 different plots, a fact which shows in the so called plot - storylines starting and then going nowhere, others starting midway without explanation. By way of example, the "claws" of the title appear early in the piece, but then disappear from the storyline, never to re-appear. A girl is driven mad - by what we do not know, but one must suspect it was reading the script - and taken to the asylum, but is not referred to thereafter, even by her (not very) distraught fiancee. The same fiancee is attached by a "phantom hand" a little later, but again, nobody thinks it worth mentioning again. As for the full frontal nudity from the unknown "star" of the film, this felt gratuitous in the extreme.
To me, this is a muddled hotch-potch of half thought out ideas. At the end of it, both my wife & I felt we had wasted an hour and a half of our lives on complete twaddle.
Doubtless die-hard fans will take umbrage and bad-mouth this review - I will await the pins into the wax effigy - but we are all entitled to have a contrary view to other reviewers, if expressed genuinely; it is a shame that another one star review was met with such hostility. How others can begin to compare this rubbish to "The Wicker Man" simply defies belief.
PRODUCT: Blood On Satan's Claw - Digitally Remastered Widescreen Edition [DVD] [1970]

REVIEW:
I first came across this book almost 30 years ago, and was gripped from the first page. I have read it many times - my original copy has had to be replaced it was so well read - and know the story well, but still return to it regularly. For me, it remains an absolute page turner, and a book I could easily read in a single sitting.
The story opens with the location of a WW2 merchant ship, the MV Cyclops, by a Royal Navy survey vessel in the natural harbour of a remote island in the south Atlantic. Records show that the ship had been reported as sunk in WW2, several hundred miles from where it rides at anchor. Furthermore, it is accompanied by a WW2 U-boat and the remains of a second WW2 merchant ship, the MV Athenian. How this came to pass, and the events of the Cyclops' last voyage are set out in the first person in the journal of John Kent, the Chief Officer of the Cyclops.
The pace is unrelenting, but not forced. The central characters are very real; they are not in control of the events that are happening to them, and the chief protagonist admits freely to being scared, for he is not the square jawed hero that so many authors of adventure fiction believe much populate the pages of their works. The reader feels for the characters and is concerned for their fate - I never find the ending an easy read, and must admit that on occasions I have felt a pricking at the corner of the eyes, such is the level of engagement one has with the characters.
As others reviewers have stated, this is a tremendous read and I cannot recommend it too highly. For me, by far the best of Brian Callison's works, and definitely one to take with me to my desert island.
PRODUCT: A Flock of Ships

REVIEW:
Like most people, I suspect, I was aware of GCHQ but before reading this absorbing account, had little idea of its remit.
The book was a complete revelation to me - not least the size of our electronic eavesdropping on friends and potential enemies alike - as well as the amount of work it carries out in the post Cold War environment. Although a heavy tome, the author has exhaustively researched his subject, using publicly available records and the result is a compelling read. Absolutely recommended to anybody with an interest in 20th century history or the way in which governments work.
PRODUCT: GCHQ

REVIEW:
I am familiar with the story of "The Man Who Never Was" from watching the film on wet Sunday afternoons as a child, compulsory viewing in a household in which WW2 was still alive, twenty years after it had ended. This book however reveals that there was far more to the story than I had previously imagined, and reads more like a work of fiction.
The central characters are surprisingly unattractive and the cast of supporting "actors" truly bizarre; the cross dressing deception chief comes particularly to mind. Many interesting facts and anecdotes arise, both before and after the body was set off the coast of Spain, and the story at times descends almost to farce, such as the local British Consul having to refuse to take control of the body on the day it was found, the increasingly desperate attempts of the British, mirrored by the local Nazis, to force the Spanish navy - which prided itself on not being in the pay of the Germans - to allow the Abwehr access to the papers and so forth.
The author admits that Operation Mincemeat was only one part of a much wider deception operation to distract German eyes from the invasion of Sicily, but nonetheless, the story is fascinating and brilliantly told by the author. Recommended.
PRODUCT: Operation Mincemeat: The True Spy Story That Changed the Course of World War II

REVIEW:
I must take a contrary review to the other reviewers and express my disappointment in this volume.
I am not a Kipling fan - I do not feel he was a great author - and purchased this volume principally having much enjoyed the film adaptation of "The Man Who Would Be King". The original, I find, was a disappointing tale, full of strange Masonic symbolism, and not the exciting tale a viewer of the film version - which follows the plot closely - would expect.
It is evident that these stories were written during Kipling's early years as a hack writer in India, churning out short stories for magazines. The stories frankly do not stand up in the modern era - some, I just found unreadable, and others impossibly antiquated. Unless you are a student of the Raj and are familiar with the Anglo-Indian language and culture of the time, this should be regarded as a curiosity only, albeit instructive that - if Kipling is to be believed and there is no reason that he should not - casual infidelity is not new and was practised widely in the Raj.
My copy will shortly be available at my local charity shop.
PRODUCT: The Best Short Stories (Wordsworth Classics)

REVIEW_TITLE: Excellent account of this forgotten war
REVIEW:
My knowledge of the Korean War has always been very limited, and like many people, mine has been slanted by the 1970s TV series MASH.
In this book, Hastings gives us a detailed yet very readable account of the origins of the war, it early prosecution and the need for the US to gain support from others to give itself the fig leaf of pretence that this was a UN operation and not the first instance of the Cold War being fought by the super powers' proxies. Considerable use is made of first hand accounts as well as archive material. It must, given the fact that it was written in 1985, be slanted towards the western experience of the war, and doubtless if written now would have the benefit of some restricted access to the Chinese record, though even now one must suspect that a truly impartial account must be difficult to produce.
A criticism has been made that the British contribution plays too large a part of the narrative. Given that the author is British, this is what the buyer should anticipate. The fact that Hastings is not afraid to criticise American prosecution of the war, together with accounts of American blunders will no doubt upset American readers, who may prefer a more partisan account. A sub text that questions why the Americans chose to support the distasteful regime in the South of a country with no strategic interest, other than in pursuit of the Truman doctrine, may also be distasteful to some, but is worthy of discussion.
A well written and clear account, typical of Hastings' output. Thoroughly recommended to the general reader.
PRODUCT: The Korean War (Pan Military Classics)

REVIEW:
Alternative or Counter-factual history is, as one of the contributors to this novel recognises, a strange beast. It is all too easy to extend the impacts of the chosen historical event far beyond reasonable bounds, as we see with the piece on Anthony & Cleopatra winning the Battle of Actium in BC 31 leading, in the writer's mind, to the Roman Empire extending into the modern day, apparently as some sort of European Federation. The problems which beset the Empire from late in the 2nd Century onwards are disregarded and the attacks on the Roman heartland early in the fifth century brushed aside in less than a sentence.
Of the essays, I thought the best that on the impacts of not dropping the atomic bombs on Japan at the end of WW2 - mass starvation of the Japanese, death of all civilian internees and POWs in Japanese hands - the most thoughtful and well argued, not asking the counter-factual crystal ball to reach too far into the future. The piece on the Louisiana Purchase is also well considered. The standard of some others however was much poorer, and in on the case of the Franco-Prussian War bizarre, the author having us believe that the US, a very minor power at that time, brow-beating Britain & France into joining an early version of NATO, against a Russian threat! Other pieces such as a theological consideration of Christ not being crucified and Martin Luther being burned as a heretic had no place, in my view, in a historical book.
The authors of these pieces - all but two of them American - are themselves chosen on an unknown basis, some being academics or professional historians, but at least two being authors of historical and other fiction and one a film producer, whose only historical background being that his father was one of those in the iconic photo of US troops on Iwo Jima. This in itself portrays another weakness, the heavy emphasis on "how would this have affected the USA" causing the writers to focus too much on historical events far in the "future". Some of the essays are themselves only of interest on the impact the events would have had on the US domestically.
This is always a difficult subject and for me, these essays generally are poorly executed and aimed too much at a US audience.
PRODUCT: More What If?: Eminent Historians Imagine What Might Have Been

REVIEW:
I first came across this work over 20 years ago when the BBC adapted this into a fast paced and exciting 90 minute play. I thus looked forward to reading the source material. Sadly, this proved once again the BBC's skill at turning turgid prose into a piece of theatre.
The premise of the novel is that Edward V and his brother Richard - the "princes in the Tower" - were not murdered by Richard III, but escaped, and Henry VIII wishes to find if they or their descendants are still alive. So far, so good. The novel opens however with almost 80 pages of semi academic discussion of the history of the previous 50 years, the whole wrapped up as a discussion between 3 or 4 of the central characters. When the narrative finally gets going, facts leading to the identity of the remaining prince are given away and the "denouement" comes as little surprise. To make it worse, having achieved satisfactory closure for the remaining prince - in a leper colony - the author then takes the character out of the living death of a leper and into a further 50 pages based upon the Pilgrimage of Grace. The author has no idea of structuring a novel.
The author is an academic who is well known to believe that Richard III was innocent of the sins history has accused him of - doubtless Jeremy Potter would have us believe Richard looked after stray kittens and helped old ladies across the road. This may or may not be true, but a novel is not the vehicle.
Having read this, it is now on its way into the bin.
PRODUCT: Trail of Blood (Panther Books)

REVIEW:
Others have expressed their views already, but I would simply add that this is an utterly compelling and magasterial work. Having been born after the period in question, I can only say "I had no idea". The Britain he paints is a tired, worn country, still to come to terms with its place in a post war world.
One of the strengths of the book is his use of source material from ordinary people, rather than relying upon the views and writings of the great & good. From the opening page, e are treated to insights we could never have known - the grumbling about VE Day and the lack of interest many indeed appeared to take in the whole affair.
It is true that the book is stuffed full of facts and at times is in danger of slipping into the academic, but this is a tremendous resource for the interested (I will not say "intelligent") general reader and is a book that bears reading again, such is its breadth and depth.
On the basis of this book, I hugely look forward to reading "Family Britain", the next in the series.
PRODUCT: Austerity Britain 1945-51

REVIEW:
Having read all four of Lisa Picard's books, this is possibly the best written, though there remains a need for some better editing; we do not need to be given the same facts more than once.
My only concern with this book is that this, as with all her books, regurgitates what she has read in her researches - my heart sank when I read "the internet" as a source in one footnote - without the professional historian's ability to critically assess and analyse. She acknowledges that some of her source material - most notably Mayhew and a self confessed Anglophobic Frenchwoman whose name I forget - was written by somebody "with an angle", but without the knowledge or skill to assess and present the material accordingly.
There is much that is of interest, but this remains "history lite", an entertaining diversion, but something for those with a deeper interest in social history. For those preferring their history "full fat" Professor Jerry White's "London In The 19th Century" is a better bet.
PRODUCT: Victorian London: The Life of a City 1840-1870

REVIEW:
This is at best a very mixed bag, comprising two novels, a novella and two short stories, all featuring some or all of the same four key characters. Frankly none of them are good, and two at least are absolute stinkers.
The first of the novels is "The Lost World", an adventure yarn from the mantle of Henty and Rider Haggard. The story is well known, but essentially a mixture of dinosaurs, prehistoric plants, ape men ("the missing link" as one character describes them) and modern man co-exist on a South American plateau the size of an English county. The scientific basis of this is thin at best, and the characters typical of their time with attitudes to match. The fact of the ape men being forced by the protagonists to become subservient to the South American Indians reflects the imperial mindset of the time. Read it as an adventure story, but do not expect great literary merit, nor a "thrilling" tale.
The Poison Belt, a novella, is a strange tale in which the Earth passes through a poisonous field in the "ether" - still a popular notion at the time this was written. The central characters are saved by breathing pure oxygen, but the occupants of the rest of the planet appears to have died; those who are regarded as "lesser" peoples "die" first, thus Australian aborigines before the whites, Slavs before Teutons, etc. This is all slightly distasteful to 21t Century tastes. Almost comical is the fact that people remain at their posts and "die" in harness, reflecting again on the attitudes of the day. The impact of being the only people left alive is not reflected upon, nor the impacts of the outcome on the world more than a trifle.
The foregoing are towers of literary genius compared to the third offering "The Land Of Mist", a 200 page peon to spiritualism - in which Doyle developed a keen interest after the death of his wife I believe - disguised as a novel. For me, this was one of the worst pieces I have ever read, and if I had been able to award a negative rating for this in isolation, would have done. If you read this collection, I earnestly suggest you save 200 pages of your life and read the Yellow Pages or something else more enlightening than this load of rubbish.
The collection ends up with two short stories. The first "The Disintegration machine" is a short 10 page piece which I took to be blackly comic. The final piece "When The World Screamed" starts of by proposing an early "Gaia" hypothesis that the planet is an organism, but then moves to the farcical by making the area below the crust some sort of sentient being. Utter rubbish.
The editor of this collection suggests in the introduction that Doyle should be regarded as a father of Science Fiction. This I cannot agree with, all bar The Lost World being a mix of pseudo-science and bilge. The first novel in the collection is just worth reading. The remainder have not aged well and are only of interest to the most fanatical Doyle fan. Overall, I would avoid.
PRODUCT: The Lost World and Other Stories (Wordsworth Classics)

REVIEW:
I purchased this book on spec, seeing it on a bookseller's shelves. It ticked many boxes:
* Historical novel - check
* Covering a period about which I know too little - check
* First of a series - check
* Written in the first person, a particular quirk of mine - check
It had all the makings of a great read, but I was immediately to be disappointed. The central character is an unattractive, being a dour Scotsman from the northern isles, who has joined the East India Company as a writer, a form of clerk, his family having been placed into genteel poverty by his late father's actions. The pace of the tale is funeral - if not slower - and one is tempted to skip pages simply to move the action on, and avoid the central character's moping over his friend Edward, or yet further sketching of local views; could the author not have made the character less dull?
The character is never at the centre of the action. He carries messages, but does not know what is in them. He hears about great events - notably the Black Hole of Calcutta - but is never there. There was a huge opportunity missed for the author to set up the Black Hole - have the central character visit it say before it became so notorious, describing its size, use, etc. Better still of course would have been fr him to have been placed in there and to be one of the 23(?) survivors, but this dramatic opportunity was missed. He meets Clive of India, but only as a messenger. We learn nothing of this complex character who should have been central to the tale.
The historical narrative is confused and I feel that I know nothing more about this fascinating period of the birth of the empire than I did before. On so many levels this novel had great potential, but fails it totally.
I van only suggest to the author that he "stick to the day job", for I shall not trouble myself again with this poorly drawn and tedious character.
PRODUCT: The Cobras of Calcutta: The Decipherer's Chronicles

REVIEW:
Until I read this book I knew little of Kenneth Horne's life, other than his work on Round the Horne and its predecessor Beyond Our Ken, together with a vague idea that he had a senior position with the glass firm Triplex.
While this book fills in many of the blanks in Horne's life as a broadcaster - it appears that he was rarely off radio and TV in the 50s and 60s - there is too little about how he balanced his two distinct careers. He claimed to work 60 hours a week for Triplex yet managed to be both a writer and a performer.
My biggest gripe with the book however is that it is in parts in danger of becoming a hagiography, and lacks in objectiveness. Horne had a complex relationship with women - 3 wives and apparently many mistresses, including a 10 year affair with his secretary. It would have been interesting to know why. Throughout however, it appears that the author is dazzled by his subject - whom he irritatingly refers to throughout as "Kenneth". Over long extracts from letters, the author's own personal views on favourite shows, sketches, etc all pad out what is, at heart, a rather thin biography of one who was no doubt a giant of broadcasting during the 50s and 60s.
There is a fascinating biography of this complex man waiting to be written, but sadly, this is not it.
PRODUCT: Round Mr. Horne: The Life of Kenneth Horne

REVIEW:
I would agree with the two previous reviewers. If like me you are looking for well made, comfy shorts, with a "generous" cut, these are excellent. I bought two pairs to take on holiday to Thailand and will buy another couple of pairs for my next trip. Unlike some other shorts I did not notice any rubbing on the thigh / knee area, which can be uncomfortable in the heat.
Length should suit most, though at 5' 6" I found they came almost onto the knee. If a little taller, they would be an ideal length I suspect. The accompanying belt is fully adjustable and thus aids a comfortable fit. The waist is also partially elasticated.
There are six pockets, including two zip pockets at either side - useful for wallets etc - and two further zip pockets on the seat. My one niggle was that the zip pockets at each side had a propensity to snag on the material around, thus leaving me on a few occasions to ask my wife for help, much to the amusement of onlookers. But for this slight design fault, I would have awarded them 5 stars.
These are not shorts for the "fashionista" or the label conscious, but if you want a pair of shorts that will last for years - they give every impression of being almost bomb proof - and that (I am told) wash & iron well, at an excellent price these are ideal.
PRODUCT: Craghopper Kiwi Shorts

REVIEW:
This is the first of Guy Walters' books I have read and I suspect it will be the last. The premise that an escaped prisoner in Colditz allows himself to be captured at the Swiss frontier and is still interred 30 years later makes for a great read. One's appetite is further whetted by the promise on the book cover that he was "involved in something far more sinister than trying to escape". Great - this has the makings of a real page turner.
The dialogue and the writing was so pedestrian, the characterisation so poor that I plodded through waiting for the twist, the denouement until I reached the final page and ........ nothing. I wasted my time on 400 pages of childish writing, incredibly implausible plotting, quite ridiculous premises - the Germans fail to find a tunnel out of Colditz after 30 years, but the tunnel has not collapsed, slipping across the East German frontier involves sliding under two poorly maintained barbed wire fences - allow the reader some intelligence please! If things had been so easy, East Germany would have been emptied years before the fall of the Berlin Wall. As for the wartime ease of escape from Colditz and their languid train trip to the Swiss border, the less said the better.
If the Trades Description Act applied to thrillers, this would most certainly not be allowed to describe itself as such. Do not waste your time on this rubbish as I did.
PRODUCT: The Colditz Legacy

REVIEW_TITLE: This is a Great IP Camera.
REVIEW:
This HikVision camera is really impressive and for the price , you can't go wrong. I have been using Foscam over the years but found this better both in hardware and software. The image Quality is Stellar. I am using this camera with my Synology surveillance station. It is very well supported. The camera need to be activated first time before use, They have put a default static IP address of 192.168.1.64 for some reason. So, i fired up the camera, plug an ethernet cable to the Router, then download the SADP tool for Hikvision and found the camera on my network, then change the IP address to within the range of my sky router(192.168.0.2 to 192.168.0.254) then use the new IP address to log into the Camera interface. Afterwards, i reserved that LAN IP address in my router for the camera and checked the DHCP box on the camera so the LAN ip address stays the same all the time. i also registered for the free DDNS account (HIDDNS), so that i can access the camera interface remotely.i also downloaded the HIK-Connect app and scanned the code on the camera to use the mobile app.
 The problem is that they are not properly explained in the manual , One need to google all this stuff/ check forums. Even the detailed manual on Hikvision website is a little bit let down.
After all this Snags, you will be rewarded with a very good quality picture with loads of functions , i must say that this camera is definitely better than the Foscams i own. I will recommend. i am using a 12v connector for this camera.
Update;******
I bought another one and I'm impressed with the image quality. Will eventually replace all my Foscam. I'd recommend. '

REVIEW:
I've heard good things about Bluedio headphones, so got these on a lightning deal.
They're well constructed, bordering on the heavy side. The leatherette ear pads are like suction cups, putting them on, I can feel the pressure on my ear drums. Once on though, that discomfort subsides, to be replaced by inferno of my ears. I've not managed to listen to an album yet without taking these off to cool my head down.
Other slight criticisms: no battery indicator, on smaller headsets I can understand this feature being absent, lack of room and all. But these are easily big enough to put a couple of LEDs on. Talking of LEDS, why do the majority of headsets have to have a constantly flashing one telling the world that they're connected? They're on the side of my head, I can't see it.
Now to the point of a headset, the sound. In short, terrible. In long, excessive bass, which muddies the mids and highs. With some EQ tweaking, it's possible to get them to disappointedly bad, but as most people will use these with phones, which often don't have EQ settings to play around with, you're stuck. The "3D" sound effect just widens the sound stage to make the already indistinct mids and highs more indistinct, and sounding farther away.
As for the mic, don't bother.
So, in summary;
Pros: Good looking design.
Cons: Uncomfortable for prolonged (more than 10 minutes) use, terrible sound, terrible microphone, no battery meter, that huge blue led.
I rarely give a bad review, and not sure I've ever given a 1 star before, but these deserve it. I really like headphones, I have lot of pairs. From cheap earbuds to �300 headphones, from no-name brands to the likes of Sony, Sennheiser, Audio Technica and Beyerdynamic. I like to think I know a decent set of headphones when I hear them, but seriously, these are really, really bad.
If you want a decent Bluetooth headset, try the Plantronics Backbeat Pros. Admittedly, they're three times the price, but they're everything these aren't -- comfortable and sound really good. Oh, and they lack the flashing connected LED, and have a battery meter.
PRODUCT: Bluedio T3 (Turbine 3rd) Extra Bass Wireless Bluetooth 4.1 Stereo Headphones (Black)

Sound via a headset is bad though, as the JBL "feature" makes everything excessively bassy, and muddy if switched off. Music play back also stutters occasionally, enough that it's bugs me enough to use a second phone for listening to when walking home from work.
Basically, an excellent for phone for internet and calls, mediocre for music.
PRODUCT: Alcatel ONETOUCH IDOL 3 (5.5) SIM-Free Smartphone - Dark Grey

REVIEW: As a day sleeper, it would be impossible to get any shut eye without these.
PRODUCT: 20 Pairs of Moldex Spark 7800 Ear Plugs

REVIEW: Comfortable, warm but a little short.
PRODUCT: Mens Plain Thermal Polar Fleece Winter/Ski Scarf (158cm x 26cm) (Black)

REVIEW_TITLE: Much better than a Subox Mini
REVIEW:
I've had two Subox Minis before (simply so I can have two different juices on the go at the same time), but when I broke one, I got this as a replacement. It's a big improvement over the other model.
Due to temperature control, I no longer have to run at a lower wattage to avoid burning the cotton, which means a lot warmer throat hit and more flavour. The best new feature is the top filling, meaning I can fill the tank fully, rather than half full like the previous version. It's also possible to lock the temperature/wattage now, so no more accidental changes when in your pocket.
In the few weeks I had it, it's been my every day vape equipment, and I've haven't had any leaks.
PRODUCT: Authentic Kanger Kangertech Topbox Mini Platinum Edition 75W Starter Kit (Subox Mini Upgraded Edition) 100% Original Genuine Kangertech Vaporizer - No Nicotine

REVIEW:
After years of using Sennheiser headphones (HD 555 and 558), I've now swapped to these as my go to pair. Really comfortable, and amazing sound. Obviously, at 250 OHM, they'll need a decent headphone amp to do them justice.
Only complaint is the coiled lead feels a little heavy.
PRODUCT: Beyerdynamic DT990 PRO Headphones - 250 OHM

REVIEW:
I love headphones, and have a lot of pairs ranging from sub �10 to over �300, from manufacturers like Sony, Sennheiser and Beyerdynamic . I like to think I know what I'm talking about when it comes to headphones. Believe me when I say, these are really good for the asking price.
I've tested these on a mobile phone (Blu Win HD, a cheap phone but excellent DAC) and a PC with a dedicated headphone amp. On the phone, they're as you expect, slightly low end biased but decent. On the PC, with the advantage of a graphic equalizer I could tweak it so these sound pretty darn good. If you want to use them on a PC with two sockets (headphone and mic) you'll need an adapter.
They're also pretty comfortable with adequate sound isolation.
The only issue I could foresee is the cable. It's a thin, round affair, which is asking for tangles and eventually breaking.
On the whole, well worth a punt to check these out.
PRODUCT: AmazonBasics In-Ear Headphones with Microphone - Black

REVIEW:
I'm a little disappointed by these.
Having owned a pair Sennheiser HD 558s for a few years, and a pair of HD 555s before that, I like the slightly biased sound and comfort of Sennheisers. If paired with a decent sound card, then these don't sound too bad. Not top notched for music, but adequate for games which is what they're for, after all. The mic however is really good, the best I've had on a headset.
The thing that really let them down is the comfort level. The headband is too thin, both width-wise and depth of padding. Also, for some reason it's taken me ages to get the ear cups to fit properly against the side of my head, but I've got there eventually. Plus, as they're closed back, expect warm ears. However, I might have been spoilt by really comfortable headphones in the past (DT 990 Pro are my current set of choice).
Summary: Reasonable sound, but a little uncomfortable. If you can get these on a lightning deal, then they're good, but not worth full price.
PRODUCT: Sennheiser PC 350 Special Edition Gaming Headset

REVIEW:
If you're happy to use the Windows ecosystem (fewer apps and peripherals than iOS and Android), then this is an excellent value smart phone. It's a good size, responsive and has all the features that most people will want.
It also makes an excellent replacement for an iPod touch, as the audio quality of music is probably the best I've heard from a phone, as long as you replace the headset abominations with something else (I currently use a �20 pair of Philips). I use this phone to listen to music on my walk home from work, and really can't fault it as a music player.
Personally, I'm a little too entrenched in the Google world, with Hangouts being my instant messenger of choice, and an Android Wear watch. If I could get a Hangouts app, I'd be tempted to ditch the watch and my �250 Android phone to use this little beauty as my daily phone.
PRODUCT: BLU Win HD 5" 4G Dual SIM-Free Smartphone - Grey

REVIEW:
These are amazing Bluetooth headphones. I use them as headphones connected via Bluetooth to my PC, so can't comment on mic.
The sound quality can't be faulted, battery life is amazing, and they're pretty comfortable considering the weight. The ANC really reduces the drone of my computer's fans.
Only minor issues I have that stop them being my ultimate pair of headphones are:
Bluetooth range isn't as good as I hoped. This is probably down the either the tiny USB dongle I use, or the brick walls between my chair and the kitchen, but I can't make a cup of tea and still listen to music :(
I would have preferred the ear cups to be more ear shaped. Seriously, who has round ears?
PRODUCT: Plantronics Backbeat Pro Wireless Noise Cancelling Headphones with Mic

REVIEW:
This has impressive cooling on my FX8350 (standard clock speed). Running on the quiet pre-set, a 15 minute Prime95 test got the CPU to a max of 38C.
The only issues I have are:
Fitting the CPU block so that the Corsair logo is horizontal makes fitting the USB cable a pain as it hits one of the thumbscrews. This probably just and AMD issue, as Intel mounts are spaced out more.
The Corsair Link software is awful. It does it's job but why would I want a diagram of the inside of my PC case? Just show me the temperatures, fan speeds, etc. NZXT's Cam software is an example of how it should have been done.
The supplied fans are a little whiny, but not enough to warrant swapping them until they fail.
PRODUCT: Corsair CW-9060017-WW Hydro Series H80iGT 120 mm High Performance All-in-One Liquid CPU Cooler

REVIEW:
Fits perfectly, and does what it should.
The only slight issue I have, is the sides are a little taller than the screen (to protect from scratches when face down, I imagine), which makes swiping in from the sides a little uncomfortable. Although, give it a week, and I'll probably won't notice.
PRODUCT: Alcatel OneTouch Idol 3 (5.5'' Inch) Case - Leegu(TM) Frosted Hard Case Shell Pack of HD Screen Protector Compatible for Alcatel OneTouch Idol 3 (5.5'' Inch) (Frosted Black)

REVIEW:
My regular headphones are either a �200 pair of Sennheisers or a �300 pair of Sonys, so I start by saying I might be a little too harsh on the sound quality of these. Having said that, they're not bad -- a little bass heavy (head shakingly at times), but the highs and mids are there, so by playing with the graphic equalizer it's possible to get a decent sound.
They're also comfortable, even as a glasses wearer. Although, prolonged wearing will make your ears warm due to the leatherette padding and closed backs, but all headphones of that style will suffer from the problem. As it's hard to tell from the photos, and there's no other mention of it, these are circumaural.
I had a lot of hassle trying to get the headphones and its microphone to work with Windows 10, but I've worked out the issue, and figured it might be helpful to others. I had Windows set up to respond to "hey Cortana", and after turning that off, everything is working fine now.
I have deducted a point for the price, as at �70 they're a little over priced.
So in summary: Reasonable sound, comfort and build quality; a smidgen overpriced.
PRODUCT: Finlux Wireless Bluetooth Headphones Black FLXBHPH6B

REVIEW:
The picture on this monitor really can't be faulted. Text is crisp, and the colour reproduction is excellent. Some people recommend against this size and resolution, as some screens (like the one 26" one I just replaced) can suffer from noticeable pixels, but at arm's length, I can't see any myself.
The only iffy thing is the speakers. They're adequate for things like notifications, but not really for music. But then again, who buys monitors for their speakers?
PRODUCT: iiyama X2783HSU-B1 27" ProLite AMVA+ HD LED Monitor - Black

REVIEW:
I'll start by saying I'm a bit of a headphone junkie. Within arms reach of me now, I have sets from Sennheiser, Sony, Beyerdynamic and Logitech, ranging in price from �80 to �250. I like headphones. However, when I'm out and about, I don't like to use big, over-ear cans, but earbuds. Recently, my phone's jack seemed to be playing up, not bad considering the amount of pocket fluff it must have accumulated in the couple of years I've had it, so rather than buy a new phone, I thought I'd take a punt on these.
Considering the price, I'm surprised at how good these are.
Sound wise, they're as good, if not better than the regular wired ear buds in a similar price bracket (�20 to �30) I've tried from the likes of Sony, Sennheiser and Philips. As these have extra features, like the Bluetooth and mic, they're excellent value.
NFC worked without a hitch when pairing with my phone.
The buttons are a little fiddly, but there's only so much space for them, so I can't fault them for that. I have an Android Wear smart watch, so find it easier to use that for controls anyway.
I can't comment on battery life, as I've not used them enough to determine that yet.
They will also pair easily with PC (as long as the PC has Bluetooth, obviously), including mic, so if you want a headset for Skype type programs, these will work.
Works as expected. The connection isn't quite as good as the original dock, but still does the job.
PRODUCT: Mallon� New Cradle Charger Charging Dock Adapter For LG G Watch with USB Cable

Decent enough popcorn movie. Pretty predictable plot and character development.
-1 star of the annoying Michael Keaton character.
+1 for real stunts rather than CGI.

REVIEW_TITLE: It's worth it just for the cost of the subscription ...
REVIEW:
It's worth it just for the cost of the subscription, but the software isn't too shabby either.
I ordered the download, and had trouble registering, as many seem to have had.
My solution was, install it but ignore the "you must install this update" warnings. The software will still load, and you can register it there. Once that's done, install the update (via the Help menu).
PRODUCT: Family Tree Maker Platinum Edition [Download]

REVIEW:
I've used two of these to replace the top fan of my Zalman Z11 Plus case. They shift a decent amount of air but also have quite a hum to them. This could be due to the air vents on the case, that fact that there's two of them now, or that they're running 50% faster than the fan they replace so I notice them more.
I got the purple, as at the time purchase, they were the cheapest available, and I'm not overly fussed about the colour. The light though is very slight, so if you're after a nice glow inside your case go for another colour.
PRODUCT: Corsair Air Series AF120-LED 120mm Quiet Edition High Airflow LED Fan - Purple (Dual Pack)

REVIEW:
I wasn't too sure about the chrome and brown leather look, but in the flesh (well, pleather) they do have a nice, slightly retro, look to them.
I've been a long time Sennheiser user (HD 555, followed HD 558, total combined about 9 years), but I've been pleasantly surprised at how good these Sony's are. They're a little warmer, less clinical, sounding than the Sennheisers, with a little more oomph to the bass, but not enough to over power the mids and highs.
They're supplied with two leads -- one for a mobile phone, with mic, click and volume buttons (volume only works on iPhone), the other is a standard 3.5mm jack lead. The one thing I'd change is make the standard cable longer. I'd guess the cable is about 1.5 metres, which is fine if you're listening to a portable device. You could replace with a regular 3.5mm to 3.5mm jack cable, but that ruins the aesthetics of them.
PRODUCT: Sony MDR1R Prestige Headphones - Silver (discontinued by manufacturer)

REVIEW: Based on a comic I've personally never heard of, this is an enjoyable game, in an Angry Birds vein.
PRODUCT: Monica Bunny Bashings

REVIEW:
I was expecting something cheap and plastic for the price, but it's really well put together, with a single piece of aluminium surrounding the internals.
From my very unscientific tests, I get slightly less than 2 charges of my Nexus 4 (twice from 20 to 90+), which is more than I wanted or required.
So if you just need a battery for occasional use, this is excellent value for money.
PRODUCT: Vinsic Tulip 3200mAh Power Bank, External Mobile Battery Charger Pack 1A for iPhone, iPad, iPod, Samsung Devices, Cell Phones (Silver)

A good variety of ear plugs and excellent value for money.
Not all ear canals are equal, so a good ear plug for one person might not suit the next. This is an ideal way of finding out which ones are good for you.
PRODUCT: Ear Plug Variety Trial Pack - 11 Pairs

REVIEW:
I wanted a bag for when I'm cycling to hold essentials like wallet, phone and other small odds and sods. I went orange, as I figured it would help make me more visible to drivers, and not as some fashion statement.
Only real niggle for me, my phone (Nexus 4) is too big for the strap pocket, but iPhones and smaller should fit.
PRODUCT: BAGBASE UNIVERSAL MONOSTRAP (ORANGE)

REVIEW: Works as it should, and is comfortable for my wrist. However, the smooth mouse buttons become slippery with even a hint of moisture on my fingers, and then makes the mouse harder to use than it should be. It might be better in the winter, when I'm less likely to sweat, but at the moment, it's just unusable for long periods.
PRODUCT: Perixx PERIMICE-513, Wired Ergonomic Vertical Mouse - 1000/1600 DPI - Natural Ergonomic Vertical Design - Recommended with RSI User

REVIEW:
I use it with my Nexus 4, and I recommend a bumper case. For starters, but the charger and the phone are slippery, and a case gives it some grip. Secondly, although it will charge through a regular case, both phone and charger get hot, so a bumper allows some air flow.
It's not as fast as a wired charge, and it takes a little getting used to were to position the phone. Handy if you're sat at a PC all day, as it can be powered via a USB port.

I've only had my bumper for a few days, so the one thing I can't comment on is durability. It seems to be constructed from two black plastic rings front and back, joined together by the buttons, and then all the gaps filled in by the clear plastic. My previous Poetic bumper failed along a seam, so time will tell how well this one fairs.
What I can say is, this is a remarkable bumper for the price. It's a snug fit, and all the buttons and connections ports are accessible. I wasn't too sure about the clear design, but I must admit it's growing on me.
Oh, and if you wireless charge (or are thinking of), it works fine with this.
Pressing anywhere on the screen turns the light on or off, so it's too easy to accidentally turn the light off.
PRODUCT: Flashlight for Kindle

REVIEW:
I don't know if I got a duff fan, or my hearing is just better than everyone else reviewing this, but mine was no where near quiet.
I wanted it to replace the stock fan on my water cooler. If all you're doing is browsing the internet, this fan is fine. But if you give the CPU something to do, it'll rev to an unbelievable volume, especially considering it's only running at 1500 rpm.
I replaced this fan with 2 Akasa Viper S-Flow fans, in a push-pull config. The Akasa fans run at around 1800 rpm, and both together at 100% are quieter than than this.
PRODUCT: Noctua NF-F12PWM Case Fan 120 mm

REVIEW: I added a couple of stars to negate the 1 star for the false positive report. The app itself works as intended, it monitors sleep and wakes me with a decent alarm. How good the monitoring is, I'm not sure, as I have nothing to compare it with.
PRODUCT: Sleep as Android Unlock

REVIEW:
I've had these for a month or so, and I have to say, they're an amazing headset for the price. They're incredible comfortable, even as a glasses wearer (some headsets put pressure on the glasses' arms), and I've not had to take them off because they were hurting.
In my experience, most gaming headsets are bass heavy and lacking mid and top end, which is good for explosions, but not for regular listening to music. These, however, sound amazing. I normally use a set of Sennheiser HD558s as my PC headphones, but these have replaced them. Don't get me wrong, the Sennheiser sound better and are more comfortable, but these are so close, it's not worth swapping them over all the time when I need a microphone.
Seriously, even if you don't want the microphone, these are still great just as headphones.
PRODUCT: QPAD QH-90 Pro Gaming Hi-Fi Headset, Closed, Black

REVIEW:
This is my first liquid CPU cooler, so I can't compare it to others, but I can compare to air coolers.
Performance wise, I've drop around 10 centigrade from the stock cooler on my AMD FX-8350. Noise has dropped too, but it's still a little louder than I was hoping; not to point where it's distracting, but not whisper quiet. I can't decide if it's the water pump or the fan, and it's not bad enough to change the fan to see.
I did have minor problems with fitting the fan following the instructions. I had trouble getting one of the bottom screws in to mount the fan to the block, but that was more to do trying to do it blind. If I had to fit it again, I'd mount the fan before installing the block to the case.
PRODUCT: Zalman CNPS20LQ Ultimate Liquid CPU Cooler

REVIEW: I've had this game for a few weeks now, and pretty much all I've played since. For a free game, the amount of content is amazing. There are 5 sets of challenges, with 30 tables in each set.
PRODUCT: Pool Mania

REVIEW:
If you liked "Dark Passion Play", then you'll love this.
The first single, "Storytime" sets up the heavier tracks, but there's more to this album than pure overpowering music. "Slow, Love, Slow" is (admittedly heavy in places) is a swing style song. "Turn Loose The Mermaids" is a beautiful folk song. The longest track, "Song of Myself", is unusual in that fact that half of it is spoken.
The second disc, like "Dark Passion Play", are instrumental versions. I really love these, and wish more bands with this style of music would do this. Sometimes I just want to listen to great music.
Seriously, if like symphonic, over the top, music, you really need to listen to this.
PRODUCT: Imaginaerum

REVIEW:
The Sennheiser HD555 are practically perfect for me -- they sound fantastic and are incredibly comfortable.
I'll start with the sound. As a night owl, I've used headphones for years. In that time, I have no idea how many I've used, but these are easily the best I've ever had. They sound good on everything, pop to classical, rock to rap.
Comfort wise, they're amazing. They feel incredibly light, and soft cushioning on the headband and cups are gentle to the head and ears. As a glasses wearer, I've had no problem with the pressure from the cups on the arms of my glasses.
I've had my ones for 4 years. After daily use, probably averaging out to 4 or 5 hours a day, they've finally broken. They've got a crack along the silver plastic part, from top to bottom. Sadly, my skill with superglue and gaffer tape won't fix them. They'll be sorely missed.
PRODUCT: Sennheiser HD555 Open Headphone

REVIEW:
The original G15 keyboard was probably the best keyboard I've owned, but I think this is better.
Everything a PC gamer could want for in a keyboard is here. The key movement is perfect. The software for Windows is excellent, but on OS X, it's a little ropey. The LCD is easy to use and read, even though it isn't tilt-able like the G15.
Changeable back-lighting and built in soundcard are plus points, I suppose, but I find them pointless.
PRODUCT: Logitech Gaming Keyboard G510

REVIEW:
I've had these for a few months now, and I think I know their good and bad points.
The good points are excellent sound quality for all but the most audiophile user. In my experience, gaming headsets are usually good for the low end (explosions and the like), but mediocre at the top end. These are great across the whole spectrum, so even regular music sounds good. The mic is also excellent. They're very comfortable, only suffering from the "hot ear syndrome" which all leatherette padded, closed back headphones have.
The bad points: They could do with being a bit louder. Even on 100%, occasionally I'd like a bit more volume. Maybe my 36 year old ears aren't as good as they once were, but I'm not some old codger. I would like to be able to customize the G keys on the side more than in certain media players and Ventrillo/Team Speak.
These two minor points aside, I really do recommend this headset.
PRODUCT: Logitech G35 Gaming Headset (PC)

REVIEW:
I've been put off by recent "remastered" albums, as all they seemed to have done is turned the loudness up to 11, sacrificing clarity in the process. But I'm glad I've replaced my worn and scratched original 1994 CD with these new fangled MP3s.
Overshadowed by albums like Parklife (Blur) and Definitely Maybe (Oasis), which both came out the same year, this is an underrated classic. I recommend switching the lights out, and just enjoying this album on its own with no distractions.
I could listen to "The Asphalt World" on repeat for the rest of my life and still enjoy every second of it.
PRODUCT: Dog Man Star (Remastered) [Clean]

REVIEW:
This headset is excellent quality for the price, especially considering it's USB.
The recording quality of the mic can't be faulted. Overall sound quality is very good, perfectly adequate for online games or VOIP. Personally, I think the playback of music is lacking at the top end, but that's just my opinion.
Build quality is excellent, unlike some headsets I've used in the past (I'm looking at you, Creative). The only thing I can fault is the leatherette pads leave my ears feeling warm after an hour or so. If the pads were fabric, they'd be perfect. Despite this, these are still worthy of 5 stars.
PRODUCT: Microsoft LifeChat LX-3000 Headset

REVIEW:
Until I got these, I've been using a set of Creative HS-600. The Creatives have a decent sound quality, but they feel really delicate. After a while the build quality got the better of them, and they died -- on the night of a WoW raid too, so timing couldn't have been worse :p
Anyway, I got a set of these Plantronics locally (couldn't wait for the post, I'm afraid). I must say, I'm glad the Creative headset went to the audio equipment graveyard, as theses are much better.
The sound quality, isn't too far off my Sennheiser HD555 headphones, and easily the best I've heard on a computer headset. They're not quite as comfortable as the HD555s, but I can still wear them for hours without too much discomfort.
The ear cups are felt covered, rather than the plastic leatherette you often get on headphones. This means the prolonged wear doesn't leave the side of your head sweating. The cups are also pretty soft, so glasses wearers like myself shouldn't have problems.
The open design is a plus point in my book. Yes, you can hear outside noise, but then you can also hear yourself, which means you're not going to be shouting into the mic.
The only downside I can find is the 3.5mm plugs aren't colour coded. Instead they have a tiny picture of headphones or mic on them, which aren't too easy to read if you're fiddly around under a desk.
PRODUCT: Plantronics Audio 370 Analogue Gaming Headset

REVIEW:
As a long term Meat Loaf and Jim Steinman fan, I wanted Bat III to be great. On the first listen though, I have to admit I was disappointed. However, after 3 or 4 run throughs, the album is well and truely stuck in my head.
Following on from Bat 2 with covering tracks from other Jim Steinman albums : "Bad for Good" the title track from Steinman's own album. "Seize The Night", the original of which was called "Carpe Noctem - Fuhl Die Nacht!" from the German stage show "Tanz Der Vampire". And "It's All Coming Back To Me Now" and "Future Ain't What It Used To Be" from the album "Original Sin" from Pandora's Box. "It's All Coming Back To Me Now" is the only one to have a major reworking, by being turned into a duet, which works really well. "Bad for Good" will always be an excellent track, but why did they ask Brian May to play on it? The beginning sounds terrible now, like Queen on an off-day. Don't get me wrong, Brian May is a guitar god, but he sounds totally out of place here.
On the whole, this album is a lot heavier than previous Bats, the tracks "Monster Is Loose", "If It Ain't Broke Break It" and "In The Land Of The Pigs (The Butcher Is King)" especially. Somehow, tracks like "Alive" and "What About Love" manage to raise the "Over the top" bar of production set by earlier Bat albums.
As I said at the beginning, this album takes a couple of listens before it really gets into your head. Just stick with it and it's worth the effort.
PRODUCT: Bat Out Of Hell 3: The Monster is Loose

Customers should be aware though, that the material is far less substantial than it appears in the photographs. Don't get me wrong, it would be great as a summer garment, but it's really quite thin. If the photos weren't so misleading I'd be rating it 5 stars, but it only gets 2 because is wasn't what I expected when I ordered - I subsequently returned it (with no problems) as it wasn't appropriate for the present it was intended as.

Would not buy again.

REVIEW_TITLE: Thank goodness I've found it online
REVIEW:
This is by far the best pepper sauce in the universe. Or any other universe. Ever.
I used to buy it from a local shop that specialised in what they proclaimed as "afro-carribean" products, but since moving I've failed to find in on the shelves of any other high street store. God bless the internet.
It's got a kick but not mad hot at all - there are plenty of alternatives if that's what you're after - but the taste is completely different from most of the hot sauces out there, and it's sublime. Aunt May's is probably the closest alternative I've found, but it pales in comparison. I guess Auntie just has better PR.
I'm staggered that this stuff hasn't gone more mainstream yet. If I was Mr Tesco, I'd be setting an aisle aside for it.
Okay, I wouldn't - that was an exaggeration for comedic effect - but it really is jolly, jolly nice.
PRODUCT: Windmill Products Hot Pepper Sauce 480ml

PRODUCT: Highlander Reflective Survival Blanket - Silver

REVIEW_TITLE: Yep. Working, decent headphones for a fiver. If you've come this far, I'd suggest you just buy the damn things now.
REVIEW:
I first tried these out only yesterday, so there's that caveat. If they suddenly go wonky on me I'll update my review, but if not, this stands.
With that out of the way, I'm hella impressed with this purchase. I go through headphones with depressing regularity, losing sound in one ear after a month or so, and so have tended towards opting for cheaper offers such as Wilko's two quid ones. REVIEW_TITLE: Impressive finish and easy to apply

I found the cloths gave me a little extra control when applying it (i.e. I didn't flick it everywhere). Smell wise, providing that you apply it and dry it in a well ventilated room the smell is gone within 72 hours. The smell is odd but not offensive.
The oil gave the wood really nice natural lustre and a great colour (far better than IKEA's own product). The protection it provides is also impressive. Water beads on the surface and doesn't soak in. It's also really easy to wipe the surface down with a micro-fibre cloth and surface spray.
My wife has quite severe nut allergies and I was concerned about the contents of the oil (as a lot of the alternatives use nut oils). However, the Rustins has been fine with not even a mild reaction from it.
Overall, were really impressed with the ease of application and the protection that it provides.

So why 4 out of 5 stars? From the description it?s not really clear that the knobs only vibrate. Yes they do move up and down a small bit but it?s mostly a strong vibration. You still get the benefits listed above but I?ve seen and tested massagers (at Brookstone in the US) that have a slower circular motion resembling the circular thumb movement that a masseuse would do. As always, I may come back to my review and change that view if indeed I find that the results are good enough.
Some have complained about the product being too heavy? well if you can comfortably lift a 1.5 liter water bottle and move it around and behind your body with one hand, then you shouldn?t have any problem using this. I guess it is a little heavy but given the strength of the engine and generally quality build I think it?s reasonable.
Net question is: is it too strong? This is very subjective. I like my massages super super strong and I?m not disappointed. I use it on the strongest setting and apply a fair bit of pressure to it. My girlfriend likes softer massages and uses it on the slower setting and she?s fine with it.
So far I?ve used it on neck, shoulders and upper-back. The results are great! I go to bed free of tension in my neck and shoulders, pain gone. I even notices a we light ?cracking? sounds coming from my cervical vertebrae. They?re very light and subtle but ? without being a trained specialist of any kind ? I would attribute them to my spine improving alignment given that most of my problems are due to an incorrect posture while sitting at my office desk in front of my PC. I will try it on the base of my feet and on my shins (other problem areas for crams and splints) and will report back.
I?ve gotten into the habit of using it every night for about 5-8 minutes max. I haven?t tried the other knob covers, I?ve only used the smooth ones. So far so good, I would recommend this product. REVIEW_TITLE: Great bit of kit although not a Juicer per se
REVIEW:
Great bit of kit although not really a Juicer per se... This is my first take (I've received 5days ago, will update it i find any material difference in the coming weeks).
I'm very happy with the purchase as this "little" �69.99 gadget is replacing �200+ worth of other kitchen tools that occupy at least 7-8x the space/weight. I got rid of my Philips HR1861 juicer and my kitchen-top blender which I probably had used no more than 10-12x over the last 3 years. I've used this 5x in the last 5 days!! The main advantages over the juicer/blender solutions are:
1. incredibly easy to clean. i put a drop of dish soap and bit of warm water and then give it a 5 second pulse. most of the stuff comes right off but i just give it a wipe with a soft dish pad and voila'! It's done... don't even put it in the dishwasher. The juicer, although dishwasher safe, was a real pain to clean. little debris of fruit and vegetable would stick to the filter and you had to scrub it with a special brush. plus the sheer size of it made it hard to fit entirely in the dishwahser
2. it's a single tool that smashes, grinds, blends, crushes and you can sip directly from the same cup. with the previous solution i had to first extract the juice from fruits/veggies with the juicer and then use a separate blend in softer ingredients (like bananas and avocados) or harder ones like ice, seeds, nuts etc. which meant an even greater mess to clean and more space occupied in the kitchen
This may be obvious to you (as it was to me) but the main thing to point out is that this is a blender not a juicer. There's a lot of reviews/tests/recipe books that refer to this as a juicer but that's not really accurate. it's a very powerful blender that will create fantastic smoothies with all sorts of fruits, vegetables, nuts, seeds and other ingredients but the result is quite a bit different from a juice. The main difference is that the pulp (and skin if u leave it) of the fruit/veggie is blended and you consume it. That's fine, maybe even healthier but you should make sure you're ok with that.
I did a bit of research on this products vs the NutriBullet and thought this was a more attractively valued solution (materially cheaper than the 900W NutriBullet) although the design, in my opinion, is a bit less refined than the NB. This looks more like something you would find in a smoothie store rather than a designer, modern kitchen. It's also a bit bigger than the NB but really not that noticeable. It's got a permanent place on my counter next to the kettle (which is still bigger than this).
One thing that I would point out, not a big draw back for me but a clarification to some of the reviews I found: the NN doesn't COMPLETELY liquify certain seeds and nuts. For example, I had specifically heard in a youtube video review that this would completely crush the little seeds in raspberries so that you don't get them stuck in your teeth when you drink a smoothie with the berries. I've found it to be untrue. I've used raspberries often in my smoothies and the little crunchy seeds are always there. I'll try to experiment with different blending lengths and consistency fluids to see if that holds true but for the moment it doesn't look like it ill completely dissolve them in the liquid. I've blended a few almonds and they get almost completely liquified although you still get a bit of texture. Again I will experiment a bit and come back if there I find out how to get them completely liquefied.
But so far so good... I give it a full 5 stars given the price/performance ratio is great. Would recommend this over a NB given the cheaper price and more powerful motor (compared to the more basic version of the NB).
PRODUCT: Nutri Ninja Blender BL450

REVIEW_TITLE: Updated review Beware, Tomtom is selling/closing its Sports unit
REVIEW:
Updated review:
Not much to add to the product review below but new news from today is that Tomtom is trying to sell or shut down their Sports division because of lack of revenue growth and profitability. Why is this relevant? Well the risk is that the online platform and app will stop being developed in the meantime. I'll keep on using my Spark but if I had to buy a new GPS watch or recommend one to someone I'd stick with Garmin and Suunto brands as they are putting lots of money in new products/services (part of the reason why Tomtom is pulling out in my personal opinion.
Bad karma for Tomtom
Old review dated 1 December 2015: "\Beware, only a handful of (v. expensive) headsets work with this watch "
I was a big fan of the older version (TomTom Multi Sport Cardio) which won me over after being a loyal Garmin user for many many years. When I read about the Cardio + Music model I was delighted, having music while running is a must for me and I always had to depend on a separate mp3 player with a separate charger etc etc. Unfortunately the execution on this product hasnt lived up to the concept.
The previous 2 reviews are very good at detailing the GPS, activity monitor features so I will focus my review on the one feature that merits the 1 star rating... the Bluetooth music function.
Before buying the device I had read that there were a few "preferred" headsets that Tomtom had pre-tested but I though these were the "woks best with" type peripherals. To my surprise, those are the only headsets that Tomtom guarantees will work with the watch. Everything else may very well not work (I have 3 BT headsets recently bought from Amazon, all Bluetooth 4.1 or above compliant, none of the work). The problem probably lies with how the bluetooth chip within the watch was placed or its configuration. I'm not a technitian but my BT headsets all work splendidly with my iPhone, iPod Nano and laptop, even at 8-10 meter distance but with the TomTom watch I get audio dropouts every 2-5 seconds. And I get these dropouts when ever I move my arm away from the headset (which happens quite repeatedly when running right?).
You may say "surely you must have a defective device". That's what I though at first... try searching on the web "TomTom bluetooth audio dropouts" or "problems connecting TomTom Saprk with headsets" it'll take you to Tomtom support forums packed with other frustrated people having the same issues. And the standard reply by Tomtom: well we tested the watch and gave a list of compatible headsets. This is simply unacceptable. They try to say that the problem is due to which side of the headset manufacturers place the antenna and to try to switch the watch from your left to your right arm. This is ludicrous as Bluetooth should work at least several meters away.
In general, Bluetooth is a standard and as such, if you comply to that standard (be it version 4.0, 4.1 or whatever) all compatible devices should work. You may have a list of "preferred" peripherals that work best but all should at least connect and work. In case of the Spark it's the opposite, less than a handful are guaranteed to work, everything else is a big question mark. And the headsets that work are all �50 or above which greatly changes the overall economics of purchasing this device. Since Tomtom knew of the limited compatibility of this watch it should've just sold the version which includes their won Tomtom branded headsets. And they should've made it clear to customers that any other headset model besides the 4 they've will probably not work.
Now, I'm very happy to work with Tomtom in trying to resolve this. Hopefully they'll release a software patch that will improve this issue. But if they expect me to go out and shelld another �50+ on a new pair of headsets they are dead wrong. I will either return the device for full credit or expect them to give me credit to buy a new pair of "compatible" headsets
EDIT (10/03/16): Tomtom has released an updated firmware (1.2.x) in mid-February. This has improved Bluetooth connectivity and, as far as I can tell, compatibility with (some) headsets. I have successfully paired both my mPow Cheetah and mPow Swift and they both hold the signal much better without having to wear the watch a particular wrist (one of the (useless) workarounds previously suggested by customer service).
Why am I not changing my rating on the watch? Well for one I?ve had to shell out an additional �50 to buy a compatible headset, money I?ll never get back. I ended up buying the Plantronics Backbeat FIT so that I could use the music feature on the watch as none of my other headsets would work. This was due to very poor communication by the company who was not telling customers that only 9 pre-approved models were guaranteed to work with the watch.
On that matter and hopefully of some help to prospective buyers, Tomtom hasn?t actually updated that list of compatible headsets even after the firmware update. So if you buy the watch and it doesn?t work with the headsets you have, Tomtom will tell you that you should?ve bought one of the compatible headsets. This is deeply flawed argument which I?ve addressed above: Bluetooth is a standard and if your product uses that standard it should work with the vast majority of peripherals, not a very expensive limited subset of peripherals. You can check that list here, note that his information is in the support forum and not explicitly advertised with the product (quite cheeky): [...]
Thirdly, while the main issues with Bluetooth are being addressed (at least with the headsets I could test) there are still a few bugs that I encounter and others have shared on the UK support forum: 1. Problems connecting with the smartphone app on both iOS and Android (often you have to ?forget device? and reset Bluetooth pairing entirely to get it to connect) 2. Problems connecting with software on Mac (often have to delete and re-install the application entirely as it gives connection errors and doesnt download the QuickFix GPS information) 3. Calibration on the step-tracker function is way off (this is the one you do on a treadmill to better calibrate step counts when GPS is off)
Bottom-line: the firmware update is a welcome first step but it doesn?t solve the issues. I continue to think Tomtom released an ?incomplete? product with many interesting features (on paper) which simply don?t work as stated. My recommendation would be to hold off on the purchase until these issues have been resolved. I?ll update my review if and when progress is made

REVIEW:
Alison Weir's thrid book proved an absolute delight to a History graduate and all round fan of the historical fiction genre like myself. This book was beautifully written and by someone who obviously knew her subject matter well. But then this is always the case with Weir's work. Her non-fiction books were a must during my degree as the level of her research and writing style made it easy to learn the basics of the subjects she wrote on.
In this book, Weir takes the story of Eleanor of Aquitaine (on which she has already written a non-fiction book some years ago)and builds the story in a believable tale which sticks pretty smartly to what is actually known about Eleanor. Unlike the supposed 'Queen of Historical Fiction' Philippa Gregory, there is little nonsense in this book. I find that Gregory focuses too much on incest and supernatural bunkum for my liking and in my mind Alison Weir is the new Queen of this genre. This book firmly places that acolade at her feet. If you have not read her other two historical fiction novels I would strongly recommend them. And if you are looking for some readable facts behind the stories try her non-fiction work took.
What I loved in addition to the story was the author's note at the end explaining her take on fiction v fact and her opinion on writing historical novels. She comments that writing on women of the past is particularly challenging because women's actions were not generally recorded in historical documents. For me this makes Weir's latest book particularly captivating, because she clearly understands completely the context of Eleanor's life and times and uses the fiction genre to 'pad out' as realistically as she can the rest of the story.
I have since ordered her Eleanor of Aquitaine non fiction book to find out more for myself!
PRODUCT: The Captive Queen

REVIEW_TITLE: Disturbing, but I still read it until the end
REVIEW:
I have read many of Phillippa Gregory's other novels and thought I would try Wideacre as it was one of her early works. The beginning of the novel is a real page turner; full of ups and downs, passions and beautiful sweeping descriptions of Wideacre. However, the main character is absolutely unlikeable and as her behaviour sinks to depths of depravity the likes of which I have certainly never read about in a novel before, the book eventually makes for a rather uncomfortable read.
I struggled through the rest of the book to be honest, yet I still wanted to see what would happen to Beatrice etc so managed to make it to the end. I did not know what to make of the novel by the time I had finished it and I can't say I really enjoyed it. However, I have bought the second in the series - I think maybe because the Wideacre story was so unlike anything else I have ever read!

REVIEW:
After deciding to pick up an action camera for my up coming holiday, I purchased the Xiaomi Yi due to the constantly impressive products that are produced by Xiaomi.
The camera arrived in a plain but stylish brown cardboard box, with a quick start guide printed in Chinese, however this is not an issue as this camera is very easy to use, more on that later.
The first thing you will notice about this camera is its impressive build quality, all the buttons feel solid when pressing and give both an audible hardware click and software beep when pressing, giving no mistake that you are taking stills or capturing video, the camera also has three LEDs to report on the status that can be seen when the camera is housed in a waterproof case. One slight issue is that the LEDs can be a little hard to see in sunlight. The camera is also very lightweight.
The camera can also be controlled via WiFi using the Android or iOS application, it also offers a live viewer (which makes up for the lack of screen) and also a way to change the setting of the camera, for example, then powering up the camera it is set to take still photos, the application will allow you to set the default to video, it also (via a firmware update) enables the option to start the camera recording video when it plugged into a power source, making it ideal for a car cam.
The camera is capable of taking a 64GB MicroSD card which in my tests I ample storage (it is also useful keeping multiple cards with you, or using the WiFi application to delete or download videos or photos). There is also a Micro-HDMI output, this is a feature I have yet to test.
Operation of the camera is very simple, after powering on the device the red LEDs (when is video mode) will stay on when ready, pressing the button on the top of the camera will and the LEDs will flash, to stop recording, press the top button again, very simple.
One slight issue I have had with this camera is the battery draining itself even with it powered off, this appears to be a design fault and is very easy to fix (https://forum.dashcamtalk.com/threads/xiaomi-yi-big-battery-drain-problem-solved.10909/), I have also read that this has been rectified by Xiaomi. One other slight annoyance is the cover for the MicroSD, Micro-HDMI and USB slot is quite hard to remove, but that might be due to my short finger nails.
Overall this is a truly excellent action camera, and the minor issues I have encountered can easily be overlooked to the price. If you are looking for an action camera you cannot go wrong with the Xiaomi Yi.

REVIEW_TITLE: Surprisingly good, a really decent little guitar, ideal first semi-acoustic/practice session guitar.

I got this with thoughts of Stagg guitars from twenty years ago in my mind, cheaply made beginners' guitars with poor action. I thought it might be okay to let my grandchildren strum on it, without worries of them damaging it unduly.
Well, something's changed.
This is a super little guitar, ideal for someone moving into electro-acoustics who doesn't want to spend a fortune. The strings aren't the greatest, but you wouldn't expect them to be Ernie Balls' at this price.
The finish is eyecatching, and the overall look is of something well-made.
It's a good little guitar for taking to wired open-mic sessions, compact and light. For young players with a small hand and reach, the cutaway makes reaching the lower frets easy.
Don't get me wrong, it's not a Yamaha, a Tanglewood, or a Guild, but it is a perfectly decent little guitar that won't leave a decent player blushing on stage. The jack connection is solid, no cutting out or crackles with our portable practice amp. It didn't need retuning after each song, and the pegs are robust and well-finished.
No razor edges to slice through a string the minute it's tightened.

REVIEW_TITLE: Great for the gym, swimming pool, cute little compact razor, reusable handle, in well-made bag, hairbrush included.

This isn't necessarily something I'd want to give as a gift, except to a very close female relative, but it's something that is really useful. The gift set comprises a well-made double compartmented toiletries bag, along with a compact palm-sized travel hairbrush, an ingenious travel razor with container, and a spare Venus razor blade.
I'm a huge fan of the Venus range, as the blades are interchangeable with all the handles. I can't be the only person who stands in front of the shelf in a shop trying to recall which razor I'm currently using, With this, there's no need to worry.
The razor will also come in handy at home as the little folding travel case has drainage holes, so can be safely left on the shower shelf.
No more coming back to your expensive bladed razor with special moisturising head to find that the lubricating strip has dissolved in a pool of water at the side of the bath.
I wish I'd had this razor years ago. Memories of physically tearing out 'spider's legs' by the roots in the swimming pool changing rooms, as I realised, with horror, that I'd missed a bit when shaving in the shower that morning... ouch,
The bag is spacious and well-made, eyecatching and practical. The fuschia pink zip should prevent it being stolen by male members of the household, although one never knows.
I loved the handleless egg-shaped little hairbrush as well, a nice alternative to the folding ones with mirrors which always lose their ability to stay unfolded in use after a year or two.
PRODUCT: Gillette Venus Snap Women's Compact Razor Gift Set, + 1 Blade Refill + Travel Case + Hairbrush + Travel Bag

The set is very nicely presented in a gift-box, but I can't help feeling that many of these sets are destined not to survive childhood.
If you have small people in the family who are Minions-mad, then it may be better to source something cheaper and more robust.
I actually thought this was an adult-sized set, and was momentarily disappointed at the mini Minions items.

4.5 stars for this, rounded up to five. It really is lovely quality, but practical.. well, possibly not.

A smart-looking compact infra-red lamp, with adjustable head, and non-slip base.
 Unfortunately mine didn't work, even after double-checking all connections, tightening the bulb, etc. I cannot recommend this, as a result.
PRODUCT: Medisana Intensive Infrared Lamp, 150 W to Relax, Treat, Relieve Muscle Aches, Alleviate Pain + Common Colds, Optimised Heat Radiation, Adjustable Tilt, Energy Saving Light Bulb, Medical Certified

REVIEW_TITLE: Added play value with a trick spinning top once constructed, guidance needed for younger children (6-10).
REVIEW:
An ideal stocking-filler for Lego addicts. Ideal, as there is just enough construction needed to satisfy that element, with the bonus of a spinning top toy to play with afterwards as well.
