Large Lego playsets have the drawback of taking up a lot of floor and table space, and at Christmas, this space is often at a premium. Younger children may need a lot of help with the construction of a large project, and be quickly bored with the results.
This Spinjitsu set should take no more than 10 minutes to construct, but then there is the fun of playing with the spinner afterwards, and trying to master the tricks. I can remember similar spinners being popular thirty years ago, and the essential principle of a whip and top is centuries old.
The age range for this set is 6-14, children of 10 and above should be able to complete it independently, thanks to the clear step by step illustrated guide. Younger children may need some help in identifying the pieces and decoding the diagrams. The handle of the spinner has a surprising number of mostly small and quite fiddly pieces, and some patience is required to put them together. The mini-figure of Lloyd sits neatly in the spinner head.
Once assembled, this is likely to remain intact, how much it is played with from that point depends on the individual chilld. Dextrous children may be able to master some of the tricks, others will quickly tire of the toy, I liked it for the added play value, although a premium price is paid for the name - I was surprised at the RRP,
PRODUCT: LEGO UK 70628 Lloyd Spinjitzu Master Playset

REVIEW_TITLE: Lightweight, comfortable neckband Bluetooth headphones, linked easily to iPhone 6s+. Decent sound quality.
REVIEW:
4.5 stars for these, rounded up to five. These are comfortable, secure little neckband headphones that work really well. They come very nicely presented for gift-giving in a box that completely disguises the contents. They charged up with absolutely no problem via the micro USB to USB charging cable supplied, the clearly illustrated instructions are very easy to follow. The micro USB charging port on the control block has a rubber cap to prevent water entering, should these be worn when running.
Once charged, a simple long (2 second) press on the Play button activates the Bluetooth connection. Make sure Bluetooth is enabled on your device; the headphones appear on the Bluetooth enabled device list as Jam Contour, which is helpful. I tested these indoors, and was able to listen to my iPhone downstairs whilst upstairs, so listening to a phone in a waist belt or pocket when running, walking or cycling shouldn't be a problem.
The sound quality is good, nothing spectacular, but perfectly acceptable, clear with a decent balance of sound. After a bit of practice, it's relatively easy to identify the embossed control buttons on the control block by touch.
Summary: Light, portable, comfortable.
PRODUCT: Jam Audio Contour - Bluetooth Headphones, In-Ear Wireless Noise Cancelling Earbuds, Sweat Resistant, Comfort Collar for All Day Wear, Hands-Free Calling + Up to 7hrs Play Time Battery Life - Black

REVIEW_TITLE: Smaller than many models, but no loss of power, a stylish steam generator iron with some novel touches,
REVIEW:
This is ideal for smaller households where storage space is at a premium. Whilst these irons are considerably larger than standard steam irons, this one has a much smaller footprint. However, there's no loss of power with this. It delivers a powerful shot of steam.
 If you have items that you never wear, because you hate ironing them - particularly linen or heavy cottons - this steam generator iron may bring them back into use.
Unlike many top of the range models, this doesn't have an optimum temperature setting, it also allows you to control the amount of steam you use, which is something I hadn't come across previously in a steam generator iron.
That may be seen as a minus point by some, and a plus point by others.
What I can say is that the soleplate is top-class, it really does glide beautifully. If you have used a steam generator iron in the past and found it to be noisy, this one is much quieter than most.
A downside is that the tank is much smaller than some, but unlike early models of steam generator irons, this one can be filled whilst switched on, with no problems. Like all steam generator irons, the actual iron itself is light and easy to use, as no water is held in the tank,
 I experienced no dribbling or spitting with this, there is a considerable amount of steam generated, and I do like to hang all items for an hour or two to air, before putting them away
If you are unlucky enough to live in a hard water area, this has a very easy anti-calc cleaning system, scale 'catches' on an internal arm, and the tank is simply flushed through - there are no expensive filters or cartridges to replace.
Summary: Not the cheapest model by any means, but some novel features, a fantastic soleplate and a compact, elegant design,
PRODUCT: Tefal GV7466 Express Anti-Scale High Pressure Steam Generator, 2200 W, 6.5 Bar, Blue/White

REVIEW_TITLE: Large = men's medium. Go a size up, reasonably well-made and very good value if they fit.
REVIEW:
Caution, these are unisex, but only if you are a man with medium sized hands, or a female with not too large hands, a 'small large'.. They are leather, they are reasonably well made, but they aren't that large at all. I have just bought a wheelchair for very occasional use, I'm just as likely to use these for cycling.
The good point about them is that they leave the fingers and thumb free for smartphone operation, handling coins and all the hundred and one tasks that are so much harder with full-finger gloves.
I'm happy enough with them, but if you usually take a large in gloves, and are male, don't expect these to fit.
At the time of writing this review, they are available for an incredible price, and very good value.
PRODUCT: KANGO FITNESS - Unisex Leather Wheelchair Gloves

REVIEW_TITLE: Too cute to use, a bulky eraser with a novel integral pencil sharpener. One for vegans?
REVIEW:
I'm not quite sure who this is designed to appeal to, possibly uni students who want something a bit quirky. I thought this would be a cute little eraser with a small pencil sharpener. It's cute enough, but it's also large, far too big and heavy for a pencil case. Vegan students might find it appealing, avocado addicts will love it.
It works as an eraser, although not that well, to be honest, it's so big, but would you really want to use something so cute?
Stationery addicts may find it ticks a lot of boxes, it's a bit big for a stocking-filler, it's a bit pricey for a Secret Santa.
A fun addition to a classroom or office - and the sharpener, the avocado stone, is excellent.
PRODUCT: NPW Extra Large Eraser Pencil Rubber / Sharpener Set - Vibe Squad Giant Avocado Eraser

REVIEW_TITLE: Brilliant. The essence of British culture at Christmas, wittily captured.
REVIEW:
I'm a Christmasaholic, I love the celebration, but what I really love is the anticipation and preparation, the keeping of timeless traditions and the feel-good factor it engenders.
This book ticks all those boxes in marking these, but it also tempers it with the addition of some very funny tales that freely admits Christmas can be hell on earth. For years, I prepared for Christmas by reading Gyles Brandreth's Christmas Book which, lovely as it is, doesn't really admit the fact that Christmas isn't always what we would wish it to be.
This book has a host of tales of British Christmases Past, laid out Twelve Days of Christmas style. ('Ten Carols Screeching', for example). There are beautifully researched and often surprising facts. The medieval language and music of 'Ding Dong Merrily on High' was written in 1924. The value of unwanted Christmas gifts in Britain was �2.6 million, in 2014 ('Six Bargains Grabbing').
That's a horrendous waste, and probably explains why most charity shops are still solvent. It's the post-Christmas influx of stuff that someone else will probably get as a birthday gift that keeps them going each year.
It's the personal tales that make this book. There is a lot of black humour. There's the bleak tale of a Christmas with norovirus in the house. The university student who flew to France for a week's Christmas ski-ing, only to find that the rest of the family were unable to join her, as they couldn't find their passports. There are also some very moving stories - a magical Christmas in Norway, from a Cornish person, who had never known snow. I know how they feel. Eighteen years of snowless Christmases in the UK was followed by eight years of Christmases in Germany, and not one white one, then back in the UK, we got the same for another twenty-five years, apart from the year it snowed on the day. Eventually in 2009, we had pre-Christmas snow that hung around for a while, deep, slushy, uneven.
Then we promptly got it the following year. It was still magical.
Rhodri Marsden's writing style is wonderfully readable, and Peter Kyprianou's 'Eighties-manual-style' drawings are often very funny, and beautifully observed.
It is a very British book, it captures the essence of British culture at the festive time of year, and I absolutely love it.
Highly recommended.
PRODUCT: A Very British Christmas

REVIEW_TITLE: Higher protein raspberry SlimFast, real fruit bits, thicker, tastier, better than the original. Easy to store resealable pack.
REVIEW:
SlimFast in a bag? Well, no, actually, this is better. Much better. The original powder makes a thin-tasting drink that you convince yourself is filling; this is much improved.
Firstly, it's a sturdy, re-sealable bag, and takes up much less room in the cupboard (and in the bin, when empty).
 The bright red scoop is round-bottomed, making it easy to spot in the bag, and easy to measure out the three scoops needed for each 250ml of liquid.
The powder itself quickly dissolves when shaken, in skimmed milk, I was pleased to see that SlimFast don't recommend almond milk, as some of their rivals do, but ordinary cow's milk.
The raspberry crush has bits in it when prepared; not lumps of undissolved powder but pieces of freeze-dried real raspberries. The drink itself is thick and very palatable. In a spirit of experimentation I made it up with both skimmed dried milk powder and water. Making it up with water doesn't give you the same 26g of protein per serving, but it is perfectly drinkable, and still tastes OK.
 Milk is better, but whereas you can't drink original SlimFast with water (well, you can, but it tastes vile), this is fine.
There's an impressive list of minerals and vitamins too. If you've moved on to protein shakes from SlimFast for nutritional reasons, this may move you back.
I've been drinking this for several days, and experienced no digestive issues, either. It tastes exactly like one of those expensive extra-thick milkshakes from the chiller cabinet of your local supermarket, perhaps less sweet.
 Really like this.
PRODUCT: SlimFast Vitality Meal Replacement Powder, Raspberry Crush, 440g - Total 10 Servings

REVIEW_TITLE: Perfectly decent shower curtain, water-repellent, mildew-resistant.
REVIEW:
A perfectly decent shower curtain, which unlike others in the InterDesign range is water -repellent, and doesn't require a plastic shower curtain liner. This minimalist design liner has sturdy, well-attached chrome grommets. The grommets are a decent size, should you have extra-thick shower hooks.
What it doesn't have is the hooks to hang them from.
 I find that my hooks only last 3-4 years before becoming brittle and/or discoloured, so eventually, I will have to buy a set to replace my current plastic ones.
At 180cm x 180cm, it's a decent square standard size, that should fit well inside the bathtub.
Other than the lack of hooks, there are no issues with this, the monochrome look will suit a wide range of decors.
I can't comment on how mildew-resistant it is, fortunately my bathroom isn't badly affected with this, but the water-repellent fabric should also help with this issue.
PRODUCT: InterDesign Mildew-Free Water-Repellent Zeno Fabric Shower Curtain, 183 x 183 cm - Charcoal Gray/White

REVIEW_TITLE: Worked well on something unsavoury, not tested on fox poo as yet.
REVIEW:
Fortunately we haven't had to test this yet on fox poo, but we have tested it on a very smelly dog who rolled in something unsavoury (possibly a dead mouse), and it came through with flying colours.
The tube really resembles a human shampoo, I loved the convenience of the squeeze tube and the flip-lid, which means you can hold a wriggling dog with one hand and flip the tube with your thumb to dispense the shampoo.
The shampoo has a pleasant scent, as you might expect, it lathers well, and rinses out easily. It certainly left our young Springer's coat fresh and fragrant. I've no doubt that it would work on fox poo too,
PRODUCT: Animology Fox Poo Shampoo, 250 ml

REVIEW_TITLE: Lovely, perfect light coloured walnut halves, fresh-tasting, sturdy, scrunch to close pack.
REVIEW:
Great. These are top-quality light halved walnuts in a sealed foil pack. The 'light' refers to the colour, these could be described as 'blond'.
For those wanting perfect halves for decoration, 11 of the dozen I selected at random were flawless, and the twelfth had the smallest chunk broken off.
 I regularly use walnuts, but particularly for my Christmas baking, and these really will meet my needs.
They have a lovely, fresh flavour, with none of the stale, bitter taste that can be a really unpleasant experience with walnuts. The sturdy paper-foil pack scrunches easily to reseal and keep them fresh, without spilling the contents. Nothing to dislike about these.
PRODUCT: Happy Belly Light Halves Walnuts, 500 g

REVIEW_TITLE: Useful guide for teens, raises awareness and empowers.
REVIEW:
I got this as my 14 and 16 year old grandchildren are now becoming politically aware. Their great-grandmother was a famous local politician and I hoped for a book that would make them aware of issues without steering them too widely in one direction.
That's exactly what I got here. Those giving it one star misread the brief in my opinion. This is a book for young people. a guide to engage them.
They are the generation that will be dealing with issues that are impossible to fully predict post-Brexit. .The future is scary enough for those of us who are due to check out in the next twenty-five years or so, they have seventy or so years of uncertainty ahead.
 They need to know how they can make a difference, and Sue Turton has done a good job here in giving some of that guidance. There could be more, my grand-daughter has worked with the National Citizenship scheme for example, an excellent scheme for giving young people a taste of independent living, working and thinking.
However, this book does a good job of raising awareness, in my opinion. Labour plan to give the vote to 16-year-olds if/when they get in to power. This book will prepare that age range better than most.
PRODUCT: This Book Will (Help You) Change the World: Protest injustice. Campaign for change. Vote for your future.

REVIEW_TITLE: Sturdy, well-made, illuminated outline lights. Good cable length, suitable for indoor use.
REVIEW:
These aren't a large scale outdoor decoration, but a sturdy set of lights, with six brightly lit outline figures that will provide a near- instant decoration for a plain wall or window once plugged in.
They are very sturdily made, and good quality, you'll be able to take these down and use them year-on-year. If you are using them out of doors, the plug isn't suitable for outdoor use, so will need to be protected from the elements
What I did like about them was the really long cable, which enables these to be used some distance from a plug point. The clear flex is unobtrusive, and won't stand out like a sore thumb.
More tasteful than many outline decorations I have seen.
PRODUCT: WeRChristmas Pre-Lit LED Christmas Characters Silhouette Light String - White

REVIEW_TITLE: A lovely stocking/Christmas decoration, very well made, photos don't do it justice.
REVIEW:
This is actually much better quality than I expected, and worth the price currently being charged, a very nicely made plush novelty stocking with some novel details.
His arms are together in front of him, and he is carrying a red plush heart on a string. He is a functional stocking as well, and will hold some small gifts, with the opening at his back.
A lovely, novel way to package up some small gifts for a loved one, and unlike a gift bag or wrapping paper, once the presents have been taken out he isn't headed for the bin, but will make an ideal wall or mantel decoration - or even hung from the back of a door.
Given the price of some gift and bottle bags, this looks really good value, and good enough to be brought out as a Christmas decoration year on year.
Everything is well-stitched on, this isn't cheap or tacky in any way.
PRODUCT: WeRChristmas 3D Snowman with Scarf Christmas Stocking - 55 cm, Multi-Colour

REVIEW_TITLE: Smart enough, no frills overnight bag with a good range of useful full-size men's products.
REVIEW:
This is an unusual gift set in that it isn't a washbag that holds the toiletries, but a full-size weekend bag. The bag has two grab handles, well attached mock-leather trims, and a sturdy enough zip. It doesn't have side pockets or any frills, but it's perfectly serviceable.
The contents are full sized too, and fortunately mine were intact, as there was nothing to protect them, rattling round the inside of the bag,other than a piece of card to make the bag more rigid. I'm in favour of minimalist packaging, but a plastic bag of some description would have been useful here.
. They are perfectly suitable products that work well, and all designed for sensitive skin. If you are a female in the habit of using products used by any males in the house, these are fine, the creme is very similar to standard Nivea creme, the shower gel is perfectly serviceable and lathers well.
As well as this, there is a 'post-shave balm', shaving foam, and an antiperspirant stick; useful products that should see some use rather than languishing for years in a corner of the bathroom.
You'd have to be very minimalist to get enough in here for a weekend, but as an overnight bag, it's fine, the lack of side pockets is perhaps a slight issue, but if you want a decent bag, then you'd certainly expect to pay more than what you pay for this, plus contents..
PRODUCT: Nivea Men Weekender Gift Pack

REVIEW_TITLE: Works really well, dried up spots, but price is a bit eye-watering.
REVIEW:
This review is the view of my adult son who has problem skin.
This Proactiv Cleansing Body Bar is stated as being gentle, but is surprisingly powerful, though without being harsh. The salicylic acid it contains is designed to gently exfoliate before acting on spots.
Having used it for a week it has dried up some troublesome spots at the back of the neck, and left the skin in much better condition without drying it out too much.
It doesn't have the look of a premium product, the price was a bit of a surprise, but it does work well. Compared with lotions and liquid body washes it should be quite economical, providing the bar is carefully stored between usages.
If you have tried other products and found that they don't work that well, this may be the one that does.
It's not the only product for dealing with problem skin that has a relatively high RRP. It might be suggested that manufacturers know that if you have spotty, problem skin, you are prepared to pay what is asked to solve the problem. This will be out of the reach of many teens due to the price.
PRODUCT: Proactiv Cleansing Body Bar

REVIEW_TITLE: Easy to swallow capsules, 30 mg of curcuminoids per capsule, 60 mg daily dose. No side effects for me.
REVIEW:
So far, so good with these easy to swallow capsules.
I've taken turmeric in the form of golden paste for some time, but it is a pain in the proverbial to prepare, so I was interested in these capsules.
At 30mg they have the same level of active ingredient in curcuminoids as many other tablets, but I've found them to have no side-effects so far.
I can put my yellow-stained saucepan and wooden spoon to one side for a while at least, whilst I take these. I do feel that turmeric is of some benefit to my arthritic joints, and as a convert, am interested in anything that makes life easier.
I've held back from giving five stars as I just haven't taken them for long enough, but I will continue to do so.
PRODUCT: Liquid Curcumin - 60 Capsules | 185x Turmeric & Curcumin Bioavailability - Ultra Bioavailable | Liquid Capsules with 500mg NovaSOL per Capsule | Ultimate Curcuminoid Supplement MADE IN UK

REVIEW_TITLE: Upmarket felt-tips, secure caps, slightly odd selection of colours.
REVIEW:
These are very upmarket felt-tip pens that don't look anything like felt-tips, until you take the caps off.
 These aren't suitable for colouring in, unless you have single sided pages and a piece of card underneath to stop bleed-through to the page below. Even then, I wouldn't use these for that purpose, the colours are bright, but not particularly suitable for colouring - there's no dark blue, or brown.
What they are suitable is for any purpose that requires a variety of bold colours that are easily distinguishable from each other. Being felt tips, gravity is no problem - these would perhaps be handy marking off a wall calendar or paper-based wall-mounted planner. The tips are slightly thick for writing, but if you want your writing to stand out, these would do the trick,
Given the price, the packaging was a slight let-down, standard clear plastic that isn't much different from pound-store products.
These are too good to fall into the clutches of children, but if they do, the ink is water-based. The caps click on firmly, and also fit neatly on the end of the pen to prevent them from being lost easily.
The hexagonal design means they don't roll easily off a table on to the floor.
PRODUCT: STABILO 68 Premium Felt Tip Pen - Assorted Colours (Pack of 8)

REVIEW_TITLE: Pleasant, fresh smell, gets the coat clean, no irritation experienced. Colour looked the same, but that's OK.
REVIEW:
This was tested on quite a smelly young Springer who has an affinity for dirt, and it worked well. Not sure about the colour enhancing properties, his coat just looked clean, soft and shiny, but most importantly, it smelled clean and he hasn't reacted to it
There's been no signs of skin irritation, or scurf, just a light, pleasant fragrance across his fur.
 The shampoo looks and feels exactly like a good quality human shampoo, it actually resembles a well-known brand in the style and colour of the packaging. At this time of year, outdoor baths are out, so if you leave this in your bathroom, do look twice before you pick the tube up.
It foamed well and rinsed out easily. Lots to like, and nothing to dislike.
PRODUCT: Animology True Colour Enhancing Dog Shampoo, 250 ml

REVIEW_TITLE: Lovely long cable on these classy plain white lights, no need to have the plug point under the tree.
REVIEW:
4.5 stars for these, rounded up to five.
 I'll be using these bright little lights as Christmas tree lights for this year. They are advised as being suitable for indoor or outdoor use, but the connection isn't weatherproof. I've never seen a plug like it, a two-pin connector with positive (+) and negative (-) terminals slots in to connections on the main body of the black three pin plug and is screwed into place.
The terminals are marked, and the connection is secure, but do make sure you look at the connections in a good light before setting it up.
They will be replacing an all-singing and dancing flashing set of lights, which I hated as I had to reset the lights every time I plugged them back in, and the control box for the lights needed to be hidden in the Christmas tree branches.
What I really liked about these lights was the long cable from the lights to the plug. You won't have to have these eighteen inches from the plug point to be able to use them.
They also aren't in a loop, but have a free end, making them much easier to wind around the tree when they are put on. The candle-style lights look sturdy enough, a downside is that they are not replaceable.
For outdoor use the cable is quite sturdy, but its clear, so should be relatively unobtrusive in Christmas tree branches or around a window.
Great also as plain white decoration lights for a bedroom, playroom etc.
PRODUCT: Festive Productions 100L LED Lights with Clear Cable, Warm White

REVIEW_TITLE: Attractive chunky unisex watch. Not the most practical timepiece, but makes a strong fashion statement. Not for large wrists.
REVIEW:
4.5 stars for this, rounded up to 5. As a fashion item, it's right up there, as a practical watch, it has its drawbacks.
The presentation case of this teen-themed watch reminds me of a puzzle given to young children as a dexterity and intelligence test. The inner clear plastic case fits snugly into a white and clear plastic outer case which has a moneybox style slot in the top. The watch is mounted on a clear plastic stand within the inner case, with the instruction leaflets tucked in to the sides of the inner stand
If you are an adult with ageing vision setting up the watch, be aware of the very small print of the instructions. There is a standard plastic stopper clip on the watch adjustment knob, which has to be removed before the watch kicks in to action, set-up is reasonably straightforward.
The description of this as a medium watch is fairly accurate. I have slim wrists, and very unusually for me with an adults' strap, the strap of this watch isn't at its shortest when I wear it. Chunky wristed adults will find this too small. The clip is chrome, the strap thick rubberised plastic.
In use, it's not the most practical watch I've ever owned. The white background of the stopwatch dials makes the white hands hard to read at times. If you glance at the watch to find out the time, it can be a couple of seconds before your eyes work out where they are if both are on the lower half of the dial.
I suspect that this won't be an issue for most people who wear this. If this is in your price range, you probably use the clock and stopwatch on your Smartphone most of the time. It's a fashion item, the 'ice' logo stands out and makes others aware that you have the brand.
PRODUCT: Ice-Watch aqua Kids' Chronograph Quartz Watch with Silicone Strap - 001459

REVIEW_TITLE: Beautifully written with exquisite photographs, not just the whiskies, but Japanese life and philosophy too. Gorgeous.
REVIEW:
Oh, this is beautiful, just beautiful... I saw the title, thought 'Japanese whisky? Suntory? and wondered if there could be much more to say on the subject.
Plenty, it transpires. This isn't just Japanese whisky, it's an exquisitely illustrated guide to Japanese culture through the medium of whisky.
Twenty years of travelling to Japan have given author Dave Broom a real depth of knowledge and understanding, and he is keen to pass that knowledge on. For any whisky drinkers who are more focused on the tasting notes and production methods of each brand, there are enough details here to keep the most fact-hungry reader happy.
However Dave Broom's skills don't stop at describing the whiskies, stills and distilleries. He describes the journeys across Japan that took him to each whisky, through the Southern Alps with 'hills folded like crumpled green crepe', on his way to Mars.
 The Mars Shinshu plant, that is, that got its odd name following a competition. How very Japanese. The distilleries stretch the length of the Japanese archipelago, from the south-west to the northern island of Hokkaido, one of the snowier places on the planet in winter.
Not only are the descriptions great at times, the photographs by Kohei Take are absolutely stunning. Most of them wouldn't look out of place framed on the wall, and that includes the interior and exterior shots of distilleries.
What really made the book for me was the author's engagement with Japanese culture and thinking. He gets it, for example, the perfect -in-its-imperfection form of a simple ceramic cup, bearing lessons in its form that speak of centuries of craft experience, handed down through generations of craftsmen. The way of whisky forms part of that tradition.
Anyone who saw BBC TV's The Art of Japan and Handmade in Japan will find familiar names and ideas in these pages. The non-whisky pages are helpfully coloured a pistachio green, enabling them to be sought out, or skipped. Though anyone skipping them is missing a real treat.
The book is itself, exquisite, with heavy, embossed covers and a silken bookmark. Anyone with an interest in whisky or Japanese crafts related to it will find much to enjoy in its pages.
A delight.
PRODUCT: The Way of Whisky: A Journey Around Japanese Whisky

REVIEW_TITLE: Convenient packaging, well-tolerated and easy to swallow capsules. Relatively low dose of 'active' ingredients per 'pill'.
REVIEW:
3.5 stars for this, rounded up to four. These tablets are four cards of glucosamine capsules, plus two cards of fish oil capsules. It's an attractive presentation, and if you travel a useful way of taking your tablets without counting pills into a travel pot.
However it's also a relatively expensive way of taking glucosamine. I've noticed some slight improvement in hip pain while taking these, but that could easily be a placebo effect.
The plus points on these are that the glucosamine tablets are easy to swallow and the fish oil capsules are the standard size small capsules..
Which is just as well, as the high maintenance dose of these is four tablets a day of glucosamine plus two of the fish capsules.
I didn't get any unpleasant digestive effects from the tablets,
These may be worth getting if you are already convinced of the benefits and going away on holiday, or prefer foiled capsules to those in a bottle for hygiene reasons. I'll certainly complete the course, but I think I'll continue with cheaper sources of joint help.
PRODUCT: Omegaflex DUO Glucosamine Hydrochloride, Calcium & High Strength Omega-3 Fish Oil and Evening Primrose Oil for Joints & Bones, 70% Concentration High EPA Formula, 60 + 30 capsules

REVIEW_TITLE: Useful, but no different to the 'free' bags with home furnishings. Flimsy single-end zip doesn't look like it will last.
REVIEW:
This is useful but... I've got two clear vinyl see through bags like this already, exactly the same quality, a slightly different shape, a single zip running three quarters of the way around, and flimsy fabric handles.
 They are fine for storage, but nothing else.
They were 'free' with my pillows and throw, and useful as they are, they were just a handy extra that came with the things I bought.
So, yes, this is handy for keeping my most used beauty bits together, but it's not great. I wouldn't trust it to use as a novelty handbag, the zip is far too flimsy and the handles aren't brilliant.
The zip is single-ended, so there's a real danger of it coming undone at the bottom corner of the bag, This could easily result in you leaving a trail of small items like pens, lipsticks, and combs behind you with you not even noticing.
The handy thing is that you can see the contents straight away, instantly find that little tube/packet/item that you want, The contents are accessible and well protected, and unlike a fabric bag, it's water-resistant. It's too big to use as a clear bag for taking on aircraft, which is a shame.
I'd probably buy a few of these if they were in my local discount store or pound store, to be honest, that's about what I would expect to pay.
PRODUCT: InterDesign Nya Travel Accessories Bag, For Personal Care/Beauty Products, Cosmetics, Toys, Art Supplies, Beach - Medium, Clear/Black

REVIEW_TITLE: Thick lotion, rubs in easily, slightly light-reflective, scented. Perfectly OK for 'indoor days' (no SPF.) 40ml, not 50ml.
REVIEW:
This seems to be a new product, a pleasant to use thick lotion, rather than a cream, with quite a strong scent. It's marketed towards women in the 40-60 age group, designed to be used with the L'Oreal Paris Revitalift Hydrating Smoothing Serum 30ml and L'Oreal Paris Revitalift Anti-Wrinkle Eye Cream 15ml.
I liked the fact that the tube is designed to be stood on its cap, which means that only the gentlest of squeezes is needed to dispense the cream.
It rubs in easily, and is quite light-reflective with a very slight shimmer, which can flatter more mature skin. There was a slightly sticky feel for a minute or two, but that disappeared, to leave my skin feeling pleasantly soft. I've noticed no reaction over a two day use.
This doesn't have an SPF, which is something that I prefer, even in winter, but for days when you know you are not going to be outside, this is fine.
 At 40 ml it falls below the 50ml of most of the Revitalift skin care range, but it does have the advantage of being in a tube rather than a jar, with virtually no risk of contamination. With quite a noticeable scent, I was careful to avoid my eye area, as I've found strongly scented creams can irritate slightly.
I'll continue to use this on 'at home' days, but prefer my SPF creams for long term use.
PRODUCT: L'Oreal Paris Centella Repair Anti-Wrinkle Cica Cream 40 ml

REVIEW_TITLE: Enjoyable, but flimsy for the cost. Have pen and paper handy.
REVIEW:
This has been a partial hit, this half-term week, with my teenage grandchildren who are board game fans, particularly Monopoly.
I can remember playing a Sixties version of this which seemed far more complex, or perhaps it was that the rules are better explained.
Don?t lose the rules sheet, do have pen and paper handy or a calculator for those who don?t have maths as a strong point. A player?s income changes constantly as they move through Life, on the board, and the impact of those changes is only totalled at the end.
That?s what makes it fun, the decisions, decisions, decisions come thick and fast. Procrastination isn?t an option, not if you want to avoid arguments.
What made this four stars instead of five was the unnecessary flimsiness of some of the play pieces. There are small thinnish cardboard tokens that have to be placed on a plastic spinner.
If the spinner had been made more robustly, this wouldn?t be an issue, but the discs slip around and under the spinner, jamming it. It?s easier to write down everyone?s choices, on scrap paper and keep the tokens out of the spinner.
Aside from this issue (and that of the thin paper money, and fiddly pegs for the ?cars?) this is a really good game that engages the players. Younger children, below twelve or so, will need some guidance with the rules and perhaps with understanding what?s written on the cards. A bright eight year old should be able to engage with this, with support.
Final word? It will be played again, but...
It?s overpriced, in my opinion, for the quality of the play pieces, I expected better from a company like Hasbro.
PRODUCT: Hasbro Gaming The Game of Life

REVIEW_TITLE: Bleak, compelling, low on feetgood factor, high on atmosphere.
REVIEW:
It took me a while to get Into this story, I?m so glad I persevered, but if you like your stories with a high feel good factor, then it may be best to look elsewhere.
The blend of faction is a compelling one, the story utterly believable.
Bernie McGill does an extraordinary job of capturing time and place, and for this five stars, I just didn?t always want to stay there long, it was pretty grim at times. It says much of the human condition, of the dull grind of life, of the impact of choices.
There must have been a fair proportion of women like Nuala in rural 19th century Ireland; the average age of marriage for men was high, and many lifelong bachelors took on younger women to ease them into old age.
Her story keeps you reading once you get into it, but I put this down feeling grateful that the twentieth century changed Rathlin and communities like it. The death of a community has many personal tragedies, and this is one you can believe in.
PRODUCT: The Watch House

REVIEW_TITLE: Helped to ease tangles, gentle pleasant scent on coat.
REVIEW:
We have two Springer Spaniels that are clipped for summer but have longer coats for warmth in winter. Being active and adventurous dogs, their fur often picks up burrs, etc, and develops mats easily. I?ve often thought of using a child?s detangling spray on them, so this is perfect.
The sturdy bottle has a trigger action spray activated by twisting the lower cap. The manual action means no nasty chemical propellants are needed, and there?s no spray ?hiss?, either.
In scent and appearance, this is difficult to distinguish from a product made for humans. There?s a pleasant, fresh smell, the liquid is clear and works exactly as a child?s de-tangler does.
Does it work? Well, yes, and in exactly the same way as a child?s de-tangler does. The liquid eases tangled hair apart gently as its brushed. Stubborn mats may still need clipping out, but this does make a difference.
The dogs didn?t seem to mind it at all, and were sweeter smelling too. Result.
PRODUCT: Animology Knot Sure De-tangle Spray, 250ml

REVIEW_TITLE: Definitely different, a beautifully detailed meditating Zen Gnome Christmas tree ornament.
REVIEW:
If you are looking for a different Christmas tree ornament this year, then this meditating Zen gnome certainly ticks several boxes. He?s sitting cross-legged, eyes shut, with his hands in the Gian Mudra position, index finger and thumb forming a circle.
Somewhat incongruously, a red cardinal is peering out of his beard. The detailing is beautiful, personally I would have preferred the ornament to be minus the bird, but it?s still very appealing.
He?s ready for hanging, with a sturdy gold thread. This would make an original little gift for anyone into mindfulness/meditation, or just as a really novel addition to your own tree. The colours are nicely muted and very tasteful, this may be odd, but it?s a quality item.
PRODUCT: Christmas Ornament - Garden Gnomes Figurine - Zen Garden Gnomes - Meditating Gnome Statues - Christmas Decorations

REVIEW_TITLE: Easy to use chain oil designed for wet conditions. Made a difference.
REVIEW:
Basically, this wet lube is still chain oil, in a bottle rather than an aerosol spray formula, with a pointed nozzle for accurate application.
I?m not an off-road biker, I use my trike in an urban environment, in all sorts of weather conditions. I frequently have to clean and re-oil the chain in winter, which is never a pleasant task.
Before use, I cleaned the chain with a cassette-style cleaner, wiped it off and dried it, then used the nozzle of the bottle to gently distribute oil along the inside of the chain.
The easiest way to do this is to hold the bottle of lube at a fixed point on the bottom inside surface of the chain, and gently turn the crank so that oil trickles from the nozzle of the lube bottle onto the chain as it glides past.
I remembered to do this 24 hours before taking the trike out, and the difference was noticeable. Unlike an aerosol, you can ensure precise application of the product.
Clean and easy to use, takes up less storage space, and is more environmentally friendly. It?s all good.
PRODUCT: WD-40 BIKE 44687 100 ml Wet Chain Lubricant - Grey

REVIEW_TITLE: Well tolerated glucosamine, fish oil and evening primrose oil combo. Hasn't worked miracles, hasn't harmed, either.
REVIEW:
I have tried a wide range of supplements to help with pain and immobility from arthritis, and this combination of evening primrose oil with fish oil, manganese and vitamins intrigued me.
 I'm unlucky enough to have quite severe joint pain, I can't honestly say that it has made a difference after five days, but the plus point for me was that everything was in one capsule.
Taking the maximum daily dose of three capsules, this is just under three weeks supply.
I've had no side-effects from this, my stomach appears to have tolerated it well, and I haven't experienced an aftertaste either. From that point of view I like it. For those of us who experience joint pain, anything is worth trying. I'm not convinced by this, but it has done no harm, which has to be a plus point.
PRODUCT: Omegaflex Glucosamine with High Strength Fish Oil, Virgin Evening Primrose Oil & Manganese, Vitamin C & E, Joint Health Support, with Omega-3 & 6, 70% Concentration High EPA Fish Oil, 60 capsules

REVIEW_TITLE: Gorgeous musky, woody scent with floral undertones and a hint of smoky vetiver. Ideal for autumn.
REVIEW:
Gorgeous, in a word. This is less floral than I expected, an initial sweetness quickly changed to a slightly smoky, woody vetiver-type scent, with floral undertones, which is really appealing.
I normally steer clear of celebrity perfumes, but this one is definitely in a different league. It's a classy, stylish perfume that I would be happy to have as my hallmark scent.
It's a very suitable scent for autumn, the 'heat shimmer' is perhaps the heat shimmer of autumn bonfires. It's also long-lasting, applied to pulse points early in the evening, the scent was still distinct and recognisable five hours later. I'd be happy to wear this through the day and into the evening.
 The presentation wasn't overpackaged, the glass bottle with plastic top is in a very stylish box, but it is quite thin cardboard, with nothing to protect the bottle inside. That's a plus point from the environmentally friendly point of view, but perhaps something to be aware of. My box was cellophane-wrapped and did arrive in pristine condition.
If you find standard vetiver perfumes too heavy and smoky, but like woody scents with a hint of smoke, this is exactly what you are looking for.
PRODUCT: Beyonce Eau De Perfume for Women, 100 ml

REVIEW_TITLE: Not just for the training pitch,stylish fully-lined tracky bottoms with hidden pockets & zipped outside legs. L= 34"-36" waist.
REVIEW:
Top marks for these lightweight but very well-made training pants. They have been given a thorough testing by my adult son,
 Not only are these good quality training bottoms, they are tailored enough to be worn to the supermarket on the weekend or for just lounging around the house, with an attractive embroidered 'Canterbury - New Zealand' logo.
There are deep zipped pockets for anything that needs to be carried while out and about, both the pockets and the outside legs have concealed zips.
The waistband on the Large size measured at 32" without stretching and 37" when stretched, so the sizing of 34"-36" (87-92 cms) for a large size is spot on, the inside leg was approx. 31 inches to the bottom of the hem.
Velcro straps make them fully adjustable at the ankle, and the side zips on the outside of the legs make for quick and easy removal. The zips go right up to crotch level, and the legs are roomy enough for really well-developed thighs. The fabric is non-stretch, so this is just as well.
The non-fray flat lace drawstrings on the inside of the waist have sturdy aglets, rather than uncomfortable knots, another plus point.
Nothing to dislike, and a lot to like about these.
PRODUCT: Canterbury Men's Open Hem Stadium Pant - Black, Large

REVIEW_TITLE: Improved packaging, but the same great product. Fixes flexes and cables particularly well - repair, not replace.
REVIEW:
I've used Sugru for a number of years, and am a convert. For anyone who has used it previously, this is an improved version. The packets are bigger, more eye-catching and easier to open without scissors.
I've used it to re-sheath damaged flexes on kitchen appliances, to repair mobile phone charging cables, and to repair a headphone cable. This family-sized pack contains enough Sugru for larger small projects.
 Using it is very simple, the foil packet is easily opened, and the putty-like Sugru is ready to use straight away. It's best to have everything ready to hand, as the Sugru starts to set in half-an-hour.
Pressing it in to place is easy. This time around I've used it to repair a hook on the back of a favourite wall clock and it's worked perfectly, the Sugru held its shape whilst drying and after twenty-four hours the clock was back in action. So far, it's held, and I have no doubt, based on previous experience, that the repair will last.
Yes, I could buy another clock, but it won't be that clock, that I've owned for some twenty-five years.
Sugru repairs the things that you didn't think were repairable, keeps items out of landfill. The Sugru website has lots of ideas for its use, as does their social media. It's good stuff, and it works.
PRODUCT: Sugru Mouldable Glue - Family-Safe | Skin-Friendly Formula - Black, White & Grey 8-Pack

REVIEW_TITLE: Imaginative dexterity game, requires some preparation and additional household items to play. Best to ignore the rules!
REVIEW:
If you are a family of serious game players, this probably isn't the game for you.
Basically it's a game that judges how dextrous you are, based on the creations you produce with pad and pencil, and modelling dough when your hands are bound by the wraps supplied.
As well as the two players a third person is required (according to the rules) to judge the creations. Cue arguments, in competitive families or groups.
It's a lot more fun to bin the rules and just have a go at the challenges, to see what you can all come up with,.The two pots of modelling dough are quite small, and as anybody who has had toddlers in the house probably knows, this stuff becomes unusable unless stored very carefully.
 The dough also gets under nails, bits flake off and the amounts of usable dough will quickly reduce, unless you are careful. It's possible to make your own playdough from basic household ingredients, and this is something you may well have to do if the game becomes a favourite.
There is a bit of preparation involved, in having to collect items such as a pillowcase and pairs of shoes with laces, as dexterity tests. Which is good fun, until you discover the contents of the airing cupboard and shoe rack scattered following a search ...
PRODUCT: Hasbro Gaming Get a Grip Game

REVIEW_TITLE: For slimline pencils only, children's and some adult colouring pencils won't fit. Does give a needle-sharp point.
REVIEW:
Three stars only for this, as it doesn't fully meet my needs. I hoped to use this to give super-sharp points to my adult colouring pencils. Unfortunately after spending ten minutes figuring out how to put in the four AA batteries, I discovered that one set of pencils wouldn't fit into the sharpener.
When it has a pencil it can sharpen it really does deliver a needle sharp point, a point to bear in mind if sharpening pencils to be used by children.
It's annoying, although given what it can do, if the user has thin pencils, then it's probably what they need.
Unlike some small devices, there is no advice given on not using rechargeable batteries, which is a plus point.
PRODUCT: PaperPro - BPS3V-EU - PencilPro Personal Battery Pencil Sharpener, Black

REVIEW_TITLE: Pleasant to use, spicily scented paste that gives good hold and washes out easily.
REVIEW:
The review is the opinion of my adult son, who rather likes this. It does have quite a strong scent, but it is masculine. It's not a big pot, at 75ml and designed to be popped into a man bag or backpack, or to use when travelling.
The paste has a much lighter, less sticky texture than hair wax products, but it did the trick and held shortish hair in the style required.
'Whisky' is an odd word to describe the scent, as the scent of whisky is quite a variable. It's spicy, but whisky didn't come to mind.
It washed out easily in the shower with a minimal amount of shampoo.
PRODUCT: ManCave Natural Texturizing Hair Paste, 75 ml

REVIEW_TITLE: An original, insightful anthology, mixing the familiar with new discoveries.
REVIEW:
The Poetry Pharmacy is a beautiful little book with a selection of poems within chosen to support the reader through times of need. So often, many of us will hear a poem at a memorial service and find comfort from it; this book is designed to help at other times too. There are poems to support mental health and well-being, offering motivation, boosting self-image and self-acceptance, not just offering comfort, but also a fresh, wise perspective. There are poems that are not poems too - for hopelessness, try the extract from Oscar Hammerstein II's 'You'll Never Walk Alone'.
William Sieghart's notes to each poem are wise and insightful, whilst Sieghart has the background of privilege to protect him, privilege cannot protect from all worries. There are many for whom reading a poem won't offer solutions, the mind has to be open to the fact that it may.
Some of the poems are very well-known; Maya Angelou's 'Still I Rise' for times of oppression, and Donne's 'No Man Is An Island', others, like Jack Gilbert's 'Failing and Flying' less so, perhaps, but deserve to be. This last poem is for divorce, offering the viewpoint that to call a marriage a failure is to ignore the fact that parts were a success - 'Everyone forgets that Icarus also flew'. An example of a different perspective, I also really liked Billy Collins' 'The Present' as an balance against all the exhortations to be mindful and live in the moment.
Many of us who enjoy poetry have anthologies that we like to dip into, this is one that offers a lot more than just something familiar at a time of stress.
Like every really good poetry anthology this offers something new with something familiar, I've discovered a new favourite poet thanks to two poems from Sheenagh Pugh, who had somehow slipped under my radar.
 If you 'get' poetry, then get this.
PRODUCT: The Poetry Pharmacy: Tried-and-True Prescriptions for the Heart, Mind and Soul

REVIEW_TITLE: Readable, engaging, a step up from popular science, debunks myths and informs widely.
REVIEW:
While many of us may not have realised that some of the myths in this book even existed, nevertheless it is a fascinating 'dip-in' book, packed full of facts, and written in a readable, accessible style. It's not a textbook, but has solid academic referencing throughout, and a huge bibliography. The author covers interesting topics such as variations in skin colour, the widely-reported myth that blonds are dying out, and the myth that only humans used tools.
The information is organised logically, from general evolution myths (natural selection always works, for example) through human origins (sample myth, all human species have probably been discovered) through evolution of the genus Homo. Finally there is a totally fascinating section on recent and future human evelution.
I particularly liked the robust debunking of Myth 40, that humans were influenced by terrestrials. Many of the myths could be books on their own,, and this is one. This book is a step beyond popular science, but is still just as readable as many books of this genre.
Summary - a fascinating, wide-ranging book, covering paleoanthropology, human biologiical variation and genomics in one volume, with engaging facts on every page. Readable and very engaging.
PRODUCT: 50 Great Myths of Human Evolution

REVIEW_TITLE: Seemed to dry out, rather than hydrate, my skin, definitely not for me.
REVIEW:
I love Murad products normally, and was looking forward to trying this. I have mature skin that is holding up pretty well with the years, it's not usually greasy or dry, but nicely 'normal'. Face masks are an occasional treat for it, I use a Murad face wash daily, and find the range generally suits my skin, if not my pocket.
In my opinion, this isn't suited to mature skin, sensitive skin or skin tending to dryness in any way.
The application is novel, a swab to run over cleansed skin gives a preparatory base 'retexturising' the skin, then the hyaluronic acid soaked mask rehydrates your face, when applied. There was a slight tingling with the swab, and a more marked 'tingle' with the face mask.
I've used hyaluronic acid products on my face before, and my skin tolerates them well. However, my face didn't feel as if it was being treated or rehydrated, as promised.
 On removing the mask after twenty minutes it certainly didn't feel hydrated, and softer. The sensation was more like that experienced after I'd used astringent products on spotty teenage skin, the exact opposite of what I'd expected. My fine lines looked the same.
 Reading the list of ingredients, they seem to be counter-productive, lots of natural essential oils, but skin-drying alcohol too, which is confusing. In my experience, the oils weren't enough to counteract the alcohol's dessicant effect.
I'm not going to use this again, unless I experience a return to greasy skin at some point. At the current RRP, this is not a cheap mask at all, and a bit of a let-down. I didn't expect miracles, but I did hope to feel this had done my skin some good, which wasn't the case.
PRODUCT: Murad Hydro-Glow Aqua Peel

REVIEW_TITLE: Beautifully illustrated guide to creating new hairstyles for long hair, a bit light on detail at times.
REVIEW:
Long hair has been very much the dominant trend with young women over the past few years, and this book is very much geared to long hair, Visually it's really attractive, with lovely line drawings of the various styles, braids, twists, plaits, buns and so on, If your hair is shoulder length or shorter, you won't find the new ideas you are looking for here. If, like me, you have fine hair, you are also at a distinct disadvantage.
Where it could have been a little clearer was on the step-by-step instructions, This probably would have resulted in a bulkier book, but if you are working through the book, and can't figure out how to do a certain style, it could be very frustrating.
There's a distinct boho vibe to the book, and nothing here that would get a teenager banned from school for being outlandish. Girls and young women of 12-20 with the right hair (long, thick) and fashion style should really appreciate this
PRODUCT: Love That Hair: Head turning styles for every occasion (Love Those/That ...)

REVIEW_TITLE: Well-made,nicely detailed figure, includes a novel accessory, but not fully poseable
REVIEW:
If you are into Star Wars, then you will already know about Bodhi Rook from Rogue One.
Collectors will have a nicely detailed figure with clear facial features and vest detailing, children will appreciate the novel zip-line accessory that slots on to Bodhi's back. (This took me back to the similar Ghostbusters figures of twenty five or so years ago.)
With such detailing on this figure, it's perhaps disappointing that the figure doesn't bend at the elbows or knees,
Bodhi won't be doing any crouch and run moves in the movies children and adults can make with the downloadable video-making app, which is a shame.
I also have slight issues with the description of this figure as a 'playset'. It's a four-inch figure with accessories, (the zipline 'backpack' and a weapon') and has limited play value as a lone item.
That's an incidental point, this is still a well-made figure with a novel accessory, that fans will appreciate.
PRODUCT: STAR WARS B9844EL20 "Rogue One Bodhi Rook" Playset

REVIEW_TITLE: Works much better than a old-style rotary whisk. Ideal for lighter mixing tasks, batters, cream, etc.
REVIEW:
4.5 stars for this, rounded up to five. This took me back! It's a far-improved version of the rotary whisk I used as a newlywed, forty years ago. If you yearn nostalgically for them, get this instead.
 It won't replace an electric mixer, but it won't need plugging in either, and is much easier to store. It's ideal for light to medium weight tasks.
The whisk has a U shaped 'stabilising bar' at the bottom, which prevents the beaters from touching the bottom of the bowl. This means that about an inch of ingredients at the bottom of the bowl/container isn't touched by the beaters either.
However, the bar is removable, and it is possible to use the whisk so that the beaters are just above the bottom of the container containing your ingredients. If the beaters rest on the bottom they don't turn quite as well, and it's a hard job using this.
I've used this to make up powdered milk into liquid milk for cooking, and it was a breeze, the beaters worked really well, and the whisk was ready in seconds. Holding the centrally placed stick shaped handle took a little getting used to, but there's no real knack to it.
I then used the milk to make both a pancake batter, and a thicker, coating batter for fish.
The whisk coped brilliantly with the pancake batter, it was more of a challenge to mix the thick batter for the fish, but with a bit of extra elbow power, it worked.
It's very easy to clean. To remove the stabilising bar you hold the top handle and pull. To remove the beaters for washing, you hold the base plate that they slot into, and pull the beaters out fairly gently.
 They are interchangeable, so there's no worry about fitting them back incorrectly. The beaters and stabilising bar washed easily by hand, but they can be put in to a dishwasher.
My 38 year old Krups electric mixer won't be retired just yet, but for quick and easy jobs I will be using this, burning a few calories, and saving a bit of electricity.
PRODUCT: Zyliss Quick Whisk, White

REVIEW_TITLE: Wax coated, mouldable cotton food wraps. Cold hand wash in washing up liquid a drawback, cannot be stored/used near heat.
REVIEW:
I really wanted to like these, but I'm afraid they are just not up to the mark, in my experience. Fifty years ago, my mother would use the wax-coated paper from bread wrappers and cereal packets to wrap leftovers before putting them in the pantry (no fridge, then).
This isn't a million miles from that idea, except that the wraps don't work as well. If you have cold hands, you could be at a distinct disadvantage using these, as it's the warmth of your hands that softens the wax coating the wraps are covered in.
The instructions with these are minimal, a brown cardboard sleeve has no real information other than you can use them to wrap cheese, fruit and veg and bread, but not meat, and that you seal with the warmth of your hands.
 A small slip of paper inside advises you to wash them in 'dish soap in cool water', which is washing-up liquid in British English.
The other information is that they will last for one year. They also need to be kept away from heat, such as hot water, dishwashers, microwaves and ovens. The 'ingredients' are listed - beeswax, organic cotton, jojoba oil and tree resin.
So you have to wash them separately by hand using washing up liquid, effectively, as most of us use warm to hot water to wash any dishes by hand.
In use, I found that they moulded quite well, and in this respect, they worked, although I suspect they won't work as well after a few washes, when the coating will start to slip off.
 I didn't enjoy cleaning them in cold water afterwards, though.
I did find instructions online for converting these into sandwich wraps using a button and string, It's an idea, but I won't be bothering.
There were also instructions on how to re-coat the wraps, or make your own.
The tree resin in the ingredients is powdered pine resin. which is available on Amazon. Having read the instructions, again, I won't be bothering.
One comment sometimes made of eco-friendly products is that they just don't work as well as products that aren't so green, and unfortunately this doesn't restore that reputation.
For anyone not wanting to use clingfilm over bowls to store food, I suggest doing what my Mum did half a century ago, and putting a plate over the bowl.
PRODUCT: Bee's Wrap Set of 3 Assorted Size Wraps, Beige

REVIEW_TITLE: High-rise, comfortable, well-fitting, not particularly attractive, but offer secure protection.
REVIEW:
The packaging on these is decidedly elegant, which is a little more than can be said for the contents. They aren't bad, but..
'Discreet' is a slight misnomer for these peach - coloured pants. These are close fitting, and well-elasticated, but they are also high-rise. If you have standard fitting trousers on, you may find these peeping shyly above the waistband.
 Which isn't so much of a problem if you are wearing a long top, not so good with shorter summer clothing or for taller women. The fact that you are wearing these isn't something you want to advertise.
Size-wise, they aren't bad. I'm a mid range size 16, and they were a comfortable fit, not too snug.
The 'plus' absorbency pants are rated 6 on the absorbency scale, which is moderate to light-heavy loss, but they don't have the bulk of some high absorbency products. Although I wouldn't wear them with tight leggings unless you have a really long top on, there is some VPL.
They are particularly useful if you are doing something active - such as cycling- where pads can easily slip and become very uncomfortable to wear, there's no such problems here. These stay in place and are comfortable.
It has to be said that the appearance isn't great. The 9 pack has three pairs with a blurry black floral design on the right hip, three pairs with a blurry black design on the left hip, and three with no hip design, just a printed bow, to indicate the front.
The designs are useful to work out which is the front and which is the back, especially handy if you are a carer trying to dress someone in a hurry.
 One tip is to put a pair of ordinary pants on over these if out for the day. If you have a standard pad with you, changing protection is far less hassle.
They do fit in public toilet disposal bins when used, so this shouldn't be an issue. .
PRODUCT: Always Discreet Boutique Underwear, Medium, Pack of 2

REVIEW_TITLE: Cute plastic uke, no frills, just the instrument. Suitable for absolute beginners, or those wanting a playable toy.
REVIEW:
A cute little plastic bodied ukulele, that is one step up from a toy.
It isn't rprobably suitable for any child who wants to play seriously long-term, but would be a good buy for those whose children are still testing the water with musical instruments.
If you have a child who is steadily working their way through after school clubs, or different hobbies, and giving up just after you have bought the relevant equipment, this may be for you, as a lower-cost investment.
The brightly coloured body may appeal to some children, and it certainly makes the ukulele stand out from others. I have the blue Rock Stars version, there's also a white one with blue butterflies.
The box contains the ukulele, and that's it, No tuning guide, first steps leaflet, first chords chart, or any sort of manufacturer's leaflet, in fact. There again, you're not paying for extras you can get elsewhere.
There are plenty of 'How To Play' guides for soprano ukuleles (this is a soprano ukulele) on YouTube, and if you have a smartphone, you can download a ukulele tuning app, if you don't own a headstock tuner.
 The good news is, it is genuinely tuneable, the tuning pegs work, the nylon strings do adjust, and you can tune it.
Mahogany bodied ukes are available from around �30, as a starting point, this isn't bad. If it's a passing fad, you're not left with an expensive memory, but something that you'd be fairly relaxed about donating to the charity shop.
PRODUCT: First Act Rock Stars Ukulele

REVIEW_TITLE: A Very British Vodka (and gin). Beautifully presented gift set, very well made, top quality throughout. Ideal brand introduction
REVIEW:
This is a touch of class. The Union Flag presentation box is beautifully made and more than protects the contents, but they are also in lovely heavyweight printed glass bottles that are almost too good for the recycling bin, they are little works of art.
Chase is an upmarket, premium brand, hugely proud of its British roots, and the packaging wholly reflects this.
The marmalade vodka was the one I first tried, the sharp taste was a pleasant surprise. This isn't a sticky sugary marmalade, it's got a nicely bittersweet tang to it.
Gin isn't my thing, but a sip was pleasantly smooth, and a passing gin fan liked the Chase gin very much. The full size bottle isn't cheap, it has to be said, but if someone is looking for a new brand to try, this could be a good introduction without breaking the bank.
The 'standard' vodka is a perfectly decent vodka, and vodka fans should appreciate the novelty of a purely British product.
Whilst it's true that you pay for the packaging with gift boxes, in the case of these three bottles you really do get some added value.
Giving a bottle as a gift, it's impossible to disguise the contents. Here you can do that, and also have the reassurance that the gift will arrive in one piece. The box is good enough to use as a decorative object afterwards, putting it in the recycling bin seems a real waste.
PRODUCT: Chase Brand Box Trio 5 cl (Case of 3)

REVIEW_TITLE: Not just for brows, works on cheekbones too. Retro pencil highlighter that is soft and easy to apply.
REVIEW:
Unfortunately my pencil was slightly damaged on arrival, with a cracked cap, but I was able to get a decent point on it with my ancient but trusty make-up sharpener. This took me back, I vaguely remember using a pencil like this donkey's years ago as a highlighter. This version is much better, and gives surprisingly good results.
The design enables precise application, but blends in well, it's a soft product that doesn't drag the skin. It's designed as an under-brow highlighter, but works on cheekbones too, for a bit of light-reflective lift.
It's compactly portable (when the cap fits) and with the off- white colour, easy to spot in your make-up bag or organiser. A good multi-use budget choice.
PRODUCT: Rimmel London Brow This Way Highlighting Pencil, Pearlescent, 1.4 g

REVIEW_TITLE: Low-rise, relatively low-absorbency discreet underwear. Ideal for more active lifestyles. Fit up to medium size 16.
REVIEW:
Comfortable, close fitting underwear that offers extra non-slip protection. These low-rise pants are normal absorbency, which isn't designed to cope with heavy loss. However, what they do offer is discreet protection, they fit well and are virtually undetectable.
The sizing is generous, for a 'medium'. I am a medium size 16 in clothing, and these are a snug, but not tight fit on me. These probably won't fit anyone larger than this dress size. Incontinence wear needs to be close fitting, but if in doubt, I would go a size up, to the large size.
I find that low-absorbency pants are suitable for activities like cycling, where it's possible for a standard pad to slip or twist quite easily, and become very uncomfortable to wear. Not to mention the risk of embarrassing leakage.
The low-rise cut of these is really practical when wearing standard-cut trousers, leggings or jeans. I've tried a previous version of these pants, and they were much higher. For anyone who dislikes the 'large-panr look' these are ideal. They have a feminine decoration, and I liked the printed bow decoration on the front. For carers, this is ideal, no confusion over what is the front or back of the garment when dressing.
Just to emphasise, that although these are underwear, they do only offer relatively low absorbency for pants, at normal absorbency.
PRODUCT: Always Discreet Underwear Incontinence Pants Normal, Medium, Pack of 2, 24-Count

REVIEW_TITLE: Beautifully packaged, really strongly scented hand cream. A top--quality cream that leaves hands cared for and perfumed.
REVIEW:
Gorgeous, a beautifully packaged hand cream that would make a lovely gift, or sit elegantly in the bathroom at home. The cream is presented in a sturdy sleeved box with the iconic Morris Strawberry Thief design in silver, both on the box, and on the tube.
 The print on the tube has a slightly textured finish, making it easy to grip with damp hands, I also liked the fact that the cream could be stood on its cap with no problems.
 I liked the scent of this,which was just as well, as it's really strong. I couldn't detect any scent of salt, I did wonder if this meant the cream had a gritty texture, on reading the description, but no, it's beautifully smooth and rich. It rubs in quickly with no hint of stickiness or oiliness, just a strong residual scent.
This is a bit too special to keep in the kitchen, and put on your hands after doing the dishes. I wouldn't recommend using this before preparing food, as I would be concerned about the perfume from the cream tainting food, but that's its only minus point.
An upmarket stockingfiller gift, beautifully packaged, that looks really classy.
PRODUCT: Morris & Co Pure Hand Cream, 100 ml

REVIEW_TITLE: Didn't want to eat, but felt bloated and gassy rather than just full. Not for me.
REVIEW:
I started to take these and had to stop, unfortunately. They certainly curbed my appetite, but the reason was that I felt bloated, full and unable to eat. I'm pretty sure that the effects that the manufacturers wanted wasn't as unpleasant for their customers as mine was.
There's also the point that the 1-2 glasses of water you drink with each tablet fills you up anyway, regardless.
I'm lucky in that I work from home, I would have not liked to have felt as ill as I did when out and about or at work. At my age (59) keeping my weight controlled is a worry, and an issue. I do welcome natural weight control methods, but perhaps this one isn't for me.
Disability forces me to have quite a sedentary lifestyle, so possibly those who are more active or in a different age range will benefit more from these.
USER_NAME: A. I. McCulloch; Natures Aid Ltd.
PRODUCT: Natures Aid GlucoSlim Weight Loss Capsules (500 mg Glucomannan, 120 Capsules, Clinically Proven, Weight Loss Aid, Vegan Society Approved, Made in the UK)

REVIEW_TITLE: Packed with sensible, practical advice on attaining and maintaining hormonal health, well-researched, good recipes.
REVIEW:
This has a lot to recommend it, in comparison with other books written advising women on hormonal health, which can offer piecemeal information, or expensive dietary regimes.
The book is of value to all women in the 35-65 age range, or for any woman concerned about hormonal imbalance, whatever their age..
Angelique Panagos writes in an approachable, easy-to-read style that presents complex information clearly and concisely. The book clearly lays out how hormones work on our bodies in the opening section, referring to 'the endocrine system's harmonic symphony and the monthly Viennese waltz'.
The second section, 'Showstoppers' is particularly valuable, outlining a range of conditions and factors that can knock everything out of tune, or stopping the show from going on - including environmental toxins, stress, our diet, and digestive functions,
Section three introduces the 'six pillars of balance', nourish, balance, nurture, cleanse, move and restore- to overcome these issues. Finally, there is 'Your Personal Plan' incorporating a food diary section with extensive advice on how to compile the diary, and identify foods that may be causing problems. Finally, there are meal plans, with almost 100 pages of tempting recipes.
What I really liked about this is the extensive cross-referencing.
 Each 'showstopper' has advice on which of the six pillars of balance are most relevant to the condition, Every recipe has a sub-heading indicating the particular value of the recipe - a recipe for simple home-made sauerkraut, indicates its value for gut health, and this recipe is cross-referenced in the health section of the book as well. The section is well illustrated, and the layout is clear,
Inevitably, some of the recipes include niche, somewhat expensive ingredients, but often, these are optional. There is an emphasis on eliminating sugar and gluten, and refined carbohydrates, but this looks like practical food that you - and your family - will want to eat.
At the end of the book there are extensive academic references for each chapter, clearly supporting the evidence the author gives.
Summary: A practical, realistic book, well-written, very readable, containing advice that is backed by research. Tempting everyday recipes to support the dietary advice given.
PRODUCT: The Balance Plan: Six Steps to Optimize Your Hormonal Health

REVIEW_TITLE: Worked nicely in my Krups Pixie Clips, just not sure it made much difference. Clear instructions supplied
REVIEW:
3.5 stars for this rounded up to four. These were used in a Krups Pixie Clips machine, in a soft water area. The recommendation is that these be used every thirty cups or so, but given that I'd had my machine for several years with no noticeable deterioration in delivery of the drink, I won't be doing this.
I bought a box of five capsules that came with a comprehensive multi-language instruction leaflet. There are several safety warnings about handling the capsules. Make sure the water tank is full, as you will need a lot of water.
They are used just in the same way as a standard capsule, with the difference that the button for an espresso is pressed first, to deliver a foaming cup of cleaning liquid.
 After waiting for one minute, the lungo button is pressed, then the used capsule is dropped in to the capsule container like any other. I used the used cleaning liquid dispensed by the machine to clean two stained cups before pouring it down the sink, it worked beautifully.
You will then need to repeatedly flush the machine by running it without a capsule in. Even after dispensing some 400 ml of water a cup of fruit tea had a slight white film. The taste wasn't affected, but do be aware.
I haven't noticed any positive or negative changes in flavour or dispensing speed.
I followed the instructions and cleaned the used capsule container carefully afterwards, disposing of the capsule carefully.
I'll use up the box of capsules I bought, but I'm not in a hurry to use the next one.
PRODUCT: Caffe Nu Nespresso Coffee Machine Cleaning Capsules, Pack of 5

REVIEW_TITLE: Unusual combination of micellar water and BB cream. BB cream a medium light shade. Two quality items.
REVIEW:
4.5 stars for this,rounded up to five. The combination of BB cream and micellar water struck me as slightly odd, and the presentation is quite basic.
 On the box, the BB cream is described as 'medium', which is perfect for me, usually, but on opening the box, the 50 ml bottle is marked as being 'light'. 'Light' thankfully, isn't a pale ivory shade, but it is quite mid-toned. It dispenses well, holding its shape well, not too fluid, or solid, and rubs in very easily for an even finish.
I've used this in the past, and although my skin is now mature, it still suits it well, giving it a fresher, even toned look that is very natural. At this time of year - early to mid autumn- an SPF of 15 is usually quite adequate.
The micellar water is described as being as an 'on the go' size. Personally speaking I prefer wipes in my handbag, rather than a bottle of liquid with a flip-top lid that could easily result in the contents of my bag having an unexpected bath. However, the actual micellar water is great, applied with a cotton wool pad there isn't a challenge it can't handle, in my experience, Even though this is a 'sensitive skin' variant, this works as well as anything I have tried. It promises a refreshed skin without rubbing, and it delivers this.
As a stocking-filler for older teens and twenties this is quite a good idea, there's nothing cheap about the contents. The packaging is fully recyclable, which is a bonus. Mine did arrive very battered, but the BB cream is separately boxed, so all is not lost if this is to be given as a gift.
PRODUCT: Garnier Micellar + BB Essentials Gift Set

REVIEW_TITLE: Easy and economical to apply, a concealer that really does work.
REVIEW:
This one's a winner - the ivory shade is a very pale peach tone , suitable for really fair skins.
The sponge tipped applicator is narrow enough for really precise application, and it blends in beautifully. I prefer the sponge tipped concealers to the roll-on type, which seem to drag the delicate skin under the eye, in my experience.
There's no such experience here, the sponge tip delivers just the right amount of concealer - useful, as the 6g, isn't a great amount.
A little more expensive than some, but you do get a quality finish with that, and it genuinely does conceal under-eye shadows.
 Recommended.
PRODUCT: L'Oreal Paris True Match The One Concealer, 1N Ivory

REVIEW_TITLE: Pack of five erasable pens. Enables errors to be easily disguised, doesn't damage paper.
REVIEW:
These are a bit more than okay, but only just. As others have said, what was sent for the purposes of the review, wasn't a multi-coloured pack, but a straightforward pack of two blue, two black, one red.
I can see these being of some value to children anxious to correct errors without crossing out, but other than that I can't quite see the point of them. The ink is lighter than standard inks, so that the marks made are fainter. The eraser -or rather, erasers - are hard plastic tips, rather than the soft rubber ones used with pencils.
No debris is left behind when you rub out, but it is still possible to detect what was written - you need to overwrite it, for this to become hidden. .
These may be of value if you are writing on something where an error just can't be made, a form that can't be copied or reprinted, for example. Children and teens may appreciate a bit of novelty value, but do be aware, if you can rub out the writing, so can others. It may be wise not to use this on anything that is really important. .
PRODUCT: UF-220 Signo TSI Erasable Rollerball Pens, Red, Sky Blue, Green, Pink, Violet Erasable Ink, Medium Nib, Package of 5

REVIEW_TITLE: Large = smallish size 14. Good quality cotton, unusual ruched sleeves. Quite short in the body.
REVIEW:
At the time of ordering 'Large = size 14' wasn't stated on the description, it is now.
The issue of size 14 being a large aside, this is a T-shirt suitable for women of 5'7'' and below, unless you don't mind exposing a bit of back or midriff. It's quite short in the body.
The white cotton is a good quality weight, and the unusual ruched sleeves add some extra interest and detail. It was snug on me, as I'm nearer a 16 than a 14.
This could be dressed up with some jewellery for a smart-casual summer evening, if we get one warm enough to wear short sleeves ever again in the North of England. I'll be wearing mine with a pinafore style top as it's just too short on me, at 5' 9'', unfortunately.
PRODUCT: FIND Women's Ruched Tie Sleeve T-Shirt, White, 14 (Manufacturer size: Large)

REVIEW_TITLE: Not for me, as lips stayed sticky. Pioneer a really retro carmine shade, ideal for the Fifties look. Stain lasts well.
REVIEW:
This is a beautifully packaged product, with a touch of class. The shade I used, Pioneer, is a retro carmine shade, a real Fifties red, and makes an impact, but unfortunately for me, the experience didn't live up to the looks.
 It took me back to the first time I used a lip gloss and left most of it behind on glasses and cups, as well as glueing my lips together. It stayed slightly tacky throughout the time I had it on.
It's not a gloss product, it is completely matte, which left me wondering what the formulation was.
The USP of the product is that the colour lasts, it does, in that staining does remain on the lips it's true, but it also remained on what I touched with my lips.
I liked the pointed end of the foam applicator which made it easy to get a precise line, and makes this three stars instead of two. If you want a really bold carmine, and aren't too bothered about eating and drinking in wear, this ticks the boxes.
PRODUCT: Maybelline Superstay 24 Matte Ink Lipstick, 20 Pioneer, 5 ml

REVIEW_TITLE: Fragrance & colour free bio powder. Very good results with light to medium soiling. A lot of powder needed for heavy staining.
REVIEW:
