This is a biological washing product for whites and colours, specifically designed for sensitive skin, with no added colour or perfume. The packaging is designed for the European market, with a number of languages on it. I've tried several washes with it on both cotton and synthetics.
The dosage recommendation is in ml, which is a little odd for a powder product.
I found it most effective on lightly soiled to medium soiled garments, using the recommended soft water dosages of 71 ml. Clothes felt and looked clean.
 The dosage instructions on the back of the pack advised using 125 ml for heavy soiling in a soft water area. That's quite a lot of powder.
 I used my own marked measuring scoops to measure out the correct amount. One ketchup stain on a top was removed, but a mud smeared pair of socks that had fallen from the washing line still bore faint traces of a mark.
My machine is a Bosch, and my normal biological gel and scoop of stain remover would have removed the stain without extra product. I'll use stain remover powder with this in future, and the powder at a lower dose. This way I'll get nearer the 18 washes per pack that the product is supposed to contain.
Like most biological products, it can't be used with wool or silk.
PRODUCT: Neutral 0% Sensitive Colour Washing Powder 72 Washes 4.752kg (18 Washes x 4)

REVIEW_TITLE: Dogs love this, good enough to be used as a training treat. Quality duck and trout based kibble.
REVIEW:
For dogs with itchy skin and digestive problems, a quality grain-free kibble is often the answer to their issues. This Barking Heads grain-free kibble contains no wheat and is predominately duck and trout-based, with vegetable additions.
 This went down really well with our two Springers, who had it mixed in with their normal working dog kibble. The 2kg bag won't last long enough to enable a total switch, but it's been really well tolerated.
The cartoon-style packaging also makes a cute statement, and the fold-over bag helps keep the product fresh.
It went down fast, and didn't cause any issues exiting.
The meat based pellets also work as training treats for our two, they are of such high quality. Pieces are a sensible size, suitable for all but the smallest mini breeds of adult dogs. Empty bowls tell their own story.
PRODUCT: Barking Heads Dog Food Quackers Grain Free Duck 2kg

REVIEW_TITLE: Eyecatching packaging, great mascara inside, good brush, easy to apply. Didn't flake, blob or give panda eyes. Recommended.
REVIEW:
Great! A straightforward brush, a lovely true deep black, a stylish item that's easy to find in the make up bag, thanks to the eye-catching colour. There's nothing to dislike about this mascara from L'Oreal.
Nothing gimmicky about this, it goes on easily and stays on, doesn't flake or leave you looking like a panda inside five minutes.
The brush isn't oversized, but picks up lashes and applies well. It dries quickly, no blobs, smudges, or bits dropping off and ruining your look.
If there is a con, it's that there's not a huge amount of product for your money, but that's not worth deducting a star for.
It removed easily using a standard cotton wool pad and oil-based eye make-up remover.
Fingers crossed that this won't dry out quickly, as it's going to be a favourite.
PRODUCT: L'Oreal Paris Paradise Mascara, Black

REVIEW_TITLE: Unusual, classy shower curtain, easy to fit, survived a wash in the machine on a 'delicates' setting. No rings supplied.
REVIEW:
This is an unusually designed shower curtain, best used with a vinyl shower liner such as AmazonBasics Clear PVC Shower Liner 180 x 180 cm. I have a black and white themed bathroom that is well-lit and not too gloomy, but I liked the extra light that this gave compared to my usual black fabric shower curtain.
For the purposes of the review, I held my breath and put it through the wash on a quick setting for delicate fabrics- basically a hand wash- after a week's use, Rather than use a detergent, I used 'Stardrops' - Stardrops Original All round cleaner 750 milliliter I did wonder how the PVC panel would stand up to my machine. The answer was, surprisingly well. There was no sign of deterioration from being spun in the machine.
 I never bother line drying my shower curtains, I usually refit them whilst still damp and open out the curtain fully so that it dries in place. This does away with having to dry the curtain indoors in wet weather.
Fitted, this is fractionally longer than my standard 180x180 shower curtain liner, and with the weight of the liner holding it down, it seems to stay in place well.
The clear window does give it an extra touch of style. If you already have shower curtain rings, don't discard them before buying this, they aren't supplied. I used the existing rings which were supplied with my Amazon Basics Shower Liner, and all was well. (If your existing white plastic rings look a bit grubby, I've found that a. magic sponge and plain water cleans them quite effectively)
PRODUCT: InterDesign Fabric Shower Curtain with Window for Bathroom, Charcoal/Clear, 183 x 183 cm

REVIEW_TITLE: An introduction to the subject. Of some value, but not if you have existing knowledge, unless a concise summary is needed.
REVIEW:
3.5 stars for this, rounded up to four, but it could easily have been rounded down.
I've really procrastinated over reviewing this book. On the one hand, it's packed full of good advice on being in touch with your emotions, but on the other, it's also full of generally sweeping statements which the majority of people who would pick up this sort of book in the first place would know already.
The real problem with texts like this is that those who could benefit most from them never read them, or glance through them, and dismiss the content. The Pocketbook is a concise guide and introduction to being more self-aware, and its handy format may appeal to some,
After mulling it over at length, I've decided that yes, there probably is a place for this in the market. It's a clear introduction to the subject, some may benefit from it, but the majority of those attracted by the title will know this already.
PRODUCT: Emotional Intelligence Pocketbook: Little Exercises for an Intuitive Life

REVIEW_TITLE: Very well presented set. Super-efficient little epilator, ideal for de-fuzzing the upper lip. Slightly overpriced?
REVIEW:
4.5 stars for this, rounded up to five.
This is a really efficient little device, I've used an earlier version of this product in the past, and was delighted to be offered it to review. One small problem was that I'd just epilated my upper lip with a standard epilator, and had to wait a few weeks before being able to fully test this.
I'm delighted to say that the efficiency hasn't changed.
The little epilation head grips the finest of hairs as it spins, and briskly tugs it out by the roots. There's a sharp prickling sensation, which quickly passes. I do find the sensation more painful than tweezering, and about as painful as threading. It's more than bearable, but you are still glad when it's over.
I used my epilator in the bathroom with sunlight coming in through the window and was fascinated to observe a small cloud of fine golden hairs rise in the air as the hair was plucked out. It certainly reassured me that the epilator was working well Afterwards my lip felt totally smooth and there was no redness visible. This is ideal for use if you don't wear make up to conceal any skin redness or blemishes.
I prefer quite gentle methods of facial cleansing, so have only been using the brush twice a week, but I'm pleased with the results I've got with this. The brush whisks away dead cells and leaves my face glowing gently. For my mature skin, twice a week is ideal.
 The replacement heads are expensive, though. It's worth taking the best care of the one supplied.
I do appreciate the storage pouch that came with this as a way of keeping everything together, though the current RRP does seem high compared with my previous, pouchless battery operated epilator. You pay a lot for the little mirror and bag.
PRODUCT: Braun FaceSpa 851V 3-in-1 Facial Epilator For Hair Removal And Cleansing Brush, System

REVIEW_TITLE: Travel-friendly alternative to fridge-based products. Seemed to work just as well as these, plus extra B6 and folic acid.
REVIEW:
Having completed a course of these tablets, I can recommend them as an easy to take and well tolerated alternative to fridge-based products. I am female, so was interested in the fact that they are directed towards women.
I take a regular probiotic product that is fridge based, and I appreciated the fact that I didn't have to buy or store that for a month, I experienced no unwelcome symptoms during this period, and in my opinion it was genuinely as effective,
I'm not so wholly convinced that I needed the extra vitamin B6 or folic acid, I already have a diet that is rich in these, but for women wanting a supplement that covers several bases, this may well be a good idea.
I'm not sure as to whether I will continue to take these long-term, as they are expensive on a per-day cost, compared with my normal regime.
However if convenience outweighs cost for you, then yes, they are a good buy.
PRODUCT: Bioglan Biotic Balance Healthy Digestion for Women

REVIEW_TITLE: Review of 'Fat Dog Slim', Great choice for weight management for older pets too. Dogs loved this tummy-friendly product.
REVIEW:
Whilst Fat Dog Slim is designed for overweight pets, it's also a very good choice for anyone looking to manage the weight of their dog with a view to helping with joint problems or weight gain post-neutering, which can sometimes be an issue.
Visually, it is quite pinkish in colour for something with a high chicken content, but obviously it's not breast or thigh meat that makes it in to dog food.
Our elderly Springer female had this with a Barking Heads duck based kibble and her normal working dog kibble mixed in, and she absolutely loved it.
She and her younger Springer 'brother' only have wet food as a treat, but there were absolutely no digestive issues with this. What went in was appreciated greatly, and what came out was indicative of a system that was working well.
If there is a con, it is that this isn't the cheapest of foods, but with an 85% meat content it isn't surprising.
Another plus point is that the lids are ring-pull style. Great if you have dogs who just can't wait for their food (our younger Springer needs a puzzle bowl to slow him down). He appreciated the fact that his wet food treat arrived thirty seconds earlier than usual.
Recommended. Ours aren't fussy, but they absolutely loved it.
PRODUCT: Barking Heads Wet Fat Dog Slim Dog Food Tins, Pack of 6

REVIEW_TITLE: Light and pleasant to apply, genuinely does make a difference, and helps your foundation stay in place.
REVIEW:
This primer does exactly what you'd expect a 'primer' to do, it gives a surface for foundation to cling to, in the same way as paint primer gives a key for further coats of paint.
Any further comparisons with paint primer would do this an injustice, this is a really lovely product, lighter than most, that provides a surface for your foundation. I used it with a Bourjois foundation that is a current favourite, and was delighted at the result, I normally only look like that in a very flattering light. It genuinely does help to even the skin out.
As the weather becomes cooler, having foundation slip from your face in warm conditions, becomes less of an issue, but this gave me confidence that it would help everything to stay in place should we ever get a warm day again up here in the North of England.
It is quite a light formulation, I won't be using it everyday, but it's definitely one for when I want to look my best.
PRODUCT: Max Factor Smooth Miracle Primer, 30 ml, Translucent

REVIEW_TITLE: Creatine with a buzz, and cheaper than the off-the-shelf supermarket products. Pleasant flavour too. Recommended.
REVIEW:
The Watermelon version of this easily-mixed powder makes a slightly sharp, not-too-sweet pleasant tasting drink, that dissolves easily with minimal residue. There are two dosage levels, 15g of powder with 300ml of water gives you a max strength dose, 7.5g with 200ml of water gives a standard strength drink. A clearly marked scoop is provided, and it's easy to measure the correct amount.
This was tested by my adult son, who works out regularly, on full strength, after a couple of days to get his system used to it. He felt he probably could have gone straight on to the full strength, as he is a regular user of similar products.
I use energy drinks myself as a boost when cycling, which is the only safe exercise I can currently participate in. I tried it at the recommended half-dose before a ride, as I'm not a serious exercise freak. I definitely felt a buzz from the taurine and caffeine. This works out significantly cheaper than the best-selling energy drink, with the added bonus of creatine.
 This will prepare eight litres of drink at standard dose, and six litres at the full-strength dose for the same price as four litres of an energy drink that just has taurine and caffeine. I wouldn't have described the taste as watermelon, but more like cranberry. Anyway I liked it, so did my son,. It's not often that supplements come in cheaper than supermarket versions of something, but this one does.
PRODUCT: AC8 Xtreme | Watermelon | Pre Workout Supplement | Energy & Muscle | 20-40 Servings | 300 grams

REVIEW_TITLE: Good formulation for dry skin, elegant and novel pump design. Formulated to disguise redness but no SPF and just 30ml.
REVIEW:
This is an elegantly packaged product that trades heavily on novelty, the two test-tube type phials within the bottle each deliver a measured amount of product that is mixed as it comes through the nozzle in to a fairly light cream, The cream has a faint greenish tinge, suitable for disgusing redness.
I don't have particularly sensitive skin and have experienced absolutely no reaction with this. It's quite pleasant to use, although it didn't rub in quite as well as I expected from the consistency. It 'sat' on my skin a little. At first I thought this was because I was using a serum, but even without this the results were the same.
Even though I have quite mature skin, I suspect that my skin isn't quite dry enough for this. My skin did feel pampered, and there was no pilling or reaction when used with other products.
At just 30ml, this won't last long when put in to daily use. Less is more with this. I feel, and I will be alternating this with my usual products, which have an SPF. This doesn't, in common with many products for sensitive skin, and this is something that is important for me.
It is a beautiful product, but the lack of SPF and the fact that this is little more than a month's supply, if used daily, brings it down one star for me. I've also had experience with pumps of a similar design failing, and wasting product.
At this price, this is something you definitely don't want to happen.
PRODUCT: ELEMIS BIOTEC Skin Energizing Sensitive Day Cream - Skin Activating Day Cream 30ml

Firstly, I'd like to say that as far as actually shaving goes, I can't fault the quality of shave that the Aquatouch gives. I generally like a really close shave with a conventional blade, and although the Aquatouch doesn't quite give that, it's certainly a good second best.
The problem is that I have now had two of these shavers die on me with basically the same problem. Each of them was barely over a year old when they developed what seems to be a pretty common fault with them, whereby they stop charging and the LED power indicator just flashes when you try to turn it on.
I opened both units up when they became faulty, and in both cases I would say that the issue plain and simply was water ingress. Moisture seems to quite easily be able to get into the plastic housing that the internal PCB is housed inside, and as per usual, water and electrics is a bad combination and components have clearly been damaged. Opening up and drying the second shaver out did revive it temporarily, but after a few weeks it died again and couldn't be coaxed back into life.
I would also like to say that although I did wet shave with these shavers, it was limited to a rinse in the sink after use, and they were not subject to use in a shower etc.
I purchased my second one of these as I genuinely liked the first one and as stated it does perform well when working. However having now had two fail with this identical problem, I now opted for an alternative brand instead.

At the time of writing these LED bulbs are �5.99. I bought 2 of them to try out in my bathroom which has a light fitting capable of holding x3 GU10 halogen bulbs. I've only ever had x2 50W bulbs in it at once though which has always provided sufficent light. My first impression after replacing the 2 halogens with these fancy LED ones was very good, the light was evenly spread and lit the whole room nicely and they were the same colour as before. However when my wife went into the bathroom (I never told her I'd made the switch) she noticed straight away that the room was slightly dimmer than usual and started giving me a bit of grief. She was right as always though and they arn't quite as bright, so I've mixed in one of the standard halogens to make it x2 LED and x1 Halogen. Everything is all good now and neither of us can notice the difference. I'm going to buy a 3rd one so I can try out having all 3 as LED and I'll update this review with my thoughts. Google tells me that a 50W halogen bulb emits 800-950 lumens of light, so that explains why these LED ones aren't going to be as bright at only 460 lumens. The energy saving however is fantastic and that's a big plus point! Going by my limited experience I would say that LED bulbs currently aren't quite bright enough on their own for general purpose lighting. If you're using lots of them under your kitchen cupboards then you'll have no problems at all, but if you're intending on using 2,3,4 of them to light your whole room then you may find that you need to mix a standard bulb in.

REVIEW_TITLE: Too small and too big at the same time!
REVIEW:
Oh dear.
I have worn nothing but nose screws since I got my nose pierced 2 years ago. I am very happy inserting nose screws without a mirror and find them very comfortable to wear, but this was a whole different story.
Material: The BioFlex material is adequate - flexible enough to be bent during insertion but firm enough to go back into shape.
Shape: This is the where we find ourselves in trouble. The post of the screw (the bit that actually sits inside the piercing) is far too short. I don't have a big nose and have often found other posts of nose screws too long to be comfortable. This post is FAR too short and subsequently squeezes my piercing, making it immediately painful to the point that I had to take it out within less than a minute. The curved screw part was also way, way too long and stuck out of my nose by a few millimeters.
Colour: It's a cloudy translucent colour with a shiny finish, making it slightly too obvious when in place.
Stud: The top of the stud is slightly thicker than the 1mm post. I think if the post had been long enough, this would have been fine. However, because the post is far too short I found that the stud part was pulled down into my piercing. This was obviously really painful.
Overall, I have to give it 1/5. Painful to insert, painful to wear and painful to take out. Ouch.

I've never written a product review despite being an active Amazon customer for many years, but these headphones have spurred me to change the habit of a lifetime.
They may be colourful and cheap, but the quality is beyond poor. The sound that comes out of these can only be described as a muffled mess of crap. Listening to a song with three vocal harmony lines, I could only make out one of them - the others were indistinguishable from the instrumental harmony backing. They manage to blur all the sound into one awful mess whilst remaining loud enough to cause actual pain to my ears.
I read the reviews of these before I bought them, but as there were some good ratings I chose to ignore the bad ones. I urge you not to make the same mistake I did - do not buy these. I have also purchased other in-ear headphones from Amazon (Exspect EX882) for only a few pounds more, and they are in a different league - clear sound, comfortable and good quality. Learn from my mistake and DO NOT BUY THESE!
PRODUCT: Groove GVEB3/PK Earbuds Earphone - Pink

REVIEW_TITLE: "It doesn't take a genius to see this girl's outstanding!"
REVIEW:
When I first heard "Other Side Of The World", I thought "OK, this isn't anything special... nice song but still..."
Then my friend Polly played me a song on her iPod called "Black Horse and the Cherry Tree" and I thought "Woah! Who wrote this?!"
I looked at the artist and I saw KT Tunstall. From then on, I was hooked. The very next day, I ran into town and bought the first copy of Eye to the Telescope I could lay my hands on. My favourite tracks quickly formed into the shapes of "Heal Over" and "Suddenly I See" (and Black Horse...)
The tracks range from mellow (Universe And U) to bluesy-jazz (Black Horse...), and even the worst track (Another Place To Fall) I would class as brilliantly-original!
But the one thing that really got me hooked is Tunstall's passion for her music, and her spectacular guitar-playing. The rawness of some of her tracks (Other Side Of The World, Silent Sea, Minature Disasters) make this probably the best album sitting on my shelf (well, that's the album cover - the CD hasn't come out of my CD player since I bought it!).
My favourite out of all of them would have to be Black Horse and the Cherry Tree. The blend of funky jazzy drumming, and daring (appeearingly) non-sensical lyrics make for the best song I've heard since since... forever!
Seriously, if you buy one album this year, make it this one. KT Tunstall is set to be THE biggest talent to come out of Scotland for years. Get ahead, and get on the Tunstall wagon NOW! You won't regret it...!
PRODUCT: Eye To The Telescope

REVIEW_TITLE: I have a TomTom multisports GPSwatch, which is currently away for repair or replacement ...
REVIEW:
I have a TomTom multisports GPS watch,which is currently away for repair or replacement by the manufacturer as the directional pad bezel keeps falling out,rendering me kinda stumped in sticky situations,whiich is a common issue with this watch apparently. So,i saw this FR15 on a �59 lightning deal,bougth it,with certain reservations,and heres my initial review,
The strap. It may sound petty ,but the strap,and in particular,the little bit that sticks out when you secure the watch on your arm,locks into place & theres no need to be constantly adjusting it. I never knew how good a feature this is until i got the FR15. Marvellous.
I was worried about Bluetooth sync to the mobile app,until i realised,the FR15 lets you see a detailed summary of all the stats from your run on the watch immediately after. This pleased me immensely & softened the blow of having no wireless sync facility. All the stats are there. Brilliant. Not a problem then.
No altimeter on the FR15?------The watch uses the GPS data to work out your altitude accurately. Again,i was mighty surprised & pleased by this. Comparing the same run on the two different devices produces identical altitude data,
Its got a back light button,as opposed to a touchscreen light which would come on all the time on the TomTom,its got a fully fledged fitness tracker onboard,and.....and.....this is the big thing for me.....the indoor training feature is a godsend. No need for a GPS fix,just hit the start button,press down,select No GPS,and the device will track you & your heartrate monitor (ANT+) until the proverbial cows come home. Perfect for indoor football & kettlebells etc etc
All in all,delighted with the purchase so far. Worth �59 ?? Definitely. Best watch in the world??? No.....worth �59??? No brainer.
God bless us,everyone

REVIEW_TITLE: Decent Mid Range Home Theatre System
REVIEW:
I'd been doing my homework on a Home Cinema System but was finding it hard to come up with one at the right price that had everything I wanted.
When this one took a �30 price drop I decided to go for it.
I've had it a week now and my impressions are as follows.
The price is good, I bought from Amazon when they dropped to �219 from �250, other retailers sell this system from between �249 and �349 so it looked like a good deal to me.
 The good points are it sounds good, big sound from nice slim tallboy speakers and good bass from a sub that's compact and easy to fit in your room, I've seem some that are huge. The blu ray player does it's job well and is easy to set up and operate and plays many formats including any discs you burn yourself.
My negatives would be
No bluetooth, it says you can connect through DNLA but I am finding this hard to set up. I made a mistake though and thought it had bluetooth, I went by the specs on another sellers website which were incorrect. If you go to Samsung's website you can actually download the instruction manuals for all their products which is good to give you the correct list of specifications and an idea of how easy it will be to operate before you buy anything.
The online features are accessible through a wired internet connection only, no wireless. I am using this upstairs well away from my phone line but all the features I would get like Netflix Iplayer etc I get these though my smart TV so that's not a problem, if not for this I would have had to get a system with wireless internet which is a bit more expensive.
The glossy black finish is a bit of a fingerprint magnet, I'm forever having to wipe everything with a cloth after using it.
If you play a movie off the USB port there does not appear to be any kind of option to resume play from where you left off if you decide to make any changes, you have to go back to the beginning and start forwarding back to where you were - annoying.
And lastly I'm still tinkering with the settings but so far when watching 5.1 surround movies I find if I get the speech to a nice level I can hear clearly when the special effects come in they are deafening so I have to sit on the volume control going up and down as required for the neighbors sake. I might figure this one out in time.
All in all it's a decent enough system though.
Edit - It's now a couple of months out of the years warranty and has now developed a problem, the unit will no longer power on with the TV using the HDMI CEC feature, I now have to put the unit on with it's own remote and when doing this there is no sound from any source, TV or the Blu Ray player or built in radio. The odd thing is if I do a reset from the settings menu it will work as it should but only until it is powered off at the mains where it just goes back to the problems I described earlier. Been doing this for weeks now and after taking it to a Samsung Repair Centre they think a new circuit board is required at a cost of �70 so I'm not all that enamoured with it now.
PRODUCT: Samsung HT-F4550 3D 500W 5.1 Channel Blu-ray Home Cinema System with 4x Tall Speakers

Anyone looking at this might ask why they should buy one when cordless mice can be bought for less than a tenner but this really is a quality product and if you stick with it you will never look back.

REVIEW_TITLE: Poor Design On What Could Have Been a Good Product
REVIEW:
I bought this Cooks grill toaster and after 10 mins. decided it was unfit for purpose.
The main issues I have with this are -
1. The toaster part is too shallow, you get 3/4 of a slice of bread nicely toasted and the top 1/4 comes out undone.
2. The grill part is too shallow and you can't make use of both heating elements, you can insert a solid steel tray and a drip tray to grill bacon, chops etc but only the top grill is browning the bottom grill is only heating whatever you have in the tray.

REVIEW:
This Freelander PD10 Typhoon is a very decent solid tablet with a real quality feel to it and is Freelander's flagship device, I bought the original PD10 and the fact it was so good was what persuaded me to go for this instead of the likes of the Amazon Kindle Fire or Google Nexus which are either a similar price or cheaper in the case of the Kindle Fire.
Let's start with the positives, the screen is fantastic a really crisp and clear 1024x600 WSVGA IPS which is quick to respond to swipes and touches. The dual core processor is fast and efficient and it boots up in fast mode like a smartphone in seconds. The GPS works well, fast to obtain a fix and keep it, no problems here. You have full access to the Google Play Market and everything runs well - 3D games, Youtube, Iplayer, etc. all works great, I have yet to experience any problems with anything I have downloaded from the Play Market. Movies play great as well, MP4, AVI etc all play spot on.
This tablet is also what's known as a 'Monster Phone' you can make and receive phone calls with it but be aware you can't hold it to your ear like a phone as the mic. to speak into is positioned high on the side so you have to hold it in front of you so you look like a candidate on The Apprentice with the loudspeaker activated talking into it. If this is acceptable the phone facility does work well as does the 3G if you wanted to fit a data only sim card instead of the phone sim so you have mobile internet on the go only without the calls feature.
The built in speaker is OK but not great, this is the norm with all tablets though, even the top of the range ones, music sounds OK on their speakers but is spot on with headphones and this Freelander Typhoon is no different, when used as the loudspeaker for the phone it's nice and clear and loud enough, same when watching movies or listening to music.
Bluetooth works well as does the wi-fi, range is decent and even though this tablet has a part aluminium back which can decrease wi-fi range over plastic backed tablets this is not the case here.
The 4 gig of internal storage might not sound impressive but you can slot in a max of a 32 gig Micro SD card which boosts it right up, I have just given the internal memory over to the device and everything I download goes onto the card.
The only negatives I have found is the built in camera flash is pathetic and not worth having, just looks like a dull LED. The 5 MP rear camera and 2 MP front cameras are OK and do the job fine but are nothing fantastic, better firmware might improve things here.
Although the auto rotate function does work for some reason the home screens can only be viewed in vertical position, when you run any apps though it goes to horizontal no problem if required, I downloaded an app called 'Forced Rotation' and this fixed this issues.
I have also found with mine that occasionally when you try to press and hold an app to move or delete it that it won't do this and just opens, this happens rarely and if you go off the screen and back to it everything is fine, not sure what's going on here, hopefully firmware updates will cure this, good thing is Freelander do support their products with regular updates and improvements.
Also the bottom menu buttons illuminate which is something the older Freelanders never had and is an improvement but the backlight looks a little cheap and could have been done better IMO.
Finally be aware that Freelander have changed the docking port on this PD10 Typhoon from the standard Android type you find on most phones and tablets to the multi pin type you find only on the Samsung Galaxy Tab it is a genuine Samsung USB and mains charger you are supplied with your device, so now if you want to use the HDMI and hook the device up to your TV it's no longer a case of buying a �3 cable, now you have to buy a Samsung converter cable which is around �40, apparently cheaper ones are in development but they are not here just yet, not sure if an Ipad cable would work either. Luckily I have other tablets in the house I can still use to watch movies off the tablet on my TV or this would really have annoyed me. I suppose a plus to this might be that there are products and accessories out there designed for the Galaxy Tab and possibly Ipad that will work on this device as well.
All in all I am very happy with my purchase and would recommend one as it really has a huge spec and range of features, but probably only if the integrated GPS and mobile data and calling features appeal to you as this is what swung it for me as this tablet is priced a good bit dearer than previous PD10's so you do have to weigh up what you want from it more carefully. Tablets always seem to be a compromise though - there's always some feature or other missing that would make it ideal but this PD10 Typhoon really has the full compliment of features.
PRODUCT: PD10 typhoon IPS Dual Core Tablet PC 7inch Capacitive Screen MTK6577 4GB ROM GSM 3G Phone GPS Bluetooth, Free Leather Case Black

REVIEW:
Got this through recently and I must admit to being very pleasantly surprised at how good it is. I opted for this 7" tablet primarily because it had GPS and was on a par price wise with GPS navigation devices so I figured this would do so much more so opted for this instead and I'm really glad I did.
This tablet is plastic but is not overly cheap feeling, the screen is very responsive and accepts swipes and touches just fine. Wi-fi appears decent and I can go anywhere in the house without losing signal, I did notice a lot of reviews of other budget tablets slating the wi-fi range.
So far everything I have downloaded from Google play has worked fine, Iplayer, Youtube, games, etc. all good. It performs tasks quickly and smoothly. A nice feature is that it comes with a voice recognition program for browsing the internet and stating destinations for the navigation software which works great, even with my Scottish accent I can just press the mic icon and say what website I want or where I want to go with the GPS navigation and it gets it right every time, saves typing them in.
The GPS aspect of this device works fine as well, I live in a low signal area difficult to get a GPS lock and this tablet manages a GPS fix from cold in around 30 seconds with no external antenna required either.
If I have to find gripes they would be as follows, the volume and on/off keys on the side are sometime easily pressed when holding the tablet, they would have been better placed up top away from the home and navigation buttons on the lower front of the tablet rather than down beside them.
There is only the most basic of instruction booklets provided, I am a total newcomer to Android and tablet devices but after a days playing around with it I had it figured out so it's no biggie.
Finally everything is in English apart from this one program in Chinese which I take to be something essential to it's operation as it's a sizeable program and there is no option to allow you to remove it, again it's no big deal, you just hide the icon away out of sight.
All in all I would recommend this tablet, I bought this as a budget entry into the world of Android tablets just to see how I liked it and I love it, It's got me wanting a 10" device now. I've no idea how they can give you all this spec for the price, the PD10 is �70 odd quid and the PD20 seems to be pretty much the same device with the addition of the car holder and charger to make use of the sat nav in your vehicle.

REVIEW_TITLE: Nearly gave up but it works great with a couple of tweeks
REVIEW:
Interesting product this. I have after something like this for sometime - ie something I can use to control my kids internet use. Yes you can do it on your router but this has a relativly simple interface. To be honest I nearly gave up on this and it was only because I was reviewing it that I persisted. For starters I could not find anything in the limited quick start guide that said where to get the app to control it so I headed over to the iOS app store and found what I thought was the correct app which is My Circle - This is in fact incorrect despite it being done by the same maufacturer and is simple called circle which is a little hard to find as a number of other apps come up before it. Also remember that you need to log into circle on your phone before it will communicate with the app. You then tell it which router to connect to and add the password. Okay so fairly simple except you have to log in and out of both Circle and your router a number of times on Wifi (the app now expalins when to do this). It was at this point that I nearly gave up as it then proceeded to find every device connected to the router. In our house that is well over 20 ie various smart plugs, laptops etc all of which I did not want to control via Circle. All I wanted to do was assign my childrens Kindle, ipad and phones to the circle and I could not find a way to do it. So I emailed there tech support department and they came back pretty swiftly. Essentially (and I will copy and paste there reply below) you need to go into device settings and when you see a device that you do not want to manage then simpy click on the device, then click on 'assign device' and then add it to Unmanaged devices instead of a profile (if you tell the app just to ignore it then it will keep appearing.
I have now set up individual profiles for each of my children and only add the devices I want to manage for them into that profile. Now I can set how much time they can go on the internet, which apps they can and cannot use and even set up different days ie weekends with later nights and longer amounts of time on there devices. Brilliant. I now love the device.
It takes a while getting there, but persistance pays off and I now think for anyone concerned with the amount of internet time there kids are using this works well.
This is the response from Circle:
Circle detects all devices on the network. There is no way to only add certain devices. You can however set your home profile to "none" as a filter level and only create profiles for your children and add their devices to that profile! You can find an article on how to find individual devices on our help site

REVIEW_TITLE: OK For The Price But With Concerns...
REVIEW:
First impressions out of the box the mirror looks very nice. The chrome coloured edging of the mirror is a little bit too bling for my taste but I have gotten used to it. The mirror works fairly well as a mirror and blue tint is noticeable at first but easy to ignore. If I get another mirror DVR I will probably get one where the screen is on the left hand side. This means that you will have more area to view as a mirror as I find I do not look at the displayed cameras when driving forward but do require a mirror.
Installing the unit was easy using the two rubber straps to attach it to your existing mirror and the power/rear camera plugs will only fit in their own sockets, but running the cables was difficult, not helped by the rear camera connector at the camera end being bigger than it needed to be. I had to shave it thinner with a stanley knife to get it squeeze through the head lining. The manual is nicely printed but like other reviewers it is next to useless as the information is not thorough enough and the font used is far too small to read easily.
As for setting it up. It is fairly intuitive and the menus are more or less self explanatory once you access the correct mode which is either video or stills mode.
I have the rear camera which is about the size of a sugar cube inside the car looking out the rear window which does a good enough job but the video quality is not great but just adequate.
After a few weeks of using the thing day to day I find it is a little temperamental and will record things I estimate about 98% of the time. Something of concern is that the little red recording graphic is not always displayed in the top left hand corner every time I turn the ignition. This leaves me unsure as to whether it has started recording anything. It also seems to occasionally miss 2 or 3 seconds when ending 1 video file and starting the next one. I have also found that sometimes the video files are only about 8 or 9 seconds long mid journey. This is not a problem but just odd as I would have thought that all the videos would be 3 minutes long unless I turn the ignition off prematurely.
A summary of the pros and cons
Pros
1. Video sharpness of the forward facing camera is OK although not a lot of detail in shadows
2. Looks quite good when mounted to the existing mirror.
3. Menu's are fairly intuitive when in the correct mode.
4. The rear view camera cable length is good. My car is 5.1m long so the cabin area is huge and there was still some cable length left to site it further away thus giving me more siting options.
5. There is reasonable range of left/right movement for the forward facing camera but I would have liked more.
6. The box it comes in is quite nice i.e. better than I expected.
Cons
1. You have to have the camera video always displayed. If you get the screen to turn off after a few minutes it does not record any video. This is a nuisance as it is distracting when driving along and also when you want to quickly check whats behind you and use the mirror as a mirror. This may be just fault with my unit.
2. The video from the rear facing camera is back to front for example number plates are back to front and it looks like you are driving on the wrong side of the road. This would probably require explaining to an insurer if I had to present them with any video evidence.
3. The dynamic range of the forward facing camera is not particularly good i.e. there is a lack of detail when recording in the shadows. This does not bode well for night time recording which I have still to test.
4. The manual is fairly useless. It is difficult to read due to the very small font and is not very thorough.
5. The unit looks like it was designed for the left hand drive market as the forward facing camera is on the left and the lenses range of movement is limited mainly to the left/middle view. This can be adjusted by moving the whole mirror but then your view in the mirror is out of adjustment.
6. The mirror sits about 1 cm or so below my existing mirror mainly because of its row of buttons. This does not sound like much but because the mirror is so large it obscures my view through the windscreen somewhat and I have to duck my head to see properly.
7. If someone else drives the car they will invariably adjust the mirror throwing the view of the forward facing camera out of alignment but this will be the same for all mirror DVR's.
8. The unit itself is a discreet matt black colour but the lens surrounding is silver making it obvious to anyone that this is not just a mirror but a recorder. I would prefer to see it with a matt black.

REVIEW_TITLE: Works Well But Battery Life Could Be Better.
REVIEW:
I will start by saying overall this is a nice unit but it has a major drawback which I will come to later. I have had a white one of these since August 2008.
The styling is very ipod like and has been constructed well enough for consumer use. Operating it is pretty simple. Press the power button and the green LED blinks until it picks up enough satellites which is usually about 30 seconds. It has a large amount of internal memory, cannot remember how much, but it is a lot. I have mine set to record every 5 seconds and a full day will use up around 1% of the storage. I have not cleared mine out since I bought it and I am only on about 30% use in total.
As for connecting it to a PC. You get a USB cable supplied and a CD with drivers etc on it. On my Windows PC I downloaded/installed the "Prolific Pl-2303 USB To Serial" drivers and DataDownloader from RoyalTek's website. Ran the DataDownloader.exe and set it to use port 4 or 6, set the device type to RGM3800 and where you want the files to download to. Power up the device, click connect, select the logs you want and click >. A status bar tells you how much it has done. From here you can either view your logged tracks and tag your photos in LOCR or use LOCR to create the KML files needed to view the tracks in Google Earth.
Now for the downside which is the battery life. It uses 2 x AAA batteries which last about 3 hours or so on fresh batteries. The problem for me is that I want to turn it on at the start of the journey/day and forget about it until I return home at the end of the day. This is not the case with this unit, invariably it has stopped logging due to the batteries being depleted because I have forgotten to check them. With it only lasting 2-3 hours the thing became virtually useless to me. I got around the power problem by adding extra batteries to it and it now lasts approximately 2.5 days with continuous use. This has obviously invalidated any warranty I had but it now suits my needs far better. I am not recommending anyone else do this.
