REVIEW:
This is my favourite design of heat sink - when the air flows through the fins they will not clog up with dust (downward facing designs always clog up and need cleaning regularly). It's as heavy as you would imagine, but stays seated securely on my vertically mounted motherboard.
Comes with paste + brackets to attach a second fan (not supplied) to the other side.
Cooling performance is good, my CPU runs at around 35 ? most of the time. During extreme processing I set the fan to go to full speed at 80?, and the temperature has never gone over ~80?. Noise at top speed just sounds like a fan robustly going fast - not too noisy, but clearly audible. The sound of air flowing through the fins contributes some of the noise. During normal use, web browsing etc. I cannot hear the fan at all.
I wanted Intel clips - I don't like installing mounting brackets, and this design can be installed on a motherboard that is already seated - but be warned that the mounting instructions are useless, they look exactly like Intel's original instructions from 10 years ago, and it's not intuitive how the clips work. I will add some words to go with the diagrams you will receive.
There are four holes on the motherboard surrounding the CPU mount - the clips on this cooler are supposed to simply push through the holes, but there's often one or two that just won't go in properly. This might help... .
1. After installing your CPU, follow Cooler Master's instructions on paste (i.e. spread a thin film of paste over the top of the CPU etc.). Make sure you're working with the motherboard horizontal - you can work vertically but it's much more difficult.
2. Make sure that the BLACK push-pin handles are fully UP before you try to put the heat sink on, don't worry about twisting them, but if you want to, twist them anticlockwise. Just make sure they are fully up, otherwise the pin cannot fit through the hole.
3. Carefully line up so that each of the pins is over a hole in the motherboard.
4. Choose any corner - gently lower the WHITE arrow head part of the pin through - and only after the white part is through the hole, push the BLACK handle down and twist - it inserts a pole through the centre of the WHITE arrow head, pushing the sides apart and locking it in place (you will hear a click). Never push down with huge force, if it doesn't go down - you missed, pull up the black handle and start over. You don't want to break the motherboard - most motherboards are designed to bend a little and are amazingly strong and flexible, but it should not require huge force.
4. Next do the diagonally opposite corner, followed by the final 2 corners. Expect the 2nd and 3rd pin to be hardest to insert.
5. If any corner pops out, go back, pull up the black handle and try again - do not worry about smearing your heat sink paste - it's a thin film of paste and won't do any harm if you put the right amount on - eventually it's supposed to fill all the microscopic gaps between the CPU surface and heat sink surface, but not run over any important parts.

REVIEW:

Intel makes really good processors, I'm utterly amazed how they fit four cores *and* a very decent GPU into this tiny processor with such reliability and performance.
It's quite expensive but there are features that justify the price for me:
1. Build in Graphics processor is very decent - it handles all web browser graphics and video, and can drive multiple screens. If you do not need the sort of power to play top end games, you will not need to buy a separate graphics card.
2. It's designed to be overclocked - I'll reserve that for the future. At the moment it doesn't need any improvement from the factory settings; but in 5 years' time, who knows? It will help it keep up with newer models, therefore increasing its longevity.
It arrives factory sealed with permanent tape over the box flap. Intel does not spend its money on packaging but it's adequately protected.
You need a cooler to go with it, I'm using Cooler Master Hyper TX3i.
As usual, pins are on the motherboard, not the CPU, and installation is easy - but also very scary, considering the price. The trickiest part is after installation - attaching the heat sink and stressing over the perfect paste application.
Temperatures are around 35? most of the time, 40-45? during 3D Mark GPU tests and 80? during CPU test.
As mentioned, I have never had a CPU that blasted through the 3D Mark tests like this - Time Spy CPU test starts at 60 FPS, and finishes at 18FPS without overclocking.

REVIEW_TITLE: Pros and cons without stating the obvious
REVIEW:
I love this case, it looks great etc. and does its job. I'm not going to say much about why I like it, it's pretty obvious from the description, which says it all.
Pros:
+ Air intakes all have easy clean filters. They are useful.
+ doors on both sides, with offset motherboard mounting panel makes installing motherboard easy, and not necessary to put the CPU and heatsink on the board in advance.
+ Cables for usb3 and front panel controls all compatible with modern motherboard.
+ Best cable management I've experienced, made possible working from both sides, and design of chassis.
+ Air flow is good.
Cons:
- You need angled Sata cables for HDDs, or you will have to bend the wire quite aggressively, the space behind the drive bays is the bare minimum. I installed 4 drives, and it was a tight fit.
- 3 speed fan controller is a blast from the past. I ignored it, it's way better to plug the fans directly into motherboard headers and let your BIOS control the fan speed according to sensors. This fan controller takes power from a sata connector and has 3 outputs for fans. It's made even worse by the cable design... they are not bound together, so there are 3 loose wires only joined at the end where the fan socket is - it's easy to get them tangled with other wires.
- The side doors are badly designed. They are really bad doors:
 1. Really stiff when case is new.
 2. Cannot be replaced properly when case is vertical, you line up the top, and the bottom pops out, and vice versa. So you have to lay the case down to put one door on, then turn it over to do the other.
 3. Don't quite sit perfectly flush, a millimetre here and there. I always spend a good few minutes trying to line it up nicely.
These are cons, but don't stop me liking the case, because the most important thing is having space to work without damaging your components, or struggling and getting hot and bothered. None of these issues caused me any stress.

REVIEW_TITLE: A good simple solution for handsfree calling and bluetooth audio streaming
REVIEW:
I have used many of these hands free kits over the years. Most of them suffer for 1 of 2 problems:
1. Poor audio quality
2. Poor audio jacks
This product suffers from neither of these - I am impressed by the build quality and also the design.
Installation:
Installation is simple. I managed to plug in my audio lead in the glovebox, route it under the dashboard to the cigarette lighter, then on then position the multi-function button next to the stereo - all with only 1 wire (power to cigarette lighter) on real show - see photos for more info.
I am also really happy to report that the cable length for the different leads is generous - with a handy Velcro strap to keep the unused cable tidy. I managed to hide this all below my gear stick surround (simply pulls up and drops into the void below).
Another really positive point is the magnetic holder on the dashboard. This means if I do accidently catch the wire with my knee (I haven't yet - but you never know) - it'll simply pull away without damaging the product. My Belkin branded one had a similar design - but the audio quality wasn't a patch on this one!
Functions:
The functions of this device are great - once paired (really easy - find and connect - it'll be in pairing mode when first plugged in - if you need to rest it - hold the back and next buttons for 2 seconds or longer) it is able to do lots:
1. Launch siri or Google now (press next button for 2 seconds)
2. Answer and hang up calls
3. Skip tracks forward and back
4. Reject calls
Most importantly - the audio quality for streamed spotifiy is great. The calls are clear and no one has complained that I sound bad - so that's much better than the Belkin one!
The only slight negative is how bright the cigarette lighter adapter is - really bright blue LED - which can be a little distracting until you are used to it - especially for glasses wearers at night - but after a couple of journeys it's great.
All in all this is a really great product with lots of features for a really competitive price.
I hope this review came across as balanced. There isn't much I don't like about the product - I will be buying another for my parents car!

REVIEW_TITLE: Nice and chunky but without being too heavy or inaccurate
REVIEW:
First off, in terms of style, the pen looks and feels lovely. Nice and chunky but without being too heavy or inaccurate.
The box it comes in is quite nice too, with the golden outer wrapper and the ends of the main box decorated with a nice inset.
However, the pen itself is quite frustrating. Once you've got the ink flowing, it writes nicely, but it can take a bit to get it going. It seems to dry out very easily (even within 30 seconds of stopping writing) and doesn't seem to start again very easily. The old 'school' tricks of sucking on the nib, or squeezing the qink cartridge doesn't seem to help much. The best way of restarting seems to be dipping the nib in some clean water then blotting some of the water off, but this can affect the ink - different shades or flow levels. I bought some official qink cartridges with the pen so its not like I'm using some terrible third-party ink.
The other problem I've found is this isn't so good as an occasional pen. I bought this principally to write cards and the occasional letter. Therefore, it only comes out once a month or so. However, I've found the ink 'disappears' between uses. Start with a full cartridge, write some best wishes on a card, put it away again, then the next time there is no ink in the cartridge. Its not leaking out anywhere, so I can only assume either the cap has some kind of soak or the fluid in the ink evaporates when not being used.
Finally, I remember Parker Pens having a smooth nib. This is much more scratchy than I remember from the last time I had a Parker Pen in the 90s which I recall having a bigger 'ball' on the end of the nib. Its not rough, and far better than those cheap fountain pens of old, but something to be aware of.
In conclusion, it looks and feels lovely, but can be a bit frustrating to put pen to paper. I think the issues are more related to the ink than the pen itself, so I may try some third party inks at the next refill.

REVIEW:
I was a little unsure about this radio before I bought it - the reviews made it sound a bit pants. So I bought it from a retailer with a good returns policy if it turned out that it was. So far, I've used it for a week, and am nothing but impressed with it.
The Setup:-
Well, I bought this product and got it working whilst waiting for the bus home - it comes with everything you need, including batteries! Simply a case of installing the batteries, connecting the headphones, turning it on and tuning it in.
Usage:-
The controls are fairly simple to use, up/down to change the volume, left right and click to select the channels, and some further options selectable via the menu's. It can sometimes be awkward selecting channels with the joystick, as sometimes when you click, you accidentally move the joystick and it selects the wrong channel. Or if you're out of range, the channel will revert to what your listening to, rather than just taking you back to the selection manually, annoying if you're listening to a 'BBC' channel, then want to listen to a 'Smooth' channel. I have been very impressed with the sound quality and reception though. Channels with higher bandwidths work very well, the low bandwidth ones (traffic/birdsong) less so (unsurprisingly). I use this daily on the train and bus to and from work, and only when in a dip on the train does it drop out. It does seem to depend which type of train I travel on, the newer ones seem to cause more interference trouble than the older ones.
The battery life is rubbish when compared to an FM radio, or even many of the newer MP3 players. I would say that battery life is 4-5 hours, however I've switched to high power rechargables, and power adapter at work, to keep the costs down.
General:-
When you first take the unit out the box, you might be surprised at how 'cheap' it feels. The main case is in shiny white plastic, and the front is of a more soft touch rubber which is much nicer. Unfortunatly the dimple on the joystick has already turned yellow after just a weeks use, and I would say that I keep fairly clean hands.
The Blue lit screen is reasonable to use, except in really bright light, but thats just a case of moving slightly.
The volume is a bit all or nothing - the first level of volume above silent is surprisingly loud; not deafening or anything, but it is a large step. Then the maximum volume isn't really massively high, maybe its because of the headphones, but you can still hear some external noise. But the headphones are comfortable for my ears even for a few hours use. I've tried some other 'phones that I have, and all work fine with the radio (given that it uses the headphones as an aerial) so as I have a habit of destroying headphones in quite a short time, I'll have no trouble changing them at a later date.
All in all, if you're after a cheap personal radio, with DAB features, I would highly recommend it, but be aware of the 'features' so that you're not disappointed.

REVIEW_TITLE: Great drive, delivers breathtaking perfromance but reality is not quite so breathtaking.

I clonedover my Sandisk Extreme Pro build to this drive and plugged it in. I made sure the drive was setup in my Asus X99 MB UEFI and away we went. Booted up just fine. Went to restart and...BSOD. Okay Cold reboot, fine. Restart...BSOD.Okay looked it up, usual stuff, update BIOS etc. (I was a couple behind but as the BIOS takes ages to setup on X99 I only do it if I have to) but for this family of boards it was recommended to switch off Fast Boot and CSM in the BIOS. I also looked up and found there was a specific bug fix for this SSD in a later BIOS so applied that. Once a bit of tweaking took place all was good. It's been solid since. I then found the Samsung NVMe controller driver and installed that.
Performance according to benchmarks is around 3300-3500MBps. So all working as it should.
However....in day to day usage I really cant tell the difference over this to my Sandisk Extreme Pro running at 550MBps. So if you feel left out by not having a NVMe...don't! It's not as big a leap as it was from that 500GB rust spinner you had.
So buy with confidence but do your homework and prep first. I think it took me a couple of hours to get it all setup as I wanted it. It's not just a straight swap like SATA to SATA SSD.
Oh yes one other foible I found. The disk cloning software I use always in the past copied and aligned drives perfectly. But I found this one wasn't aligned a couple of weeks after installing. I guess I didn't bother checking as all had been perfect in the past. Anyway the drive is now adjusted and aligned. No difference to performance.

REVIEW_TITLE: Great board but flakey USB 3.1 ports. If you don't need 3.1 maybe get the standard version?
REVIEW:
Okay it was time to get a new rig together after using a 2008 spec dual Xeon CPU Dell Workstation and thinking its time to get a machine that doesn't use 230W at idle! So I built a new i7 5820k/ box around this motherboard mainly because I was intrigued by the built in USB 3.1 feature. I am a huge user of external caddys and dockers for HDD/SSD work so this was a nice to have. So we built the machine up with Windows 10 Pro as I wanted out of the box support for a lot of the new hardware that 7 just doesn't notice till its told to. Upgraded the BIOS and set the board up using the UEFI Bios etc.
Having a locked down Dell for a while and not building enthusiast machines as often, meant I was a little rusty but some YouTube homework beforehand helped. I also used the AISuite software to tune up the overclock. I chickened out when it hit 4.2GHz and toned it back to 4GHz. I also had to upgrade the old H-50 AIO to the bigger and superb Artic Cooling 240 AIO as the temps on load were hitting 85+. You can uninstall the AISuite after as the settings stay in the Bios.
So the end result is a great machine that's pretty quiet, sips 65W at idle and can really stretch its legs if required.
However, there is one issue. Those USB 3.1 ports....yeah they don't work all that well. Not sure if its poor driver issue or a Windows 10 issue but the 3.1 ports just disappear from time to time. I look up Device manager one day and the ASMedia 3.1 ports are listed, then the next day...gone. A few days later...back again. All the other USB 3.0 ports are rock solid. Using the current March 2016 drivers too. It could be something that's sorted out down the road but its a bit of a shame. Not enough of a hassle though to send it all back. I can live with it.
Update July 2017 - Seems the USB3.1 ports are working and more stable. I've since upped the BIOS and maybe newer Windows 10 updates have helped. I re-enabled the ports about 5 months ago and they have only 'vanished' once for a short period in that time. Other than that been a good board to own.
Update Sept 2017 - Well I've given up on the 3.1 ports. I've updated the ASMedia firmware and drivers a few times and they still come and go as they please. Just not reliable. Other than that this board has been great.

Update July 2106. - Okay having had this box a few months we have noticed our TV viewing has nosedived.The reason? I mentioned to my other half that I wasn't watching as much TV due to to the TV guide not giving an instant synopsis of the program highlighted like my old Topfield did. She remarked that she had been thinking the same thing. If you want a synopsis, you have to manually select the info using the fiddly remote. It's a tiny thing but it has put us off watching Freeview TV, so we now use the FireTV/Prime/Netflix for 90% of TV viewing. With the Topfield I would go through the guide and instantly see anything that peaked my interest and set it to record, job done. Amazing how one lacking feature can spoil it.

REVIEW_TITLE: The Chromebook Missing Link. The affordable premium Chromebook we've all been waiting for.
REVIEW:
Purchased this two weeks ago after spotting it a few months back online pre-release. I saw it and I wanted it. This is the true missing link between the cheap �250 Chromebooks and the �800+ Pixel. It's a big step up from my trusty little 2012 11" Samsung. This machine is superb! The version I have is the 4GB i3 version as I wanted longevity. Most of the reviews are for the Celeron version and they all state its 98% perfect performance wise but as I keep a laptop for several years I spent the extra on a little more horsepower. I don't regret that as it's super slick for web use. I have handed it around to other tech friends and all of them agree it's about the fastest machine for web use they've used. I have a dual CPU workstation for my main machine and this little Chromebook is faster for browsing. Decent hardware and a lightweight OS win here!
The built quality is excellent, it feels great to hold and look at. The keyboard is great though maybe the keys could have been a little larger. The screen is retina searing bright at full setting (I run it at about 75%) but looks great. It's a matte finish so should please most people. I've found scaling web to 120% makes most web pages fit nicely on the 1080p screen. The trackpad is superb and I love two finger scrolling. The only two downsides to the design are - it's a fingerprint magnet and the inner screen bezel is standard Dell workaday plastic. Ahh well it didn't cost �800...
The machine also has upgradable SSD capability so don't worry about getting the 32GB SSD option as you can always add another yourself later on. I might do after the warranty runs out. But I have slipped a 64GB MicroSD card in, in case I want to carry any media around. It's a fairly flush fit so shouldn't fall out. As for other options, I really don't know what benefit you'd get from buying the i5 version but it's nice to have the option. Battery life is rated in days for me.
So to sum up this is a premium looking and performing Chromebook. Well worth checking out and paying the little extra for. It will look a lot better than any equivalent priced Windows laptop and probably be faster too for the 95% of tasks average Joe uses tech for. And before you ask, I'm a big Windows user. However, it's sometimes nice to use a computer that doesn't require heavy maintenance to run daily.

EDIT Feb 2016. I finally got round to getting one of these SSDs to test. Oh boy it's as bad as I thought. The Write performance is dreadful. If you try to copy more than 3GB of data to it the performance plummets from 240MBps to 200...180...160...140...90...70...40MBps and further. Basically you have a SSD with the write performance of a USB2.0 stick. Quite how Crucial could design such a terrible SSD fails me. If you are copying your old HDD build to this then be prepared to wait a long time. The vastly superior BX100 is like a Ferrari in comparison. In fact the cheapy Kingston V300 would be a better performer. Laughable.

REVIEW:
I wrote this review to help other Mini drivers looking for the perfect phone cradle. My iphone gets a lot of use in my car for Sat-Nav and playing MP3s or streaming music so I was looking for a cradle that gave me a clear view of the phone screen and easy access if needed. I drive a 2011 Mini Cooper and dashboard and physical space is at a premium (I'm over 6 foot) so finding the right item was becoming a lengthy (and expensive) task.
I tried many cradles before I settled on this one: cup holder extended arm cradle (got in the way of gear changes), small behind steering wheel vent mounted cradle (could not see screen clearly or access phone easily) and several windscreen or dashboard mounted cradles (they either obstructed view or did not stick sturdily enough). On top of all this I wanted to connect my iPhone 5 with aux and power cables and with the positioning of most of the other cradles the cables either didn't reach, or were so long they got in the way.
When I came across this cradle I couldn't believe I hadn't thought of this solution before. I haven't used CDs for years so using the CD slot to support this cradle would not cause me any issues; in fact, it would make a redundant facility useful again. Also, it would place the iPhone right in the centre of the dashboard where I could view Sat-Nav clearly and access the phone if needed. I was slightly concerned that the position of the phone may block or obstruct essential functionality on the dashboard and my other worry was stability (would my iPhone shake around, rattle or even come loose). After reading the other reviews I decided to give it a go.
I am really pleased that I did. And I would say that (for my needs anyhow) this is possibly the best mount for a Mini Cooper. It is positioned perfectly for access and viewing, does not obstruct any essential functionality (OK it may be slightly in the way of some but not anything you use regularly) and it is really sturdy - no shakes, rattles or drops. It's even positioned perfectly for the short coil cables I bought (separate aux and power c.�5 each - not the expensive official Mini connecting item for c. �50).
Overall, I'm extremely happy with this item and, for the support/enhancement it has brought my driving experience, and in comparison to other cradles I have tried, it is offered at a very good price.
The only reason I did not give it 5 stars is for the red rubber used in the gripper. If this was black the item would merge more seamlessly into the dash when the phone is not attached.

REVIEW_TITLE: Great for back garden fun but not for serious camping
REVIEW: I was looking for a lightweight tent to strap to my Vespa so I could shoot off for weekend camping over the summer. This seemed to fit the bill as it was a decent size (3 man) at only 2kg! I was a bit wary as I had not heard of the brand and there were no reviews here on Amazon - but i took the plunge after finding a few reviews on some USA sites - ordering the orange/yellow as it was the only colour available here (though I believe this tent is available in 4 colours). It arrived promptly (2 days earlier than stated on super saver delivery) and was, as stated, very lightweight and packed very small - perfect for strapping on the Vespa. It went up very quickly (about 10 mins even without English instructions) but it felt a little flimsy. The internal groundsheet was seemingly made of the same material as the flysheet, obviously to keep the weight down, but would this last more than a couple of uses, and, more importantly, keep out the wet from the ground and the sky in a British downpour? This, coupled with the '3 man' tent actually only being, in my opinion, a '2 man' tent meant that I decided to send the item back. Shame, as overall I do think its a great design and it went up and down quickly. I'm just not sure that it would keep out bad weather over a long period or hold 3 people (even without luggage/boots etc). I'd say it's not really for a serious camper - but its great for fun in the back garden. Another tip - if you are to order this item, select a colour other than orange/yellow if available. As soon as I took the items out of the bag, insects swarmed from who knows where, drawn to the brightness of the yellow in the summer sun, and when the tent was up - it was practically covered in bugs. I organised the return with Amazon on the Sunday afternoon and it was picked up at 9:10 am the following day - amazing service! I give this item 3 stars because it fitted the requirements I originally ordered it for (small and lightweight for the Vespa), but in reality, as a proper camping tent, it did not fill me with confidence.

When talking about Jackson Pollock, for example, he discusses possible sources for his inspiration for drip paintings whilst not once mentioning Lee Krasner (wife of Pollock who was producing drip paintings before they even met). Over all, though, a good read.

I am very glad I decided to invest in this book.

REVIEW_TITLE: Accounting for taste, this is a great watch
REVIEW:
If you want a circular face then there are plenty of other watches. I like the square! It adds a tiny bit more to the cards that a circle wouldn't have but that's basically irrelevant - liking the shape is what counts.
Android Wear needs to be indirectly reviewed through these watches because it doesn't exist on its own: it's good. It feels like it has more to do to grow into itself but it doesn't feel like a beta. Voice recognition is great (even as a Scot) and there is an aspect of convenience to being able to manage some notifications without taking out a phone.
The WiFi is handy if your phone is charging in another room, and I'm not sure I've used the GPS directly but it's good to know it's there.
The charger slot takes a bit of getting used to but is manageable when you realise the guard folds all the way out. The speed of charging is excellent and if you keep usage light you can definitely forget to charge one night.
I like the look of this watch, I think it's handy and I think it's really cool. It's a great compliment to Android and at this price point it's well worth being a trial watch. Having had this, I'm already sold on Android Wear and Sony's capacity to make a brilliant accessory.

REVIEW_TITLE: Nice machine. It does what it is designed to do well.

I've had this PC for two months now. I like it and would recommend it to anyone who is looking for a small laptop / netbook to do general purpose PC stuff, which is after all what it is designed to do. If however you are looking for a powerful laptop, look elsewhere.
Good points:
- Fantastic battery life. 7 Hours claimed, I have achieved very close to this
- Small size but not particularly light
- Keyboard size quite acceptable (I was concerned that it might be too small)
- Screen is clear and very readable (I was concerned that it might be too small)
- It does well what it is designed to do
- I like the protective sleeve
- I like the Large hard drive 160 Gbytes
- It comes with a 2 years warrenty. Most of the competition only offer 12 months
Bad(ish) points:
- Not a power PC (if you need a power PC for gaming or graphics & wideo editing, look elsewhere)
- Hard drive partitioned into 2 drives C: and D: which is bit confusing if you do not understand partitions. Also a 50:50 partition split is not ideal.
- Asus keeps changing models so frequently its hard to keep up and know whether one is buying the latest model or a previous/ discontinued one.
- Its standard screen resolution is 1024*600 however, this is adjustable to 1024*768 virtual or 1024*768 compression.
- Maybe the next itteration should provide a slightly larger screen say 11" rather than 10.1" and a standard resolution of 1024*768. My Canon camera and printer software insisted on having a 1024*768 resolution before it would install. I opted for the 1024*768 virtual mode which was a bit irritating having to scroll up and down to see the full image. (The compression mode distorted the images)
Enjoy
PRODUCT: ASUS Eee PC 1000H-WHI066X Netbook, Windows XP Home Preloaded, 1GB RAM, 160GB HDD (White)

REVIEW:
The mouse overall is very good. - The software runs correctly, the customization is nice and all of the macros work correctly. The mouse works fine both wired and wireless and switches between the two fluently with about 2-3 seconds break between the mouse being usable again after the cable is pulled to go wireless. The mouse also has an economy setting which makes the mouse take much less battery life.
The mouse is extremely responsive and is great to play League of Legends with due to the fast reaction time and high sensitivity. The only thing I could possibly complain about is the battery life (it has an inbuilt battery that charges when the mouse is plugged in via the wire) the battery tends to last about 8 hours with the polling rate set to 1000hz (meaning it sends data to the computer every 1 millisecond, 8 times faster than a regular wireless mouse so this is understandable).
The cable is also of very high quality and doesn't feel like it's going to break any time soon and the port on the mouse works very well.
Lots of people will say 2000 DPI is low for a gaming mouse but most of the time within games you actually want your DPI to be lower, especially if you're playing first person shooters (the one I play being counter strike: Global offensive, and the mouse was amazingly responsive and great for playing this game.)
The mouse is also very comfortable when held in the hand and is a pleasure to use for long periods of gaming due to the ergonomic design, and the padding on the outside to make it comfortable.
Overall:
I paid �15 for this mouse and for that price it is a steal, however even at the full price of �45 I would still highly recommend the mouse to anyone who is looking for a gaming mouse and perhaps a mouse which can be used on a laptop whilst using the economy mode. I rate this 4/5 stars and would buy from this company again and recommend this mouse.

REVIEW_TITLE: It's not "All about the Bass" with these!
REVIEW:
Packaging - Once removed from the plastic packaging, you are then greeted with a black box which flips open. This makes the headphones already feel premium, which you then realise is not the case. Your audible experience begins when you start listening to them.
Design - The headphones look really nice, they look really expensive, but soon enough you come to realise that they are actually made from cheap materials. However, the only thing I like from the design is the textured pattern on the headphones.
Sound - The bass was really disappointing and wasn't really what I was expecting, especially since these headphones claimed to have or enhance "Xtra Bass" which these headphones failed to live up to. The "Highs" and "Mids" sounded alright. For some reason, the headphones seem like they are really quiet, no matter how loud your volume is, they still sound quiet.
Comfort - They felt comfortable enough for me to use. However, they seem to leak a bit of sound, but not enough to get moaned at. The length of the wire is at an adequate length. However, it would have been much easier if the wire was only linked to one headphone, instead of both.
Overall, my experience with these headphones wasn't that great, and I definitely wouldn't recommend them to friends and family, especially at this price range.
I would recommend the Sony MDR-ZX660AP headphones.

REVIEW_TITLE: Simply the best and most capable Media Centre app on Fire TV - nothing else on the store comes close.

However, it doesn't have the Python scripting part so you won't be using it to do any dodgy streaming, which is fine by me as it's supposed to be a media centre.
Before people complain that you are paying for a cut-down version of something that is free, they should be aware that Kodi needs to be sideloaded and isn't guaranteed to keep working/supported on FireTV in the future as both updates to FireOS and Kodi come out. This is 'official' on the App store, should be around for the foreseeable future and will auto-update as new and better versions come out as well as staying functioning with new versions of FireOS. It should also be optimised to work well on the various configurations of FireTV (it's specifically targeted at Fire TV hardware) whereas Kodi may or may not work well on things like the Fire Stick as future versions of it come out.
This is definitely worth the price and as it's coded by one of the two people who did the original Android port of Kodi, it's worth buying to show support for their efforts both now (to bring an official Kodi based media centre to the Amazon App store) and for the work done in the past to bring Kodi to the Android platform generally.

REVIEW_TITLE: Overpriced and ultimately, frustrating and disappointing.
REVIEW:
Overpriced and ultimately, frustrating and disappointing.
I'm a sucker for gadgets and I also like stuff that hooks up with my mobile phone. So when I decided to start tracking my health, this looked like a great device to effortlessly monitor blood pressure. Especially since I already had the fitness tracker from Withings.
Even better, it came up in a Black Friday deal and I got a nice price reduction on it vs the normal retail price - so far so good.
Initial impressions were very good indeed ... it was easy to use and worked flawlessly. Build quality was generally very good - apart from a poorly designed battery cover and it really 'looked the part' feeling like quality bit of kit, justifying the high price. If I had written this review at that early stage of ownership, I'd have given this gadget a glowing five-star review.
Unfortunately however, in the months of use since then the monitor has become more and more unreliable. Connection problems over bluetooth have gone from 'once in a blue moon' to 'often enough to be annoying'. This is particularly frustrating as in order for the device to even take a reading, the bluetooth connection must be established. Now this problem could be caused by my phone which I have found can be flaky with some bluetooth kit. However, I would consider it a poor design choice on the part of Withings as it would have been much more sensible if the monitor could go ahead and record readings on its own and then sync the stored measures when the opportunity arises later.
But far worse that that, the Withings Wireless Blood Pressure monitor flat out fails to take readings on an all too regular basis for no reason that I can discern. The rate of failed measurements has steadily increased over the months. At first, there were hardly any and the few occasions where the reading failed it was clear that I hadn't secured it properly on my arm. Now however, it seems to fail at least 50% of the time, even when the device is obviously properly secured. This is enormously frustrating as by the time you faff around with turning on bluetooth on the phone, waiting to get a good connection and take the reading, quite some time has passed and you only find out that the process has failed at the very end. It's not uncommon for it to fail two or even three times in a row before reading. Even then, you can't be sure that the reading is accurate as the anxiety and frustration caused by the messing around has most likely pushed your BP up and in any case, having seen it mysteriously fail a couple of times can you really be sure the the reading is 'good'?
Given that this device is extortionately expensive compared to 'non-connected' digital blood pressure arm cuffs, it utterly fails to deliver on the premise that you are paying all that extra cash for convenience as the unreliability just leads to frustration and massive inconvenience (especially if you are trying to take a reading in the morning when in a rush for work). You can't help but be taken by the irony of a device intended for people concerned about high blood pressure to actually seem to aggravate that problem!
I therefore advise people to avoid this piece of equipment - it is almost offensively overpriced and in my experience at least, simply doesn't deliver on the promise that is implied by the wireless capability and the price premium. Maybe I just got unlucky and got a 'bad' one but looking around the other reviews here, lots of people have suffered increasing unreliability after a good initial start. Such a shame as it was so good at the start when it worked properly.
My recommendation is to look around for a decent regular BP cuff for a half or even a third of the price. That's certainly what I'll be doing next after binning mine in frustration.

REVIEW_TITLE: It has no onboard support for local network sources like DLNA at all
REVIEW:
It does what it says on the tin - gives you the ability to play media from a DLNA source - but the GUI is somewhat unintuitive and confusing at first. That said, the popular XBMC is also a bit confusing the first time you set it up for DLNA playback. Hopefully the developer will continue to work to update the GUI.
Obviously, codec and container support is limited to what the Fire TV has onboard so it may not play every last video or audio file that you have in your library, though all the popular formats are supported by the Fire it would seem.
There's a decent range of network protocols supported, so you're almost certain to get it working with your networked source.
Also, this sort of DLNA playback functionality really should be built into the Fire TV box. It has no onboard support for local network sources like DLNA at all, it's totally an internet streaming device out of the box. Still, the price for this app is low and it will get you started with playback from your local network.

You should be aware that it can only support the codecs that the Fire TV supports natively, so you may find that this will not play more esoteric formats unlike something like XBMC which should play almost anything. For mainstream stuff like typical mp4 or divx video files, or mp3 audio files, it's good.
Really though, this functionality should be built in to the Fire TV. Well done to the developer for filling the gap but it's still a pain to have to pay for something that should be standard with a multimedia 'set top box'.
Note: This is a receiver only so you'll need to use something to select and control your media. Skifta or Bubble work well on Android and allow you to 'cast' the media from your device as well as a server such as a NAS.

REVIEW:
This is a pretty nifty little USB charger and probably meets the needs of gadget lovers pretty head on.
- Nice simple design and good quality finish (the soft touch is very nice).
- Five ports from a single charger should be able to meet the needs of travellers especially, when there is only one plug free and many gadgets to charge from it.
- Ability to deliver full-power charges even for power-hungry devices like Tablets is a definite advantage. Often, single-port plugs won't even deliver full power for a Tablet so to have it on up to five connections is a boon.
- Auto detect instead of having dedicated USB ports for specific kinds of device means more flexibility and convenience.
- Using a standard 'Figure of Eight' connector for mains connection is a great feature. It means you can site the charger away from the plug socket, very handy if the socket is in an inconvenient or hard to reach place. Also great for travelling as you can just use the appropriate cable for the local electrical socket system - even if you can't source one before you leave you can nearly always easily get one at your destination. Much better than the proprietary plug adaptors that many chargers use.
Only a couple of slight caveats:
- The 'auto-detect' didn't seem to deliver full power for my Galaxy Tab 7.7 (GT-6800) Tablet using the official Samsung USB data/charge cable, as the Tablet didn't show the 'charging' icon but instead just indicated that power was connected as is typical when making a normal connection with a PC USB port. However, it did appear to deliver more than the 500mA charge of standard USB, if not the full 2.1A current. When I used a 'micro-USB to Samsung connector' on a standard micro USB cable it did however deliver a full charge and 'charging' was indicated on the Tablet. So not too big a deal.
- Unlike other reviewers here who reported near to no power draw, I found that the charger consumes about 0.9W when nothing is connected, or everything is fully charged. That's still a pretty small amount but enough to make me switch it off at the mains when not using it.
I'd still give the unit a full five stars despite those two very minor niggles as it is pretty much exactly what I was looking for in a USB charger. I always like it when a manufacturer takes the time to research and design something that people actually need.
Good value and very good product

REVIEW:
I bought this product to replace an old Wireless G router and BT Openlink medem combo that I was using to connect to my Plusnet connection.
Configuring the plusnet connections was very simple as many of the normal ISPs presets come pre-configured in a drop down so all that was required was to select "Plusnet VDSL" and then supply my plasnet username and passowrd... and I was quickly back on the internet..
One of the things i like about this router is it's versatility, it will support:
- Normal ADSL (phone line internet)
- VDSL ( fibre to the cabinet) often marketed as "Fibre broadband" that is delivered to you're home via the phone line
- External modem Ethernet connection - IE connect to cable modem, or G.Fast Modem (if that ever comes to you're area) or Fibre modem
- 4G USB modem
As such it's fairly future proof and a house move or change in available technology in you're area should not mean a need to replace this router with another
Wired connection is working as Gigabit.
Wireless network will be presented as two seperate networks, a 2.4Ghz network and the new faster 5Ghz network. This allows support for my older devices that dont support 5ghz whilst allowing my newer devices to enjoy the performance improvement.
Copying files around my internal network is now roughly double the previous speed achieved
Range seems to have extended well and can now get WiFi with full strength in rooms where it was previously patchy.
set up and configuration including changing all the network names, changing passwords, port forwarding, IP allocation all fairly simple
overall I'm pretty happy with this product
PRODUCT: TP-Link AC1600 Wireless Dual Band Gigabit VDSL/ADSL Modem Router for Phone Line Connections (BT Infinity, TalkTalk, EE and PlusNet Fibre) 2 USB, 2.0 Ports, UK Plug (Archer VR600)

REVIEW_TITLE: A strange format, very dated and VERY much targeted to American culture. Avoid.
REVIEW:
Wow, what a curate?s egg this is! I was drawn (sorry) to this by the images on the cover, more specifically the jack-in-the-box and Halloween pumpkin, both of which appeal to my style of art. Unfortunately that doesn?t really represent the main content of the book. In fact, describing the content of the book is not that easy, as it has quite random information in places.
The book is plot into various sections and subsections, the main chapters based around the months of the year but with subsections for particular themes or advents (Christmas, Back to School, Halloween etc.). The pages are then chiefly a series of step-by-step images on the right with text headed as ?Know . Understand . Do? on the left. It?s these left-hand pages that are odd, as if the author made a decision to have them and then struggled to think of things to fill the page with. It?s also difficult to work out who this is is aimed at - some things described are glaringly obvious for adults (you know what a Christmas tree is, right?) yet the vocabulary used is clearly too complex for a younger child. The book is also aimed heavily at American readers, often in a nauseating picket fence and apple-pie style that belongs more in the 1950s.
So, ignoring the 50% of the book dedicated to American history or information you never realised that you already knew, what about the drawings of ?cool stuff?. Given what I?ve written above you may not be surprised to learn that a large proportion of the items to draw are US flags, military eagles dripping blood, school bus, popcorn, apple pie, Martin Luther King and Christian symbolism. If this is your thing then fine but also be aware that the drawings are not that good and in many cases look really dated. It reminded me very much of the ancient books clip art we used for creating school magazines on Gestetner duplicating machines back in the 1980s.

REVIEW_TITLE: Fantastic sounding but not perfect for portability or noise cancelling
REVIEW:
Summary
=======
These are excellent sounding headphones once you?ve run them in for 24hrs. They?re very well made but slightly heavier than the mainly plastic competitors such as Bose. The noise cancelling works well but on the strongest setting the sound quality does degrade slightly. Finally, they don?t fold down as small as you might like for travelling.
Sound
=====
Like all of the Bowers & Wilkins headphones I?ve owned, these MUST be run in for a period of time to sound their best. This is because headphones and loudspeakers are mechanical - the drivers physically vibrate to create sound. Cheaper headphones use materials like paper in their drivers and their sound doesn?t really change, but hi-fi manufacturers use stiffer materials for better sound, like metal or Kevlar. Straight from the production line these are very stiff and need a period of use to reach their optimum. I connected the PX to an iPad with the headphone lead supplied and left them playing at 50% volume for 24hrs. To do this you?ll need to use the app to turn off the proximity sensing, otherwise they?ll stop playing when not on your head.
All sound testing was done with the Spotify playlist ?Songs to test headphones with? and a random selection of songs picked for me by Apple Music. Once run in, the PX have a detailed, dynamic sound with a very wide soundstage. The sound is a little different from the typical B&W house sound - there is still a warmth that stops them from being too harsh with all the detail retrieval, but I didn?t notice any of the mid-bass bloom that people either love or hate about the P9 Signature. They passed the best test that I can ever give headphones: I forgot I was supposed to be reviewing and just got carried away enjoying the music. The PX are very transparent and clearly show the difference between good and poor recordings; though nothing sounds really bad, good recordings are much more apparent. The drivers are tilted towards your ear in the same way as the P9 Signature, but while I can?t say I?ve noticed it to make a difference in the P9, there is a definite stereo image with these. Listening to Three O?Clock Blues from Eric Clapton and BB King, I got a real sense that BB and Lucille were in front on my right and Eric with his Strat on my left. A keyboard player, drummer and bassist were spread across the rest of the stage in a really impressive and highly enjoyable way. The other benchmark for quality hi-fi is to hear something you?ve not heard before. I had this with When Things Go Wrong from the Steve Miller Band, where a harmonica is clearly playing along on the far left of the soundstage.
Given that all of this was with standard Bluetooth from an iPhone, I imagine the sound from a Bluetooth aptx or aptx HD device would be even better. Unfortunately I don?t possess anything that could confirm this. The sound from a wired connection is slightly better as you would expect, but note that the PX must have some charge level to be able to listen even with a wired connection.
Noise Cancelling
=============
Noise cancelling can be enabled either with a button on the right ear cup or, with more options, using the app. The app lets you customise the effect using three presets and a slider. The Office and City presets apply mild cancelling and have an equally mild effect on the sound. Flight provides the strongest effect but also noticeably changes the sound, becoming more ?squashed? which is a little disappointing. The Bose QC25 that I?ve generally used only when flying don?t exhibit this change to the sound character. It?s a while until I next fly so I can?t report on how effective it is.
Design
=====
The PX look and feel the part, clearly a well engineered piece of equipment with comfortable leather ear cups and padding on the headband. I have quite large ears and found them most comfortable with my earlobes tucked inside the cup. This provided a good level of isolation even without enabling the noise cancelling. What I don?t like is the band connecting to the outside of the earpieces. This is no doubt done for reasons of sound quality, being similar to the P9, but it means the band is proud of the side of your hear by a couple of inches. This makes them look physically bigger and more obvious when out and about, plus increases the chance of something getting caught in the gap. While testing I went into the garden and almost had them ripped off my head by a tree branch.
The second thing I don?t like is that they don?t fold flat properly. They do fold flat, but after wearing them a few times the headband curves at a shallower angle so the earpieces are wider apart when folded flat and no longer go into the bag unless you squeeze the headband. Even then, they naturally twist inwards inside the bag, making it bulkier. Related to this is wearing them around your neck when not in use. As soon as you remove them (or lift an ear cup) the sound pauses and they will go into standby after a few minutes. If you then hang them around your neck the earpieces won?t fold flat against your chest unless you remove and reverse them first. It?s a real shame as when they?re the wrong way round (L&R) they lay neatly against the chest and don?t constrict neck movements, but the right way round the opposite is true.
Overall, as a wireless set of headphones they sound fantastic. As a noise cancelling set of headphones they?re also very good, unless in Flight mode when they?re merely good. There are a couple of niggly physical design flaws that would make me think twice about wearing them in certain situations, and they?re not quite as portable as they might be. Fundamentally the sound is the most important thing to me, and they sound so good that I would only drop one star for the things I don?t like, but you may consider it as 2 dropped if portability and noise cancelling are the primary requirements.
PRODUCT: Bowers & Wilkins PX Wireless Headphones, Noise Cancelling - Space Grey
