PRODUCT: Sony HT-ST5000 800 W Soundbar with Dolby Atmos, High-Resolution Audio, Wireless Music Listening, 4K HDR Pass-Through - Black

REVIEW_TITLE: Stark, honest, bleak and an example of just how powerful music can be.
REVIEW:
Fire On All Sides is James Rhodes? follow-up to his memoir, Instrumental. It follows Rhodes, a classical pianist, on tour and documents his state of mind, thoughts and actions during the tour. Severely abused as a boy, Rhodes struggles with his personal demons in an honest fashion that doesn?t beg sympathy (and deserves it all the more as a result) giving a warts-and-all, expletive-ridden account. It?s stark and horrific in places,
For readers with a mental disability, there is much to recognise in the anger, isolation and despair that Rhodes articulates in a natural fashion. Although educated and eloquent, this isn?t a thesis-style paper but Rhodes journalling his thoughts as they really are. In amongst all this is an account of how music saved his life and his sanity, along with information on his favourite composers and musicians. The one flaw in all this is that there is no beginning, middle and end as such: the tour progresses and Rhodes struggles on, with the occasional lighter moment for relief. I found it hard to read for long periods, partly because of this but also because of the content. It?s not for the faint hearted.
I?m not sure who the market for this type of book will be. People with mental disabilities, like me, will be able to identify with the feelings of anger and problems in interaction with other people; there is a strange and slightly embarrassing comfort to be had in knowing that someone else is not only like you, but considerably worse. There will also be fans of James as a musician looking to find out more about him, but in my experience the average person doesn?t want to know, which is a shame as they are the ones who most need to know. Read it, and encourage your friends to do so.
PRODUCT: Fire on All Sides: THE INTERNATIONAL BESTSELLER

REVIEW_TITLE: Vibrant colours (only 1 green though) and decent coverage - use with pastel sticks for detail work
REVIEW:
The CarbOthello (weird name) pencils are essentially chalk/pastels in pencil form. Unlike pastel sticks they allow you to create detailed lines and without getting residue all over your fingers (and therefore the paper as well). Like pastels they are soft and quite fragile though, so when you need to sharpen them you need to be as careful as you would be with waxy colour pencils.
This set of 12 includes black, white and 10 vibrant colours. There are 4 blues though and only one green so landscape artists may be a little disappointed. They cover quite well given the pencil size tip, but are best used for details alongside pastels for broader coverage. The results can be smudged easily so fixer will be needed once your masterpiece is complete. The box states that they are ?partially aquarellable? which I assume is Stabilo language for ?you can add water? but I didn?t try this.
PRODUCT: STABILO CarbOthello Metal Box of 12 colours - Chalk-pastel coloured pencil

REVIEW_TITLE: Same great stuff, now skin-friendly too!
REVIEW:
I wasn't aware the Sugru I'd used previously wasn't 'skin-friendly' and haven't had a problem using it, but I guess this is re-assuring if you do have sensitive skin. When opening a fresh pack, it does have a vaguely minty smell at first so you need to be careful where children are around. In this pack I have the white and grey coloured packs, which do vaguely resemble chewing gum.
The first pack I tried was black and I found this left a faint black stain on my fingers but otherwise it works exactly the same as the original. Mould it into shape for up to 30 minutes and then leave for 24 hours to set. It doesn't last forever but you can extend life by keeping in a cool place and some people have said in the fridge extends it further.
PRODUCT: Sugru Mouldable Glue - Family-Safe | Skin-Friendly Formula - Black, White & Grey 8-Pack

REVIEW_TITLE: A soft, lightweight, yet warm jumper. Ideal for smart casual or business dressing.
REVIEW:
This 100% cashmere jumper is soft, lightweight and an attractive navy blue. The only size available for review was large whereas I would normally buy an XL, although I prefer jumpers to fit snugly and XL are sometimes a little too loose for my taste. I have a 44? chest and 36? waist and the jumper is probably a little too small across the chest, especially if wearing a shirt underneath. For a 42? chest it would probably be perfect if you like a slim fit.
Wearing it provided a good level of warmth, yet it?s thin enough to be able to wear under a suit jacket. It looks smart and would be suitable for casual wear or for work as the autumn chill approaches.
PRODUCT: FIND Men's Cashmere Crew Neck Jumper, Blue (City Navy Gp-6066), Large

REVIEW_TITLE: Everything you expect from a DK book, but best suited to drawing newcomers
REVIEW:
This is a typically well laid out and designed DK book with large illustrations and easy to follow text. If you like the DK style (for the record: I do) then you won't be disappointed with Artist's Drawing Techniques. The book does cover a wide range of different techniques, from pencil to pen & ink, coloured pencils, charcoal and pastels but due to the size of the illustrations and the relative amount of text, each medium is given basic coverage.
For someone just getting into, or back into, drawing then it works well as a basic guide. On the other hand if, like me, you already have a number of drawing guides then you will find a lot of information that is common to all of them. For example: colour theory, hatching, stippling, tonal values. The DK design and layout is better than some of these others though.
The reason I've dropped one star is that I like to be motivated by the sample illustrations in a drawing guide. If I like the work of the artists then I am more likely to be inspired. The illustrations in this book are good, but are mostly 'classic' subjects - portraits, landscapes, animals and fruit. My personal tastes are a tad more modern and graphic but that is just my perspective and I'm sure the subjects protrayed will appeal to many others.
PRODUCT: Artist's Drawing Techniques: Discover How to Draw Landscapes, People, Still Lifes and More, in Pencil, Charcoal, Pen and Pastel

REVIEW_TITLE: As toys to be played with, these are fine. Collectors may be disappointed.
REVIEW:
These are two nice figures for a Star Wars fan to play with (child or adult!), made as they are from sturdy plastic. The rocket launcher of course did not feature in the film and does seem rather... unwieldy. Speaking of which the Poe Dameron has no means of actually holding or operating the device, although he can hold the blaster firearm also included. The projectiles travel a reasonable distance and at a force unlikely to hurt a child.
The First Order Snowtrooper has his own rifle that he can hold.
Now, if you're thinking of buying this as a collector rather than as a toy you may be disappointed. While the Snowtrooper looks good, not surprising since it's mainly a featureless white uniform and helmet, Poe doesn't look much like Oscar Isaac. In fact, my first impression was of George Lazenby as James Bond. Still, at this price point most toys are of similar quality.
PRODUCT: Star Wars The Force Awakens Poe Dameron and First Order Snowtrooper Deluxe Pack Figure

REVIEW:
The Pentel Graphgear is my favourite mechanical pencil for sketching on the go. The metal body gives it a nice weight in the hand and the grip section near the tip stops it slipping in the fingers. Best of all, pressing on the clip to open it (to clip it on your pocket or bag for example) retracts the lead holder into the body to protect it. Simply press the end button again and it pops out ready for use. In the end is a rubber with a decent length and these are replaceable.
The body also has an indicator for the grade of graphite in use, simply rotate this to show HB, B etc. I now have two of these pencils, keeping one with HB and the other with 2B. Now I can travel light and not have to take pencil sharpener or protective case for traditional wooden pencils.
PRODUCT: Pentel 0.7mm Graphgear 1000 Mechanical Pencil

REVIEW_TITLE: Useful, once you realise these macros are intended for building solutions
REVIEW:
At first flick through, I wondered about the value of the Macro examples in this book. A lot of them initially appear to be things that you would do manually without more than a few mouse clicks: opening workbooks, copying a sheet from one workbook to another, emailing a file from within the app. More advanced examples include changing views in pivot tables or hiding rows and columns.
But actually, these are useful pieces of code for use when creating solutions to distribute to other people. Say you need to create a report with a pivot table and send it to someone else. You could create the pivot and send the file with a set of instructions, telling them how to see different views of the data. But how much more user-friendly to create some buttons that they can select that shows the data graphically in different ways.
So the real value in this book is in giving you the sample code to create automated solutions for non-technical folk or those with basic Excel skills.
PRODUCT: Excel Macros for Dummies, 2nd Edition (For Dummies (Computers))

REVIEW_TITLE: Expensive but worth it if you rely on your cables
REVIEW:
Being a Belkin cable, this is premium priced compared to some brands, but it feels like a premium product. The connectors fit snugly and securely and the reasonably thick feel inspire confidence that it won't wear like some Apple branded cables do.
Considering this is carrying up to 100W of charging capacity, I'd rather it be thicker than flimsy. I keep this in my rucksack and take it backwards and forwards to work each day (as decent cables have a tendency to go 'walkies') and it's showing no signs of wear and tear.
Recommended if you need to rely on a cable and regularly need to disconnect it.
PRODUCT: Belkin F2CU049bt2M-BLK 2 m USB-C to USB-C Monitor Cable - Black

REVIEW_TITLE: A good option for regular label printing or network sharing in a small office; print quality is good and offers good value
REVIEW:
The DYMO LabelWriter Wireless is a black plastic box with a grey stripe that looks stylish and reasonably sleek. My desk accessories are mainly either black or grey so it fitted in well. There is a fairly large power brick between it and the mains but the lead from the brick to the printer is quite long so it can stay out of sight. Given that it's intended for network sharing, it's large enough to hold a decent supply of labels yet still retain a reasonably small footprint.
The box contains the printer itself plus the aforementioned mains cables, a USB lead if you can't use the wireless function and starter pack of labels. After powering on, the labels need to be fitted on the spindle inside before proceeding. At first it seems as if the spindle unscrews but while it rotates freely, it isn't a thread but a series of grooves. One half of the spindle is pulled or pushed across these grooves to allow the label roll to be inserted. While doing this it makes a brittle noise that doesn't inspire confidence. Anyway, the labels are then fed from the bottom into a slot, at which point the printer will auto feed them. It's important to make sure the label roll is firmly to the left side (facing the printer) and that you do the same when feding through the slot, otherwise they will feed at an angle. Finally there's a grey label guide that needs to be slid across.
Joining the printer to the network was simple - push a very small button on the rear (next to the the USB port) to make the wi-fi symbol glow and then press the WPS button on your router. Once the wi-fi symbol on the printer stops flashing, it is connected.
Next is to install the DYMO app. I didn't want another app on my phone so installed the Windows app from the DYMO website. 160MB seemed a lot but it does install itself into Microsoft Office if found, for direct printing. Before loading the DYMO Label app, you need to run an app called DYMO Add Printer Utility first to identify the printer on the network. I guess you don't need to do this if using USB.
Finally you're ready to print something. My advice here is firstly, select the Large Address label type as this not the app's default. Secondly don't print anything you want to use on the very first label on the roll. In my case it wasn't a full label and was also covered in gunk from the tape that seals the roll.
The app gives you a number of templates to choose from, some with graphics, or bar codes and others just plain text address labels. I chose the latter and the printer straight away shot out the printed label, which you can tear off by pulling downward across the metal teeth. The quality is perfectly good for labels, not quite as sharp as a laser printer but cheaper to run in the long run especially if you look for compatible labels here on Amazon.
PRODUCT: DYMO Label Writer Wireless Printer - Black

REVIEW:
Have bought this every year since getting into stargazing with my wife. We're only amateurs so love the simple instructions and clear maps of the sky, which seem to be subtly better this year possibly the quality of the printing has increased over the 2017 one.
The information is informative but not dry or boring and there is useful information at the back on where dark skies can be found across the UK. For townies like us, it's useful to know where to head for the best chance of seeing the 'faint fuzzies'!
PRODUCT: Philip's 2018 Stargazing Month-by-Month Guide to the Night Sky Britain & Ireland

REVIEW_TITLE: Excellent recording quality; price befits a device that want to be taken seriously but it doesn't quite feel like a pro tool
REVIEW:
Philips have a history of decent voice recorders for dictation purposes and with this product are stepping up to the professional music recording market, with a corresponding increase in price. If all you want is a dictation machine or journalists recording interviews, this feels like overkill. The quality of recording is excellent though so if money is no object you will be pleased with the results.
It's a chunky and reasonably weighty device and feels like a quality item although it seems to be of a mainly plastic construction so the pristine finish may not last too long. There is a soft case provided in the box, along with a separate XLR connector for external microphones or instruments. I got this for my wife who sings part-time and have to use the XLR add-on in order to use the tripod bush, which is on the base of it. A muffler is provided, which is good and helps to reduce wind noise for external recordings.
It's quite a complex device to use and there are lots of options in the menu. The main manual is on the device's storage so you'll have to connect to a computer to get the PDF off.
Recordings can be made in mp3 or full quality PCM at up to 24-bit quality, at the cost of greatly increased storage. The quality is very good though especially if the singer likes to analyse their performance and breathing.
PRODUCT: Philips DVT 7500 Digital Audio Recorder

REVIEW_TITLE: The album that should see KWS overtake Joe Bonamassa in the white blues singer/guitar player stakes
REVIEW:
I've been listening to this album via Apple Music daily for the last week or so and just had to order the CD. Not often I bother to do that nowadays with streaming so easy, but every so often a really good album comes along. One that's worth listening to in CD quality.
I've been a fan of Kenny for a couple of years, since hearing the Live! In Chicago album and I've bought all his others on CD as well. The last studio album Going' Home was released three years ago and maybe Joe Bonamassa's more frequent album releases and tours equate to his greater success over here but Kenny is a much better singer and equal in the guitar stakes.
This is the album that should see him rated higher than Joe in my opinion. The songs here all work as proper songs, where with Joe I'm often listening more to the licks and waiting for the solo than to his voice. Kenny's solos and licks fit the songs really well, not out-staying their welcome or overpowering the songs or the rest of the band, who are tighter than a gnat's chuff.
I guess this will be categorised as Blues but there are a wider range of rock influences here, even Country on Hard Lesson Learned. Highlights are the title track, the hot horn Diamonds & Gold, the bouncy fun of She's $$$ and Down For Love but there are no duds on this album!
PRODUCT: Lay It On Down

REVIEW_TITLE: A perfect gift - nicely packaged, look very smart and perform very well
REVIEW:
This set of mills comes in very nice packaging that automatically made me think of giving them as a gift to someone. If that's your intention then they certainly look like a premium item. The mills themselves are nice and chunky to hold and look very smart on the dining table. I prefer the square shape to cylindrical ones for the purposes of grip. There is an S and P marked on them which you might think is a bit silly since you can see the contents, but the mechanisms are different - ceramic for the salt and steel for the pepper - so it's important to put the right contents in each. They arrive pre-filled (well, pre-half-filled) which I found unusual but the date on them was 2019 so should be fine.
In use they work well and are easily adjustable for coarser or finer results. I'm very pleased with them!
PRODUCT: Cole & Mason Kempton Salt and Pepper Mill Set, Metallic, 13 cm

REVIEW_TITLE: Very lightweight and comfortable to wear at the expense of padding for gear
REVIEW:
This backpack is extremely lightweight, which is great for cabin baggage as well as carrying. I was able to fit a 15" MacBook Pro in the laptop compartment, plus a 10.5" iPad Pro with keyboard cover in the tablet compartment. The two front compartments and top are each capable of holding a kindle or notebook. The 'secret' compartment in the back is full width but quite narrow, fine for passports, tickets and a phone.
On the sides are compartments that could hold a small bottle of water, one of them has a rain cover for smaller contents. Besides these on the inside are a mesh zip compartment and two other pockets for cables. This just leaves some full height free space in the centre, which could hold a lightweight fleece or jacket maybe. Even with all of these full, it was quite well balanced and comfortable to wear.
One downside of the lightweight construction is the minimal padding and protection. The laptop and tablet compartments are lined with soft material but it will not provide much protection, particularly to the laptop, which rests on the base. The North Face Surge backpack I normally use for commuting suspends the laptop in the center, thus offering more protection. It also has a lot more compartments but it is much more expensive and heavier when empty.
The Belkin is great for casual use though and I've enjoyed using it for art trips to carry my sketch pads and pencils/watercolour paints in the center plus laptop and iPad.
PRODUCT: Belkin F8N902 Active Pro Commuter Backpack for 15.6 inch Laptop with Reflective Strip, Security Pocket and Waterproof Base - Black

REVIEW_TITLE: Stylish, minimalist and well designed. A little pricey and no storage for a spare lightning lead though
REVIEW:
I've had an Apple pencil for about a year, but it's only recently that decent storage solutions have begun to appear. There have been solutions for the pen itself and iPad cases with pen holders, but storage for the easily lost spare tip and tiny charging connector was always the problem. This Belkin case-come-stand could be the solution I, and others have been waiting for.
The packaging certainly looks expensive with its gatefold, magnetic sealed cardboard top and gives the impression of a quality item. Given the price, it probably needs this marketing effort, since it's 5 times more expensive than the zipped wallet style case I've been using. Removing the case from the box, we have a two-tone box that is solid white shiny plastic on the base and dark grey matte finished plastic forming the lid. On the left hand side of the top surface is the belkin logo and on the right a circular well that forms the stand for the pencil. The pencil is inserted tip downwards for protection. When inserted this way the pencil is stable with hardly any wobble. It looks minimalist and stylish on my desk.
Remove the magnetic lid and in the base are a slot for the pencil, with a circular well under the tip to aid removal, much like the original Apple box. Above this and to the left is a half length slot with a sliding cover. Slide the cover to the right to reveal (from left to right) storage for: the lid while charging, the lightning connector and the spare tip. A neat feature is that the sliding cover is damped so that it can be left to reveal only the first, or first and second compartments. This is useful in that if you only need to reveal the first compartment to store the lid while inserting the pencil into your iPad, the other two small parts are still safely covered. Alas there's nowhere to store a lightning lead but I guess if you're travelling with an iPad you'll already have that stored elsewhere.
With the lid on, there is minimal rattle from inside. The magnet keeping the lid on is reasonably strong - I was able to pick the entire case up just gripping the lid and it took a deliberate shake to make the base disconnect accidentally. It should be quite secure when travelling then but placing in a narrow compartment in a bag is probably still wise. Overall, yes it's quite expensive for a pencil case but consider that Apple want around the same for a leather sleeve for just the pencil and maybe it's not so bad after all.
PRODUCT: Belkin Case Plus Stand for Apple Pencil - White/Grey

REVIEW_TITLE: Perfect for travelling - solid build, small size and fast performance
REVIEW:
With its brushed aluminium surface and chrome edges, this little Lexar SSD is very stylish. It's a little weighty but in a re-assuring, solidly-built way. I prefer this to plastic flexible construction for portable products: it feels like it was built to last.
The connection port is USB-C but a USB-A to standard USB3 6 inch cable is supplied. The device is small, at 7cm wide and 5.5cm tall; it's just under 1cm thick.
I plugged it into my MacBook Pro, which found it immediately. Copying small (under 10MB) files was so quick there wasn't even a progress bar. I unplugged from the Mac and connected to my Windows 10 PC, which also identified it immediately. Copying across a 1.3GB folder containing Imelda May's current album in hi-res took 13 seconds to complete. A 2.5GB folder of hi-res Verdi operas took 24 seconds. Impressive!
With its small size, good build quality and fast performance I think this is an excellent little drive.
PRODUCT: Lexar SL100 512GB Portable SSD - LPSSD512RBEU

REVIEW_TITLE: Charges various types of device efficiently without becoming hot. Not cheap but a quality item.
REVIEW:
The Belkin PocketPower is a stylish black slab that is slightly smaller in length and width than an iPhone 6/7 and a tad deeper. The only markings on it are the belkin name and their dotted figure logo in grey. It's a little heavier than the phone but entirely portable with its smoothly rounded corners. There are two USB ports, a micro port for charging the battery pack and a type A USB for connecting to the device to be charged. A 7" cable is supplied for charging the PocketPower.
Straight out of the box I connected it to my iPhone 7, which had around 35% charge at the time and it charged it to 100% in a little over an hour. I then connected the charging port to my desktop PCs USB3 socket and left it to fully charge. There are four green LEDs on the edge that show charging progress. Unfortunately I was working at the time and didn't notice exactly how long it took, but 4 hours later it had all 4 LEDs lit.
Once the battery pack was fully charged I used it to charge up my work BlackBerry from about 1/5th power to full charge, followed by my iPhone again (the following day) and my iPad Pro from 80% to 100%. There were 2 LEDs still lit after all this so I decided to try and charge my AKG Y50BT headphones. The red light came on on the headphones to indicate charging but when I checked 10 minutes later the lights had gone off on both the headphones and the PocketPower. Trying again lead to the same result, but the PowerBank still had some juice left so I assume this was the voltage fluctuation circuitry kicking in. Final test was a Kindle PaperWhite, which charged up with no issues.
At no time during all this charging did the Belkin become hot. There are a number of claims made about safety features, of which the heat control is one. The shutoff in the event of voltage issues, which I think is what happened with the bluetooth headphones, is another. Normally you have to take the manufacturers word for such features but it looks like they are true. Possibly this is what contributes to the price, as a comparison of competing products shows many cheaper alternatives from smaller companies.
I was quite impressed by the device though the price may deter some, but the safety features may be enough to persuade you.
PRODUCT: Belkin PocketPower 5000 mAh Ultra Power Bank, High Speed Portable Charger for Apple iPhone 8/8 Plus/X/7 Plus/7/6s/6s Plus/6/SE/5/Samsung Galaxy S7/S8/S8+/Google Pixel/Huawei P9 - Black

REVIEW_TITLE: No frills but no fuss either, it just works!
REVIEW:
This is an unassuming black plastic box that may not win many prizes for style but the function works perfectly. That is, of course, so long as your chosen device supports the HDMI output from USB-C. If not then you've still got a 4 port USB3 hub. Being made of plastic it is very light and portable. It's also reasonably solid and only flexes when pressure is applied to top and bottom.
The output cable is captive so can't get lost. Simply plug your device's USB-C power plug into the Aukey and then the Aukey's cable into the device. External devices can then be plugged into the USB3 and/or HDMI ports. The Aukey can support two external USB hard drives connected simultaneously and it's recommended that one is connected at each end. There aren't many more instructions in the manual, but then that about covers it. With a Mac laptop it just worked, including the HDMI but if you have a different device worth checking the Amazon product description for known issues.
PRODUCT: AUKEY USB C Hub HDMI Port ( 4K ), 4 USB 3.0 Data Transfer Ports and 100W USB C PD Port USB Type C Multiport Adapter for MacBook Pro 2016 / 2017, iMac 2017, Chromebook Pixel, Samsung S8 and More

REVIEW_TITLE: Five stars for the product but the 10 year warranty seems to be just a marketing thing
REVIEW:
There are lots of brands of screen protectors on the market and they seem to come and go regularly. I think the last three I've had have all come from different brands and none of them seem to be around any more. All of which makes me wonder how much value there really is in the 10 year warranty promised with the Eiger. Note that it only covers manufacturing defects and not deliberate or accidental damage. Good luck proving that.
In the box are the protector itself, instructions, the warranty card and a cleaning kit. The latter contains a cleansing wipe, lint free cloth and dust removal sticker. If you've ever fitted one of these before you'll know the drill but the instruction are quite clear if not. I usually find having some sellotape to hand is useful not only to dab off dust spots that are left behind but also to lift the protector as trying to pick the edge with a fingernail can damage it and cause it not to stick completely.
With the slightly curved edges of the phone it's not quite so easy to line it up perfectly using the circular home button cutout. The speaker cutout is a better bet. Once on, the screen is perfectly clear and there's minimal drag for finger swipes.
PRODUCT: iPhone 8 Plus Screen Protector, EIGER [Japanese Asahi Glass], [Case-Compatible] for Apple iPhone 8 Plus, iPhone 7 Plus Screen Protector Tempered Glass inc. Cleaning Kit in the Pack (EGSP00101)

REVIEW_TITLE: Not quite as black as the ink in Sakura Microns but a good set of pigment liners nonetheless
REVIEW:
Pigment fine liner pens are the go-to tool for zentangles, mandalas, doodles and urban sketching. While Sakura Micron pens are the popular choice, there are other options and the Staedtler pigment liners are one such example.
I've used the Staedtler pens before and have found them to be quick drying (so no smudging) and lightfast. This set contains probably every width you are likely to need from 0.05 through to 0.8, all clearly indicated on the lid and the body so no need to worry about mixing up the lids. Since they can apparently be left for up to 18 hours with the cap off and not dry out this is useful. I'm not in the habit of leaving the lids off for anywhere near that long so not able to comment on whether that is true.
The pens have a matte finish so are easy to grip and feel well made. The nice thing about the case is that the lid can be folded back behind the pens to make a useful angled stand. In use the pens make good quality lines and are almost identical to the marks made by similar Sakura pens. The Sakuras do seem to be slightly darker though: side by side, the Staedtler lines look more like a very dark grey in comprison. I think if it were possible I would drop half a star from the Staedtlers for that, but otherwise these are good quality pens for practice and general portability.
PRODUCT: Pigment Liner STAEDTLER Pigment Liner, Pack 5 + 1

REVIEW_TITLE: A decent refillable gel pen from Pentel with a medium tip and smooth flow of quick-drying ink
REVIEW:
The Pentel EnerGel pen is a refillable metal bodied gel pen as opposed to the standard plastic disposable gel pen. The body is nicely weighted and has chrome highlights on a violet coloured background; whether the colour appeals to you is a question of taste. The button has a solid action to reveal the writing tip but is a bit wobbly afterward; the clip is solid and grips well so it shouldn't fall out of a pocket. Note that the writing tip is supplied with a small silicon seal attached, which needs to be picked off before first use.
Unscrew the barrel at the centre to reveal the refill, which is labelled as Pentel 07 LR7. These currently cost around �10 for a box of 12 on Pentel Liquid Gel Refill - Black Amazon.
The pen writes very smoothly as you would expect for a gel pen and the ink dries quickly though it will smudge if you immediately touch the last mark made. The colour is a deep black and seems to be permanent. For my writing the 0.7 tip is a little too thick and I found myself writing slightly larger than normal to compensate for this. If you normally use a medium tipped pen you should be fine with this size.
Overall it's a nice pen and feels better in the hand than a plastic disposable but I'm not sure I would refer to it as 'premium'.
PRODUCT: Pentel 0.7 mm Tip "EnerGel Sterling Black Ink" Pen - Violet (Pack of 12)

REVIEW_TITLE: Very well articulated figures can't make up for the high price and useless Sandman part unless you buy the set
REVIEW:
This is one from a series of Spider-Man related figures that each contain a component part of the Sandman. If you buy all the figures you can build the Sandman who is not available separately. Given that each figure is around �27, that makes ol' Sandy an expensive guy. Of course this makes him especially collectable and potentially valuable in years to come but there are no guarantees. Three of the figures in the set are Spider-Man himself, one in his modern black suit and the other two 'multiverse Spider-Men' being Spider-UK and Spider-Man 2099.
They are well made and very poseable with multiple joint movements, but are just not good value at this price hence the 2 stars dropped. Parents buying one of these will find themselves under pressure to complete the set for a not insignificant outlay.
PRODUCT: Spider-Man Marvel Legends Series Shocker Figure, 6-Inch

REVIEW_TITLE: Part training manual, part sketchbook, Jake Spicer guides you in really seeing your subject as well as making marks on paper
REVIEW:
This is a drawing guide/sketchbook with a handy rubber band closure. It contains a succession of sketching exercises followed by blank pages for you to practice yourself. A range of subjects and techniques is covered for both pencils and ink. Equal focus is given to making marks on the paper as it is to really looking and seeing the subject. Although you can dip in and pick an exercise at random, following them in order will give the ideal progression. Jake Spicer encourages you to find an exercise you enjoy and keep practising it. This is great advice as it can become a chore to repeatedly practise something that gives you no pleasure - you are far more likely to give up.
I'm always suspicious of books that make claims to teach you something in a defined period. After all, we all learn at a different rate. But I've no doubt that anyone from complete beginners to the more advanced will learn something new from this book. For example, creating the illusion of depth by drawing less detail in the objects further away was something new to me. If you do all the exercises, by the end of the book you will know about tone, values, perspective, shapes and so on. Like any book on the subject though, it's practicing these skills that ultimately defines whether you are able to draw to the standard you aspire to.
PRODUCT: You Will be Able to Draw by the End of This Book

REVIEW_TITLE: A mini marvel in sound terms, this little speaker punches well above its weight
REVIEW:
This little speaker (about the size of a coffee mug minus the handle) certainly punches above its weight in terms of sound. The capitalised EXTRA BASS had me a little concerned that this would be similar to the - more expensive - Wonderboom but I needn't have worried; the SRS-XB10 wants to play music rather than just thump away brainlessly.
Playing 'Too Far Gone' from Lindsay Buckingham and Christine McVie, the vocals were clear as were the guitars and keyboards. The bassline was clearly distinguishable as actual notes and helped the track bounce along well and equally impressive was the drum sections following the choruses, which sounded full but with the snap intact. Following this up with some Royal Blood, the little speaker did well to convey the power and attack of their sound.
There is a rubber loop attached to the SRS-SB10 for hanging it from things. When suspended there is a reduction in bass as the speaker uses the surface it's sitting on for reinforcement. It's water resistant (not waterproof), pairs easily through bluetooth and can be doubled up with a second speaker if you wish. For the size, weight and price it's a mini marvel in sound terms!
PRODUCT: Sony SRS-XB10 Compact Portable Wireless Speaker with Extra Bass - Black

REVIEW_TITLE: A good quality propelling pencil for a budget price, with spare lead to boot!
REVIEW:
This is a decent propelling pencil from the trusted Pentel brand. The P200 is lightweight with a largely plastic build and grooves for grip. Underneath the button is a rubber, which pulls out to reveal the lead holder, or hi-polymer as Pentel call it. One is already loaded, with 5 spares in the barrel plus another 12 are in a separate storage case. The lead is 0.5 in width, which is a nice fine line for general use. The rubber has a good length of spare so shouldn't run out too quickly.
I normally prefer the Pentel GraphGear1000 automatic pencil and given the choice would take it over the P200. The P200 is a little too light in the hand for me and I prefer the silicon grip on the 1000. It also withdraws the lead sleeve for protection while in your pocket, while the P200 does not. Still, you could buy 5 P200s for the price of a GG1000!
If you are after a good quality automatic pencil with lead (sorry, hi-polimer) that doesn't snap unless you press really hard then the P200 is a good choice at a budget price.
PRODUCT: Pentel P200 Automatic Pencil, 0.5 mm - Black

REVIEW_TITLE: Nice, stylish towels but the striped ones are less soft than the plain grey in this set
REVIEW:
This is a nice soft-feeling and stylish set of towels that would grace a modern bathroom. They are a decent size and nice weight, though my wife prefers bath sheet size towels that wrap right around. They have a good absorbency and it's interesting to see the label says to use minimal softener when washing them, to maintain that absorbency.
I've dropped one star as there is a slight difference in the softness of the towels in the set - the plain grey are noticeably softer than the striped, so it would be worth looking for a single colour set so as not to fight over who gets which one!
PRODUCT: Silentnight Towel Bale, Grey/Stripe, 4 Piece

REVIEW_TITLE: A good performing and solidly built mouse for pre-teens; the stickers supplied are not alternatives for the mouse body
REVIEW:
This is a pretty good mouse for a child or possibly anyone with small hands. It's clearly aimed at children with the cartoon character decoration and variety of styles available. For some reason I assumed the stickers that are advertised to come with it are alternatives for the for Sneaker Head character design, while they are actually just a sheet of chibi style stickers that are clearly not intended for use on the mouse.
The mouse takes a single AA battery (supplied) and is advertised to last for a year, though obviously this is for 'average' use. Sliding the bottom of the base down reveals the battery and the USB dongle, which is pretty neat and better than some others I've had where the dongle is either separate or clips in externally and soon becomes lost.
It paired quickly with both a Windows 10 PC and a MacBook laptop and worked perfectly well with both. It glides smoothly across the desk and both buttons give a reassuring and solid click. Similarly the wheel rotates smoothly and without any wobble and also gives a sold click when pressed. One star dropped for the stickers which are just a gimmick like the freebies inside breakfast cereal but otherwise a good solid mouse.
PRODUCT: Logitech M238 Wireless Mouse, Doodle Collection with 15 Premium Stickers, 12-Month Battery Life for Windows, Mac, Chrome OS and Linux - Sneaker Head

REVIEW_TITLE: A good introduction to watercolour for anyone who thinks it's limited to flowers and landscapes
REVIEW:
Watercolour is for flowers and landscapes right? Wrong. In this book professional artist Veronica Ballart Lilja demonstrates that watercolour is actually very versatile.
After the traditional opening chapters on colours, brushes and paper for the complete novice, the remainder of the book focuses on mixed media. In other words, using watercolour and other materials such as pencils, charcoal, ink etc.The latter sections are a series of tutorials using these techniques and introducing stenciling and collage to make a range of different pieces of art.
The pictures are colourful and modern throughout, which helps to dispel the staid reputation that watercolour can have and will certainly stimulate young and old alike. The only reason I've dropped one star is that the tutorials are a little hard to follow. In these days of YouTube free lessons, trying to follow instructions on creating an image based on a few images and lines of text pales somewhat in comparison to watching it being done.
PRODUCT: If You're Bored With WATERCOLOUR Read This Book (If you're ... Read This Book)

REVIEW_TITLE: Smart, stylish, well made and the non-slip feet are great
REVIEW:
Having used a mix of synthetic and wooden chopping boards for many years, the worst problems with the plastics were slipping and staining. The non-slip feed on either side of these Joseph Joseph boards (and the storage case) are rock solid. No more damp kitchen towel underneath! Having a variety of colours is also great because it reduces staining.
The large boards are a decent size and about the size I've used in the past so no issues there. They also have a very slightly curved surface so that juices spread to the edges. This is quite useful but can lead to spills if you don't keep it level when carrying to the sink or dishwasher.
Stored upright in their stylish grey sleeve they don't take up too much space on the worktop and are easily accessible with their bookmark style tabs. Very please with them.
PRODUCT: Joseph Joseph Index Chopping Board Set - Large, Graphite

REVIEW_TITLE: An enjoyable guide to getting great pictures using real-world equipment and no post-processing
REVIEW:
This book is largely made up of full page pictures, with the occasional double page spread, with the opposite page providing the background story, tips on how to get that type of image and the technical camera settings. The recipe style 'how to get this type of image' has proved popular and this is in a similar vein to Scott Kelby's Digital Photography Book series.
The overall concept is: how to get a usable image directly from the camera without needing to tweak anything on a computer first. For a photo dinosaur like me, we had no choice back in the film days but it's easy to become lazy and fix wonky horizons later. Of course the great thing with digital cameras is that you can immediately see if there are exposure problems. Adjust your settings and take another one. But sometimes it's not possible to do that - the subject has moved, or the light has changed.
Gordon Laing has a conversational style that almost feels like a one to one session. What I really liked is that the book doesn't waste time with the "this is a camera, this is a lens, this is a shutter speed..." early chapters but assumes you already know the basic stuff. Something to bear in mind if you are a total beginner but practically every other photo book has that information at the beginning. It's nice to find a book that doesn't try to be all things to all people.
The photos themselves cover a fairly wide range of subjects but mainly outdoor, urban and travel. There are one or two portraits but if that is your main subject of interest you might be disappointed. Many of the pictures are taken on CSC cameras thus appealing to a wider group than just those with DSLRs and proving that professional images can be taken with any camera if you apply the techniques Laing describes. I especially liked the real-world tips like supporting the camera on items of clothing. We all know that we *should* take a tripod everywhere but most of us do our photography on family holidays and it's rarely possible. All in all, it was good to read a book that goes back to the old-school getting it right first time but in a way that makes use of the functionality that cameras have built-in.
PRODUCT: In Camera: Perfect Pictures Straight Out of the Camera

REVIEW_TITLE: Good quality pouches but the zip shaves off bits of the seal and a premium price for the Leitz brand
REVIEW:
The Leitz Traveller Pouch Set contains three S/M/L sized transparent pouches with zip style seals. See-through travel pouches have an obvious use for your allowed liquids when passing through airport security, and being able to store odds and ends like USB leads together is useful if your baggage doesn't have compartments. In the product images they have currency in one but that seems a bit odd to me - why would you want anyone else to see where your money is when travelling abroad?
Anyway, the pouches are made of a strong plastic and the zip seals (like those on reseal-able food bags) are not loose so won't come undone accidentally. However they are pretty stiff in closing and I found that the metal zip mechanism actually shaved off bits of the plastic seals (attached is a photo) which look like dandruff inside the pouch.This is disappointing given that, being Leitz branded, they are quite expensive compared to similar items that are available through a quick google.
PRODUCT: Leitz Small, Medium and Large Traveller Zip Pouch Set Complete Range, Plastic, Clear

REVIEW_TITLE: A hybrid SSD/mechanical drive that doesn't do enough to make a significant benefit
REVIEW:
The Seagate FireCuda is a hybrid of a traditional hard drive (running at 7,200rpm) with an 8GB flash drive that operates like an SSD. It's a full size 3 1/2 inch drive so much larger than an SSD but of course considerably cheaper than a 2TB SSD would set you back.
The idea is that the applications that you use most often will be intelligently placed on the 8GB portion and therefore load at the speed of an SSD. I can see this being useful if you have an SSD as a boot drive and a second, larger, mechanical drive for data storage. In my own PC the SSD runs the operating system and the apps I use most commonly, while other apps are installed on a separate drive.
The FireCuda concept sounds good in theory but with only 8GB you are pretty restricted if you use large apps like photo or video editing suites with lots of plugins and extensions. In fact if you have a lot of apps and use most of them regularly, the effect on the drive of swapping things in and out of the 8GB section could actually slow things down. A better option would be to go for a larger SSD as drive C and just keep data on a larger physical drive.
I found the drive to be pretty quick and responsive but that could just be the 7200 speed. Compared to the wow factor of using an SSD for the first time, I wasn't blown away by the performance of the FireCuda. It may give a slight edge over a 'normal' 2TB drive but not enough to make it a preference.
PRODUCT: Seagate FireCuda 2TB 3.5" Internal SSHD

REVIEW_TITLE: Work well for noise reduction but the harmonics generated by the cord can be annoying
REVIEW:
The 3M earplugs are orange thermoplastic rubber (TPE) flanges much like the ones that come supplied with In Ear headphones. They are designed to push completely into the ear with only the small finger grips left externally. This is achieved by lifting the top of the ear slightly. If you've used In Ear headphones before, you'll be familiar with the movement but it can take a little bit of practice.
Once inserted properly, they do reduce the volume of external noise; not completely but this is safer than complete silence. When I put them in I had the television on in the background and despite the volume being greatly reduced, could still make out the voices afterward. The two plugs are joined by a blue cord, which is good to avoid losing one (the bright orange colour of the plugs helping as well) but has two downsides: (i) if you are using the plugs to reduce the noise of machinery that you are operating there is the risk of it becoming entangled and (ii) there are a lot of harmonics from the cord - as it rubs against clothing the sound is transmitted into your ears. Both of these can be reduced by putting the cord around the back of your neck rather than in front, but the harmonic issue doesn't completely go away.
In the pack is a massive sheet of instructions (maybe A2 sized) folded multiple times but the English section is reasonably small. Much of this is safety and cleaning instructions. They are re-usable and can be cleaned up to 50 times.
PRODUCT: 3M 1271C 87 - 98 dB Corded Reusable Ear Plugs Protection, Beige

REVIEW_TITLE: A popular choice for card makers and crafters
REVIEW: I got this for my wife who is into card making. She said it's good quality, sticks down well and is a good width for smaller cards.
PRODUCT: Scotch 15 mm x 10 m Refill Cracked Expressions Washi Tape Roll - Blue

REVIEW_TITLE: A waterproof and rinse-able bluetooth speaker with average sound
REVIEW:
The unique selling point of the WONDERBOOM is that it is waterproof, floats in water and can be rinsed under the tap if it gets dirty. This makes it ideal for the beach, assuming that you're not annoying anyone else with your tunes of choice. It's also very simple to use with over-large volume buttons and two other buttons for on/off and pairing. It's small and reasonably light with a blue material loop for carrying.
If you want something for the shower, bath or beach then it could be ideal. The only possible weakness in the waterproofing is that it does need to be charged through a micro USB port, so the port is covered with a rubber seal. On my sample this was a little bit loose and although I didn't have any leaks during testing, in repeated use it might gradually become less of a seal.
So far so good. How does it sound though? The promotional blurb claims "deep powerful bass" and the ability to go loud. Well it does go pretty loud but the bass is much less the sound of a musical instrument than the sound of a heavy book landing on a desk. Deep certainly, but not musical. It's also detached from the rest of the sound which stops some way short of a full midrange. The overall effect is of trying to listen to music on an average speaker while someone is piling hardbacks for the charity shop.
If you really, really need something waterproof and sound quality is not a priority then this could be a good choice. Personally, I'd rather have something that sounds better and not get it wet.
PRODUCT: Ultimate Ears "UE" WONDERBOOM Bluetooth Speaker Waterproof with Double-Up Connection - Fireball Red

REVIEW_TITLE: Perfect for sketching and watercolouring on the move
REVIEW:
Water brush pens are great for art journalling on the move. With these three pens, my Winsor & Newton Cotman Water Colour Paints - 12 Half Pans and Moleskine sketchbook I can quickly sketch and wash on the move.
If you've not used them before, the bottom half of the brush can be filled with water and gently squeezing sends water through to the bristles. If you need to change colour then simply squeeze water through and wipe to clean. Obviously there is a limit to the amount of water that each pen can hold so you may have to take a separate water source for refilling if you have a large surface to cover or do a lot of different sketches.
PRODUCT: Pentel Aquash Water Brush Pens, Assorted Tips - Pack of 3 (Fine, Medium and Broad)

REVIEW_TITLE: A nice relaxing effect but not as good as a cold flannel for my irritated eyes
REVIEW:
I suffer from itchy and sore eyes towards the end of the day, largely because I work in technology and spend hours looking at screens. I normally find a cold flannel helps when the itchiness gets too bad but my optician recommend I try heat instead. Enter the Optrex Warming Eye Mask.
The packaging lists various warnings and pre-requisites, some of which are obvious and presumably exist to prevent stupid people from suing Optrex. The 'don't fall asleep while wearing' one is useful though, as I found they made me quite drowsy. As I mentioned above though, I normally need these at the end of the day so that is also a factor.
The mask is essentially two squares with a nose slot at the bottom with a loop each side that goes around your ears. Some other reviewers have said that they would prefer a closer fit to the eyes but I have a large head so found they were close enough for me.once wrapped around the ears. The heat appears quickly and on first use I was a little alarmed at how quickly they reached maximum temperature, not knowing how hot they would eventually get.
There is a vague aroma that I might not have called lavender if the box hadn't told me but it's not unpleasant and adds to the overall relaxing effect. After 15 minutes the heat started to fade away. On removing I found the cooling effect of the air very pleasant and I generally felt quite relaxed but the itchy sensation was still present - reduced, but still there. I don't think I would buy these specifically for me dry eyes problem as the cold flannel works almost straight away but the effect of the masks is akin to the airlines that hand out hot flannels on long haul flights; refreshing and relaxing.
PRODUCT: Optrex Warming Eye Mask, Lavender, Pack of 8

REVIEW:
The Pentel brush pen is a great portable solution for inking/rendering or for anyone who wants to avoid the potential mess of separate brush and ink.The ink is pure black and gives beautiful contrast on Bristol Board or other surface intended for ink. In a normal sketchpad it can bleed through onto the page beneath and in doing so look more of a very dark grey. In a Molskine it didn't come though completely but it could be seen on the rear of the page.
The great thing is that the nylon bristles never go hard (as long as the lid is tightly on when not in use) and give a lovely transition from broad to narrow line. If you've never drawn with a brush before this is a good way to try out and practice (you'll need a lot of practice!) without buying expensive sable brushes and bottles of ink. The cartridges also last a long time before needing to be replaced.
The only slight negative for anyone who has used a brush I would say is that the body of the pen is a lot shorter so might mean changing your grip style. If that's a problem, check out the Kuretake Sumi Brush Pen Blister -No8pen, which has a longer body and a different balance.
PRODUCT: Pentel XGFKP/FP10-A Brush Pen and Two Refills, Black Ink

REVIEW_TITLE: Not quite as effective as Gaviscon liquid but the best solution for flights and travelling
REVIEW:
Gaviscon liquid is ever-present in our house as my wife has a hiatus hernia and suffers from regular indigestion. I also take it but fortunately not as often as her. It's still the best and fastest acting remedy we've tried.
However liquids are a problem when travelling by air, unless you pay over the odds in the duty free shops. This is where the tablets come in when we go on holiday. Neither of us find them to be as quick acting as the liquid and you sometimes need to chew a few more but they do still work. A pack of 48 is more than enough to get us through a fortnight holiday in most locations (maybe a trip to Mexico or the far east would need more!)
PRODUCT: Gaviscon Peppermint Tablets, Pack of 48

REVIEW_TITLE: Caveat emptor - poor manufacturing and quality
REVIEW:
I can't believe these are the same quality of pencil beloved by Roald Dahl for writing. In my box the eraser has been squashed onto the end so that the wood is splintered around it, the graphite is scratchy and faint and the wood does not sharpen smoothly. If you want an excellent writing/drawing pencil with a rubber on the end, the Palomino Blackwing Pencils - Set of 12are the best I've ever used. Of course they cost considerably more but you get what you pay for. The Tombow Mono 100 HB Pencils (Box of 12) and Uni Hi-Uni Wooden Pencil - HB - Box of 12 are almost as good but without the eraser.
If this is the quality of product that comes from Mexico then maybe someone should build a wall!
PRODUCT: Genuine - Dixon Ticonderoga Cedar Artist Pencil, No.2, 12 pack

REVIEW_TITLE: Fast and reasonably priced, photographers this is one for you
REVIEW:
It wasn't so long ago that the maximum size of an SSD was 128GB and only about big enough to install the operating system. The main benefit of an SSD is read speed so placing the OS on one results in faster booting and - if there's room - loading the apps you use the most. This is the first reasonably priced 1TB SSD I've seen but what benefit can you get from the greater size?
I'm a serious amateur photographer and use Photoshop and Lightroom, both of them with a range of plugins, fonts, brushes and other tools. All of these increase the load time of the apps and the amount of disk space used. Not a problem for a 1TB drive though: Photoshop loads blazingly fast even with the plugins.
The second advantage for photographers with laptops is being able to edit pictures while away from home. Like many 'togs, I keep my raw files stored on a NAS server at home, but the 1TB SSD means I can download files from the camera onto the drive and do initial editing away from home. Or even at home, as loading 20MB files over the network or USB is much slower than having them locally loaded from the drive.
PRODUCT: WD 1 TB 2.5 Inch SSD Read 545 MB/s, Write 525 MB/s - Blue

REVIEW_TITLE: Gets the slaphead seal of approval!
REVIEW:
As a slaphead I have to use moisturiser daily but I also have oily skin. So finding a mosturiser that protects from the effects of the cold wind without making my skin prone to spots is the challenge. This is the first ManCave product I've used but if this is an example of the quality, I'll be checking out the rest of the range.
I'm always cynical about 'natural' ingredients like Shea Butter and Nordic Cotton but regardless of that I was surprised by how smooth my scalp felt a few minutes after using the product. It spreads well so you only need a small amount and it absorbs quickly. It is only lightly scented, apparently something called Woodsman though it just smells vaguely medicinal to me. Maybe I'll burst into a few verses of the Lumberjack Song later.
PRODUCT: ManCave Natural Sensitive Moisturiser - 100 ml

REVIEW_TITLE: A hard size to find in supermarkets but you can't go far wrong with a Duracell
REVIEW:
The type N battery is one of the less common battery types, so can be hard to get hold of in supermarkets and newsagents. My mum has a bedside clock that uses them so I got them for her as a spare set. The date on them is 2020 so they will be fine in the drawer until she needs them. The existing batteries in the clock are Duracell and they've lasted over a year so far, longer than the ones that originally came supplied with the clock.
Hard to give a 5 star 'love' rating to a battery! They do what you expect them to do, no more, no less so a 4 star like it is.
PRODUCT: Duracell Specialty Type N Alkaline Battery, pack of 2

REVIEW_TITLE: Sleek and adds minimal bulk; but the clear back shows up fingerprints, the camera lens lies flush and grip is minimal
REVIEW:
This Belkin case adds minimal bulk to your iPhone while adding a decent level of protection. I say decent because I wasn't tempted to drop it to prove the protection. On my previous iPhone 6 I had a Thule case, which did add an element of bulk but also gave a level of confidence that I don't get to the same extent with this. Specifically the Thule had a 'grippy' surface that never slipped out of my hand; the Belkin has dimples on the edges but these add minimal grip. The case apparently has 4 foot drop protection but as I'm over 6 foot and more likely to drop it on a hard surface while standing or walking than while sitting,
I thought the clear back would show off the jet black finish of the phone while preventing it from getting scratched, but the UV protection takes away from that. Also, being clear it shows up fingerprints quite badly.
In the end though I did buy another Thule case for the additional comfort factor; protecting my investment in the phone is more important to me than minimal bulk.
Update - one other thing I noticed with this case is that the rear is not deep enough to fully protect the camera lens, which ends up flush with the rear of the case and could get scratched.
PRODUCT: Belkin Air Protect SheerForce Drop and UV Protection Case with Push + Click Buttons for iPhone 7 - Matte Black

REVIEW_TITLE: It's a battery and it comes with a 'battery tester' that didn't work but at least the battery did
REVIEW:
It's a battery, it's one of those awkward oblong ones with the connections seemingly created in the steampunk era, and it's a Duracell. It's now in one of my smoke alarms, replacing the one that had been in there for at least 4 years. If I remember to update this review in however many years' time, and you remember to come back to check I did, then we'll see if it lasted as long.
The only other thing to say is that the packaging apparently contains a tester to tell you how much power there is in your battery. It's a liar. It told me all the ones I tested were dead, including it's partner in the box, which does have life. I'm always dubious about battery testers anyway - who goes around taking batteries out of things to see if they've got life? Just switch the thing on!
PRODUCT: Duracell 9V PP3 Ultra Power Alkaline Battery (LR22). 1 Pack

REVIEW_TITLE: Useful length for a spare USB power lead but note that this is only USB 2.0 rated for data speeds
REVIEW:
USB Type C is the latest connector type and is starting to appear more commonly on devices, notably the latest MacBook Pro. Type C is similar in ease of use to the Apple Lightning connector (the two are NOT interchangeable) in that the cable can be inserted either side up or at either end, both are the same. It is backwards compatible but as the connectors are completely different you will need an adaptor, thus opening up a secondary market for over-priced dongles.
Type C will also be used to transfer video and audio along with the new Thunderbolt 3 standard, so it is worth noting that this Amazon cable is rated as only USB 2.0. It's therefore perhaps better suited as a secondary power lead to leave at the office than to connect peripherals but at least 6 feet is a decent length to be from a power socket.
PRODUCT: AmazonBasics USB Type-C to USB Type-C 2.0 Cable - 1.8 m - White

REVIEW_TITLE: A complete waste of money - just buy the pens
REVIEW:
I wish I had seen this in an art shop before I ordered or I would not have bothered. The 'sketchbook' is basically 10 sheets of A4 paper folded in half with a piece of brown card on the outside. On half of the resulting A5 pages are outlines of animals (NOT including the fox on the exterior of the packaging), with a double-spread owl in the centre; the remaining pages are blank.
The product images on this page are very misleading - the photo of the partially completed fox with pens scattered across the work surface is at least 4 times the actual size of any of the outlines in the 'sketchbook'. Also the "learn to draw with artist Iain McArthur" (Derwent can't even get his name right - it's MacArthur) amounts to little more than a couple of close-up pictures of the fox on the back of the box and, inside the sketchbook, a page of dots and lines that you can draw over.
Save your money and just buy the pens.
PRODUCT: SG Education DER 2302322 Derwent Graphik Inked Up Set

REVIEW_TITLE: Useful for sticking to stuff. And writing on them.
REVIEW:
It seems a bit old fashioned to use Post-it page markers in this e-book era, but I find them really useful for marking my place in textbooks. At the moment I'm working my way through "1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die" and colour tagging each one I've listened to so far. Starting with red for Albums I Never Want To Hear Again right through to green for Albums That Are Surprisingly Good. I haven't got to the Hip Hop era so I'm trying not to use too many reds yet :-)
Joking aside, there isn't much new to say about Post-its. They're sticky bits of paper that... stick!
PRODUCT: Post-it 12.7 x 44.4 mm Notes Markers Jaipour Pads (Pack of 5)

REVIEW_TITLE: For Filofax Personal size organisers this is a very useful hole punch
REVIEW:
I got this specifically for my wife, who goes nowhere without her Filofax PERSONAL size organiser, which has 6 holes. In order to punch the holes in the correct position, the plastic slider has a pre-marked setting specifically for this size binder. For this purpose it works perfectly, punching up to 10 sheets of normal organiser thickness paper, i.e. not very thick.
There are markings on the device for other organiser sizes but I have none other available to test with.
PRODUCT: Rapesco Adjustable 6-Hole Organiser/ Diary Punch (White)

REVIEW_TITLE: A tough and effective case for your precious camera gear when travelling
REVIEW:
Having been into photography for over 30 years, there have been many items of equipment and accessories I've owned over the years. One thing I've always wanted, but never got around to buying, was a hard camera case. Thanks to AmazonBasics I finally have the chance to try one out.
The great thing about hard cases is not having to worry about putting your precious lenses and body into the hold of an aeroplane. With ever decreasing cabin allowances I often struggle to take more than one lens when flying. This AmazonBasic case is seriously tough. I stood on it and it didn't bend at all, useful if you need to see over a crowd. I didn't try throwing it or dropping from a great height but dropping from shoulder height onto a brick patio resulted in nothing other than a minor scuff.
Inside, the foam is split into cubes that can be pulled out to fit the size of your kit. How much you will fit in depends on the size of the hardware - you might get a full mirrorless system in with several lenses and room to spare for a flashgun. A bigger pro-size DSLR body will still leave room for two to three shorter zooms or primes.
The one thing I was a little disappointed with was the lack of any instructions for the pressure gauge dial. Presumably this is used before/after travelling in the hold of a 'plane, but which end of the dial should be used for each, and when (straight from baggage collection or after a period of time?) is left to you to find out.
PRODUCT: AmazonBasics Hard Camera Case, Medium

REVIEW_TITLE: An excellent fantasy adventure that occasionally veers into young adult territory
REVIEW:
I'd never read any of Laini Taylor's previous books before Strange the Dreamer. I almost stopped reading it after the prologue, which seemed to me at the time to be a barrage of simile and metaphor, obstructing rather than enhancing.
Fortunately Chapter 1 onwards is more focussed, progressing the story of Lazlo Strange and his obsession with the fabled city that has its name stolen. The cast of characters increases gradually, each with their own defined personality, as the nature of the adventure at the heart of the story is revealed. The book has been described as Young Adult but for the most part I found it to have a much wider appeal, with memorable characters, vividly described locations and a central mystery/problem to be solved.
It's only as romance develops for Lazlo that the story loses pace and steps into the Young Adult category. At first sweet, the romantic scenes begin to drag, with lengthy descriptions of kisses. If that market is the target then maybe this is a smart move, but until this point it had been a rollicking good story. Fortunately the latter chapters pick up as events escalate to a climax and set the scene for the second half of the story.
Much better written than other popular series like The Hunger Games, I thoroughly enjoyed Strange the Dreamer and look forward to the second instalment. It's so close to being a modern classic, but not quite in the Philip Pullman league yet.
PRODUCT: Strange the Dreamer

REVIEW_TITLE: High quality build and sound quality from a single box wireless speaker, just be a little careful about room placement
REVIEW:
The Zeppelin arrives in a large box and is quite a bit heavier than I expected, but heavy in a re-assuring sense. It just feels like a quality item. Once out of the box, I placed it centrally in the room, joined it to my wi-fi via the downloadable app and it appeared as available in iTunes on my PC and my phone/iPad. All I had to do was select it and start streaming music.
The sound initially was clear and detailed, especially on voices but lacked a little integration across the frequency ranges. There was plenty of bass but it somehow sounded a little separate from everything else. One thing I have learnt from various B&W headphones is that they take some time to run in, or loosen up from new. My wife had a friend over to visit so I cued up a 1970's playlist and left it playing as background music for them for several hours. A good sign was that her friend stayed longer than intended as they reminisced over the music that was playing.
After letting it run in for around 20 hours altogether, I sat down to listen properly again. By this time the sound had opened out and was much more balanced. Lots of detail, no frequency drowning anything else out and a good sense of rhythm and timing. One thing that was a little strange was the sense of stereo. Sitting centrally opposite the Zeppelin, it was quite hard to place the vocals in a stereo sense and I found that moving slightly to the left or right affected this as well. Of course, expecting proper stereo imaging from a one box speaker is asking too much but I found it almost distracting. Placing the Zeppelin nearer the corner of the room and at a 45 degree angle helped in that regard.
The only reason to point this out is that the Zeppelin is not cheap and there are very good one-box wireless speakers at lower prices. However for filling a large room with music at a decent volume, the Zeppelin never distorts or struggles and the sound is the nearest to true hi-fi quality that you're likely to get from one box without forking out for a Naim mu-so.
PRODUCT: Bowers & Wilkins Zeppelin Wireless Speaker - Black

REVIEW_TITLE: A decent webcam but not massively better than recent models. The background replacement function is just OK
REVIEW:
The C922 is a good quality webcam with clear picture quality and useful dual microphones. As with the most recent Logitech models it clips to a range of monitor thicknesses from my MacBook Pro to a Dell 27" monitor. Also supplied is a mini desktop tripod that is useful in difficult lighting conditions (strong side light for example). I initially had a few problems but this was due to using a USB3 pass through port on my Dell monitor. Fortunately the cable was just long enough to reach a USB2 port on the PC itself and those problems then went away.
Given that the C922 is capable of 60fps (at 720p) I was expecting to be blown away by the picture quality. In fact it seemed to be no different to my previous Logitech model (can't remember the model number but it has a Carl Zeiss lens) although the low light picture processing works quite well. I did notice that some of the picture processing is carried out by the host computer so there is a performance hit in terms of CPU. Not much of an issue for me when Skyping but the product is being promoted for gamers, where processing is everything so might be more of a problem for them.
Part of the price relates to the background replacement functionality, which lets you superimpose your own image onto backgrounds, replacing the actual background. The Personify ChromaCam software to do this is supplied. I thought the usefulness of this would be minimal but the Personify website gives some examples that illustrate that it could be beneficial, for example replacing the "...bustling office behind you on a videoconference call at the office". In reality that does not work. You need a plain background that's evenly lit and with a decent contrast level to the subject (that's you). Complex backgrounds bleed through quite badly so that ruled out my desk, with a packed bookcase behind me. I had to use my laptop and move the kitchen table to get a background and lighting level that met the requirements.
If you're after a good quality webcam there are cheaper options that will give the same quality of image. If the background replacement is the killer feature then be aware that it only works to a decent level if you can meet the pre-reqs.
PRODUCT: Logitech C922 Pro Stream Full HD Webcam with Mic and Adjustable Tripod - Black

REVIEW_TITLE: 3 1/2 stars really - it sounds great (with some caveats) but not enough to justify the premium price in a competitive market
REVIEW:
The T7 is about the size of a thick hardback novel or, to compare with other portable bluetooth speakers, almost exactly the same size and weight as the Creative Soundblaster Roar. It's also well over twice the price of the Roar, which features the added ability to take calls and play from an inserted Micro SD card. I like the Roar a lot, so the T7 has to sound much better to justify its price.
I am a fan of Bowers & Wilkins products but some are better than others. One thing they all have in common is the need to run them in for a period of time before they sound their best. Straight out of the box they sound brittle, a little harsh, and without much bass. Fortunately after just a couple of hours the harshness toned down and they sounded better albeit without much bass at first. The bass sounds mainly emerge from the rear so I found that placing it near a wall helped considerably and on a bookshelf was best of all. In this position the sound was nicely balanced and integrated.
The speaker unit itself sits in the centre, surrounded by a translucent honeycomb area that absorbs vibration, not as a means of shock proofing but to improve the sound. Around the outside edge is a silcon layer into which are integrated the on/off, volume, play/pause and pairing buttons. These are very hard to see indoors but are raised slightly for feel. The 'gold' colour is more like a dull brass but it's stylish enough, the whole being vaguely reminiscent of a Stylophone The Original Pocket Electronic Organ.
It goes pretty loud, enough to fill a large room, but the sound quality starts to diminish when you push it. Okay it's a small box and the laws of physics apply limits to what it can do but the midrange becomes strangely squawky, not what I'd expect at this price. For my purposes, on a bookshelf in my study providing background music while I'm working, it's perfect. It manages to retrieve lost of detail and present it in a musical way that's very enjoyable. The rechargeable battery also lasts ages - more than 24 hours at a time at reasonable volumes.
But is it significantly better than the Soundblaster Roar? In pure sound quality terms yes, in terms of the detail retrieved yes. But the law of diminishing returns applies and it's not so much better that the extra cost is worthwhile. I also compared it to the Libratone One Style, which is similarly sized. It's splash-proof and much more portable thanks to the integrated carry handle; again, it doesn't sound quite as good as the T7 but is perfectly good enough for portable use. It can also be charged via USB, which neither the Roar or T7 can.
Ultimately the competition is fierce and the T7 is too expensive for sound quality alone.
PRODUCT: Bowers & Wilkins T7 Portable Bluetooth aptX Wireless Speaker - Gold

REVIEW_TITLE: Much better than the P5 Series 1: bags of detail, more balanced and suited to a wider cross section of music
REVIEW:
Two things to know about Bowers & Wilkins headphones (and speakers): 1. They MUST be allowed to run in for 24-48hrs before they sound their best; 2. There is a B&W house sound that is what I call a traditional British Hi-Fi company sound. The latter isn't surprising if you consider companies like B&W, Naim, Linn and Cyrus are bringing their trademark front room sounds to the portable and wireless markets.
The P5 Series 2 looks almost identical to the original version. The only obvious difference is the Bowers & WIlkins logos on each side, which are in chrome on a dark background - the opposite of the originals. The black leather and chrome design looks every bit as classy as the original but I think the new style logo is better. The original P5 were the first B&W product I've owned and I've had a love/hate relationship with them. When I first bought them I hated them, but at that stage I didn't know about the need to run them in. They were also the company's first attempt at headphones and they erred on the side of warmth and smoothness to the sound. Perfect for certain types of music but unsuited to rock or blues where a little more 'bite' is required. Could the second attempt be better?
Before listening I plugged them into my old iPod Classic and left it playing at almost full volume for a day. The main internal difference in the series 2 are new drivers that are now designed to act more like a loudspeaker driver. The first thing I noticed was much more clarity, detail and energy to the sound, definitely not laid back like the series 1. This is without making them bright or tiring to listen to, they are also far more balanced across the frequencies. Playing 'Catfish Blues' but Heritage Blues Orchestra was great: lots of detail, space around instruments and the song bounced along in a really enjoyable way. The same applied to pretty much everything I tried; the series 2 are suited to a much wider range of music.
I mentioned the B&W house sound earlier, which some people refer to as a 'mid bass bloom'. Some B&W products show more of this than others and it seems to be more apparent with compressed files than CD quality or above. The P5 Series 2 lean more towards the neutral while retaining the best elements of the family sound. They're a much better headphone than the Series 1.
PRODUCT: Bowers & Wilkins P5 Series 2 On Ear Headphones with HiFi Drivers, Wired, Black

REVIEW_TITLE: Covers the subject in depth but goes from beginner to intermediate perhaps a little too quickly
REVIEW:
I bought this book as I've gotten into drawing sacred geometric designs using the small book Ruler and Compass: Practical Geometric Constructions (Wooden Books). While I'm able to follow the constructions in that book to a certain point, I wanted to understand a bit more of the theory.
Pretty early in the book, Mark Ryan introduces the concept of 'proofs' or using logical reasoning to make a series of deductions. He states that there aren't many practical applications for proofs, but actually I found them to be familiar. I work in IT and often need to analyse why something is not working: the thought process is actually quite similar and I found the approach to proofs quite interesting. The mathematics side of things on the other hand starts quite gently at first but I found the bombardment of new terms and symbols in the first 30 pages a little too much to take in without re-reading several times. As this is a For Dummies book there is humour scattered through, such as the points of a polygon labelled as ROTFL. Alas I was still stuck on WTF at this point.
Maybe my brain just doesn't absorb this type of information quickly but I found I had to regularly re-read sections several times before the Archimedes moment kicked in. Like other reviewers have said, it kind of feels more suited to the intermediate student than the casually interested but there is a lot of information in here and it's certainly better than the stuffy old textbooks I had to use at school.
PRODUCT: Geometry For Dummies, 3rd Edition
