Its pretty straight forward feed the fruit/veg into the tube and go, it works very quickly and literally eats through the fruit in next to no time, which is quicker than the booklet says to leave machine on for! The juice comes through a spout and into the jug which is provided (you have to place under the spout). We had apple juice in no time and its excellent stuff. I was uneasy as to the going for a juicer for a while, but really glad I did. The downside for me was the sheer size of it and having to clean it.....but thats always going to the case when using a machine like this, quite fiddly to clean up! All in all this machine is really excellent, I have not used a juicer before so cannot compare of older or alternative models but I would not hesitate in recommending this item!

REVIEW_TITLE: A good budget trimmer, but with a few important issues.
REVIEW:
This is a good choice for a budget paper trimmer, as long as you're happy to buy the replacement blades quite frequently. You tend to find out that the blade is no longer as sharp as required when it starts to give the cut edge the kind of distressed look that Tim Holtz would be proud of. If you're using expensive cardstock, that can be annoying. You can also buy a scoring "blade" that creases rather than cuts, which has its uses, but not for folding A4 into an A5 card (see later). With a sharp blade, it's a good trimmer for the price. I like the way the blade and blade transport lifts up to allow card to be put into place easily. The "guide wire" I tend to ignore, as it doesn't seem to lay perfectly straight, but the imperial and metric measurements on the sides of the card "channel" give reliable measurements.
Two issues:
This is advertised as an A5 trimmer. Unfortunately it is about half an inch too narrow! If you want to cut A4 accurately into two pieces of A5, this trimmer can't actually help you. Although the rulers on the sides of the channel are marked accurately, they aren't long enough! If you line up the long edge of a sheet of A5 with the leftmost edge of the platform (as shown in the picture), you'll slice several millimetres off the other edge of the sheet. This is also very annoying if you want to use the scoring "blade" to fold A4 in half, which is pretty common in the crafting world.
Secondly, the blades are replaced by sliding the blade to one end of the transport, where the running edges widen and the blade can easily be lifted out. Unfortunately, if you store or carry the trimmer vertically, the blade comes to rest at this removal point. Several times, I have picked up the trimmer, thought "where's the blade?" then looked on the floor by my feet to see it lying there blade upwards. I have also lifted up the blade transport to put in/remove paper and inadvertently flicked the blade out and onto the floor.
A couple of very basic but very annoying (and potentially painful in one case) design flaws.
PRODUCT: Fiskars 22 cm A5 Portable Paper Trimmer

REVIEW_TITLE: Adds a new dimension to your stamping!
REVIEW:
I'm falling in love with Card-io stamps after seeing them being demonstrated properly. They are very small, and repetition is the key. Stamp a few of the bottles onto the card, then take 2/3 different, complimentary ink colours for the leaves and stamp multiple images, inking the stamp then stamping three times before re-inking to get different intensities of colour. Leave some areas with just the lighter images and stamp the hops into these areas. It's so easy to create a fantastic card with just a few stamps and three/four ink pads.
Each set of Card-io stamps has a stamping guide on the insert sheet, giving recommended ink colours and initial stamping ideas, which is a very handy feature!
Highly recommended: use in conjunction with the Card-io Majestix acrylic rods: Acrylic Rod - 25mm. For use with Cardio Majestix Mini Stamps
PRODUCT: Card-io Last Orders Majestix Stamp Set

REVIEW:
I used to be put off stamping due to the potential for a card-destroying mis-stamp at a key stage of the process. I would die-cut shapes for adding stamped sentiments, as they were easy to re-make, but that was about it.
This stamping platform has changed all that! The magnets are powerful little blighters that hold down the cardstock firmly. They have neatly-rounded edges, so if you have to slide the magnet across the surface, there are no scratch marks left behind. Being able to position the stamp carefully on the card is a key selling point for me - you can now fine-tune the position before closing the stamping plate. The stamping plate makes contact with the back of the stamp when it is perfectly horizontal, so there is no sideways movement of the stamp at the crucial moment where the stamping plate meets and adheres to the stamp. The position of the stamp relative to the card is now fixed, so you can stamp, then re-ink and stamp again knowing that the stamp will always print in exactly the same position (as long as you don't move the card, but the magnets take good care of that!). This means that an incompletely-inked stamp is no longer the end of your card, and you can clean the stamp and re-ink it in a different colour while it is still attached to the stamping plate, meaning you don't have to cross-contaminate your ink pads in order to achieve images with two or more colours.
No need to worry if working with a small stamp and a big ink pad, as the surface of the stamping plate never touches the card, unlike getting ink on the edges of a standard stamping block.
Another great use is to be able to rotate the card to add the same stamp to the four corners - push the card into the corner of the frame, line the stamp up with the corner, then press the plate onto the stamp - it will always stamp at the same position in that corner, so stamp - rotate the card 90 degrees - stamp again and repeat. You can build up perfect, geometric patterns in this way. So many uses! Can't wait to really try it out.
PRODUCT: Tonic Studios - Tim Holtz Stamping Platform

REVIEW:
This album has been on repeat play since the very first listen. It's certainly my favourite album of Blondie's "reboot" (so to speak) and listening to it gives me flashbacks to "Blondie", "Plastic Letters" and "Parallel
Lines". The songs, without fail, are what I think of as 'going somewhere'. The standard verse, chorus structure is tweaked with so many inventive bridges, unexpected changes in the metre of the lyrics and moments when the song seems to stumble over but remains in perfect time (love this stuff - it keeps the songs fresh and exciting). This is all securely underpinned by wonderful musicianship that adds so much depth to the melodies. Debbie's voice is seemingly unchanged after all these decades. Clem Burke's drumming remains among the best in the business. Kinda makes me wish Jimmy was on the album too...
The collaborations work so well; you can hear the influence on the song, but it remains a Blondie track. To have a collaboration between Blondie and the sublime Laurie Anderson is such a treat, with the song Fragments having several phases, including a short break in the middle of its nearly 14 minute running time.
Perfect music to blast out in the car on a summer road trip.

REVIEW_TITLE: Brilliantly detailed stamps - shame about the lack of quality control.
REVIEW:
Brilliant designs from Tim Holtz as always, but the production method left a little to be desired.
There are six different but complementary hexagonal patterns (just like you'd see on a Moroccan carpet/rug). You get each design on a larger and a smaller stamp. The larger hexagons are approx. 4cm and the smaller versions are 2.5cm when measured between parallel sides.There are also five border stamps, three of which give you a tassled rug edge and two of which are more general - one with a stylised flower/diamond pattern and the other has a dashed line/sawtooth pattern. These are all 15.5cm long, varying in depth from 4mm to 1.8cm.
The red rubber gives the most incredible detail - I used them with Versafine Vintage Sepia ink on kraft card and the result was brilliant - add a couple of brightly-coloured bits and pieces for a great effect.
That's the good stuff - and it's really *good* good stuff. The disappointment comes with the final production.
They are on a single sheet of red rubber with a grey, cling surface on the reverse.The stamp pattern is printed on the reverse of the stamp. They also went to the trouble of cutting the stamps for you, so that you can pull them out and replace them back into the sheet for storage. Perhaps I got a bad batch, but this should have been caught by quality control:
- The reverse print of the stamp does not line up with the actual stamp.
- The die they used to cut out the stamps does not line up with the stamps. All the hexagonal stamps are off-centre, making the stamp and the reverse print both off-centre but in different directions. In two cases, the die had cut part of the actual stamp detail away.
These dies are clearly designed to tessellate and so allow you to create a full carpet on your card; this means you need to get twenty or thirty individual images lined up correctly, one-by-one. With the off-centre cutting of the die, and the incorrect positioning of the pattern on the grey backing, it is very difficult to get the stamps to print where you want them to. It is even more of a problem if you are combining different stamps to build up your pattern, switching between stamps as you go. You end up with some shapes overlapping and large gaps between others. The only real solution will be to cut out the stamps again by hand, then try to ignore the print on the reverse when positioning the stamps.
PRODUCT: Stampers Anonymous CMS270 Tim Holtz Cling Stamps, Multi-Colour, 7 x 8.5-Inch

REVIEW_TITLE: So nearly perfect! A welcome record of a much-loved show.
REVIEW:
Review of double-disc blu-ray set.
Saw the original at Drury Lane once - not that impressed. Saw the 2014 production, as seen here, and saw it again and again - such an improvement in terms of pace, staging, you name it! Day seats meant that I was on the front row of the stalls numerous times for just �20 - brilliant!
And now we have the film of the show. I saw it at the cinema. For some reason, the volume was so low that you could hear the subwoofers from the action movies on other screens, not to mention the munching of popcorn and slurping of drinks, so I'm looking forward to watching this movie on my terms!
OK - it's a brilliant record of a brilliant show. The cinematography is superb. The only fault I can find is that editing room floor must have been littered with the footage filmed from the static cameras that must have been there on the night of the 25th Anniversary Performance. Cameras that must have filmed the stage as a whole. One of the reasons I loved this production was that the stage was used to its full extent. You could look left and right and see other stuff. "Dressing the stage", I believe. When Alistair Brammer is giving his truly stupendous rendition of "Why God Why" stage left, there is a wonderfully understated bar scene stage right. I mean, I'm not complaining that the camera spent a lot of time on close-ups of Mr Brammer during this scene, but the atmosphere the bar actually adds is lost. During "What a Waste", there is action everywhere - a few wide shots would have been very welcome. Almost nothing of the go-go boy as he teases the Mormon - one of the funniest parts of the show. Instead, to put across the delightful mayhem of this scene, there are lots of, well, close-ups. Superimposed. Moving across the screen like those old films of firework displays where they tried to cram as many actual bursts of stars as they could. I'd rather have a little more choice of where to look.
Even in the final scene - the one which I thought was ruined by the addition of Ellen, the Engineer and John faffing about with Tam stage left, while (is this really a spoiler?) Chris bids farewell to Kim stage right - the film does a close up of Chris/Kim and all but ignores the others.
It was a big theatre with a wide stage. The production team did a fantastic job filling the stage. That is sadly missing here.
Rant over! There is plenty to praise in this film:
There can be very little of the actual 25th Anniversary Performance left. Most of the shots are clearly from Steadycam on stage, which will have been filmed after the event. This actually makes the film more interesting, as swings and new cast members had joined the show. It was fun debating "Well, I'm sure Niall was the Mormon at the start of 'What a Waste', but that wasn't him later on upstage with the pole dancers." It was also great to see that all the cast members had their close-ups. A very nice touch.
The colours are strangely muted - especially in Act II. For example, Ellen's hideous lemon-yellow dress (who thought that was a good idea?) looks almost sepia in the film and decidedly more tasteful as a result.
The close-ups show the amazing performances being given. Eva Noblezada - a truly remarkable find - and Rachelle Ann Go express such a depth of emotion it truly has to be seen in close-up.
I strongly recommend this film. It's not quite as effective as the film of the Australian production of Love Never Dies in terms of portraying an actual stage performance - Miss Saigon looks more like it was filmed on a sound stage rather than in a theatre - but it is still an excellent portrayal of a much-loved show.
PRODUCT: Miss Saigon: 25th Anniversary Performance [Blu-ray]

REVIEW_TITLE: Is it just me, or are there some key elements missing?
REVIEW:
Love the look of the finished product! I bought this because I liked the idea of being able to simply die-cut the individual pieces, stack 'em up and get a layer view of a Christmas fireplace. Lots of additional dies for Christmas stockings, garlands, greenery branches...
But it seems to me there are a couple of dies missing. They aren't there - they weren't meant to be there, but their absence makes the process of building this scene rather less straightforward.
The mantlepiece die, which is the second layer behind the Tree/Chair outline layer, has a some fancy "woodwork" as part of the actual mantlepiece. It looked like the circles and long-thin lines running up the "legs" and across the front of the front of the mantlepiece were embossed by the die. But they aren't - they are cut out of the card.
Behind the mantlepiece die-cut goes the fireplace piece. The arch of the actual hearth is cut out of the middle of the card, and the bricks are also cut out. The rest of this piece forms the wall behind the mantlepiece layer. That's where problem #1 crops up - you can see the brickwork through the "legs" of the mantlepiece. The brickwork is narrow enough that it doesn't show outside the mantlepiece, but it looks very odd being able to see through the cut-outs in the actual mantlepiece. So - there should really be another die that cuts out the mantlepiece shape, but without the decorative holes, so that it can be placed behind the original mantlepiece to create a nice 3D effect where the chisel-work is emphasised, and the bricks behind it are hidden.
As for the fireplace piece, you can't cut the arch without cutting the bricks. So, if you've cut the mantlepiece and first brickwork layer (with holes where the bricks go) out of, say, yellow card, then you cut the layer that goes behind the "brick holes" in red, so that the red card shows through the holes to give red bricks, you can't cut out JUST the arch of the hearth (assuming you want to place a black layer behind it for the inside of the hearth) - if you cut the arch out of the red card, you also cut out the bricks again. Missing? A single die the same shape as the arch of the hearth to cut out JUST the archway from the red card that goes behind the brickwork layer.
With those two dies "missing", you have to start cutting your own shapes out to create the pieces that stop the bricks showing through the mantlepiece, and allow you to layer the fireplace with a black "inside" and red bricks.
Maybe I'm missing something? Suggestions welcome!
Otherwise this is a great little set...
PRODUCT: docrafts Xcut Build-A-Scene Dies Shadow Box Die - Fireplace (Pack of 14)

REVIEW_TITLE: A hugely useful die and stamp set for your short but emphatic sentiments!
REVIEW:
I'm new to die-cutting, and wanted a fun way to add lettering to my projects. This is the kit for me! There are seven different pennant sizes: Three are triangular (3.5cm across the top and 5.7cm top edge to point, 2.9cm across and 4.4cm top edge to point, 3.5cm across and 3.5cm top edge to point). Three are based on rectangles: one has a triangular point at the bottom (2cm across, 3.3cm top to bottom), one has a semi-circular edge at the bottom (2.3cm across, 2.9cm top to bottom) and the third has a triangle cut into the bottom edge (2cm across, 3.3cm to outer downward-pointy edge, 2.5cm from top to central pointy-upper-inner-bit). All six of these cut the outer edge of the pennant. They ALL have a paired inner die, with the cutting edge approx. 2mm inside the cutting edge of the outer die. The inner dies all make two small holes close to the upper edge to allow them to be threaded. The final pair of dies are an outer and inner cut for the"Hello" ribbon shape - this does not have threading holes.
The lettering stamps are a nice, solid font. These look ideal for use with embossing powder. Looking forward to using them this weekend.
PRODUCT: Sizzix Framelits Dies 14/Pkg W/Stamps By Stephanie Barnard-Alphabet Banners

REVIEW_TITLE: Good template, not such a good shape-cutting system overall.
REVIEW: The Fiskars shape-cutting system as a whole is flawed. Even with a fresh, sharp blade, the hearts came out highly unsymmetrical as the blade found it difficult to rotate to match the actual curve of the heart. The template itself provides a good range of sizes and the inner surface is not vertical, so it would be ideal as a template if using pens/pencils, but for cutting out heart shapes? No. Better to invest in a die-cutting machine, which is what I ended up doing.

REVIEW_TITLE: Handy addition to a handy little die-cutting machine.
REVIEW: These folders give you a much better length to work with - still limited to 4.7cm width, but you get what you pay for. They don't last long, but this machine was such a bargain.
PRODUCT: Diamond Press "Size B" Blank Folder Refill, Clear

REVIEW_TITLE: Nice shapes, but the system as a whole isn't reliable.
REVIEW: I tried with the Fiskars shape-cutter, I really did! This template was the one where I gave up. With the sharpest, newest blade, and the perfect cutting depth set on the shape-cutter, these stars still turned out uneven. The template would be fine if the system itself worked as designed, but that little blade in the shape-cutter rarely turns properly. Every star I cut looked different. The curvature of the edge going out to the point was different to the curvature coming back into the middle.

Love the original Ratchet and Clank trilogy and the PS3 "full games", all of which I have played to the end. Some R&C games, however, switch from the camera following Ratchet's movements to the stupid "camera looks the direction you point it to look" system. If you turn and run, you have to use the other "joystick" - it's probably got some other name these days - to actually look in the direction you're physically travelling in. It's no big problem if you're used to those major shoot-em-up games, but if you're a casual gamer like me, this separate camera control makes absolutely no sense whatsoever.
I gave up at the stage where you had to jump from one magnetic walkway to another under severe time constraints - you had to look where you wanted to jump, using that second joystick to look. Totally unintuitive to my brain, and it made the game too frustrating for words.

REVIEW:

Once you've poked all the pieces out to make the holes (some of these pieces are fiddly to remove), glue the filigree glitter card over the solid mirror card shape and the result is rather impressive. REVIEW_TITLE: Blue Jacaranda seeds sprouting after just a couple of weeks!
REVIEW:
Very promising start! All the Blue Jacaranda seeds sank on their initial soaking, indicating that they are all viable. Just two weeks later and half of them have already germinated. I started the two Acer varieties last week - all but a couple of those seeds were viable, and as there were more than the stated number of seeds anyhow, I see this as 100% success rate so far.
The seeds arrived in a sturdy box (about the size of a DVD case) containing five packets of seeds, individually sealed in (resealable) plastic bags, with a clever resealable paper envelope containing the seeds in a small plastic envelope. Detailed instructions are provided for each variety, with tips and alternative methods.
This is a good selection: The Acer seeds need to be put in a warm place for 8-10 weeks before being put in the fridge, while the Ginko Biloba seeds need 8-10 weeks in the fridge first - great organisation allowing you to start them all off at the same time without filling your fridge with bags of compost! Very pleased - and tempted to try RP Seeds' other collections.

REVIEW_TITLE: Perfect recording of a perfect show
REVIEW:
Saw this show a couple of times at the Criterion Theatre in the West End. A wonderful evening, listening to Bacharach's songs performed to perfection by Kyle and his crew. The staging was sublime - like a homely living room gone crazy. There were sofas all over (quite literally - there were sofas at various heights on the back wall of the stage, which the cast were able to climb up to and sit on, and sofas stage left and stage right for audience members to sit on). Kyle's interpretation of the songs of Bacharach is truly inspired, with crafty segues between the songs, and the dovetailing of snippets into other songs ("What's it all about?" crops up in a number of songs, and in the most delightful way).
If you didn't see the show, but enjoy the songs, then this is an ideal addition to your CD collection.

REVIEW:
Brilliant set of dies! I bought a Crafter's Companion Diamond Press earlier this week, and it has a tiny 8cm by 4.7cm folder. I was able to fit ALL of the holly leaf/berry dies into the folder and cut them all in one go. As other reviewers have mentioned, these holly leaves actually look like holly leaves!
One of my requirements was to be able to cut 0.5mm magnetic sheet using the die - the Diamond Press worked in combination with these dies. You have to press the final shape out of the sheet, but it is properly cut all the way round. Very pleased!

REVIEW:
Perfect for making fridge magnets - just make sure you are decorating the correct side, as they are not fully reversible - one side attracts fridge doors firmly; the other side doesn't exert enough force to stay in place.
I originally intended to cut the sheet to shape and glue it to the decorated wooden shapes I had created. Then, I found it was far more efficient just to decorate the magnet itself - the Pebeo Moon and Prisme paints that I use work perfectly on these sheets, then I add Gedeo glazing resin to finish them off - and they remain in position with this kind of "load".
No problem cutting the sheet with XCut palm punches. Even the smallest of the HobbyCraft level punches will cut this magnetic sheet and produce a shape with a clean outline.
Finally, this is the only material that I have been able to get any success with when using the Fiskars Shape Cutter - the pieces press out cleanly with a single outline etched by the blade. Sadly, the blades are blunted after just two sheets, but they are easily replaced.

REVIEW_TITLE: Ideal for use in silicone moulds
REVIEW: I can see I'll be getting through plenty of this resin. Gives excellent results in silicone moulds - every detail is picked out clearly. Easy to prepare (mix two parts resin to one part hardener and stir thoroughly) and the air bubbles that are inevitably produced tend to rise to the surface and pop on their own, but a quick flaming with a candle lighter gets rid of the rest.

REVIEW: Well, I'm still very new to this 3D-TV lark, but I find that watching 3D on the television is far better than seeing it in the cinema, for some reason. The thing that really impressed me about I, Robot is that the 3D is unobtrusive once your eyes have settled down, as it were. I don't believe that this filmed was actually filmed in 3D, which means there aren't all those trite "in your face" moments that can make 3D so cringeworthy. Instead, the depth of field generated by the 3D simply adds to the overall high definition clarity and makes it feel like you are looking at reality rather than a trick of the light. The cityscape at night is quite breathtaking, as is one of the final scenes where the robots are looking up at the figure on the hill. The film loses a star for the dreadfully overt product placement, which marrs the film far more than any hokey "let's poke things into the audience" 3D stuff.
PRODUCT: I, Robot (Blu-ray 3D + Blu-ray)

REVIEW: I'm surprised they still make these, but they are perfect for transporting Zentangle tiles. The picture is a little confusing, but they are completely transparent and colourless - they look like that old smoked glass in the picture.
PRODUCT: 2 Capacity Clear 3.5'' Disk Case / Mailer (Pack of 10)

REVIEW:
Well, this is a great example of Blu-ray 3D - one to use to demonstrate to your house guests. Cirque du Soleil know how to put on a good show, with costumes, choreography and music all used to enhance the incredible circus skills on display. I'm fairly new to HD and 3D, but this was superbly detailed.
At any one time, there will be a number of things going on and you can follow your interests, nudge your buddies and say "look over there!", taking in the whole spectacle. Or rather, you can when you're seeing them perform live, and the few annoying aspects of this film relate to the filming and editing of the various shows included in this movie. During ensemble acts, the constant switching between camera angles means that the performer you were watching, who was just building up to something quite spectacular, is replaced just at the wrong moment by another performer building up to something dramatic. In some acts, you spent more of your time wondering what you were actually looking at than enjoying the act itself. There was one act where (is this a spoiler? It's not exactly part of the plot), the floor lifted from horizontal to vertical. And when it was vertical? Well - they turned the camera through 90 degrees so that it looked horizontal again.
The acts are carefully planned for dramatic effect. They tend to start off slowly then build up the speed and drama. As a result, the over-use (or, in fact, the use at all) of slow-motion serves to disrupt the natural flow of the act. There are so many cuts between slow-motion, normal speed and (it appears) speeded-up footage in this film, that the end result is a rather confused mess. On the Wheel of Death, for example, the wheel turns faster towards the end of the act - and so they shift into slo-mo, which ruins the effect completely. To make it worse, the music and the actual performance continue unaffected, and the slo-mo bits are often "action replays" of one specific manoeuvre, so when you return to the normal-speed act, you've missed a bunch of other stuff! The finale (spoiler alert? The plot is pretty obvious from the start) - when the woman finally finds "The Aerialist" and turns out to be a bit of an aerialist herself - is also marred by the over-use of slo-mo. An aerial pas de deux, where they fly around in a series of breathtaking holds, has been meticulously choreographed, but just as you're watching them soaring up into the heavens, we get switched to a slo-mo close up of her dress billowing around her legs. When you go back to seeing the both of them, they are in the middle of their next move.
They may seem like minor points, but they coloured the overriding impression I took away from watching the movie. Not "great costumes", "awesome 3D" or "incredible performances", which are all very welcome, but "dreadful editing". Shame, really!
PRODUCT: Cirque du Soleil: Worlds Away (Blu-ray 3D + Blu-ray) [Region Free]

REVIEW_TITLE: So pleased to be able to play SSX3 again!
REVIEW:
I have the silver PS2 with the two silver controllers, and after years of use, they stopped working. This controller is an official PS2 product and it worked first time this morning when I tested it out with a quick race through Metro City.
Other commenters have cast doubt on the legitimacy of the controllers by pointing out things like the lack of packaging and only having a US patent number. I checked the controller carefully on arrival - it was in a plastic bag and wrapped in bubble-wrap, but the cord had the cable tie and plastic wrap that I remembered when unwrapping my original controllers from the box, and the US patent number is all there was on the original controllers - the old and the new both have an identical information panel on the underside of the controller, with a note that you need to refer to the packaging for information on patents in other countries.
Looking forward to starting SSX3 over again this evening. Such a shame that they didn't do a PS3 version of these earlier SSX games like they did for Ratchet and Clank. The PS3 SSX game is dreadful in comparison.
PRODUCT: Official Sony Satin Silver DualShock 2 Controller (PS2)

REVIEW:
These photo-coasters are simply brilliant! Good quality construction with a metal holder underneath for the photograph and four padded cushion "feet" to protect surfaces. You are provided with a single-use plastic cover for the photographs to protect them from spills - don't peel off the strip that covers the adhesive until you are happy with the picture you have chosen, as it is fairly strong and once stuck down would be hard to undo without damaging the cover.
The glass top is of a good thickness, and the white border is completely opaque with a perfectly straight edge. It makes for a perfect frame. Very pleased!
PRODUCT: 4 Glass Coasters Photo Gift Set - Insert Your Own Photos - Black Stand

REVIEW_TITLE: Oh. Is that what all the fuss was about?
REVIEW: Saw this back in the days before the Video Nasties bill. Remembered the ending (who wouldn't?) and some of the dialogue. Rose-tinted specs then kicked in over the decades. Watched this blu-ray release - very disappointed. Is it really uncut? Some dialogue I remember very clearly isn't there, and I know that the nightmare that gets repeated throughout the film yields more and more information/gore/plot twists as time goes on, but the soundtrack suggests cuts still exist. Ah yes - the soundtrack. This made the film nearly unwatchable. The protagonist's demented screams are, quite literally, deafening - the soundtrack is so muddy that most dialogue is inaudible, so you crank up the volume and then along come the screams. Down goes the volume. Then dialogue starts. Up goes... ah you get the idea. Most annoying of all - no bloody subtitles, so you are left with constant fiddling with the volume control as the only option. Rather wish I'd kept to the memories of my viewing of this film back in the eighties...
PRODUCT: Nightmares in a Damaged Brain [Blu-ray]

REVIEW_TITLE: What did they do to Huey?
REVIEW:
Ooooo-Kay. Saw the show in the West End a couple if times with Beverley Knight and Killian Donnelly in the lead roles a couple of times and absolutely loved it - hoping to catch Matt Cardle as Huey before it closes. Now I know Huey's character is not meant to be the brightest of minds, but Killian played the role with bags of charm - no wonder Felicia fell in love with him. The guy on this DVD? I'm surprised Felicia didn't slap him round the face and tell him to get knotted! Why? Put simply, he plays the young Huey character like a dirty old man with what we used to call "learning difficulties". He's an American actor, so why he has to put on such a dreadful a southern drawl I cannot fathom - it sounds like he's having difficulty speaking and it is really off-putting. Much as I love the show, I couldn't bear watching this DVD and turned it off half-way through act one, after the scene where Felicia visits him at home for the first time, where his slurred speech, posture and gurning became too much.
Oh for a DVD of the West End production.
PRODUCT: Memphis: The Original Broadway Production [DVD] [2012] [Region 1] [US Import] [NTSC]

REVIEW_TITLE: This is a must-have for any Zentangle enthusiast!
REVIEW:
This is the one to get, folks! An absolute bargain on Kindle at �3.49 (when I bought it) and visual instructions for 104 official Tangles! The book may be in German, but the step-by-step instructions are purely visual, and the name of each Tangle is "in English" (not that they could translate the Tangle names into German, of course, seeing as they are mostly made-up names). I find that some Tangles need to you be able to draw certain shapes well in freehand, rather than following the mechanical processes - the majority of these Tangles are of the kind that don't depend on your ability to draw specific shapes (thankfully - I have almost no artistic skill at all!).
An index at the back shows all the Tangles in alphabetical order, 25 per page, making the selection of a particular Tangle for a specific part of the string an absolute cinch.
The final crowning glory of this book is that each page has examples of variations for each Tangle, together with completed standard tiles, Bijou tiles and Zendalas - so much inspiration! And that's before you get to the Gallery sections of the book. Brilliant!
PRODUCT: Das gro�e Zentangle-Buch: 101 Lieblingsmuster (German Edition)

REVIEW:
This book is mainly about the history of Zentangle, health benefits of tangling, the stuff you need to tangle... The psychological stuff is moderately interesting.
If you want to actually learn how to tangle, look elsewhere. There are nine tangles described. No step-by-step drawings, which makes tangles such as the "hairy tangle" pointless, as the key is to follow clear rules on how to build up your tangle, so "draw curvy shapes" followed by "draw more curvy shapes" doesn't really help. Two of the tangles are new to me, and pretty good, but that doesn't warrant buying a whole book (a very short book to boot) when there are other titles out there with a much better collection of tangles.
PRODUCT: Zentangle Basics: Zentangle - Find Inner Peace (Zentangle art for Beginners) (Basic Zentangle Book 2)

REVIEW:
If you've seen the original "The Heat Is On", then you've also seen this - exactly the same story, just with different actors. They also re-use quite a bit of the footage as "before and after" content. The behind-the-scenes stuff is great, as in the original. Really interesting to see how they choreographed the scenes with Tam, especially the ones with the guns and knives, so as to reduce the emotional stress on the very young actors they use. The interviews are fine, but they keep jump-cutting. Three seconds of one interview, then off to someone else; back to the original interview ten minutes later. I'd much prefer nice, solid interviews where you could focus on the characters/actors.
As for the musical numbers and actual scenes from the show - just recycled cutting-room-floor footage from the trailer. Very disappointing. Chris and Kim singing "Last Night of the World" - for three seconds, then the music continues, but you see them when they are singing "Sun and Moon", when they are snogging, when they are running off stage... Nothing you can't already see on YouTube. No extras at all - they could have included the West End Live performances, one or two songs from the actual show all the way through, the interviews uninterrupted and, ironically, the complete trailer.
If you want to see a much better example, try the Bombay Dreams DVD - one of the extras was a selection of full songs, including promotional videos and two or three songs filmed, in full, at a performance. The "Product Link" button has disappeared, but "Salaam Bombay Dreams" is still available here on Amazon.
PRODUCT: The Heat Is Back On: The Remaking Of Miss Saigon [DVD]

REVIEW_TITLE: A handy little book for practising your tangling!
REVIEW:
Basically, it's a book for practising your tangling! The paper is smooth, not like the "official" tiles, and already has the four dots marked out to give you the "correct" size - apologies for the quote marks, but Zentangle(TM) is supposed to be more "organic" than pre-printed dots-in-the-corners. Still, you know how big your tangles should be. The paper is a good thickness and the official Micron pens do not bleed through.
The elastic closure is handy, although that nice graphic on the front is just a strip of paper that folds loosely over the cover - it slips off and leaves you with a completely plain cover, which emphasises the purple/pink colour scheme, which a) isn't very Zen in itself and b) seems to ignore the fact that blokes tangle too. Two shades of green would have been more calming, so half a star lost there.
In the back of the book, there is a very handy "My Tangle Directory" of six pages with nine small squares (and an index panel under each square) per page. This is to allow you to draw and label the basic tangle patterns as you learn them - a brilliant idea, BUT another half-star is lost because the first seven (why seven?) directory squares are already completed, so any wish you may have to organise your own directory is dead in the water from the start! The real problem is that the seven sample tangles include some of the more complicated designs that I would never choose to use, and they aren't drawn the way I would draw them.
What I'm actually waiting for is a small, zipped wallet that will hold this book, with pen/pencil/tortillion slots and a pocket for official tiles for when I feel like creating on the go...
PRODUCT: Pocket Tangles: Over 50 Tiles to Tangle on the Go (Pocket Creatives)

This device worked first time with my iPhone 6 - and the buttons on the front of the device control the music my iPhone is transmitting, so I can skip tracks and pause without having to touch the phone. The sound quality is pretty good, too. Having the cable to the 3.5mm jack is a great idea, and means that the cable isn't dangling all over the place. Very neat and tidy.

Anaglyphic 3D. Basically, you get to see the film in 3D, but as it uses colour separation to create the 3D effect, the film appears to be monochrome. REVIEW_TITLE: Good for the price, with a few points to note...
REVIEW:
Well, it fits my arm OK, and the phone fits inside with its protective case on, so that's pretty much job done.
Except...
The clear plastic that goes over the screen is shiny, making it very difficult to see the iPhone screen when outdoors. I usually have to take it off my arm so that I can look at it straight on as I can't see the number pad for entering the unlock code while wearing it on my upper arm.
The phone holder has a front and a back. No flat edges, just the stitching that holds the two halves together. This means that the headphone hole is on the side of the holder the goes against your arm. To put the headphone into the socket, you have to pull the hole inline with the headphone socket. Once the headphone jack has been inserted, there is a permanent lateral force on the headphone plug as the material tries to return the headphone hole back into position. Only a small force, but it's there nonetheless.
The flap that secures your iPhone in place is just that. You prise the flap up, put your iPhone in, then lower the flap. There is a few mm overlap when you have just an iPhone, but the overlap is non-existent if you have a phone protector in place. If you try using the holder upside-down, so that the iPhone screen is the correct way up when you raise your arm, then water will be able to get in via the flap when your arm is lowered.
Having said that, this item is cheap and cheerful; the above are important points to note, but if you are happy taking the armband off to use your phone and don't mind that lateral pressure on your headphone plug, then this is a good buy. It also keeps your iPhone nicely dry.
PRODUCT: iPhone 6s Armband, Anker Sport Armband for iPhone 6 / 6s (4.7 inch) for Sports, Running, Jogging, Walking, Hiking, Workout and Exercise, Sweat-Free High-Quality Neoprene with Headphone and Key Slots and 2 Extra Cuttable Strips

REVIEW_TITLE: Good enough sound quality and noise-blocking, one minor irritation...
REVIEW:
One star lost due to the rather odd behind-the-ear clips that you have to put onto the wires yourself. There are so many headphones out there, and this pair is sold as 'Sport In-Ear Headphones', why not just have the clips fitted at the factory. Having to fiddle about squeezing the wire into the ear clips, trying to get the actual headphone in the right position - quite frustrating. After all that, there will still be a piece of flimsy wire between the clip and the headphone, so the benefit of having something solid behind the ear, forcing the headphone to remain in place, is lost.
Anyhow - the sound quality is fine for a budget model and, once you have the correct size earpiece in place, outside noise is blocked quite well, although you will need to push them back into your ear properly every now and then.
PRODUCT: AmazonBasics Sport In-Ear Headphones

REVIEW:
Please note that this book has been reprinted a number of times. The version I bought on 15/5/15 has high-quality paper, and there is no trace of ink bleeding through to the other (printed) side of each page. Even IF you get a version with the thinner paper, there are more than forty pages, eighty sides of pictures to colour, so if you only coloured half of the designs, then at just under a tenner, each single-side design is costing you less that 25p. With the better quality paper, that drops to 12p per side.
What is great about this book is that Johanna gives you space to add your own inky drawings to hers - if you want to! One page will have a circular or square design in the centre, the opposite page will have the edges filled, with a matching circular or square white space in the middle. Some designs flow over two pages, with white space around the design for your own additions. What this does is allow you to leave that white space - it gives the designs room to breathe, while most colouring books fill each page, edge to edge, which makes them look a little chaotic. This white space, I find, makes this book even more relaxing to complete. Johanna adds typed suggestions to the incomplete pages, but even this is done in a sympathetic way, with old-style typeface, random letter sizes and the text flowing along the edge of the existing design. The text becomes part of the artwork, rather than having an ugly block of text in one corner.
The book is flowers, trees and animals - you'll need plenty of shades of green! The basis is on reality - many of these books have the internal spaces of animals filled with a giddy mass of geometric lines and patterns, just to add complexity to the drawings. None of that here, thankfully.
If this is your first foray into the world of adult colouring book, I really can't think of a better introduction.

REVIEW_TITLE: Fiddly? Flimsy? Only until you've built it properly...
REVIEW:
When you first get this little gizmo out of the box, your first thought will be "cheaply made and rather flimsy". I was certainly a little disappointed, but then when you consider the price, you have a very clever design, fully motorised and just requiring assembly.
Once assembled (and you need to be careful to get the support posts in the correct positions), it becomes a far more solid piece of kit - even when the steel balls fall from an upper level, the track that catches them doesn't move. Same when the balls whizz round the corners. I do find that everything needs to be in the correct position, and before switching on you need to press the orange half of the staircase back down, but once you've done that the balls ascend the staircase perfectly, rolling smoothly from side to side in perfect unison.
There are three positions where the balls get stuck - but they are supposed to! I hope people aren't thinking that's a malfunction. As the balls reach the top of the staircase, they roll down the first section of track and the first two balls get caught in the two holes. The third ball then rolls over the top of the two "stuck" balls, falls down to the next level and knocks into a vertical panel that then releases the ball trapped above. The released ball falls through the hole, and releases the next ball. Meanwhile, the ball that performs the first release falls through a different hole and gets caught in the next trap - the seesaw pipe. The whole process starts again, and the second ball to fall into the seesaw pipe makes it tip up and both balls roll back to the start.
The only place I've have the balls get stuck accidentally is where the first trapdoor panel swings to the side. This just adds a little randomness to the device - the next ball down will clear it. If the balls stick anywhere else, then you just need to make sure that all the pieces are correctly positioned and the joints are firmly connected. The same applies if the balls start falling off the track.
Great fun - and truly mesmerising. Watching (and hearing) the balls rolling up the staircase is rather hypnotic...

REVIEW:
Pebeo products really are the best for crafts such as glass painting. The Prisme range create interesting effects on their own, but when you combine them with the Vitrail range, you can get a huge range of effects. The Prisme range are opaque, so are not ideal for glass painting where you intend to illuminate the object from behind, such as a votive holder or something to hang in the window, but when combined with the transparent Vitrail products you can get the best of both worlds. The basic Prisme effect reminds me of looking at cells through a microscope. Tiny circles form around the "seed" particles in the paint - the thickness of the layer of paint appears to affect the size of these circles.
One small point - when it says "Stir well before use" it means it! The stuff in the paint that acts as the "seed" for the effect needs to be distributed well, otherwise you'll get some early work that has loads of the little "blobs" and your later work will have fewer and fewer.
As for the Discovery collections from Pebeo, I'd recommend them every time if you want to try out a new range. You get a good selection of colours for a very reasonable price and, for most hobbyists, the bottles last for a good time. When you start running out, you'll also have a very good idea of which individual, larger bottles would be the best bet.
PRODUCT: Pebeo 20 ml Prisme Discovery Collection, Assorted Colours

REVIEW_TITLE: Perfect recording of a bizzare yet brilliant show
REVIEW:
Like most people, I went to see Urinetown - The Musical at St James's Theatre with no idea of what to expect. From the first introductory speech by Officer Lockstock (Jonathan Slinger), with contributions from Little Sally (Karis Jack), I was hooked. Although the plot is based on oppression/revolution/resolution, the approach this show takes is one of a kind. The music covers a range of styles, with some wonderful jazz/swing (Snuff That Girl) and the incredible "Run Freedom Run" where Bobby Strong rallies the rebel poor in the second act, with its gospel/spiritual cries of "Halleluyah", a song which is earning the cast mid-act standing ovations in the new West End transfer at the Apollo Theatre. Even more interesting is the almost Baroque overture, with a heavy reed presence that sounds like a wind ensemble playing a classic Divertimento. Brilliant stuff.
The lyrics carry much of the humour, but you can only really appreciate the music and the humour fully when you have seen the show performed live. One good example is "Cop Song", where Officers Lockstock and Barrel describe the journey to the infamous Urinetown. As they describe the four miscreants, their attempts to get around the restrictive laws on public urination (not allowed!) and the punishment they received, the London production uses some brilliant physical theatre to bring the punishments to life.
This recording is of the original Broadway cast recording, made back in 2001. Why it took so long to open in London is a mystery, but huge thanks to Julian Stoneman, Jamie Lloyd et al for bringing the show to London. The Broadway cast on this CD are on top form in this recording, with Hunter Foster playing the key role of rebellion leader Bobby Strong. I just hope we see a recording of the current London cast sometime...
PRODUCT: Urinetown / O.S.T.

REVIEW_TITLE: Back on form after season 3 - almost!
REVIEW:
Four hour-long episodes (or eight half-hour episodes as I saw them on BlinkBox). As I said in my review for season 3, this final season would have been better if following on directly from the end of season 2. That way, we wouldn't have had to put in so much effort suspending our disbelief regarding the truly bizarre storylines of season 3.
Facing the inevitable, Cathy starts putting all her affairs in order. Starting with sorting out her job, then her family, acting on her wish not to die at home and, finally, her estranged Father. All sensible stuff to do, but the scriptwriters set her about these tasks in some rather ridiculous ways, which leave you thinking "well what on earth did you expect to happen, Cathy??"
Fortunately, the final episode truly redeems the series, and allows the show to bow out with you remembering the great aspects of this show. It is very moving, as expected but, surprisingly, it wasn't Cathy or Paul that made me cry - it was Adam! You'll see why when you watch it, bless his cotton socks!

REVIEW_TITLE: Bit like that Dallas season where Bobby had been in the shower
REVIEW:
The Big C is a bold concept, and the brilliant Laura Linney leads an excellent cast in this moving and oddly amusing show. Season three, however, is a real let-down. Not in terms of the acting, but the rather dire plot lines.
There is plenty to fill seasons 1 and 2, with her refusing to share her diagnosis and any chemotherapy in 1, then sharing her diagnosis and getting treatment in 2. Plenty of plot lines that follow the basic theme and make perfect sense.
Season 3, which could be subtitled "In Remission", sees her returning to living a "normal" life after her treatments appear to have worked. What causes the problems here is that the stuff she does is just, well, plain silly. And as for her son joining a religious sect (I don't know of many Christian groups who behave like those in the show - their solution to "saving yourself until you are married" is really bizarre), it just doesn't ring true - especially the way that Adam treats the stuff he found in the self-storage unit at the end of season 1. I can see why Cathy would wonder about having another baby, but the plot line with Susan Sarandon (who plays the role very well) is dire.
Season 4 starts in such a way that you could easily slip straight from the finale of season 2 to the start of season 4 without any real bother. I almost wish they had planned it to be shown that way.

REVIEW_TITLE: Ready to start all over again?
REVIEW:
If you have collected the original Hexbug Nanos, then no doubt, you'll be in a rush to add the V2 Nanos to your collection.
If so, be aware that, although the hex and track pieces will fit the new tubes, there are some major incompatibility issues. If you want to use these sets to add to the flexibility of your original Nanos, there are a number of disappointments in store:
The main issue is that none of your original Hexbug Nanos will be able to navigate these tubes. If you have a single downward tube, then they will fall down quite happily, but they will get stuck in the bottom of the tube if they try to go upwards, so they will only be able to fall down a tube if you place them on the top level yourself.
There were no online codes in this kit, or in the Nano V2 Orbit kit, even though the Nanos were advertised with the usual "Very Rare" text, which implies collectible Nanos. There are plenty of empty pages in the specimen book online, but it doesn't look like the V2s are going to fill those pages. There is also no sign of sets of these V2 Nanos like there were the Refraction, Orbit etc. sets of the originals.
If you want to use your existing hex pieces other than at ground level, the vertical spacing required is different to the spacing provided by the original black posts. Even the smaller u-tube won't meet the upper hex piece if stacked using the original black posts. The larger V2 sets have new-style stacking posts, but they need the holes as found in the V1 construction hex pieces - the standard/glow in the dark hex pieces can't be used with these new posts. Also, it does not appear to be possible to purchase the V2 stacking posts separately, so you'll need to buy the larger V2 sets to get any.
The sets when seen as a standalone system are entertaining enough. It is fun to see the Nanos traveling up and down the tubes, although watching them crawling along upside-down once they have travelled through a vertical u-turn is a little odd. There is room in the tubes for two Nanos to pass each other, which is pretty much essential if you don't want to be pulling the tubes apart to rescue them. I have knocked a couple of stars off for durability due to the connections between the tubes. They either come apart too easily or you have to pull harder than you'd expect, which could result in damage to the tubes. The "squeeze sides to release the tabs" is a good idea, but it doesn't always work as intended.
All in all, a fun experience if you enjoyed the original Nanos, but don't expect to be able to combine your existing collection with the V2 Nano kits in any meaningful way.
PRODUCT: HEXBUG nano V2 Infinity Loop

REVIEW_TITLE: Most complete recording of Starlight - albeit in German
REVIEW:
This CD is still available from the Starlight Express Theatre in Bochum. I bought a copy for 16 Euros when I saw the show there last month. If you love Starlight but haven't seen the German production yet - GO! It is truly awesome.
And this CD is brilliant - recorded live in the theatre, complete with audience applause. About the only thing that this recording omits is the entry of the national engines. You get all of the incidental music and linking scenes, and the overture is the extended version where, after the Mother tells the kid to put his trains away and sings him to sleep with a segment of the title song, the Starlight Express theme starts quietly, then swells to a crescendo as the trains start zooming around the huge auditorium tracks.
A timeless show - and this is a great record of the show from the late 1980's. "Liebesexpress" (Engine of Love) has replaced "Call Me Rusty", "Hilf Mir Versteh'n" (Make Up My Heart) has replaced "He Whistled At Me" but - thankfully - "Ne Lok mit Lokomotion" (A Lotta Locomotion) has yet to be replaced by the dreadful "Whole Lotta Locomotion", and "Du Allein" (Only You) is still there. Mind you - "I Do" is a great new addition to the show.
This CD is an essential addition to any Starlight fan's collection.
PRODUCT: Starlight Express - Original Live Album Bochum [Doppel-CD]

REVIEW: I think I've written before in reviews of historical fiction about the tricky balance between historical detail and narrative excitement. Authors seem to fall one way or the other with only the very best, Bernard Cornwell or George McDonald Fraser seeming to get the right blend. This book leans towards the narrative drama rather than the historical fact especially at the beginning where some of the modern language jars. It struggles to find the right tone until it gets to the Crimea where it gets reasonably good at painting a picture of the period and conveying the action at the same time. The central character is interesting and looks like he is going to get even more interesting, although the requirement for his motives to be purer than his actions is not required. I'll end with a note to the publisher. You will have lost readers for this book by putting the wrong uniforms on the front cover. It won't matter to some but history enthusiasts can tell the difference between Peninsular War uniforms and Crimean War. And we will judge you for it.
PRODUCT: The Scarlet Thief: The first in the gripping historical adventure series introducing a roguish hero (Jack Lark)

Having the author's note, demonstrating how much work he has done, at the beginning makes this worse - the publisher should move this to the end. When he gets into the political and military action then he is good but too often the book seems to progress from one historical event to another. The characters are okay but the 'good guys' seem a little too enlightened and a bit wet for what was a pretty brutal bunch of people. More grit please.

The plot itself is quite gripping, although it suffers a little from being the introductory volume which makes it a bit slow in places reflecting the fact that this seems to be the calm before the storm (I hope). REVIEW_TITLE: A review by my son aged 10
REVIEW:
A short review by Henry Sullivan aged 10
Princess Label Maker to the Rescue is the 6th book in Tom Angleburger's best selling series Origami Yoda. I really enjoyed reading it and I'm sure your children would love it to.
The book is set in an North American middle school, named McQuarrie middle school. It all starts when the principal is sent a collection of stories [from the children's point of view] about a terrible learning program, called FunTime. The culprit of the sending call themselves Princess Label Maker. The stories also include the children, with the help of their Star Wars Origami puppets, help other children with their problems and mishaps. To really understand the book, you have to read the previous books.
Princess Label maker to the rescue! is aimed at 8-14 year olds, like me. It contains some rude words [only swear words to some parents].but can easily be forgiven. As the book has some different writing styles, which younger children may not be able to read. It has plenty of humour to get your children generating ideas for their English lessons [especially nonsense poems].
I think Princess Label maker is one of the BEST Origami Yoda books I have ever read. To conclude I would really encourage you to buy this book if you have a child aged 8-14, because, like me, I believe they will really enjoy reading it from start though to finish.
PRODUCT: Princess Labelmaker to the Rescue: An An Origami Yoda Book 5 (Origami Yoda 5)

REVIEW: I'm not a music technology buff so was really looking for a simple sound system that I could play my music on as well as the radio. This does this all very well with a good sound. Set-up demanded concentration and some detective work but was by no means impossible. I got the radio stations set-up but was having difficulty accessing my itunes library until I switched from doing it on an ipad to my PC. Then it was easy. I'm now working through all the functions but it seems to be very straightforward.
PRODUCT: Bose � SoundTouch Portable Series II Wi-Fi Music System - Black

REVIEW: This is an engrossing short novel about a group of friends and lovers as they progress towards one couple's break-up with flashbacks to how they arrrived at this point. The chapters flit between each characters viewpoint and you get to see a different take on the actions that took place as you progress. The story is good, the characters are realistically flawed and human although they occasionally seem a little too articulate for real life, especially in the depths of upset or despair. However this is a minor criticism and I was thoroughly sucked into their world, so much so that I wanted more at the end.
PRODUCT: Friendship and Afterwards

REVIEW: Don't read the reviews. Just read the book. Go in with an open mind. It is wonderful. You will love it.
PRODUCT: The Universe versus Alex Woods

REVIEW_TITLE: A wonderful tale of a man and his owl
REVIEW:
First and foremost this is a deeply moving, but never sentimental story of one man and the owl he reared from a chick. It is written with a restrained, wry 'Englishness' that conveys the powerful bond between man and owl as they move live first in a London high-rise flat and then in the Sussex countryside. As the story unfolds you get a real sense of a time and place, primarily Seventies Britain, that no longer exists.
Writing from detailed diary entries (some of which are quoted) the author goes into detail about Mumble's behaviour. His careful observations are delivered with clarity and humour, and demonstrate formidable knowledge as well as his background in history publishing (with comparisons to military aircraft proving particularly insightful). He breaks the story and the careful observations with succinct and useful chapters on various aspects of owls, in our culture, in their natural habitat etc.
In summary highly recommended as a heartfelt but restrained celebration of the life of Mumble the owl, an education about these fascinating creatures and a compelling evocation of a time before iphones and the internet.
PRODUCT: The Owl Who Liked Sitting on Caesar

REVIEW: The Quarry books are always a pleasure. Expect a mildly un-PC, fast-moving thriller with plenty of action, well-drawn characters and a satisfyingly cynical and laconic narrator. Required reading when you want a piece of quality escapism.
PRODUCT: The Wrong Quarry (Hard Case Crime) (Hard Case Crime Novels)

REVIEW_TITLE: A competent if slightly workman-like start to a new series on an interesting subject.
REVIEW: Grahm Hancock's War God is a fictional retelling of the first part of Corte's assault on the Mexica (Aztec) empire in 1519. The writing is fast-paced, gritty and professional and the story rattles along, criss-crossing between the different characters as they gradually draw closer together. The setting (as you'd imagine) is bloody, with human sacrifice and slaughter ever present, which makes it difficult to warm to some of them, particulalry at first. As historical fiction it is effective. Initially I was less happy about the mystical element to the story (basically there are some gods floating about) particularly because some of their interventions seemed to be there as plot contrivances rather than as an integral part of the story but I was less bothered as time went on and the afterword explained it a bit better.
PRODUCT: War God: Nights of the Witch

They evoke the period well, with a particular (as you'd expect) feel for the military background of Watson and his earthy sidekick Bowler, but also have a modern rawer feel which is no bad thing. The mysteries are good, the recurring villain (no spoilers) is compelling and they are quite funny in places. I'll definitely pick up the next one.

REVIEW_TITLE: I'll never trust a forecast again
REVIEW: A surprisingly interesting look at the science of forecasting and how it applies to everything from baseball to terror attacks. Cogently argued and well-written this book made me think a lot about how the world around is presented by media, government and pressure groups. It is a relieve to read something which reflects the uncertainty of the world that we live in, that argues we should reflect this uncertainty and beware those who don't. An excellent book with only one tiny downside in that it is rooted in the American experience, in baseball, and the US economy, some of which I had to work to follow, although this is offset by the author's clear explanatory style. Recommended.
PRODUCT: The Signal and the Noise: The Art and Science of Prediction

We played it every night after tea and loved it, so much so that a couple of other kids joined in as well. It took them a little while to grasp the cooperative aspects of it and there was still an element of competition, in wanting to get the treasures but we very quickly got most of the rules and started playing. A couple of rules were not entirely clear but they became apparent as we went along. I would thoroughly recommend it as a wonderful alternative to TV, ipods and computers as away of sitting together and having a lot of fun. You'd be surprised how tense it all gets when the waters start to rise, bits of the island starts to disappear and you are racing for the helicopter pad!

In many ways some of the supporting characters are more engaging than the hero who, like many heroes, seems to have the ability to be right a lot of the time. The best written parts of this book are the battles, where the author's army experience really shines through and the action leaps off the page and you can practically smell the gun-oil. Thoroughly recommended as a ripping yarn.

The story is compelling, characters are well-drawn in all their frailties and there are some genuine shocks along the way, particularly when they all meet! REVIEW:
A very brightly coloured, well laid-out, and simple to follow detox/'youthing' guide, with the focus on de-ageing yourself rather than pitching a diet plan or kick-starting a weight loss programme, though in effect it's the same thing. An interesting twist. What man or woman wouldn't be interested in knocking off 5 years in this looks-conscious world by eating beetroot? There are concise 'science' bits on the best and worst foods to eat, the reasons why, and how you can most easily add them to your daily life.
There are some good overviews in the opening chapters: the main reasons why we age: poor digestion, hormonal imbalance, inflammation and advice on how to reduce their effects through a better diet. It does hammer home the 'youth' mantra, so if you are at all paranoid about getting older, this book will not make you feel any better about it. Focus on the health benefits, otherwise you may never leave the house again!
The 2-week detox is hard-core, but for a vegetarian or someone interested in becoming one, it's a great "short-sharp" diet plan. It isn't going to cost you a small fortune to buy it all, as most of the ingredients can be bought from your local supermarket these days, and she doesn't demand you only buy organic. You will also lose weight and feel better for it.
However, the EYY (Eat Yourself Young) lifetime eating regime she encourages you to adopt looks to me a little impossible (and miserable to anyone who isn't a vegetarian already) to stick to. Juicing takes time. Baking omelettes for breakfast take time and this just isn't viable for someone without a nanny or far more free time than most of us have. I appreciated the questionnaire sections which assess the state of your health, body, and the review of which bad stuff I put into it vs good stuff, and how I could change that ratio for the better, as there are a number of good, useful ideas.
However, I think there are other books which may not be as well-designed, but might give you a better, more convenient and detailed long-term solution.
PRODUCT: Eat Yourself Young: Take Years Off Your Looks with This Revolutionary New Eating Plan

The latter third is better than the bit preceding it.

It is forced to tie things up neatly with a Hollywood ending which is a shame as an Ellroyesque trilogy would have been interesting.

These insights are invaluable in understanding better how battles were fought and won. In this book he has gone even deeper, taking a number of swords from different periods of history and looking at them in depth, at their manufacture, design and use. He brings practical experience in wielding these weapons plus tremendous knowledge and enthusiasm. Blended together they make a tremendous book for anyone interested in history as well as swords and swordsmen.

The worst thing about Carte Blanche? It is just a bit dull. Fleming never needed a big plot twist at the end to build excitement. Don't bother.

REVIEW: Recent photographs from the war in Ivory Coast show casually dressed men in a street, all clutching AK47 variants, making this history of a weapon as relevant today as it ever was. Chivers brilliantly demonstrates that the AK47 specifically and assault rifles in general have had a far greater impact on the Cold War and post cold war world than any nuclear or biological weapon. This is a very detailed history of a weapon that dominates our world and as such it should be read by anyone who wants to understand modern warfare and the geo-political landscape we now exist in.
PRODUCT: THE GUN: The AK-47 and the Evolution of War

REVIEW:

When I picked up the book (great cover and treatment) and read the quotes I was very excited and my expectation was high. As I progressed through the book that expectation remained, I kept waiting for it to become something truly special and the fact it didn't left me vaguely disappointed.
This was a shame because it is a perfectly good book. A well-written look into the mind of a jaded, aged werewolf and the world of supernatural goings-on that he inhabits. The action is fast-paced, ferocious and exciting, with plenty of gore and visceral sex to keep you entertained. There are enough plot surprises to keep you amused although ultimately they get a little silly and I was unconvinced by the world of WOCOP etc.
Enjoy it as a superior horror/thriller, nothing more.

REVIEW_TITLE: The truth is a lemon meringue!

The characters are marvellous, the baddies are wonderfully evil and stupid and the heroes have their own comic foibles. Personally I prefer to read these myself so I can enjoy the word-play and sly jokes but this audio book is fun and the author does a good job. Buy every single one of them and read them to your children and friends. The world will be a better place for it.
PRODUCT: Mr Gum and the Biscuit Billionaire

I therefore approached this book with caution, particularly as the cover seemed a very lazy copy of a number of other Crusader books that have gone before. I was however very pleasantly surprised. The history was not rammed down my throat at the expensive of action and characterisation. On the flip side the history wasn't horrifically mauled just to satisfy the author's desire for more excitement. It was a good engaging story with interesting characters who managed not to come across as twenty-first century characters trapped in a different time-zone. Their was a good blend of excitement and reflection and I'm looking forward to the sequel.

However, once I had finished The Ten Thousand I needed another Kearney fix so started it. Although not quite as good as the Monarchies of God series this is still brilliant. Now i'll just have to get hold of everything else he has written.

REVIEW_TITLE: Run away and join the Legion...
REVIEW:
This is 'proper' military history at its best.
Our Friends Beneath the Sands: The Foreigh Legion in France's Colonial Conquests 1870-1935 starts in a place you wouldn't expect but the action soon shifts to the hot deserts of Algeria, before moving onto Vietnam, Benin, Madagascar, Morocco, The Western Front and back to Morocco again. This is the Legion of Beau Geste and (ahem) Jean-Claude van Damme's Legionnaire but the truth is much more interesting than the fiction.
Windrow writes succinctly, vividly and with authority on both the political and social background to the Legion and its campaigns and the military actions that took place. As you might expect he is at his very best on the battles and the soldiers that took part in them. Camerone (which precedes the events in this book) would not be the last time elements of the Legion were trapped and surrounded by numerically superior forces and forced to fight it out in vicious firefights like the siege of Tuyen Quang in 1885.
The maps are excellent which you might expect from Windrow but which is unusual for a book of this type. The photos brilliantly capture the men of the Legion and their battlefields in which they fought on, although it is a shame there are no colour photos of the ground the author walked when researching it.
Altogether definitely worth it for anyone interested in the French Foreign Legion or looking for fresh outlook on the colonial experience which is not centred on the British Empire.
PRODUCT: Our Friends Beneath the Sands: The Foreign Legion in France's Colonial Conquests 1870-1935

REVIEW:
I love James Ellroy. I've read everything he's written, love the LA Quartet and American Tabloid and went to see him speak to get my copy of this with high expectations. Possibly they were a little too high.
This is everything you'd expect from Ellroy, a brilliant evocation of the dark underbelly of America, with compelling characters both real and imagined who face and are generally defeated by rampaging personal demons as history flows around them. In that sense it is good.
In another sense I think the book required a more judicious edit and not just because of the typos. Two thirds of the way through the gloriously complex plot became merely convoluted and the whole thing started to drag before a rushed ending where the dying starts.
Maybe I'm being unfair. I reread American tabloid and Cold Six Thousand before starting it and maybe I had fatigue. Maybe it will be better on a second read. Hmmm...
