REVIEW_TITLE: First half is too long but otherwise a story told in a very clever way
REVIEW:
This was chosen as my latest book club book. It seems to be a combination of personal story and history - what could be wrong with that.
At 437 pages, I read the hardback which had a good size font that was very clear.
It was a clever decision to tell the story in the first person from the perspective of one of the twins. The girls were treated horribly and the reader is able to understand that properly when we see it from deep within the action. The innocence of the story makes the book much easier to read than I had anticipated. It could have been very downbeat and pessimistic (dour, maybe?) but Dasha's naivety and natural positivity lifts the narrative to make it very accessible. Dasha's voice is careful and made me think of "Room", the novel from a few years ago.
As the children mature, the tone of the voice changes and becomes more knowing with understanding creeping in. We also get to appreciate the huge gulf between them as people.
The story is full of shocking details of the treatment that the girls had to endure. Through their carers we also get glimpses of the world moving on outside.
I found the pace very slow in the first half of the book with lots of repetition - emphasis is fine but there can be too much of it. Halfway through and they are still at school.... tighter editing may have given even more impact to the story.
The twins are real and you will never forget that while you are reading. It's worth looking out a photo of them to get even more understanding of their day to day challenges.
The fictionalised style works well and the complete book has a feeling of a piece of historical fiction - there is no need to quote references to give the story authenticity. The author is trying to achieve understanding and she does that well using the detail of their very early lives which could be possibly be remembered later on.
At one point there is a huge jump in time which is unexpected and jars with the slow pace up until that stage. Oddly the girls (or women) don't seem to have aged emotionally during that gap and there is a clumsy rush to bring the reader up to date with Russian history. Maybe the point is that nothing happened to the girls during this period.
At the end of the book there is an Afterword that brings together some of the facts behind the book and completes the historical context. I pondered whether or not this would be better at the front but decided it was put in the perfect place.
PRODUCT: The Less You Know The Sounder You Sleep

REVIEW:
I read this book a few years ago as a book club pick and enjoyed it very much. I'm struggling to focus on lengthy novels at the moment (too much going on) and thought I would try some short stories.
Just after reading the first story I had fallen in love with reading again. This author writes beautifully, shifting perspective and treating her characters as real people. Thoughts move about in time and focus, with life never really going to plan.
I hadn't thought I would remember the stories but they are all wonderfully familiar as they developed.
There is a fantastic confidence in this writing - characters are used in different stories and time moves forward without explanation. There is a feeling that you are dipping in and out of the lives of old friends.
Never does a story have an obvious twist at the end but they all have very clear conclusions, some disturbing, some surprising and some completely natural.
PRODUCT: [(Runaway)] [ By (author) Alice Munro ] [August, 2013]

REVIEW_TITLE: Good idea but I didn't engage with Joan so the novel lost meaning for me
REVIEW:
The book explores a relationship between Joan and Gavin. Joan is 10 years old and has a condition which enables her to remember every detail of everything she has ever experienced. Gavin is a friend of her parents and, having recently been bereaved when his partner died suddenly, he comes to live with Joan and her family.
The narrative moves between Joan and Gavin and we see the same events from their perspectives. It's an interesting concept which feels well considered although I decided that it was too ambitious to put such different characters together as the main focus.
I found the adult characters well drawn but never engaged properly with Joan. She is meant to have a very adult outlook on the world because of her memory condition but I was never able to care about her. It's not important to like a character but if you don't care about them then it's really difficult to enjoy a book and, from a good start, I quickly found that I disconnected from the whole story
PRODUCT: The Reminders

REVIEW_TITLE: Timeless story which is written very well
REVIEW:
I've been given this book to read for a college course and was really excited. It was first published in 1951 and was the start of a post-apocalyptic genre which has become very popular today. This story become very famous in the 1980s when it was filmed for the BBC, imprinting the image of the triffids in everyone's minds. I had never read the book though.
It's a fairly small book at 270 pages, split into 17 chapters and is written in the first person narrative. This makes it really feel as though you are seeing the world though Bill's eyes, which is rather ironic based on the blindness that has hit the population.
All the way through I found it fascinating to think about the author's thought process - was it sci-fi? was it fantasy? or is it rather prophetic?
As the reader you really get a feel of the narrator's shock at the events as they unfold and appreciate how quickly the new world becomes normality to him. Bill's voice is strong and consistent through all that happens to him.
It's intriguing to see the instinctive reactions of those that have been blinded and how that effects the behaviour of those still able to see.
The writing is intelligent and stands up well to the passing of time. There is an ageless quality to the disaster as once the electricity goes then this world could be anytime in the past century.
I found the story telling brilliant and never doubted the plausibility of the plot. The reader's intelligence is never questioned and there are no obvious answers to anything.
Time passes and is dealt with well without the dates being fed to the reader on a plate.
Initially the story is based in London and I particularly like that as I could recognise many of the places that Bill was exploring with fresh eyes.
PRODUCT: The Day of the Triffids

REVIEW:
I've never bought one of these collections before but had the opportunity to review this book so was curious to give it a go.
As a first time buyer I expected it to be more up to date (not realising that the artist died more than 20 years ago).
Turns out that it is a feast of nostalgia, reaching back to cartoons that were drawn in the 1950s through to those from the 1990s and everything in between.
Where the cartoons need some knowledge of news events a paragraph is added explaining background which helps and proved to be very nostalgic - putting the current news into perspective.
Each year the publishers produce a collection based around a theme - this year's being holidays (summer, Christmas and Easter).
I found the book surprisingly good fun to read. I'm not a convert but may buy for certain people at Christmas.
PRODUCT: Giles The Collection 2018

REVIEW_TITLE: Does what it is meant to do more than adequately
REVIEW:
Unsurprisingly this product arrived in it's flat state so is quite a large parcel. The corrugated card is shrink wrapped in cellophane to keep to 10 pieces of card together.
Assembling the box is fairly intuitive but I did need the instructions for the first one I did. The pieces are cut well although the finished box is not a perfect fit, it's certainly close enough for most purposes. There is a strange tab that sticks out on the fastening bit of the box - I thought I had folded it incorrectly but can't see another way to do it (it's not on the picture though)
I'm going to use the boxes as storage on study shelves but they could have hundreds of uses.
I can't find it in me to get overly excited about flat pack boxes but they do the job for which they are intended
PRODUCT: Bankers Box Missive Value Mailing Box, 28x20x11

REVIEW:
This parcel arrived and it was a much heavier box than I had imagined. I could carry it but with great difficulty. This proved to be a sign of what a sturdy unit it is.
Unpacking the pieces seemed to take ages and I was a bit concerned that assembly would be difficult but I was wrong, 15-20 minutes and it was fully assembled.
We had a bit of a discussion about whether the shelves should be installed with the lip upwards or downwards and decided that either works well.
I'm going to leave the casters off to begin with but will hang onto them to give me options.
It's very solid and fits well into the gap that I planned.
PRODUCT: AmazonBasics 5-Shelf Shelving Unit on 4'' Casters, Chrome

REVIEW_TITLE: Okay but only for an easy, undemanding read
REVIEW:
"It's okay" sums up my reaction to this book. Alice and Ben meet briefly in a park and then each of them spend the next 31 days fantasizing about being a couple.
I like a novel that has a rigid structure and this story had that. Although the plot was only over 31 days, the font was big and there was plenty of white space, reading the book seemed to drag. I decided that the only way to read a book like this is in one sitting (and I nearly did that).
I got a bit bored with the characters. Alice and Ben were interesting initially but they were not developed as far as they could have been - I wanted to know more about reasons for their behaviours - Ben, in particular, was very contradictory, hinting at autism strongly in some parts but nothing like it in other areas.
The plot was fun to begin with but gradually petered out and the ending just felt a bit damp.
PRODUCT: 31 Days of Wonder

REVIEW_TITLE: Glad I read this book - fictional account of a refugee experience
REVIEW:
This was the latest choice of my book group. It appears to be part of a fairly small print run which makes the book feel like a curiosity. The novel is printed on lovely bright, white paper using a clear, sans serif font - 239 pages split into 29 chapters.
I know very little about Laos and the conflicts in which the country has been involved so I found that I had to work quite hard at the beginning by reading the book very slowly until I felt comfortable enough to start to appreciate the characters.
We hear three different viewpoints, a mother, a father and their eldest daughter. This is interesting but I found the movement of timescales confusing initially. The plausibility of the voices is good but I found that the differences between them were not enough for me and the book could have been more relevant if we had heard from Nuo alone.
The story has a very current feel to it - this family unit could be any family escaping from any country, trying to find their feet in a new life whilst constantly pining for their old world.
There is a court case that is referenced at various points and resolved towards the end - I felt that this was not developed sufficiently and proved to be a distraction from what is a very strong story.
Overall though, it's a powerful enough story to conquer the niggles that I had with the style and I am very pleased that I read this book. It is very readable and should be given to anyone who has problems with refugees to give more understanding about what they may have experienced. The plot is not complicated and the strength of the novel is the family relationships that are explored.
PRODUCT: Across the Mekong River

REVIEW_TITLE: Useful storage option and looks good
REVIEW:
This is the way to extend the functionality of a longstanding product.
It mixes like any other mixer but I like the function of storing the blades with the product so they don't easily get lost.
Aside from that the actual mixer is slightly bigger and heavier than my existing mixer but nothing I can't get used to. I do like the design which is more stylish than most.
I had a problem with the handle as the mixer is so heavy that it easily slips in my hand, especially when they are a bit greasy with cooking materials.
It does seem to be a little more costly than equivalents but not much.
PRODUCT: Russell Hobbs 22960 Easy Prep Hand Mixer

REVIEW_TITLE: Good quality product but not sure about the price
REVIEW:
This product is delivered wrapped in a plastic bag which serves the purpose but wouldn't stop it getting bent in the post.
All the screws and rawlplugs to attach to the wall are included but the base is sturdy enough for the rack to stand on its own (maybe against a wall to give it a bit more stability.
The build quality is reasonable although I'm aware that there are many other options for a cheaper price.
I'm going to use this in a bathroom to store creams and lotions.
Look carefully at the dimensions as it's bigger than I imagined for a "spice rack" but it suits my purpose perfectly.
PRODUCT: InterDesign Classico Wall Mount Spice Organizer Rack For Kitchen Storage, Chrome

REVIEW_TITLE: Unusual style which didn't work for me
REVIEW:
I do enjoy a heart wrenching story and this looked promising. It is a novel but is written in the first person making it seem very personal.
The book is just under 280 pages with occasional chapter breaks, although they are not numbered and named.
The tragedy is immediate - the narrator's pregnant wife is suddenly very ill and she has been rushed to hospital with a probability that the baby will need to be delivered early.
We see the hospital experience from Tom's view, sharing his shock and panic. His stream of consciousness jumps about, processing what is happening around him in an illogical way.
Initially I felt sucked into Tom's head and started to feel real grief on his behalf. Quickly though I lost interest in him. The author seems to try to exaggerate some of the events (e.g. the trip along the endless corridor to move Karin seemed almost ridiculous). I could understand many of Tom's actions but felt that the breathless pace could have been varied to give the narrative more engagement.
I also felt that the blurb of the novel gives away too much of the story and there was no tension about what the end was going to be - which took away the reality for me.
This could have been a very good novel but it didn't work for me.
PRODUCT: In Every Moment We Are Still Alive

REVIEW_TITLE: Boils and pours well but I don't like the design at all
REVIEW:
The product is packaged well with a pleasing amount of recyclable packaging.
I concerned about the emphasis on descaling products (there is even a discount for the Russell Hobbs Descaler on the box). I know that kettles do need descaling occasionally but I suspect that limescale will damage the aesthetic quality that gives this kettle it's distinctive looks. Extra maintenance immediately put me off!!
A blue light comes on while the kettle is boiling which is pretty but it's not very bright and actually boiling in the dark was needed for a maximum effect. The bubbles look lovely at the time but there is always condensation left at the top of the kettle after it has been used and that looks very unattractive.
The kettle looks much bigger than my previous one even though it has only 0.1 litre more capacity. The shape of the kettle does not taper at the top which makes it look clumsy.
It is not too noisy when boiling and pours well without a hint of a dripple.
PRODUCT: Russell Hobbs 21600-10 Illuminating Glass Kettle, Black, 1.7 Litre, 3000 Watt

REVIEW_TITLE: Great product - not completely convinced about the door attachment
REVIEW:
This is a very sturdy product. The material is light but the back piece and the pockets (front, side and bottom) are reinforced by some very thick cardboard.
Size wise - a couple of pairs of shoes could fit into one pocket comfortably.
There are the fittings for the unit to be attached over the door but I prefer a couple of screws in the back of a door as you don't then see the small pieces of metal sticking out into the room.
PRODUCT: InterDesign Aldo Over-The-Door Fabric Closet Storage Organizer For Purses, Handbags, Shoes, Sunglasses - 3 Pockets, Linen

REVIEW_TITLE: Quick holiday read but implausible as there are too many plot strands which are extreme and too convenient
REVIEW:
It can be difficult to write a new book when you're trying to reproduce the success of previous novel so I was curious to give this one a try.
The story is about two women - are are led to believe they are sisters but there is nothing to link them initially. One is paralysed and in a care home but we get into her head to see her frustrations at being able to communicate effectively. The other woman has just starting working in a prison and is very nervous when there are some strange things going on.
I work in a prison and so understand the characters caution but quickly became impatient with her approach to security - lots of procedures were not accurate but I'm be happy to give artistic licence to the author is the plot is strong (most readers will not have experienced prison and will go with what they read).
The problem is that the plot isn't good enough. It's very fast paced and the novel took no time to read but I found many elements of the plot ridiculous and they pushed the boundaries of coincidence way too far. Some of the detail of the prison and court system were unlikely and much was simply wrong (e.g. women's prisons are not catagorised A/B/C/D like the men's). The extreme declarations of anger and love between the main characters often felt out of place and did not fit the people. The medical treatment that Kitty received felt far too convenient and unlikely to have worked that quickly.
This is OK as an unchallenging holiday read but it was disappointing that the author put so much into the plot. In my view the plot should have been thinned out, allowing the characters to concentrate properly on the main issues.
PRODUCT: Blood Sisters: The #1 bestselling thriller from the Sunday Times bestselling author of My Husband's Wife

REVIEW_TITLE: A coming of age novel with so much more
REVIEW:
I was given this book by a lovely American lady I met on holiday. We spent some time verbally swapping books and then progressed to physically swapping the books we had each just finished.
In the acknowledgements, at the beginning, the author says that this book is based on a short story she had written earlier under the same name. I started the book a little guarded because of that comment as I wondered if the story had just been stretched to fit the novel format but there was no sign of that in the beautiful narrative that followed.
The novel is just over 300 pages, split into fourteen chapters which are then subdivided into small sections. The narrative is first person - Lily is 14 during 1964 and living in the south of the US. Her mother died 10 years earlier and she has a difficult relationship with her father. Rosaleen is a negro who looks after Lily and becomes involved with the Civil Rights movements at the time that the country is starting to change. The plot seems to balance political, personal and sensual - relating everything back to Lily's feelings and emotions.
This is a wonderful read which puts you in the head of Lily, observing everything going on around her. I found that I could understand how she was able to step away from much of the bad in the world and ignore the practicalities, living just for the moment.
The voice of Lily is very strong. She is young but the sadness and trauma that she has seen has made her strong. Through her eyes we see the treatment of negroes at the time and, along with Lily, try to make sense of the change that is in the air.
I found it particularly interesting how the author is able to manipulate time. Three weeks for a teenage girl is a long time but for most of the readers this will feel like hardly any time at all. The impression was that Lily had been living with the Boatwrights for months but every so often the author slips in a date to the narrative as a reminder that it has been no time at all.
Lily is charming and makes me smile all of the way through the book. She is serious and flippant - understanding and naive. She takes in everything and nothing. Most of all she is a great character who will stay in my head for some time as a person with no colour at all ("skin pigment really doesn't matter")
PRODUCT: The Secret Life of Bees

REVIEW_TITLE: Simple to setup with no unnecessary options
REVIEW:
This product does exactly what it promises for a great price and is exactly what I wanted.
Lots of bathroom scales offer wifi and various facilities which are of no interest to me.
This weighs in kilos or stones and shows 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 which may be important when losing weight!
It's simple to setup and looks stylish in the bathroom
What more can you ask!
PRODUCT: Salter Digital Body Weight Bathroom Scale (Ultra Slim, Easy Read Tempered Glass, Step-On Technology, Electronic Precision, 15 Year Guarantee) - Silver/Black

REVIEW_TITLE: I was delivered a bowl rather than a vase but it's very beautiful
REVIEW:
The product is presented in a stylish box which is great if you are giving it as a gift.
I was testing this for Amazon and was actually sent the bowl in the same range rather than the vase - but no problem.
It's very beautiful - shiny inside and out.
When I took it out of the packaging, I thought the bowl was scratched but it just needed a wipe and then looked perfect.
It's clear what a vase is to be used for and I'm less sure with the bowl but it's about the size for nuts and crisps so that'll work.
Whilst being used I was surprised how little the surface gets marked which is great - although any marks wipe off very easily.
PRODUCT: Georg Jensen Cafu Stainless Steel Vase, Mini

REVIEW_TITLE: Very promising start but it lost me a bit
REVIEW:
Post apocalyptic is not usually a genre of fiction of which I am a fan but I've read a few recently and enjoyed them so was eager to read this one when given the opportunity as it seems to review very well. I've read a couple of this author's novels previously but can't remember anything about them.
This book is 370 pages split into 51 chapters.
Most people have died from some sort of virus and we follow a small group of survivors in the Orkney islands. Straight away there is a curiosity with the group teaching history to the children and not being sure how far to explain - they now consider the numbers of people who dies in WW1 and WW2 as "puny" against those who have died more recently.
With the remote setting and the mysteries of the islands the setting becomes almost fantasy as a new world is imagined.
I was very comfortable with the plot and intrigue on the island as the survivors struggled with the drama and urge to return to a stable community. When the action moves to the mainland the plausiblity is stretched and various parts of the plot felt quite silly (a fireworks factory still with its fireworks - really?)
Generally the characters are drawn very well and they fit in comfortably with the story. The youngsters needed little back story but I felt I wanted to know more about the main two people (I found out afterwards that this is the third in a trilogy so maybe I should have started with the first?).
From an amazing start the book goes too far into the realms of the unlikely and towards the end I began to disengage completely, particularly as the pace of the action ramped up.
Maybe if you are a fantasy fan or have read the first two books then this would be good but I wasn't keen.
PRODUCT: No Dominion: An action-packed post-apocalyptic thriller (Plague Times Trilogy)

REVIEW:
This product comes in a smart looking box which reflects the colours of the hairdryer itself, including the gold trim.
There is a huge amount of packaging - the actual dryer has a protective layer which is great but then each accessory is individually wrapped in plastic with another plastic bag to hold them all together in the box.
The product is a sort of satiny cream with a gold trim which is attractive. It is initially very heavy and big - particularly when I previously had a Remington hairdryer which was a little smaller and a lot lighter.
It is the power that makes this a good dryer and didn't seem quite as heavy when in use - mainly because you're having to hang on in order to control the power.
PRODUCT: Remington AC9140 Proluxe Hair Dryer - Rose Gold

REVIEW_TITLE: Love the size and colour but they could be firmer
REVIEW:
These extra wide file dividers are really great as they stick out far enough that they can still be seen in most folders.
I has used these dividers in an A4 lever arch file with accounts paperwork in them and they work very well.
The card would be better if it were firmer as the tabs did get folded quickly and became creased although that wasn't a major concern
Liked the colours and and marbling effect
PRODUCT: Elba A4 Extra Wide 10 Part Pressboard Divider

REVIEW_TITLE: Great value for a product that does exactly what I want
REVIEW:
I've now been using this for a while and it's great. The product comes very neatly packed in a small box and I was impressed. It is light on the wrist and looks good.
I've had 2 fitbits previously and both have broken (one the charge point stopped working and the other the button fell off). I debated buying another but thought I'd try a much cheaper product as I really only just the step counting function. This one seems to review well so thought it was worth a try.
No charger is included but it uses a standard USB cable so that wasn't a problem. The body of the tracker clips off the strap and is very quick to charge.
Downloading the app on my phone was easy and it is very simple to use.
I love that the device strap has a regular buckle rather than a clip as some do. I also love that the steps show in large print so that I don't need glasses to see it on my wrist.
It's also worth reminding myself that this is 1/5 of the price of a fitbit.... It's difficult to be accurate but I think that this product in comparable with the fitbit in its step count.
One small negative is that the device has lost connection with the app but a restart sorted that out quickly.
PRODUCT: Fitness Trackers,Yamay Activity Tracker Watch Heart Rate Monitors Waterproof IP67 Smart Bracelet Fitness Wristband Pedometer Watch Sleep Monitor Step Counter Large Screen(0.96'') for Walking/Running/Cycling Work with iOS and android Phone

REVIEW_TITLE: Well written with lovely humorous tone but the subject matter is really only suited for those interested in cars
REVIEW:
I've a head full of stuff at the moment and have been struggling to concentrate on reading at the moment so thought I would try this light, comic book that I had originally bought for my husband (who liked it very much).
It is written as a combination between memoir and travel book - imagine Bill Bryson does Top Gear?
I'm ten years younger than the author and a woman which precluded me from some of the experiences that he describes but there was much of the nostalgia that I understood and remembered very well. My parents had an Austin 1100 as their first car and I never understood why they had a new car when they did not have much money, so was interested to learn here that the second hand market was being suppressed to support the British car industry.
The time of him growing up I found great to read but the book became much more remote when he started to get his own cars as I struggle with the man/car relationship and I quickly found myself getting bored. To the credit of the author he stays with him theme and continues to talk almost non-stop cars right through to the end.
The book is well written and I did read it but think that the subject matter did not engage with me even though I did enjoy the light comedy and pathos which are both scattered through the book.
PRODUCT: The Auto Biography

REVIEW_TITLE: Well presented but the format is becoming less relevant
REVIEW:
We were in the city for four days on an organised tour so I wanted something to back up the information we were being given.
In this book there is a good historical context with over 50 pages used to introduce the city and its various elements.
Half of the book is taken up with the various areas of St Petersburg which are described in good detail with specific places of interest being given additional information.
I found that a few things were out of date which is where the internet really wins. We went to the Hermitage and were looking for a section which had been moved since the book was published.
Internet access is not easy in St Petersburg so a book to carry around is great and the maps are very good.
Most of the section on hotels and restaurants are irrelevant as websites are more up to date, some useful tips in the Survival Guide was presented in a way which is very easy to read.
Everything in this book could be found elsewhere but it is well presented here and easy to access.
I still like this publisher but am finding that guide books are becoming less relevant to travel today.
PRODUCT: DK Eyewitness Travel Guide St Petersburg

REVIEW_TITLE: Beautiful little novel full of unique character - a romance without a love story
REVIEW:
I loved the unique quality of this author's previous novel "The Presidents Hat" so was looking forward to trying this one.
The novel is 215 pages, split into many, titled, chapters.
Again this story has a really interesting story at it's core. A middle aged doctor receives a letter from a recording company asking him to go to a meeting along with his band members to discuss a possible contract - the problem is that the letter has arrived 33 years too late. The band members have all moved on but Alain decides to try to track them down so he can listen to the original song again.
There is plenty of dark comedy alongside much pathos. All the characters have regret and have changed in many ways.
Using this seemingly superficial topic, the author dives into the modern France, exploring its political and artist scene with plenty of comments on them both.
The book is set in France but this state of the nation novel could be set in many western countries with their extreme politics and people desperate for change.
It is a small book but covers such a wide range of topics without ever going off course or preaching.
PRODUCT: French Rhapsody

REVIEW:
I've read many novels based in Russia and finally got to visit. While still in Russia I'm now pondering the next big holiday and Japan is high up on the list so this novel cam along at a good time.
The book is 275 pages, split into 27 chapters and written in a fairly large font so it's an easy read.
The story is Diana's - she is a nurse in the US who takes an opportunity to go to Japan to look after a toddler who she had cared for in the US as a baby. Through Diana's eyes we see a section of Japanese culture.
Diana has complicated emotional reason for leaving the US and she starts to get pulled back when the job in Japan gets complicated.
I thought this author writes wonderfully about Japan and builds up a picture of the society that many know little about. The streets, houses, food and culture are all intense and are a big element of the plot. The calm and control work well to contrast with the developments in the plot of the story. She manages to show that whilst the society may be different people are the same everywhere.
As the story progresses I found the plot became unlikely and I wasn't convinced about Diana's actions. This didn't spoil the book though and I did love the way the story was finally brought to a close.
PRODUCT: Yuki Means Happiness

REVIEW_TITLE: Great little collection with the usual varying quality of short stories
REVIEW:
There are some lovely little stories in here, not all brilliant but plenty of them are.
I found it quite hard to get into the first story but once I did then the book took off with some well observed descriptions of human emotions.
The stories are all based in Africa but the deeply human element translate to anywhere in the world.
Words are chosen carefully and the perfect one is always selected with an ability to describe such a huge amount with so few pages.
PRODUCT: What It Means When A Man Falls From The Sky: The most acclaimed short story collection of the year

REVIEW_TITLE: Great plot and this really could have happened!
REVIEW:
I'd never read any books by this author but had had him highly recommended many times. He normally writes non fiction but this is a novel only based loosely on the truth.
Before the story starts there is a huge list of characters - some real and some fictional. I thought this looked ominous and the plot was going to be very complicated, actually I found the list really useful and referred back to it for a while until the characters developed. I found the names quite complex for a while but quickly got to know them and the plot soon started to move at a cracking pace.
There is no doubt about the fictional nature of the plot as most of the characters are created but there is enough truth here to make the plot very intriguing. The Soviet Union was such an unstable place during this period and no-one was safe - this is shown very clearly by the author of this book. He shows the fear in everyone and the portrayed images to be so different to how the people were actually feeling.
Using the teenage children in the plot is a great device to play with their innocence and lack of experience whilst being able to compare Old Russia with New Russia.
Time moves on as the strands of plot come together but the author never patronises the reader which makes for a great book. You will need to think when you are reading this.
As the author has such a great knowledge of the truth, I found that this novel played with my mind and made me think that this could all have happened in Stalinist Russia.
I was reading the book whilst in Russia which helped with my reading experience but I think it would be great anywhere.
PRODUCT: One Night in Winter (The Moscow Trilogy)

REVIEW_TITLE: Good narratives but wanted a larger area map
REVIEW:
We went to Moscow in a guided group and so were restricted about where we went. This book helped with small sections on lots of places so we could easily get a little information about many parts of Moscow.
I think this would be ideal if you were visiting the city on your own for a few days. It's not an easy city to get round as the signs are all in the Cyrillic alphabet so any help is useful.
The information on hotels and restaurants is largely out of date and much better accessed via various websites. I liked the walks in the book as they are a great way to sample the sights.
There is a section at the beginning about the history and that was really useful as the city has had many changes.
The maps are good although we were staying a few miles out and so needed additional maps. I couldn't find a map of the wider area in the book and think that would have been really useful.
Great narratives throughout as I have come to expect from this series
PRODUCT: DK Eyewitness Travel Guide Moscow (Eyewitness Travel Guides)

REVIEW_TITLE: Too much of the same with no development but I still laughed sometimes
REVIEW:
I read The Rosie Project a while ago and completely fell in love with Don Tillman so I was looking forward to seeing how his life had moved on with Rosie around.
The book has 420 pages split into 39 chapters.
I've heard the author being interviewed a couple of times and he has performed readings from the book so I have imagined his voice as the "voice of Don Tillman".
It's a definite sequel and I think that this book would be less effective if you did not read the first one.
There are lots of sections that made me laugh out loud but i think that the whole book is a disappointment after the first. Don is still wonderful but the plot gets far too complicated and becomes a distraction from the great character. Don ties himself up in knots and Rosie ends up doing things which I felt were quite uncharacteristic.
PRODUCT: The Rosie Effect: Don Tillman 2

REVIEW_TITLE: Dark mystery thriller which is a great read
REVIEW:
I've previously read a couple of novels by this author with the same translator and enjoyed them hugely so I had big expectations of this book.
It doesn't disappoint on any level. In some ways this is a regular mystery story which keeps the reader guessing all the time. What makes it stand out from the crowd is that this novel is so dark. It is not written in the first person but the reader gets completely into the head of the main characters, understanding his anxieties and obsessions.
Lots of strands of plot are lightly touched on, leaving the reader to fill in the detail which makes everything seem more frightening. In contrast there are some sections that are so shocking they actually took my breathe away.
I read this book in one day although it is only just over 220 pages.
PRODUCT: Three Days and a Life

REVIEW_TITLE: Beautiful - I hope this author is able to write some more about this village.
REVIEW:
I was curious about this novel as I have read many other novels based in World War Two and also happen to live in a small village in Lincolnshire (the setting for this book). The author is old enough to remember this period which should give the book a genuine feel.
Looking as his history, the author has not written a novel for many years but he is a very experienced writer in other forms and that shows in the quality of this book.
From the start there is a warm comfortable feeling. It is as if the reader is being taken by the hand and walked through the village, seeing all the people and peeking into their worlds which vary hugely as you would expect.
It's a simple book with no complicated plot structure and no major events which overpower anything else (except the war, of course) but ever part of it is written beautifully, in a way that creates the scenes perfectly. There is a very light touch with the description - being able to paint such wonderful pictures with just a few words is quite an art.
All the time the author is aware that he is relaying a story, occasionally even reminding the reader about the circumstances where they have previously met some of the characters.
It's not a big village but there are a lot of people in the book. Once we get to know them they are feel natural very quickly but it does take some work from the reader to familiarise yourself with them all. They get involved with all sorts of things and the author tells us about them all without ever judging anyone's actions.
Lots of elements of the book are great but what shines is the ability to be able to balance the huge political background of the times with the tiny struggles that individuals face everyday.
I'd love to think that the author gets such great feedback that he decides to write some more about the village.
PRODUCT: There Was a Time

REVIEW_TITLE: Enjoyed it much more than expected - gave me lots to think about
REVIEW:
I'd been recommended this book by a number of people, however I'm cautious of this genre as I often find them too unrealistic for my taste.
This novel is 333 pages long, split into 53 chapters. Short chapter usually help a book to read quickly by giving it pace so that's a good start.
The story starts with a death on stage then quickly becomes more menacing as a killer flu virus spreads rapidly around the world. Lots of people with interconnecting stories are introduced and there plenty of ominous warnings about the imminent end of the world as we know it. Having established the scenario the pace slows a bit as the characters come in. It picks up again once the links start to be established and I was hooked.
It's a complex story with plenty of drama. The narrative focuses on a few people who are still alive twenty years on but there are plenty of references back in time to explain what has happened since the virus first struck.
There are loads of unanswered questions which gives the story a genuine feeling.
Characters are allowed to develop but it is clear from the beginning that characterisation comes a second place to the descriptions of the post apocalyptic world in which they live.
After the initial panic, the book becomes very reflective and this is when it is at its best. Looking back at the futility of civilisation and the strength of humanity to survive.
Towards the end I found the plot stretched the boundaries, that it had successfully established, too far and I wasn't convinced that the ending matched the rest of the novel. This was always going to be a tough story to conclude and the author did a good job.
PRODUCT: Station Eleven

REVIEW_TITLE: Sturdy product which is very useful but rather utilitarian to look at
REVIEW:
This product is described as being "indispensable" - I'm not quite convinced about that but it is pretty useful.
It is a hard, white plastic square tube, the front of which opens up. You can then pull out the washing lines giving a rectangle hanging space.
It would need to be fixed very firmly to the wall as you have to pull out the lines quite forcefully. Very long screws are provided to fix the unit to the wall and I understand why when using it.
This unit would be useful in an airing cupboard to give extra drying space or above a radiator and can be tucked away when not in use.
When folded away it is not a particularly attractive unit but basic and utilitarian.
The washing lines themselves are sturdy but with a little flexibility.
Hopefully this will last for some time.
PRODUCT: Leifheit Telegant Wall Dryer - 30 Protect, 70 cm

REVIEW_TITLE: It was OK - interesting idea but not sure the execution worked
REVIEW:
I knew little about this book although, having been offered it to read, I have read reviews and was excited about some of the high profile recommendations it is getting.
The book is just under 300 pages, split into chapters which are named "The Constellation of...."
The narrative is first person and written in the form of a person telling the story to her friend.
The time frames jumped about a lot of the narrator tried to come to terms which what had happened to her as a child. I think the author did this to try to show the way that the mind jumps about all the time although I'm not sure it really worked - the brain moves far quicker than a writer can attempt to put on the page and the result was quite clunky.
I liked the premise of the bed bound teenager and thought that her languid life was shown very well - I also enjoying reading the character of the mother as I could relate to her frustration.
PRODUCT: The Things We Thought We Knew

REVIEW_TITLE: Great little snapshots which seem to say so much in just a few pages
REVIEW:
I'd never read any Chekhov before and had been given a couple of his short stories to read as part of a literature appreciation course. I decided to buy a collection and read a few more.
This book is less than 200 pages and contains 26 stories, along with a 12 page introduction which gives a background to the author as well as introducing some of the tales.
The stories are all fairly short and very readable. I was surprised how much I enjoyed them.
Every story that I read was great and Chekhov seems to capture a moment in time by bringing into the head of the reader.
Some of them are very moral whereas others observe without making any judgements.
I was blown away by the bleakness of almost all of the stories and loved the emotions that they stirred up in me - sadness, disgust, anger.
If you want to get a real glimpse of Russia in the late nineteenth century then this is a great place to start.
PRODUCT: Selected Stories (Wordsworth Classics)

REVIEW_TITLE: Great kettle - love the shiny black design
REVIEW:
I think its reasonable to say that Black & Decker aren't known for their kettles so I was curious to see what their design experience could bring to a domestic product.
The capacity is 1.6 litres (compared to my current Tefal of 1.7) - slightly less than I've been using but the overall product is much more compact which I like.
The packaging is good with the kettle being tightly protected. Instructions are short which makes sense for a kettle.
I wasn't sure about the plastic because it does feel like plastic but quickly got used to it. It is very light and should stop any limescale building up like it does on the metal kettles. I do like the black shiny colour which looks very stylish.
There is a good grip on the handle that makes the kettle feel very safe when you're pouring it. The pour is good and it doesn't drip.
It is surprising how different kettles make varying noises when boiling - this one is different from my last kettle but not objectionable in any way.
One feature that is very useful is that when you use all the boiling water the kettle can be refilled with cold and immediately switched back on - not all kettles do this!!
PRODUCT: Black & Decker 24240 Plastic Kettle, 1.6 Litre, 3 Kw, Black

REVIEW_TITLE: Interesting example of the time and enjoyable read
REVIEW:
This is a small novel of just over 150 pages, split into 10 chapters and it's really easy to read. I have been given this book to read as part of a literature appreciation course - I read Room With A View many years ago but remember little of it and had not heard of this novel.
The writing is brilliant from the start. It's very funny and the characters are compelling. Every sentence seems to contain some witticism - this is a novel which needs to be read slowly in order to catch everything.
It is a short novel and the plot is straightforward - lots happens in such a few pages and it has to be straightforward. Forster clearly sets out back stories, relationships and potential for conflict.
The plot takes the form of a farce with the characters rushing about without thinking of consequence - everything happens quickly with people and actions being exaggerated for comic effect. There are several elements of the plot which are simply preposterous and made me gasp!
I found the book very implausible but understood that he was playing with stereotypes of the times. Once used to that then the book becomes quite sensitive as the characters are drawn to their fates.
PRODUCT: Where Angels Fear to Tread (The Penguin English Library)

REVIEW_TITLE: Amazing start but the second half is awful
REVIEW:
I've read some good stuff recently but haven't picked up a psychological thriller for a while so was excited about this one. The cover looks really spooky which promises a good read.
And it's fair to say that I've not read a book like this before. There are two characters - Jack and Syd - who have bought their first house together. They find it to be very uncomfortable with an unsettling atmosphere. The story is told by the couple and we flip between their first person narratives. We are looking at the events after they have happened with Jack and Syd using the process of writing as a way to understand what they have been through. Each of them reads the others chapter before they write the next and the book takes on some sort of delayed conversation.
It's all breathless and emotional with lots of raw feelings. I couldn't help but compare this to the "found footage" type of film making used in The Blair Witch Project and others.
As it is a stream of consciousness the thoughts skip about all over the place and that makes it very plausible. Their minds also focus on seemingly random events which, again, I felt very realistic. In the beginning of the book a few clues are placed casually and not expanded at the time which hooked me in and made me want to keep reading.
It was a big disappointment when the action caught up with the writing in the second part and the plot gets mad. The subtlety and atmosphere of the first part is lost and the novel becomes very clumsy. I had been hooked enough by the characters to read through to the end but by the time I got there I really didn't care who did what. The police character isn't plausible at all and I thought she could have had a narrative to show her view of the story. It might have been better to stop the first person narratives altogther in the second part as that would have marked a complete change over?
The structure of the first part is so great and it is sad to see what the author did to create drama in the rest of the book.
PRODUCT: The House

REVIEW_TITLE: Simple, effective product if you accept that potatoes usually need to be chopped a bit first
REVIEW:
This product comes in a good firm box so if you are going to store it in a cupboard (probably) or give it as a present (less likely) then it can stay in the box.
It's a really simple idea in that you put the vegetable in the slot and push it through then the blades cut the vegetable into sticks - width depending on which of the two attachments you are using.
Like many people I have found that potatoes need to be cut before they can be chipped but it works really well for other veg for crudities - carrots, cucumber, etc.
It's got a good firm handle and is easy to wash - either in the dishwasher or just under the tap.
PRODUCT: Leifheit Chip Cutter

REVIEW_TITLE: Great product but needs careful usage
REVIEW:
This is brilliant stuff and I've been using it for years. It's a sort of wax type product but much softer so is easier to apply - it's more solid than gel though so it feels like you are putting on a product rather than just some greasy stuff.
This range of products all have wonderful scents and they remind me of going to the hairdressers - which is usually a pleasurable experience so opening the jar always makes me smile.
The only downside is the inner lining under the screw top to which the product always sticks making it quite messy to get out of the jar to begin with, although you get used to it after a while.
Somehow the product feels sticky in the jar but doesn't when it gets onto your hair - very clever.
The style will hold comfortably for hours as well.
PRODUCT: BED HEAD by TIGI Manipulator Texture Paste 57 g

REVIEW_TITLE: Good pen but expensive and 12 pens the same is a lot of pens
REVIEW:
I was given one of these pens to test out.
It's a sturdy pen and I like the grip on the barrel of the pen. There is a Pentel sticker on the pen when it arrives but that is easily removed without leaving any residue.
I hadn't read the description very well and was expecting it to write in pick, although it is black as described. The pen writes very well from different angles and is very smooth.
The cartridge is held in the barrel and popped out like a ball point pen although it is definitely a gel pen
The pen is sold as appropriate for left handed people as it does not smudge, although I found that it does smudge a little if rubbed immediately after writing. I suspect it doesn't smudge as much as other gel pens though.
It's expensive at over �60 for 12 pens and I'm not sure I would pay that - I also don't think I would want 12 pens all the same.
PRODUCT: Pentel 0.7 mm Tip "EnerGel Sterling Black Ink" Pen - Pink (Pack of 12)

REVIEW_TITLE: Good size and interesting facts but needed more history
REVIEW:
This guide is a good size to carry about and has some great facts which are interesting to find out more about the city.
There is a map that can be carried separately which was a good map and easy to use.
There are some walking trails around the city in the book but these are weak and not presented well - a friend had a different guide book which was much easier to use when we were trying to follow a route.
I wanted more historical information than this book gave and found that I needed to read other texts.
As ever there is much focus on specific restaurants and hotels which are capable of changing very quickly and there are many review sites which recommend places to eat and stay much more efficiently.
PRODUCT: Krakow Marco Polo Pocket Guide (Marco Polo Travel Guides) (Marco Polo Guides)

REVIEW_TITLE: Generally a good read - I enjoyed the historical context but the plot had weaknesses
REVIEW:
The Edwardian era which led up to World War One is an interesting period. There was massive social change just about to start and the world was beginning to become much more liberal after many years of strict Victorian morals.
I've read a previous novel by this author and enjoyed it so was curious to read this one. It is nearly 400 pages, split into 25 chapters.
This story is about Della, a young girl in the period immediately prior to the war. Her auntie encourages Della's passion for flying and supports her financially. I know very little about flying and enjoyed the opportunity to learn about it on a very simple level. There is a fair amount of detail but the enthusiasm comes through strongly and there is enough of the personal story to keep any reader's attention.
The historical perspective is fascinating, particularly when you read the section at the back which gives information about the research and the facts behind the fiction.
I found that the personal side of the plot is weak compared to the history although I still enjoyed reading it. Some moves in the plot are very predictable and the build up to the conclusion of the story seemed to be rushed and improbable.
PRODUCT: The Wild Air

REVIEW_TITLE: Brilliant book and totally appropriate - I loved everything about this book
REVIEW:
This book was chosen as my latest book club pick. It had been shortlisted for the Bailey's Prize and the author appears to have won awards for previous novels.
The book is just over 300 pages split into 49 chapters.
It is relatively unusual for novels to be set in the 1950s which was a fairly uneventful decade in comparison to the rest of the century.
Putting the characters together in a hospital serves as a vehicle to give a good cross section of society and observe how people get along together - or not!!
We learn a lot about the general society of the time including the realisation that life is much cheaper than today. There is a healthy acceptance of death which may have been related to the not long finished world war.
Everyone judging everyone else but quickly seems to appreciate that there is much more below the surface of each character and it is interesting to consider the leveling effect of possible death.
I particularly admired how the narrative switched between characters, all of them observing the constrained situation in which they have ended up.
There are some wonderful phrases used in the text as the author seems to portray the period perfectly.
Somehow the atmosphere in the hospital seems to mirror the outside society and the revolutionary changes that are starting to happen. So much is covered around the plot, dealt with using great sensitivity and no degree of prejudice - class, sexuality, morality, healthcare and much more. These difficult subjects are handled with a very soft touch that often brings a smile to your face.
When we finally get to Part Two the characters are so familiar that the author seems to have grown in confidence and switches between the people without any confusion. I'm not completely convinced that the move to a different country was necessary but I accepted it very quickly.
Also worth noting that I loved the lead up to the ending as well as the actual ending itself.
PRODUCT: The Dark Circle: Shortlisted for the Baileys Women's Prize for Fiction 2017

REVIEW_TITLE: Interesting plot but not an engaging read
REVIEW:
The synopsis of this novel makes it sounds like a memoir and that is what drew me to it. There are many true stories of parents having to fight for their children in order to live better lives. This is not a real story but seems to be trying to illustrate many of the struggles going on everywhere and everyday.
The book is nearly 300 pages, split into many small chapters narrated alternately by Anna and Tom (the parents) with the occasional chapter by Teddy or Isaac (the boys).
There is no doubt it is a heart wrenching story but I found that the characters never managed to engage me in the way that I have been in the past by novels of a similar style. Part of the problem is the very small chapters which are written in the first person. Switching about so frequently meant that it took a long time to get any empathy for the situations. They all refer to themselves as "I" as it is first person and I found that I frequently had to stop and think who was narrating.
Teddy's voice is only a minor role but I found that unconvincing and thought the story would be better served to hear from only the parents
Having said all that though the plot is good and this novel will appeal to many just on that. I was disappointed that it didn't grab me in the way that I expected.
PRODUCT: The Way Back to Us: The book about the power of love and family

REVIEW_TITLE: Well written parody in a great style but feels out of date already
REVIEW:
I had the opportunity to read this book and was curious!! The referendum vote seems to have encouraged many books of this type which are "gifted" between liberal Remainers to skim read or put on a shelf in the toilet to be ignored - I've been given a couple of similar books which have ended up next to the toilet.
Reading the back of the book I was interested to see if Alice would find anyone who could make any sense of the madness around her - but thought it very unlikely.
To book aims to bring the debating and decision making down to the level of a fairy tale and it does very well. Alice is the undecided observer who listens to the general confusion and prejudice around her. There are many funny lines and the poems, in particular, are very good with a definite feel of Lewis Carroll.
At times I found myself laughing out loud and at other times cringing about how close the descriptions of people are to the real deal - guess we are all animals in a way??
I read this book in the middle of June when the world seems to have shifted yet again. The general election has happened and several dreadful human tragedies have played out on TV and social media. The effect of time doesn't make the book any less funny but it does make it much less current, in fact it felt decidedly out of date.
It was very much written as a snapshot of time which must have been a gamble for the author. The UK is changing so much at the moment and this book does feel "past it" already. Still funny though.....
As an example one great quote was "a decision that barely anyone understood is being carried out by a bunch of people who don't think it should happen" - how true!!
PRODUCT: Alice in Brexitland

REVIEW:
Bought this for my husband for Christmas as he has always been a fan of Phil Collins.
The author appears to be very honest with his experiences and it was interesting to read more about the man behind the headlines.
I think the book was probably slightly longer than it should have been but it's still pretty good.
PRODUCT: Not Dead Yet: The Autobiography

REVIEW_TITLE: Really enjoyed this book which shows us a snapshot of society in New Orleans
REVIEW:
I've read this book as part of a literature appreciation course. I'd heard of neither the author or the book so it really was an unknown commodity.
The book is 220 pages split into 39 chapters. Also worth noting that this version uses a fairly large font and has notes on the pages so no searching at the back of the book.
There is a brief introduction to the author but no detailed analysis of the novel. This was very pleasing as I really love to read a classic novel without having been told how I should be enjoying it.
The plot is great - it deals with society, class, feminism, expectations, marriage, motherhood and many other issues. All wrapped together with many small vignettes of moments in time. This author was primarily a short story writer and this becomes very clear when reading this book as you can see that many of the small chapters could almost stand alone as short stories.
Edna is wonderful as a heroine, she is full of flaws but manages to hold herself above the other characters whilst not being afraid to display her weaknesses.
It's a complex situation and there are some huge decisions to be made. Kate Chopin shows the reader what is happening without ever judging the characters or patronising the reader. The reader can judge Edna but such judgements would be foolish without taking time to try to understand her.
This tale is still very relevant today although it not as shocking as it probably was in 1899.
PRODUCT: The Awakening (Vintage Classics)

REVIEW_TITLE: Does everything useful that the more expensive models do and great value
REVIEW:
Having been recommended an electric toothbrush by my dentist, I've already got an Oral B brush as he said they are the best on the market. It is quite a whizzy one with various features and was relatively expensive.
So I was curious to see what this one was like as it's the same company but much cheaper.
In all honesty it looks pretty much the same and seems to operate in the same way. It doesn't have some of the advanced features (for example my existing brush links to wifi - who knew that was a thing? - and I used it once). The battery seems to last as long and it still have the timer which I've never quite worked out anyway.
All in all, I think this is fantastic value and I would definitely buy in the future.
PRODUCT: Oral-B Pro 600 Sensi Ultrathin Electric Rechargeable Toothbrush Powered by Braun (Ships with a UK 2 Pin Plug)

REVIEW_TITLE: Fine balance of life between the personal and the outside society
REVIEW:
This book sounded like fun - there is an apartment block in Paris which is the centre of the story and is fed by the stories of all the individuals that live there.
It's 250 pages divided into 43 chapters.
The first page starts full of wonderful description. I could see every detail of the attic room in which Edward was waking up. The building is created as a blank canvas and gradually pictures are created by looking at the various people. From the start we learn about the building as well, with it's various creaks, scuffs and floors. The weather is very hot which effects everyone and everything. We see the sun coming up in the first couple of chapters which shows the building gradually waking up as everyone starts their days.
I thought that the prose were just spectacular, managing to be intensely intimate and all encompassing at the same time. I usually read at quite a fast pace but found that I was slowing down to soak up the rhythm of the sentences.
To begin with there is much mention of the floors that the various people live on and I got a bit distracted trying to work out where everyone was. I ended up drawing myself a plan and felt that the author could easily have put a plan at the start.
Having very quickly got used to the comfortable life in the block, the plot shifts fast into a more edgy view of society and I realised that the "Dividing Walls" of the title are going to be metaphorical as well as physical.
This is the first novel from this author and I'm really impress with the ambition to show such a specific problem in society in such a brave way. The book shows how the rise of extremism in it's many forms is effecting the lives of the normal people and how easily anyone can be drawn into hatred.
There is a clever balance between the personal and society which is unusually good. There is a general feel of how lives are effected by national politics. This seems to be achieved by many small observations set among the ancient problem of intolerance. Hate is shown in a very passionate way which is quite scary to read at some points.
When the end approaches it feels very natural and seems to leave many unanswered questions as normal life does. I'm looking forward to reading more from this author.
PRODUCT: These Dividing Walls

REVIEW_TITLE: Beautifully written but will not encourage me to read more Hardy novels
REVIEW:
I read this novel for the first time as part of a literature appreciation course.
It's not an easy read and it shows many parts of society which are not comfortable - particularly the shocking opening.
I very much enjoyed the process of talking through the novel but not sure I would pick up any more Hardy out of choice as I grew tired of the down beat version of life.
There is no doubt though that the book is written beautifully and his descriptions of the countryside will stay with me for some time.
PRODUCT: The Mayor of Casterbridge

REVIEW:
The observation of youth culture is not a topic I would normally read about and many novels tackling this subject would tend to be marketed as YA novels. However, this book was highly recommended as a book which should be read by all people so I was curious.
It's almost 300 pages split into 39 chapters.
Gang culture doesn't touch my life on a day to day basis so it is easy to dismiss it as nothing but a curse to society, however anyone who is prepared to invest time in a book like this is looking for so much more and the author gives us that.
It is clear that Polly Courtney has researched the world she is using and she appears to get into the minds of the various gang members involved in the story.
Initially it's difficult to get used to the authentic language that is used but the glossary at the front really helps - within a few chapters I felt quite at ease with the dialogue. This makes the story feel very real as you manage to get into Alesha's head and start to understand her distrust of the unknown. I really got a feel for the immediate way that she runs her life with no thought for the future.
The process of reading this book is hard as it forces you to challenge your own opinions of Alesha. We see how she makes her decisions about what is the truth and how she applies her prejudice to her judgements. The difficult part for the reader is to think about what you would do, given her background and her limited access to resources.
Her teacher edges towards being a cliche but she is used well and serves an important role in the plot in providing an alternative view for Alesha to consider
It's very hard for most people to sympathise with those involved in gang culture - this book does not judge the gang members but tries to understand, which is the best that all of us can do. I found myself becoming angry and frustrated by her life which shows how strong the character was to me.
To read this book then you'll have to have a curiosity about gang culture and, if you have, then you'll find this book fascinating and very rewarding. I hope that this novel will make you question your beliefs as it did with me.
PRODUCT: Feral Youth

REVIEW_TITLE: Lovely product which looks good enough to be a gift and is great value
REVIEW:
The product comes in a pretty box although the box is slightly too big for the bottle which makes the bottle rattle about a bit. The bottle itself is plastic and has the same pretty illustrations as the box
There is a screw top then a removable foil lid to keep the product fresh.
To get the lotion out you flip up the lid of the screw cap and squeeze. This is great when there is plenty of lotion in the bottle but I can imagine that it will be more difficult as the level gets lower and this bottle will end up being stored upside down.
The scent is lovely and quite unusual - it's definitely lavender but there are lots of other tones in there as well, such as violet and sometime more musty which I think is the amber. I love a lavender scent but this is even better.
The lotion is lovely and thick which lets it soak in very smoothly.
After several hours my skin still felt soft and there was still the lovely scent.
PRODUCT: Heathcote & Ivory Lavender Fields Softening Body Cream, 250 ml

REVIEW:
And it is really a very short introduction. We've got 130 pages of small text in a small book which is smaller than a normal paperback. The first 70 pages covers the period to approximately 1900 and, being printed in 2012, the rest covers up to Putin's influences.
The text is a bit dry at times but is it a very informative read. I learnt loads and would recommend it to anyone wanting a general background to the country.
PRODUCT: Russian History: A Very Short Introduction (Very Short Introductions)

REVIEW:
Lots is written about World War 2 and it always makes a great backdrop to a story, particularly where a plot explores the investment of ordinary people with the Nazi regime. This book focuses on three women who come together as Germany surrenders - they are are then used to show the personal impact of the Nazi regime on Germans and what came about after the war was over.
The book is approximately 350 pages and is broken up into 38 chapters which move about in time and place. The time flips are used to add backstory at appropriate places and are used appropriately to show us how they got to the castle and what happened to them afterwards.
We follow the three women who come from very different places and react in ways that are surprising at times to all the changes through which they go, although they have many things in common.
It's a very gripping book and I couldn't put it down. There is a feeling of reality all the way through and there have clearly been a lot of research gone into preparing this book (which you understand at the end). We get a view of the practical measures brought into Germany after the war to deal with the aftermath connected with both the local area and the wider world.
The structure is very orderly with the chapters being labelled with dates as well as places. This order seems very fitting with the Germanic culture running through the characters.
It's a powerful read and really made me think about what happened to women like these. The world was not kind to ordinary Germans after the war and it is interesting to consider this - this book does this beautifully and sensitively.
PRODUCT: The Women of the Castle: the moving New York Times bestseller for readers of ALL THE LIGHT WE CANNOT SEE

REVIEW_TITLE: Great socks and they don't slip
REVIEW:
These are very good socks. They are small enough to wear under any trainer type of shoe and not show. They have a rubber strip in the heel which prevents the sock from slipping (and it worked!!).
I've got some other socks which aren't as good as these ones.
I slightly regret getting so many black socks and would have preferred white as they seem more summery but, as they don't show, it doesn't matter to much.
Also worth mentioning that they feel quite thick and seem to prevent the shoes getting smelly.
PRODUCT: Malloom� 5 Pairs Bamboo Fiber Net Loafer Boat socks Liner Low Cut No Show Socks

REVIEW_TITLE: A couple of irritations when using but the product is good in other ways
REVIEW:
I've never had a Braun iron before so was interested in this one.
It arrives packaged with the ironing plate well protected. I'm never happy with too much packaging and there isn't much here but it's not very well designed so that the iron was rattling about a bit in the box - not enough to be damaged though.
Without reading the instructions the product looks very intuitive and familiar. The instructions though are very good - written in many languages but with a great visual section which covers all the functions of the iron.
There is a self clean function but it is clumsy and I have seen much better options on other irons when you just press a button. Here you have to release a part which then tends to spring out.
The lid for the water tank doesn't sit very well and needs to be pushed quite firmly to shut it.
Steam function is good and the plate for the actual ironing is very smooth - it has a curved surface at the back which sounds great but I found I didn't really notice it when using the product.
The most irritating part of using the iron is when you put it on its heel as the cable gets in the way. The place that the cable comes into the iron needs to be flexible and this iron doesn't have as much movement as other irons which makes it a bit awkward to use.
Plenty of volume for the water in the tank and it seemed to last for a long time. I tended to iron with a high temperature and a low steam level which worked very well for most clothes.
There is a button on the top which operates the water spray and I kept pressing this by mistake when just holding the iron which was a bit annoying.
PRODUCT: Braun TexStyle 7 Pro steam iron SI 7042GR

REVIEW:
I've read a few novels by this author previously and they are usually good so I was looking forward to this book.
We meet Grace at the start of the story. It is just after WW2 and she is in an unsatisfying marriage, struggling to cope with her children with weather extremes seeming to mirror the lives of Grace and those around her. The book is full of beautiful description which quickly builds atmosphere as temperatures change wildly. The style of the writing is very journalistic and snappy - "Grace is... then ... happens, then .... happens" - this gives the book a good pace and enables the author to slow things down when the weather becomes hot and languid. All the way through it is compelling how the atmosphere effects the characters so much.
The novel is set in a time where the world is very different but I was uncomfortable with the speed with which Grace moved on and was maybe not as bought into her loveless marriage as I should have been.
The plot became very predictable at around the half way point so I was delighted to be shaken up as it progressed and hooked me back in again.
This is a reasonably good read which I will recommend to friends. It's not going to be a particular challenge and will do anything to inform but will entertain.
The book is approx 250 pages split into 12 chapters.
PRODUCT: The Stars are Fire

REVIEW: This has a bit of an odd smell but is not unpleasant and really cheap. I approached using it as if it were a body spray then it seems OK. As a perfume it doesn't really compete on quality
PRODUCT: Milton-Lloyd Cosmetics Grasse Experience Parfum de Toilette 50 ml

REVIEW_TITLE: Good product which works for hours but could do with an applicator to avoid getting under your fingernails
REVIEW:
Presented in a smart box with a slip cover, this jar sits neatly in the box with no unnecessary packaging. The jar is matt black and I found that the labels peel off easily leaving an attractive product which could be reused for other things.
There is a screw top lid which, when undone, shows the jar to be thick glass.
The product sits well in the jar and looks good quality as it is quite thick. The cream needs to be dug out a bit and an applicator would be really useful. When rubbed in well, the cream sinks into the skin quickly and skin feels softer immediately.
The scent is lovely - it's advertised as "sleep inducing" which I would contend but it is very pleasant.
Any product that hydrates the skin is good and this certainly does that. I've been using through out the day and it's effects can still be felt on my hands several hours after application so would be very effective over night..

REVIEW:
This author's previous two novels were recommended to me by many people but I didn't get on with either of them. I felt her worth persevering with though so was interested to read her latest - it's less than 200 pages so shouldn't be too much of a problem!
Actually. I was completely blown away by this book - it's amazing.
The first thing that struck me is the gorgeous prose that flows beautifully and almost demands to be read out loud. The narrative moves from dialogue to description seamlessly but there is never any doubt about the context - very clever. I found myself actually becoming breathless at some points in the novel.
Half way through the book there is a change of pace which gives a very different (but no less brilliant) feel.
I was particularly impressed by the intensity of this novel which must have required such restraint to keep so short.
There is a recurring theme of a Van Gogh painting, the colours of which hang over every page
There are two narrators but none of the irritating flip flopping that many authors use - we get to understand one character who then hands over to another in a perfect way.
I may have to go back and try her other novels again

REVIEW_TITLE: Not as painful as people say!!
REVIEW: After debating it for a while, I am SO glad I finally bought this epilator! After years of shaving I decided to switch to waxing but I found it too time consuming and messy and ended up with loads of ingrown hairs. I was put off buying an epilator because I'd heard they were really painful but i finally decided to bite the bullet and I'm so happy I did. I've used this three times now. I won't lie the first time did hurt, but it wasn't like a soul crushing unbearable pain (Also I have only used this dry, apparently using it wet is less painful). The second and third times I've used this have been so much less painful because there's just less hair there already! the gentle cap does help with the pain BUT it takes way longer. The little light really helps highlight the hair so you dont miss any. It does grab smaller hairs than waxing but don't expect 100% smooth legs like you get with shaving - I feel like this is well worth that compromise as you only have to use it once every week or two. Would definitely recommend!

The garment is OK however one needs to be aware that in garments coming from Asia the sizes do not correspond to the UK sizes.
An M size is much smaller than a size 14. If you are a size 14 order at a size L (large)
